about/index.html.summary: About nanoql nanoql is an open-source library for quantitative finance on .NET, under the Apache License 2.0. Its models, curves and pricers are plain functions of immutable inputs, and its market conventions are data. Where it comes from nanoql builds on open-source work, and every file it ports records where from: QuantLib. nanoql's core is derived from QuantLib 1.44, and its results are checked against QuantLib's own. Its design differs: it has no observers, lazy objects or global evaluation date. Where porting finds a defect, nanoql usually fixes it, and each place its results depart from QuantLib's is documented in Divergences. QLNet. nanoql's extensions port QLNet's mortgage-backed securities, with their prepayment models, and its amortised-cost bonds, checked against QLNet 1.13.2. FpML. nanoql's conventions files accept the codes of FpML's coding schemes, such as its day-count and business-centre codes, beside nanoql's own names. Their copyright notices and licences are on Licences and notices. nanoql is an independent project: the QuantLib and QLNet projects, and ISDA, which publishes FpML, are not affiliated with it and don't endorse it. Who maintains it nanoql is sponsored and maintained by Masseef (nanoql and Masseef). It is developed in the open on GitHub: anyone can report an issue, ask in its Discussions, or send a pull request, signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin. Contact Questions and ideas: GitHub Discussions. Security reports: see Security. The code of conduct: conduct@nanoql.org.

about/masseef.html.title: nanoql and Masseef | nanoql
about/masseef.html.summary: nanoql and Masseef Masseef sponsors nanoql and maintains it. How Masseef uses nanoql Masseef's platform prices through nanoql. It calls nanoql's public API from adapters behind its own pricing interface: the trade, its market data and its conventions go in, the results come out, and nothing is held between calls. Because nanoql's pricers are stateless, the platform can reprice a trade as of any past date, and revalue a portfolio in parallel, with the same results each time. What stays open nanoql is complete on its own: nothing in it depends on Masseef, and it needs no Masseef product to run. Fixes Masseef makes to nanoql are made in nanoql's public repository, under the same licence and the same review as anyone's. nanoql stays under the Apache License 2.0.

about/related.html.title: Related projects | nanoql
about/related.html.summary: Related projects QuantLib QuantLib is the free, open-source C++ library for quantitative finance. nanoql's core is derived from QuantLib 1.44, and the core's results are checked against QuantLib's: QuantLib's Python package and its C++ build generate the test vectors nanoql commits. QLNet QLNet is a C# financial library derived from QuantLib. nanoql's extensions port its additions for the bond market, mortgage-backed securities with prepayment models and amortised-cost bonds, checked against QLNet 1.13.2. Neither project is affiliated with nanoql or endorses it.

about/security.html.title: Security | nanoql
about/security.html.summary: Security Reporting a vulnerability Please report a vulnerability privately, never in a public issue: through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting, on nanoql's repository: report a vulnerability; or by email to security@nanoql.org. Say what is affected, how to reproduce it, and the impact as you see it. We aim to acknowledge a report within two working days, and to fix a confirmed vulnerability as quickly as its severity requires. A fix is published with a GitHub security advisory, and a CVE where one applies; we credit the reporter unless asked not to. A wrong numerical result is a bug rather than a vulnerability: please report it as an issue, unless it can be exploited. Supported versions Fixes go into the latest 2.x release only.

api/NanoQL.ConventionProvider.html.title: Class ConventionProvider | nanoql
api/NanoQL.ConventionProvider.html.summary: Class ConventionProvider Namespace NanoQL Assembly NanoQL.dll The market conventions the library's presets and market builders read when they are built: QuantLib's coded values, the system's configured defaults, or a provider of a user's own. public abstract class ConventionProvider Inheritance object ConventionProvider Derived ConventionSet Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The provider follows CultureInfo's shape. QuantLib returns QuantLib's coded values unchanged; Default is the system's defaults, QuantLib until set; Current is the innermost active scope's provider, opened by Use(ConventionProvider), or else Default. A scope flows with asynchronous calls, as a culture does, so two flows can build under two providers side by side. A provider is immutable: setting Default replaces it whole. A preset reads Current once, in its constructor, and passes its QuantLib values, its reference, to the provider, which returns the values to use: the reference unchanged when nothing is configured. A preset's nested presets (an index's calendar, a currency's triangulation currency) are built inside the same provider's scope, so a construction takes all its values from one provider. The provider is read only when an object is built, never while it prices, so a price doesn't depend on the scope it runs in. An index keeps the provider it was built with, and every clone of it keeps the same one. A market builder takes the provider of its index, reads its defaults for the options it isn't given from it when it builds, and builds inside it; the CDS builder, with no index, takes the provider current when it is created. An object that builds a builder inside passes its own provider to it: a swap index's underlying swap takes the swap index's provider, even on an Ibor index built under another, so its defaults are the swap index's provider's and its floating leg's conventions the Ibor index's. Whatever is built on an index after its construction follows the index: a swap index's underlying swap, a rate helper's swap when a bootstrap re-dates it, an engine's auxiliary swaps. An object that builds after its construction with no index to follow keeps Current from its construction. QuantLib's registry defaults (Default, Default and EvaluationContext's defaults) are built under QuantLib, whatever is current when they are first read. So a change of Default reaches the objects built after it, and everything built on them. Objects built before it keep their conventions, and an object built on an index takes that index's provider, so set Default before building indexes, and rebuild them to take a change, as curves are rebuilt. A provider of a user's own (a database's, a service's) derives from this class and overrides the members whose values it configures. Each member takes the preset's or the builder's name and its reference and returns the values to use, and the base class returns the reference. Every member is called inside the provider's own scope. api/NanoQL.Coupons.AnalyticHaganPricer.h.summary: Class AnalyticHaganPricer Namespace NanoQL.Coupons Assembly NanoQL.dll The pricing of a CMS coupon by static replication with Hagan's analytic forms (his 3.4c, 3.5b and 3.5c): a vanilla swaption's price plus a convexity term in the g-function's slope at the forward. public sealed class AnalyticHaganPricer : HaganPricer, IMeanRevertingPricer Inheritance object FloatingRateCouponPricer CmsCouponPricer HaganPricer AnalyticHaganPricer Implements IMeanRevertingPricer Inherited Members HaganPricer.SwapletPrice(FloatingRateCoupon, EvaluationContext) HaganPricer.SwapletRate(FloatingRateCoupon, EvaluationContext) HaganPricer.CapletPrice(FloatingRateCoupon, double, EvaluationContext) HaganPricer.CapletRate(FloatingRateCoupon, double, EvaluationContext) HaganPricer.FloorletPrice(FloatingRateCoupon, double, EvaluationContext) HaganPricer.FloorletRate(FloatingRateCoupon, double, EvaluationContext) HaganPricer.MeanReversion CmsCouponPricer.SwaptionVolatility object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Hagan's forms presume G = P(Tp)/A0, the payment's discount over the annuity, which the numeric pricer doesn't need, since it divides by G. QuantLib's shift models' G is P/A0, so their analytic convexity term is high by P/P(Tp) against the numeric twin; here it is QuantLib's term times P(Tp)/P, both on the forwarding curve. On an index with an exogenous discounting curve, where the annuity and discount come from that curve and the g-function from the forwarding one, every model's convexity term is normalised as the numeric pricer normalises its integrand, discount·G′/G for annuity·G′. The standard and exact-yield models on one curve keep QuantLib's bits. So an index given a discounting curve equal to its forwarding one prices its analytic term up to the model's own approximation, 3e-4 of it, away from the same index without one. On a shifted lognormal volatility a strike at or below −shift, on an adjusted fixing above −shift, which QuantLib's Black formula refuses, prices a caplet at the adjusted fixing less the strike and a floorlet at 0, the formula's limits there (QuantLib's check, its Black formula at −shift + 1e-12), so a capped coupon struck there pays its cap and a digital coupon struck at 0 on an unshifted volatility replicates to probability 1. The timing adjustment corrects the fixing of an in-arrears coupon (Black76), or of any coupon not paid at the index's maturity (BivariateLognormal, with the correlation given). Unsealed, as in QuantLib, whose subclasses override AdjustedFixing(IborCoupon, EvaluationContext, double?). Every member computes the coupon's values inside the call (see IborCouponPricer). api/NanoQL.Coupons.CPILeg.html.summary: Class CPILeg Namespace NanoQL.Coupons Assembly NanoQL.dll A helper class building a sequence of CPI coupons, with the inflated notional at the end: QuantLib's CPILeg. public sealed record CPILeg : IEquatable<CPILeg> Inheritance object CPILeg Implements IEquatable<CPILeg> Inherited Members object.GetType() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks An immutable builder: each method returns a modified copy. ToLeg() builds the leg, in place of QuantLib's conversion operator, and attaches QuantLib's default CPICouponPricer. A period with a zero fixed rate is a fixed-rate coupon paying its floor or cap; a period with a cap or a floor and a non-zero rate is refused, as QuantLib refuses it. The notional flow comes last, even when the schedule has a single date. A builder has no value equality. With neither a base CPI nor a base date, every flow's base date is the schedule's start less the lag, as QuantLib gives it, but every flow observes its base on the schedule's start with the leg's lag; with a base date, the notional flow observes its base as the coupons do, on the base date plus the lag. So the coupons and the notional flow share one base CPI, where QuantLib's can differ (CPICoupon's remarks), a documented divergence. Remarks The payoff of a capped coupon is N T min(a L + b, C), of a floored one N T max(a L + b, F), and of a collared one N T min(max(a L + b, F), C), where N is the nominal, T the accrual time, L the floating rate, a its gearing, b the spread, and C and F the strikes. A capped rate decomposes as (a L + b) + |a| min((C − b) / |a| − ξ L, 0), with ξ = sgn(a): the swaplet's rate less a caplet on the fixing, struck at the effective cap (C − b) / a, and at a negative gearing the cap becomes a floor on the fixing, and the floor a cap. The rate is the underlying's swaplet rate plus the floorlet's minus the caplet's, all through the underlying's own pricer, read from one view of its rates for the call, so a pricer whose per-coupon state costs more than its queries builds it once, as QuantLib's one initialize serves the three. A copy with another pricer (SetPricer<T>(T, FloatingRateCouponPricer?)) carries the pricer into a copy of the underlying too, as QuantLib's setPricer sets both. The coupon copies the underlying's terms when it is built, its nominal from ContractNominal, since a constructor has no context. Unsealed, as in QuantLib, where the capped Ibor and CMS coupons derive from it. Constructors CappedFlooredCoupon(FloatingRateCoupon, double?, double?) Remarks The payoff of a capped coupon is N T min(a L + b, C), of a floored one N T max(a L + b, F), and of a collared one N T min(max(a L + b, F), C), where N is the nominal, T the accrual time, L the inflation rate, a its gearing, b the spread, and C and F the strikes; at a gearing that isn't positive the cap becomes a floor on the fixing, and the floor a cap. The rate is the swaplet's plus the floorlet's minus the caplet's, through the pricer of the underlying when there is one, as QuantLib's. A copy with another pricer (SetPricer<T>(T, InflationCouponPricer?)) carries the pricer into a copy of the underlying too, as QuantLib's own setPricer sets both; QuantLib's setCouponPricer calls the non-virtual InflationCoupon::setPricer, so a coupon built on an underlying keeps the underlying's old pricer there, which the copy fixes by construction. Remarks Payoffs: a cash-or-nothing call pays rate + ξ·payoff·H(rate − strike), a put rate + ξ·payoff·H(strike − rate); an asset-or-nothing call pays rate + ξ·rate·H(rate − strike), a put rate + ξ·rate·H(strike − rate), with ξ = +1 for a long option and −1 for a short one. A naked option's rate in the payoff is 0. Each digital is the spread of two capped (call) or floored (put) coupons on the underlying, at the strike plus and minus the replication's gap, so its rate reads the underlying's pricer through those coupons, each building the pricer's state once, as QuantLib's coupons each initialize it. A fixed rate (a fixing before the evaluation date, or on it when the context enforces today's historic fixings or the index holds it) pays the digital's payoff directly. The coupon keeps its underlying's ex-coupon date and fixing convention, which QuantLib's drops to their defaults, no ex-coupon date and Preceding, so its fixing date is its underlying's. Unsealed, as in QuantLib, where the digital CMS, Ibor and CMS spread coupons derive from it. A copy with another pricer (SetPricer<T>(T, FloatingRateCouponPricer?)) carries it into a copy of the underlying, as QuantLib's setPricer sets both. api/NanoQL.Coupons.HaganPricer.html.summary: Class HaganPricer Namespace NanoQL.Coupons Assembly NanoQL.dll The base class of the pricing of a CMS coupon by static replication, as in Hagan's "Conundrums..." article: a caplet's, a floorlet's and the swaplet's price from vanilla swaptions, through a g-function of the yield-curve model. public abstract class HaganPricer : CmsCouponPricer, IMeanRevertingPricer Inheritance object FloatingRateCouponPricer CmsCouponPricer HaganPricer Implements IMeanRevertingPricer Derived AnalyticHaganPricer NumericHaganPricer Inherited Members CmsCouponPricer.SwaptionVolatility object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable: each public member computes, inside the call, what QuantLib's initialize(coupon) stores in the pricer before its queries, the g-function with its memo among it, and a capped or collared coupon's rate reads its three rates from one such state. WithMeanReversion(double) and WithSwaptionVolatility(SwaptionVolatilityStructure?) return copies of the pricer's own type, where QuantLib's setters replace its quote and handle in place. The standard model reads the swap index's tenor as its length in years, where QuantLib reads its length in the tenor's own units, so an 18-month index was 18 years; a tenor that isn't a whole number of fixed-leg periods (18 months on an annual leg) starts with a stub the model can't price, and is refused. On a lognormal volatility a caplet struck at or below 0, on a forward above 0, where QuantLib prices the caplet at a strike of 1e-10 and so drops the strike, is the coupon's expected rate less the strike, the limit of the replication's own formula there; the floorlet there is 0, as QuantLib's. A forward at or below 0 has no lognormal rate distribution, and its caplet refuses, as QuantLib's. Derived inside the library only, by NumericHaganPricer and AnalyticHaganPricer, since its per-coupon state is internal. api/NanoQL.Coupons.LinearTsrPricer.html.summary: Class LinearTsrPricer Namespace NanoQL.Coupons Assembly NanoQL.dll The pricing of a CMS coupon on a linear terminal swap rate model, whose slope is linked to a Gaussian short-rate model (Andersen and Piterbarg, Interest Rate Modeling, 16.3.2). public sealed class LinearTsrPricer : CmsCouponPricer, IMeanRevertingPricer Inheritance object FloatingRateCouponPricer CmsCouponPricer LinearTsrPricer Implements IMeanRevertingPricer Inherited Members CmsCouponPricer.SwaptionVolatility object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The integration's cut-off is set by LinearTsrPricerSettings: explicit lower and upper bounds; the strike where a vanilla swaption has a given ratio (1%) of the at-the-money swaption's vega; the strike where the undeflated payer or receiver price falls below a threshold; or a number of standard deviations of a Black-Scholes process at the at-the-money volatility. The bounds are applied in every case: on a shifted lognormal section to the strike plus the shift, so a zero lower bound is the shifted model's lowest rate; on a normal one the lower bound is min(−upper, lower), unless the bounds are given explicitly. Immutable: each public member computes, inside the call, what QuantLib's initialize(coupon) stores in the pricer, and a capped or collared coupon's rate reads its three rates from one such state. WithMeanReversion(double) and WithSwaptionVolatility(SwaptionVolatilityStructure?) return copies, where QuantLib's setters replace its quote and handle in place; the day counter of the model's slope is the volatility's the pricer holds, where QuantLib's keeps its constructor's volatility's after setSwaptionVolatility. QuantLib's fixes here: the price-threshold strategy searches with its threshold, from the bracket's midpoint, where QuantLib's passes the vega ratio and a guess at the bracket's end, which Brent refuses, so every threshold gave the default bounds' price; the standard-deviations strategy sets each option's own bound, its lognormal width k·σ·√T and the shift subtracted once; below a reversion of 1e-4 the model's shape is −expm1(−a·τ)/a, τ at 0, where QuantLib's reads every such reversion as 0; on a lognormal section and a forward above −shift a caplet struck at or below −shift is the coupon's expected rate less the strike and a floorlet there 0, where QuantLib's refuses, a forward at or below −shift keeping QuantLib's refusal; every section is wrapped at the coupon's forward, where QuantLib's keeps a section's own at-the-money level, which on the SABR and ZABR cubes is an interpolated forward; and the vega-ratio search reads a normal section's vega from Bachelier's derivative, where QuantLib's section refuses it. Telescopic value dates. The flag is taken, with QuantLib's check (a lookback without the observation shift can't use it), and on an averaged coupon it selects the averaging pricer's approximation, as QuantLib's does. ToLeg(EvaluationContext) builds the leg, in place of QuantLib's conversion operator: one coupon per schedule period, a fixed coupon at the spread where the gearing is zero, each floating coupon observing the index on a schedule of the observation tenor from its start to its end. A missing trigger is QuantLib's Null<Rate>(), its value, which a coupon's checks and pricer read as QuantLib's do. api/NanoQL.Coupons.RangeAccrualPricerByB.summary: Class RangeAccrualPricerByBgm Namespace NanoQL.Coupons Assembly NanoQL.dll The range-accrual pricer in the BGM model: each observation's range is a pair of digitals on the index's forward rate, the forwards from the coupon's start S and its end T lognormal with the expiry and payment smiles' volatilities and a correlation, priced without the smile, with the smile through a call spread, or with a smile correction. public sealed class RangeAccrualPricerByBgm : RangeAccrualPricer Inheritance object FloatingRateCouponPricer RangeAccrualPricer RangeAccrualPricerByBgm Inherited Members RangeAccrualPricer.SwapletPrice(FloatingRateCoupon, EvaluationContext) RangeAccrualPricer.SwapletRate(FloatingRateCoupon, EvaluationContext) RangeAccrualPricer.CapletPrice(FloatingRateCoupon, double, EvaluationContext) RangeAccrualPricer.CapletRate(FloatingRateCoupon, double, EvaluationContext) RangeAccrualPricer.FloorletPrice(FloatingRateCoupon, double, EvaluationContext) RangeAccrualPricer.FloorletRate(FloatingRateCoupon, double, EvaluationContext) object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Each observation's digitals are deflated by the discount at the payment date times the fixing at the coupon's start. A trigger at or below ε/2, ε = 1e-8, prices as the deflator, as QuantLib's. A coupon in progress: QuantLib's call-spread route and its smile correction take the variance and the drift over the before-fixing phase clamped, max(S, 0)·λS² + min(U − S, U)·λT², and its drift and volatility functions carry the after-fixing branches for S ≤ 0; its no-smile route alone takes S·λS² + (U − S)·λT² unclamped, high on a started coupon when λS < λT and a NaN refusal when λS > λT, so here it is clamped as the other two. And an observation whose fixing is known is counted by its fixing f, deflator × (1{f > l} − 1{f > u}), the two digitals QuantLib's range reads, where no QuantLib route prices a past one: known as QuantLib's index decides it, its fixing date (the observation date less the fixing days) before the evaluation date, or on it once its fixing is published or the context enforces it. Before the coupon's start every route is QuantLib's. api/NanoQL.Coupons.html.summary: Namespace NanoQL.Coupons Classes AmortizingPayment An amortizing payment: a simple cash flow that more detailed cash-flow analysis can tell apart. AnalyticHaganPricer The pricing of a CMS coupon by static replication with Hagan's analytic forms (his 3.4c, 3.5b and 3.5c): a vanilla swaption's price plus a convexity term in the g-function's slope at the forward. ArithmeticAveragedOvernightIndexedCouponPricer The pricer for arithmetically averaged overnight-indexed coupons. AverageBMACoupon A coupon paying a BMA index, whose rate is a weighted average of the relevant fixings: each fixing weighs the actual calendar days for which it is valid within the interest period. Before the weights are computed, the fixing schedule is adjusted for the index's fixing-day gap. AverageBMALeg A builder of a sequence of average-BMA coupons. AveragingMultipleResetsPricer The averaging pricer of multiple-resets coupons: each reset's fixing weighted by its accrual time, over the accrual period, geared and spread. BachelierYoYInflationCouponPricer The Bachelier-formula pricer of capped and floored year-on-year inflation coupons. BlackAveragingOvernightIndexedCouponPricer The Black pricer of capped and floored averaged overnight-indexed coupons. BlackCompoundingOvernightIndexedCouponPricer The Black pricer of capped and floored compounded overnight-indexed coupons. BlackIborCouponPricer The Black-formula pricer for Ibor coupons, capped, floored or not. BlackYoYInflationCouponPricer The Black-formula pricer of capped and floored year-on-year inflation coupons. CPICashFlow A cash flow paying the performance of a zero-inflation (CPI) index: the notional times the ratio of the index observed on the observation date, with the lag, to its base. It isn't a coupon: it has no accruals. CPICoupon A coupon paying the performance of a zero-inflation (CPI) index: a fixed rate times the ratio of the index observed at the accrual end, with the lag, to its base value. CPICouponPricer The base pricer of CPI coupons: the swaplet is the fixed rate times the index ratio; a volatility-dependent optionlet needs a derived pricer. CPILeg A helper class building a sequence of CPI coupons, with the inflated notional at the end: QuantLib's CPILeg. CappedFlooredCmsCoupon A CMS coupon with a cap, a floor or both on its rate: a CappedFlooredCoupon over a CmsCoupon it builds. CappedFlooredCoupon A floating-rate coupon with a cap, a floor or both on its rate. CappedFlooredIborCoupon An Ibor coupon with a cap, a floor or both on its rate: a CappedFlooredCoupon over an IborCoupon it builds. CappedFlooredOvernightIndexedCoupon A capped or floored overnight-indexed coupon: the cap and the floor apply to the coupon's effective period rate (the default) or to its daily rates. CappedFlooredYoYInflationCoupon A year-on-year inflation coupon with a cap, a floor or both on its rate. CashFlowVectorsFunctions Cash-flow vector builders: QuantLib's free functions of cashflowvectors.hpp. CashFlows Cash-flow analysis functions. CmsCoupon A CMS coupon: a floating-rate coupon fixing on a swap index. CmsCouponPricer The base class of the pricers for CMS coupons, on a swaption volatility. CmsLeg A builder of a sequence of CMS coupons, capped, floored or not. CompoundingMultipleResetsPricer The compounding pricer of multiple-resets coupons: the product of each reset's growth, less one, over the accrual period, geared and spread. CompoundingOvernightIndexedCouponPricer The pricer for compounded overnight-indexed coupons. Coupon The base class of coupons accruing over a fixed period: still abstract, it gives derived classes the accrual-period calculations. CouponPricerFunctions Setting pricers on a leg's coupons: QuantLib's setCouponPricer and setCouponPricers, which return a new leg here, where QuantLib's change the coupons. DigitalCmsCoupon A CMS coupon with a digital call, a digital put or both: QuantLib's DigitalCmsCoupon. DigitalCmsLeg A builder of a sequence of digital CMS coupons: QuantLib's DigitalCmsLeg. DigitalCoupon A floating-rate coupon with a digital call, a digital put or both: QuantLib's DigitalCoupon, priced by call and put spread replication through capped and floored coupons on its underlying. DigitalIborCoupon A Ibor coupon with a digital call, a digital put or both: QuantLib's DigitalIborCoupon. DigitalIborLeg A builder of a sequence of digital Ibor coupons: QuantLib's DigitalIborLeg. DigitalReplication The replication strategy used to price the digital option embedded in a digital coupon, and the gap of the call spread that replicates it. Dividend A predetermined cash flow paid on a stock: a dividend. DividendFunctions The free functions of QuantLib's dividend.hpp. EquityCashFlow A cash flow paying an equity index's ratio, I(T)/I(0), or its growth, I(T)/I(0) - 1, the default, times the notional; with a pricer, the ratio the pricer gives, such as a quanto-adjusted one. EquityCashFlowFunctions QuantLib's free function setCouponPricer for equity cash flow pricers, on immutable legs. EquityCashFlowPricer The base of the equity cash flow pricers: the index ratio a flow pays, per unit of notional. EquityQuantoCashFlowPricer The quanto pricer of an equity cash flow paid in another currency: the index's ratio forecast on its dividend curve quanto-adjusted by the equity and exchange-rate volatilities and their correlation, struck at the index's fixing, and discounted on the payment currency's curve. FixedDividend A predetermined cash amount paid on a stock. FixedRateCoupon A coupon paying a fixed interest rate. FixedRateLeg A helper class building a sequence of fixed-rate coupons. FloatingRateCoupon The base class of coupons paying a floating rate: an index fixing, geared and spread. FloatingRateCouponExtensions FloatingRateCoupon's modifier, which returns a modified copy of the receiver, keeping its static type, where QuantLib's setPricer changes the coupon. FloatingRateCouponPricer The base class of pricers for floating-rate coupons. FractionalDividend A predetermined fraction of the underlying's value, paid on a stock. GFunction Hagan's G(R): the payment-date discount over the annuity as a function of the swap rate, under a model of the yield curve, which the CMS replication integrates against; GFunctionFactory builds them. GFunctionFactory The factory of Hagan's g-functions, one per yield-curve model (GFunctionFactoryYieldCurveModel). HaganPricer The base class of the pricing of a CMS coupon by static replication, as in Hagan's "Conundrums..." article: a caplet's, a floorlet's and the swaplet's price from vanilla swaptions, through a g-function of the yield-curve model. IborCoupon A coupon paying an Ibor index's fixing, geared and spread. IborCouponPricer The base class of pricers for Ibor coupons, capped, floored or not. IborLeg A builder of a sequence of Ibor coupons, capped, floored or not. IndexedCashFlow A cash flow paying an index ratio: the notional times I(T)/I(0), or times I(T)/I(0) - 1 when only the growth is paid. It isn't a coupon: it has no accruals. InflationCoupon The base class of coupons paying a rate from an inflation index, whose pricer computes it: QuantLib's InflationCoupon. InflationCouponExtensions QuantLib's InflationCoupon::setPricer, which changes a coupon, as a copy of the receiver's type. InflationCouponPricer The base class of inflation-coupon pricers: QuantLib's InflationCouponPricer, which differs from the floating-rate pricers because it deals with inflation indexes and their lags (the option may look three months back and the index two). InflationCouponPricerFunctions QuantLib's free function setCouponPricer for inflation-coupon pricers, on immutable legs, with the swap and bond forms beside it, as CouponPricerFunctions has for floating-rate pricers. LinearTsrPricer The pricing of a CMS coupon on a linear terminal swap rate model, whose slope is linked to a Gaussian short-rate model (Andersen and Piterbarg, Interest Rate Modeling, 16.3.2). LinearTsrPricerSettings The linear TSR pricer's integration bounds: QuantLib's LinearTsrPricer::Settings, whose with… members return a copy here. MarketQuotedOptionPricer A vanilla option on a swap rate priced on a swaption volatility's smile section: Black's formula on a zero-shift lognormal volatility, Bachelier's on a normal one. MultipleResetsCoupon A coupon paying a rate compounded or averaged from several fixings over its accrual period, one per period of its reset schedule, each fixing its fixing days before its period's start. MultipleResetsLeg A helper class building a sequence of multiple-resets coupons: QuantLib's MultipleResetsLeg. MultipleResetsPricer The base of the multiple-resets coupon pricers: each reset's fixing plus the rate spread, which the compounding and averaging pricers combine into the coupon's rate. Its prices and options are QuantLib's refusals. NumericHaganPricer The pricing of a CMS coupon by static replication, as in Hagan's "Conundrums..." article, by numerical integration over the prices of vanilla swaptions. NumericHaganPricerIntegrationLimits The numeric Hagan pricer's integration limits after an optionlet's price: QuantLib's lowerLimit(), upperLimit() and stdDeviations(), which that price sets in the pricer's mutable members. OvernightIndexedCoupon A coupon paying the interest, depending on the averaging convention, due to daily overnight fixings: compounded or averaged, with QuantLib's lookback, lockout and observation-shift conventions. OvernightIndexedCouponPricer The base pricer for coupons indexed to an overnight rate, compounded or averaged, capped or floored. OvernightIndexedCouponPricerExtensions OvernightIndexedCouponPricer's modifiers, which return a modified copy of the receiver, keeping its static type, where QuantLib's change the pricer. OvernightLeg A helper class building a sequence of overnight-indexed coupons. RangeAccrualFloatersCoupon A range-accrual floating-rate coupon: the geared index rate plus the spread, accrued over the share of its observation dates on which the index fixes between a lower and an upper trigger. RangeAccrualLeg A helper class building a sequence of range-accrual floating-rate coupons: QuantLib's RangeAccrualLeg. RangeAccrualPricer The base of the range-accrual coupon pricers: the coupon's rate is its price over its accrual and the discount at its payment date; its options are QuantLib's refusals. RangeAccrualPricer.State A range-accrual coupon's state for one call: QuantLib's pricer members after initialize. RangeAccrualPricerByBgm The range-accrual pricer in the BGM model: each observation's range is a pair of digitals on the index's forward rate, the forwards from the coupon's start S and its end T lognormal with the expiry and payment smiles' volatilities and a correlation, priced without the smile, with the smile through a call spread, or with a smile correction. Redemption A bond redemption: a simple cash flow that more detailed cash-flow analysis can tell apart. SimpleCashFlow A predetermined cash flow: an amount paid on a date. StubIborCoupon An Ibor coupon for a broken period, fixing on indices chosen by a StubIndexSelection. StubIborCouponWeightedIndex An index fixing as a fixed-weight linear combination of Ibor indices: QuantLib's StubIborCoupon::WeightedIndex. StubIndexSelection The index selection for irregular Ibor coupons. TimeBasket A distribution of values over dates: a map from each date to its value, in date order. UnitDisplacedBlackYoYInflationCouponPricer The unit-displaced Black-formula pricer of capped and floored year-on-year inflation coupons. VanillaOptionPricer The price of a vanilla option on a swap rate, deflated: the replication's building block in Hagan's pricers. YoYInflationCoupon A coupon paying a year-on-year inflation rate, with a gearing and a spread. YoYInflationCouponPricer The base pricer of year-on-year inflation coupons, capped and floored ones included: the swaplet is the gearing times the coupon's fixing plus the spread; a volatility-dependent optionlet needs a derived pricer. YoYInflationLeg A helper class building a sequence of year-on-year inflation coupons: QuantLib's yoyInflationLeg. ZeroInflationCashFlow A cash flow paying a zero-inflation index ratio between the start and end dates less the observation lag: with the dates in June and a three-month lag, the ratio is taken between March fixings. It isn't a coupon: it has no accruals. Interfaces IMeanRevertingPricer A (CMS) coupon pricer with a mean reversion, which can be calibrated to CMS market quotes: QuantLib's MeanRevertingPricer mixin, an interface here as nanoql's mixins are. Enums BlackIborCouponPricerTimingAdjustment The timing adjustment a BlackIborCouponPricer applies to the fixing: QuantLib's BlackIborCouponPricer::TimingAdjustment. DurationType The type of a duration: QuantLib's Duration::Type. GFunctionFactoryYieldCurveModel The yield-curve models of Hagan's g-functions: QuantLib's GFunctionFactory::YieldCurveModel. LinearTsrPricerSettingsStrategy How the linear TSR pricer bounds its integration: QuantLib's LinearTsrPricer::Settings::Strategy. RateAveragingType How the rates of sub-periods make a coupon's rate: QuantLib's RateAveraging::Type. ReplicationType The strategy by which a digital coupon replicates its embedded digital option: QuantLib's Replication::Type. StubIndexSelectionConvention The convention selecting the index an irregular Ibor coupon fixes on: QuantLib's StubIndexSelection::Convention. QuantLib has no stream operator for it.

Add(ExchangeRate, Date?, Date?) puts a rate first among its pair's entries, so the latest added takes precedence where date ranges overlap; Lookup(Currency?, Currency?, EvaluationContext, Date?, ExchangeRateType) finds a direct, triangulated or chained rate in QuantLib's order. QuantLib keys its rates by the pair's numeric codes, min × 1000 + max (exchangeratemanager.cpp:89-98), which loses every rate of a currency coded 1,000 or more (QuantLib's crypto currencies, 10000 to 10007, or any currency of one's own: a lookup from it throws, and no chain passes through it), and can't tell apart two currencies sharing a code (CNY and CNH, 156: a USD/CNH rate answers for USD/CNY). Here the key is the pair of currencies, ordered as QuantLib's key orders pairs, the codes and names breaking a tie; a chained lookup tests which pairs involve a currency and which currencies it has passed by the same identity, where QuantLib uses the numeric code (:95-98, :159, :170), and chains as QuantLib's chain does. So QuantLib's order and answers stand wherever the numeric codes are distinct and below 1,000 and the currencies' names distinct, BGL and BGN apart: three documented divergences (Divergences/ExchangeRateKeyTests.cs, Divergences/SharedNumericCodeTests.cs, Divergences/CurrencyNameAndCodeTests.cs). Two registries are equal when they hold the same pairs, each with equal entries (rate, start and end dates) in the same order. The hash combines one hash per pair, computed when the registry is built. Properties Default Gets the registry holding QuantLib's known rates alone, its state at start and after clear(). public static ExchangeRates Default { get; } Property Value ExchangeRates Methods Add(ExchangeRate, Date?, Date?) A registry with one more exchange rate, valid between two dates. public ExchangeRates Add(ExchangeRate rate, Date? startDate = null, Date? endDate = null) Parameters rate ExchangeRate The rate. startDate Date? The first date it is valid on; null for the earliest date, QuantLib's Date::minDate(). endDate Date? The last date it is valid on; null for the latest date, QuantLib's Date::maxDate(). Returns ExchangeRates The new registry, the rate first among its pair's; this one is unchanged. Exceptions ArgumentNullException rate is null. ArgumentException A date is default(Date). NanoQLException A currency of the rate is QuantLib's empty one. Clear() The registry without the added rates: Default, QuantLib's known rates alone. public ExchangeRates Clear() Returns ExchangeRates Default; this registry is unchanged. Equals(ExchangeRates?) public bool Equals(ExchangeRates? other) Parameters other ExchangeRates Returns bool Equals(object?) public override bool Equals(object? obj) Parameters obj object Returns bool GetHashCode() public override int GetHashCode() Returns int Lookup(Currency?, Currency?, EvaluationContext, Date?, ExchangeRateType) The exchange rate between two currencies at a date. Direct rates are preferred; with Derived, a rate is triangulated through a currency's triangulation currency, or chained through other currencies, where no direct one is held. public ExchangeRate Lookup(Currency? source, Currency? target, EvaluationContext context, Date? date = null, ExchangeRateType type = ExchangeRateType.Derived) Parameters source Currency The source currency. target Currency The target currency. context EvaluationContext The evaluation context, whose evaluation date is the date when none is given. date Date? The date; null for the context's evaluation date. type ExchangeRateType Whether only a direct rate is returned, or derived ones too. Returns ExchangeRate The rate; 1.0 between a currency and itself. Remarks Where two or more chains are possible, which one is returned is QuantLib's choice: the first by the pairs' order. Exceptions ArgumentNullException context is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException type isn't a member of its enum. ArgumentException date is default(Date). NanoQLException No rate is held for the date ("no direct conversion available", "no conversion available"), or a currency is QuantLib's empty one.

Two currencies are equal when their names and their codes are, compared ordinally, whatever their other data; the hash is the name's. QuantLib's operator== compares names alone (currency.hpp:179-182), so its BGL and BGN, both named "Bulgarian lev", are one currency there: the code tells them apart, a documented divergence (Divergences/CurrencyNameAndCodeTests.cs). api/NanoQL.DiscretizedAsset.html.summary: Class DiscretizedAsset Namespace NanoQL Assembly NanoQL.dll The discretized asset class used by numerical methods: an asset's values on a lattice, rolled back in time. [WorkingType] public abstract class DiscretizedAsset Inheritance object DiscretizedAsset Derived DiscretizedDiscountBond DiscretizedOption DiscretizedCallableFixedRateBond DiscretizedDermanKaniDoubleBarrierOption DiscretizedDoubleBarrierOption DiscretizedBarrierOption DiscretizedCapFloor DiscretizedConvertible DiscretizedDermanKaniBarrierOption DiscretizedSwap DiscretizedVanillaOption Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A working type, as a random-number generator is: mutable, owned by one calculation and not thread-safe. An engine builds its assets inside its calculation, initializes them on a lattice, rolls them back and reads their value; no immutable object holds one. Its values and buffers. Values is a view of the current step's values in the asset's own buffer, which the asset's code reads and writes as QuantLib's values_. The asset holds two buffers. A lattice reserves both at the widest step a rollback from the initial time passes through (ReserveCapacity(int)), then steps back into the spare one (StepValues(int)) and makes it the current one (CommitStep(int, double)), so a rollback allocates nothing, where QuantLib's allocates an array per step. A view is valid until the asset's next step or reset. Adjustments. PreAdjustValues() and PostAdjustValues() run the protected PreAdjustValuesImpl() and PostAdjustValuesImpl() once per time: each remembers the last time it adjusted at, starting at QuantLib's QL_MAX_REAL, and, as QuantLib's, Initialize(Lattice, double) doesn't forget it, so an asset initialized again at its last adjustment time skips that adjustment. An extension point, as in QuantLib: the discount bond, the option, the swap, the swaption and the callable bond derive from it, as later ports' cap, vanilla option, barrier and convertible assets will. The rate r is given with the convention that a unit of the source is worth r units of the target. QuantLib's default constructor, an empty rate whose value is Null<Real>(), isn't ported: no member builds one. Equality is nanoql's, where QuantLib has none: two rates are equal when they have the same source, target, rate (by Equals(double)) and type, and, for derived rates, equal chains. The exchange-rate registry's equality reads it. Chain(ExchangeRate, ExchangeRate) refuses two rates over one pair of currencies, which QuantLib chains into a rate from a currency to itself (EUR→USD at 1.1 with EUR→USD at 1.2 gives USD→USD at 1.0909, which exchanges 100 USD into 109.09 USD): a documented divergence (Divergences/ExchangeRateChainRefusalTests.cs). The exchange-rate registry's chained lookups chain as QuantLib's, since their steps are never over one pair in its key. api/NanoQL.Experimental.AnalyticDiscrete.summary: Class AnalyticDiscreteGeometricAveragePriceAsianHestonEngine Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll Kim, Kim, Kim and Wee's analytic engine for discrete geometric average-price Asian options under the Heston model: the joint characteristic function of the log geometric average, QuantLib's Phi, inverted by a Fourier integral. [Experimental("NQL0001")] public static class AnalyticDiscreteGeometricAveragePriceAsianHestonEngine Inheritance object AnalyticDiscreteGeometricAveragePriceAsianHestonEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The value, with QuantLib's additional results ("dcf", "s0", "strike", "expiryTime", "term1", "term2", "xiRightLimit", "fixingTimes", "tauK", "adjustedStrike", "prefactor", "kStar"); "term2" is the integral's term on the route below, so the value is D × prefactor × (±term1 + term2), as QuantLib's. An arithmetic option is priced as the geometric one on its fixings to come, unseasoned, QuantLib's use of the engine as the arithmetic Monte Carlo's control variate. Documented divergences. QuantLib cuts its integral at ξ 100 on 128 Gauss-Legendre points, before the integrand decays at short maturities and small variance (−51% on a ten-day Asian at v₀ 0.0025; Divergences/HestonGeometricAsianCutoffTests.cs), and leaves out [0, 1e-8 ξ_max]. Here: Phi in a stable form, ω̃ through tanh and the logs of the Riccati factors through log1p, where QuantLib's terms of order 1/σ² cancel at small vol of vol and its cosh and sinh overflow at long maturities (Divergences/HestonGeometricAsianSmallParameterTests.cs); below a vol of vol of 1e-4, a cubic in σ through the Black-Scholes limit at σ = 0; at a vanishing square root, γ = 0, the forms' limits (κ = 0). Before the integral, a switch: a point mass at v₀ = θ = 0, priced at its intrinsic; and the discounted intrinsic where a Chernoff bound on the extrinsic value, from Phi at real s up to the moment explosion, is at or below 1e-12 × max(the discounted intrinsic, D F_G/100) (Divergences/HestonGeometricAsianIntrinsicTests.cs). The integral on Carr and Madan's damped contour: the out-of-the-money option on its own strip where that strip is at least 0.5 wide, else on Lewis's middle strip, the other by parity; Lord and Kahl's α inside the half of the strip next to its pole; the explosions by the closed-form first-zero test of the Riccati factors (Divergences/HestonGeometricAsianExplosionTests.cs); cut where Phi's modulus falls below 1e-14 of its value on the contour's axis, or at the engine's ξ_max where that is later; split at the decades of ξ and at the peak's width below 1; on NanoQL's adaptive Kronrod rule at the price's tolerance scale, max(the price, the lower bound, D F_G/100), in two passes, accepted where two breakpoint sets agree within it, a third on disagreement, each set capped at 1e6 evaluations (Divergences/HestonGeometricAsianStrikeScaleTests.cs). Refused, with "variance too small for the Heston geometric engine near the forward", where the switch doesn't fire and the cut lies past ξ 1e7, which no checkable route reaches. F_G exact, S₀ D_q(t)/D_r(t), where every fixing time is one t and none is past, where Phi(1, 0) is 0/0; the call floored at D max(F_G − K, 0), the put at its mirror. Times run on the engine's clock, Clock(HestonProcess, FdmQuantoHelper?, LocalVolTermStructure?), from the earliest reference date of the process's curves, each discount read at its instants. A fixing before the evaluation date is left out, as the Monte Carlo engines leave it, where QuantLib reads its negative time into the intervals; one from the evaluation date to the clock's origin is taken at the origin, as a past fixing at the spot (Divergences/AsianLateSettlementTests.cs). api/NanoQL.Experimental.AnalyticHestonFo.summary: Class AnalyticHestonForwardEuropeanEngine Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll Kruse's analytic engine for forward-starting, strike-reset European options under the Heston model ("On the Pricing of Forward Starting Options under Stochastic Volatility", 2003): the vanilla's probabilities from the characteristic function at each variance the reset may reach, integrated over that variance's law at the reset. [Experimental("NQL0001")] public class AnalyticHestonForwardEuropeanEngine Inheritance object AnalyticHestonForwardEuropeanEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks An unsealed, immutable object holding the process and the integration order, its public members QuantLib's (Propagator(double, double), ForwardChF(double, double)), with a static Calculate in the engines' form. QuantLib's nested integrations: 128 Gauss-Legendre points over the variance at the reset, 128 over the characteristic function's argument; within 1e-3 of the reset, the vanilla's integral alone. The value, with QuantLib's additional results ("dcf", "qf", "expiryRatio", "resetRatio", "moneyness", "s0", "fwd", "resetTime", "expiryTime", "P1Hat", "P2Hat", "phiRightLimit", "nuRightLimit"). Documented divergences (Divergences/HestonForwardEngineTests.cs), each leaving QuantLib's bits where it doesn't apply. The propagator's product e^(−(Bν + Λ)/2) · I_(R/2−1)(√(ΛBν)) underflows times overflows to NaN for resets just above the 1e-3 cut, where it is taken as e^(−(Bν + Λ)/2 + x) · Iₑ(x), x = √(ΛBν), QuantLib's own exponentially weighted Bessel function, wherever QuantLib's product isn't finite and nonzero. At κ̂ = κ − ρσ = 0 QuantLib's B is 0/0 and R 0·∞: below |κ̂t| of 1e-2, B = 4 r(κ̂t)/(σ²t) with r(x) = x/(−expm1(−x)), and R = 4κθ/σ² where κ̂ = 0. QuantLib's outer integral, 128 nodes over [0, max(2, ...)] in the reset variance, can't resolve the propagator at short resets, where it is narrow, nor where 2κθ < σ², where it is singular at 0: at a vol of vol of 0.2 a one-day reset prices 10.376 against Monte Carlo's 8.662 ± 0.019, at 0.5 a 182-day reset 5.100 against 5.177 ± 0.014. Where QuantLib's nodes miss the propagator's unit mass by more than 1e-6 the expectation is taken in closed form: QuantLib's characteristic function from the reset is affine in the reset variance, so its expectation over the propagator is the CIR transition's moment-generating function, and each probability is one Fourier integral on the half-line, adaptively, where QuantLib's inner integral stops at a fixed limit that small reset variances outrun. That limit also fails short tenors, where the return's distribution is narrow: at a reset today a one-day call at the money prices 0.297 against the vanilla's 0.420 and calls out of the money below 0. QuantLib's probabilities stand on its reset-today route and on its outer integral only where each is within 1e-7 of the resolved route's, the same half-line integral at v₀ or the closed form, the resolved route elsewhere; the resolved integral runs on Gauss-Legendre pieces whose width doubles from 1 to at most min(8, π/|log K|), half the strike factor's period, until three pieces in a row contribute at most 1e-17. Times run on the model's clock, HestonProcess's model time from the earliest reference date of its curves, each discount read at its instants, none accrued before its curve's own date. api/NanoQL.Experimental.BaseCorrelationL.summary: Class BaseCorrelationLossModel<TBaseModel, TInterpolator, TInitTraits> Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll The base correlation loss model, its interpolation by the portfolio's (live) amount percentage: the tranche's expected loss is the difference of two equity tranches' to its attachment and detachment, each priced by a base model at the correlation the surface gives at its level. Inheritance object DefaultLossModel BaseCorrelationLossModel<TBaseModel, TInterpolator, TInitTraits> Implements IDefaultLossModel Derived GaussianLHPFlatBCLM Inherited Members DefaultLossModel.SetBasket(Basket) DefaultLossModel.ProbOverLoss(Date, double) DefaultLossModel.Percentile(Date, double) DefaultLossModel.ExpectedShortfall(Date, double) DefaultLossModel.SplitVaRLevel(Date, double) DefaultLossModel.SplitESFLevel(Date, double) DefaultLossModel.LossDistribution(Date) DefaultLossModel.DensityTrancheLoss(Date, double) DefaultLossModel.ProbsBeingNthEvent(int, Date) DefaultLossModel.DefaultCorrelation(Date, int, int) DefaultLossModel.ProbAtLeastNEvents(int, Date) DefaultLossModel.ExpectedRecovery(Date, int, DefaultProbKey) DefaultLossModel.Basket DefaultLossModel.BoundBasket object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The literature is immense; beyond the introductory level (precrisis) see chapters 19, 20 and 21 of Dominic O'Kane, "Modelling single name and multi-name credit derivatives", Wiley Finance, 2008. Freely available: "Credit Correlation: A Guide", JP Morgan Credit Derivatives Strategy, 12 March 2004; "Introducing Base Correlations", JP Morgan, 22 March 2004; "A Relative Value Framework for Credit Correlation", JP Morgan, 27 April 2004; "Valuing and Hedging Synthetic CDO Tranches Using Base Correlations", Bear Stearns, 17 May 2004; "Correlation Primer", Nomura Fixed Income Research, 6 August 2004; "Base Correlation Explained", Lehman Brothers Fixed Income Quantitative Credit Research, 15 November 2004; "Pricing CDOs with a smile", Societe Generale Credit Research, February 2005; and for bespoke base correlation "Base Correlation Mapping", Lehman Brothers' Quantitative Credit Research Quarterly, Volume 2007-Q1. Typical postcrisis data is in JP Morgan's Global Correlation Daily Analytics. The crisis problems, pricing stressed portfolios or tranches over the maximum loss, are the base models' responsibility: users select a base model accordingly, a copula or a random loss given default one. This is not a bespoke base correlation model (bespoke as to the basket's composition, not just its attachment levels), whose loss interpolation is on the expected loss to match the two baskets: the surface should refer to the basket priced. To be done, as in QuantLib: bespoke portfolio models. Most statistics are not implemented, not impossible, but the model is intended for pricing rather than portfolio risk management. The base models are QuantLib's four setupModels specialisations, each a type implementing IBaseCorrelationModel<TInitTraits>, and immutable: each statistic builds the two at its correlations, where QuantLib's sets the correlation quotes they observe. Bound to a basket with realized defaults, the equity baskets hold the live names, their notionals and recoveries, over the restated tranche: QuantLib's take the live notionals on the whole pool, which its basket refuses ("unmatched data entry sizes in basket"; Divergences/BaseCorrelationLossModelTests.cs). A correlation the surface gives outside [0, 1) is refused, naming the date and level, where QuantLib's base model returns NaN below 0 and refuses above 1. An equity tranche's attachment leg is 0, its basket [0, 0] not priced: QuantLib's prices it, so its LHP base refuses where the surface extrapolates below 0 at level 0 and its inhomogeneous pool base throws on every equity tranche ("a out of range", its own \todo: "is failing for equity tranches at least"). QuantLib specializes the interpolation for BilinearInterpolation and BicubicSpline alone; any 2-D interpolator builds it here, Bilinear and Bicubic among them. Some interpolators may take the correlation out of [−1, 1]. The correlations hold a row per loss level and a column per tenor, the shape QuantLib's checks enforce, where its header names them correls[iYear][iLoss]. The loss levels are checked as QuantLib's checkLosses checks them, increasing in (0, 1], a check QuantLib defines and never calls, so it interpolates on unsorted levels. The correlation is read from the interpolation with extrapolation always on, bilinear off the grid where the interpolator is, so off the grid it can leave [0, 1]; the extrapolate flag is QuantLib's and unread there too. The base-correlation model refuses a correlation outside [0, 1). To be done, as in QuantLib: the relation to a given basket is to be made explicit for bespoke models; a matrix data structure, and the data structure for a basket whose current losses aren't zero. The 2-D interpolator is left open because of the arbitrage issues of its choice: non-local ones like cubic splines affect the past (calibrated) coupons of previous tenors. api/NanoQL.Experimental.Basket.html.title: Class Basket | nanoql
api/NanoQL.Experimental.Basket.html.summary: Class Basket Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll A credit basket: credit names, each with a notional, drawn from a pool of issuers, and a tranche of the pool's loss, with the default loss model that gives its loss statistics. [Experimental("NQL0001")] public sealed class Basket Inheritance object Basket Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable, of its terms and its evaluation context: it computes QuantLib's computeBasket() at the context's evaluation date at construction, its live names, notionals and keys, its settled loss and its remaining tranche, and keeps the context, since QuantLib's statistics take no date of evaluation and its cached state is that date's. QuantLib's constructor computes that state before it sets the tranche's attachment and detachment amounts, so its remaining amounts read 0 until the first statistic (basket.cpp:57-68); here they are computed after them (Divergences/BasketConstructionOrderTests.cs). SetLossModel(IDefaultLossModel?) returns a basket of the same terms and context whose LossModel is the model bound to it, its precomputation run once, there: QuantLib's flows set a model on a basket and change it through observers, which become rebuilds. A basket with no model refuses its statistics with QuantLib's "Basket has no default loss model assigned." The live reads take the live names' positions: QuantLib's remainingNotionals(d) and remainingProbabilities(d) index the live list's positions, not its names (basket.cpp:196-220), so after the first of three names defaults they read the first two names' values (Divergences/BasketLiveReadsTests.cs). Every curve read before a curve's reference date is a default probability of 0, where QuantLib's refuses it ("negative time"). Realized defaults. QuantLib's basket misprices once a name has defaulted: its expected tranche loss adds the whole settled loss, its models tranche the live names' loss against min(D, A + max(0, L − A)) where its own header means max(0, A − L), its n-th-to-default probabilities ignore the defaults, and an unsettled default's recovery is a null; its header warns "Baskets with realized defaults not tested/WIP." Here the names defaulted by the evaluation date leave the pricing basket: the lost notional L writes the tranche down from its attachment, the recovered notional amortizes it from its detachment's side (min(D, N − recovered)), and the model is bound to a basket of the live names over that restated tranche, each latent model restricted to their rows (PricingBasket). Its statistics add the realized tranche loss: the expected tranche loss, the percentile and the expected shortfall add it to the live model's; ProbOverLoss(Date, double) maps its inception fraction onto the restated tranche, 1 at or below the realized loss; the loss distribution is the live one shifted by the realized loss; the event counts take the order less the realized defaults, 1 (and QuantLib's zeros) once they reach it; the vectors run over the live names; the name-indexed reads take pool positions, a defaulted name's recovery its settled one and its default correlation refused. A default not settled for the name's key's seniority is refused, QuantLib's own \todo (basket.cpp:128-131). An event dated after the evaluation date isn't realized there, so it stays out of the restatement, and the reads with a date argument keep QuantLib's use of such "programmed" events for jump-to-default analysis (basket.hpp:138-141). api/NanoQL.Experimental.BetaRiskSimulati.title: Class BetaRiskSimulation | nanoql
api/NanoQL.Experimental.BetaRiskSimulati.summary: Class BetaRiskSimulation Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll The simulation of a BetaRisk: each path's events arrive as a Poisson process over the period, each event's loss the maximum loss times a beta draw, X / (X + Y) of two gamma draws. [Experimental("NQL0001")] [WorkingType] public sealed class BetaRiskSimulation : CatSimulation Inheritance object CatSimulation BetaRiskSimulation Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The draws are those of QuantLib built with MSVC 14.44, its oracle's standard library: a 32-bit Mersenne Twister seeded with QuantLib's constant 5489, no parameter, as std::mt19937's default; each uniform from two of its integers as MSVC's generate_canonical forms it, the first's top 21 bits and the second's 32, (g₀ >> 11) + (g₁ << 21) times 2⁻⁵³, truncating where the standard's form rounds; the exponential as −log(1 − u)/λ; and the gamma by Knuth's published algorithms (TAOCP vol. 2, §3.4.1) in the order MSVC draws them: Ahrens-Dieter's GS below α = 1, the exponential at α = 1, a product of uniforms for an integer α below 20, and Ahrens' tangent method otherwise. They are written from those algorithms and this description of MSVC's behaviour; the standard leaves a distribution's algorithm to the implementation. The event times are the inter-arrival times cumulated, so the count is Poisson's and a path's dates ascend: QuantLib's draws each event's time afresh, so its count is geometric, a mean of e^(λT) − 1 for λT (3.48 for 1.5 at a two-year return period over three years), and its dates come unordered, which the notional path reads as ascending. A path of one event or none is QuantLib's bit for bit up to the first path where QuantLib's next fresh draw falls inside the period and the cumulated time doesn't; the streams part there (Divergences/BetaRiskTests.cs). A working type: each simulation owns its generator, stepping it in place. api/NanoQL.Experimental.BinomialDoubleBa.title: Class BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine | nanoql
api/NanoQL.Experimental.BinomialDoubleBa.summary: Class BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll The binomial engine for double barrier options: a discretized double-barrier asset rolled back on a Black-Scholes lattice over a binomial tree, built on the process's curves and volatility flattened at the option's maturity. [Experimental("NQL0001")] public static class BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine Inheritance object BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks QuantLib's template on the tree and the discretized asset: Calculate<TTree, TAsset>(DoubleBarrierOption, EvaluationContext, GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess, int) takes both as type arguments, the tree built through Create(StochasticProcess1D, double, int, double) and the asset through Create(DoubleBarrierOption, StochasticProcess, TimeGrid?), DiscretizedDoubleBarrierOption (QuantLib's default), DiscretizedDermanKaniDoubleBarrierOption or a user's own. The delta and gamma come from the lattice's first two steps, the gamma and delta null where the nodes don't separate, and the theta from the second step's middle node, as QuantLib's. As QuantLib's, the engine takes a spot beyond a barrier to the lattice, which knocks it at its first node. Documented divergences. The tree runs on the risk-free curve's day counter from the earliest reference date of the structures, each structure on another day counter or reference date flattened on it from its discount or variance at the maturity date, and the asset's exercise times read on the tree's clock, as BinomialBarrierEngine, where QuantLib flattens each curve from the risk-free curve's date on its own day counter (Divergences/BinomialDoubleBarrierMismatchedTimesTests.cs); where every structure shares the risk-free curve's day counter and reference date, the tree is QuantLib's. The time grid and the lattice take their step count from the tree, its columns less one, where QuantLib's take the count given: the Leisen-Reimer and Joshi trees build on one more step at an even count. The copula is arbitrary, though the model was designed for a Gaussian setup. QuantLib's template parameter is a loss latent model; the constant-loss model is the only one with the conditional recovery it reads, so it is the model's. To be done, as in QuantLib: the random recovery models, and the probability inversions the cumulative functions already computed. The binomial's weight α mixes it with a two-point mass at the floor and ceiling of the expected count m, both of mean m, so the conditional variance matches the pool's: α = (V − V₂)/(V_B − V₂) with V the pool's count variance, V_B the binomial's and V₂ = (c − m)(m − f) the two-point mass's, all in QuantLib's units of a count over n². QuantLib takes V₂'s place with −(c − m)² − ((f − m)² − c²)(c − m), not a variance, so its conditional distribution misses the variance it exists to match, 10,656 for 11,718 on three names (Divergences/BinomialLossModelTests.cs); on a homogeneous pool V = V_B and α = 1, QuantLib's, taken where V equals V_B to 1e-12 in these units, since V_B − V₂ vanishes like the squared distance of the probability from 0 or 1, where the two variances' rounding differs most, and would move α (by 2e-7 at a distance of 1e-10); below that difference the variance a weight of 1 misses is negligible. Bound to a basket with realized defaults, the model prices its live names over the restated tranche. The statistics read the notionals of the names alive at the evaluation date: QuantLib's read those alive at the statistic's date beside the evaluation date's recoveries, so a default programmed after the evaluation date reads past a vector, undefined; here it reads QuantLib's model without the event. A percentile or shortfall whose search leaves the loss distribution, which QuantLib reads before its start or past its end, is refused. The percentile at 1 is the tranche's loss at the largest attainable loss, as its interior's are tranche losses, where QuantLib's returns the pool's largest loss (binomiallossmodel.hpp:355). api/NanoQL.Experimental.CDO.html.summary: Class CDO Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll The collateralized debt obligation: a mezzanine CDO tranche, its loss given default between the attachment D₁ and the detachment D₂ > D₁. For purchased protection the value is the protection value V₁ less the premium value V₂. [Experimental("NQL0001")] public sealed class CDO : Instrument Inheritance object Instrument CDO Inherited Members Instrument.Validate() Instrument.FetchResults(InstrumentResults) object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The protection leg: the probability distribution of the loss given default LGD = (1 − r)·L is built at the premium schedule's dates with intermediate steps tᵢ, the expected protection payoff Eᵢ = E[Pay(LGD)] at each, Pay(L) = min(D₂, LGD) − min(D₁, LGD), and V₁ = Σᵢ (Eᵢ − Eᵢ₋₁)·dᵢ with dᵢ the discount factor at tᵢ. The premium is paid on the protected notional, D₂ − D₁ less the expected protection payments: V₂ = m·Σᵢ (D₂ − D₁ − Eᵢ)·Δᵢ₋₁,ᵢ·dᵢ, with m the premium rate and Δ the day count fraction. The loss distribution is Hull and White's probability bucketing ("Valuation of a CDO and nth to default CDS without Monte Carlo simulation", Journal of Derivatives 12, 2, 2004), which allows varying notionals and default term structures. To be done, as in QuantLib: the cases where Eᵢ₊₁ < Eᵢ, which Error counts. QuantLib's older CDO, computed by the instrument itself: Calculate(EvaluationContext), nothing cached. Its "today" is the yield curve's reference date, as QuantLib's. The maximum loss given default Lgd is the sum of the names' losses given default, which QuantLib's sums onto an uninitialized value (cdo.cpp:73-77). A default probability before its curve's reference date is 0, where QuantLib's refuses it. QuantLib's OAS, cleanPriceOAS, effectiveDuration and effectiveConvexity re-run the bond's attached engine with a spread written into its arguments. Here they take the engine as a delegate that takes the spread, such as (bond, context, spread) => TreeCallableFixedRateBondEngine.Calculate(bond, context, model, 240, null, spread), and compute as QuantLib does: on the engine's NPV, at its curve's reference date, not its settlement value, so the spread of a bond's own clean price isn't 0; with Brent's solver bracketing from QuantLib's step of 0.001; and with the spread converted between continuous compounding and the given conventions on the given curve, which serves only that conversion. An engine that ignores the spread, such as the Black engine, gives a flat price, which the solver can't bracket, as QuantLib's can't. Unsealed, an extension point, as QuantLib's base is. api/NanoQL.Experimental.ClubsTopology.ht.title: Class ClubsTopology | nanoql
api/NanoQL.Experimental.ClubsTopology.ht.summary: Class ClubsTopology Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll The clubs topology, after H. M. Emara, "Adaptive Clubs-based Particle Swarm Optimization": each particle belongs to a default number of clubs, and its social best is the best of its clubs' members; a club's best leaves a random club (down to a minimum) and its worst joins one (up to a maximum), and every reset iterations the others return to the default: QuantLib's ClubsTopology. [Experimental("NQL0001")] public sealed class ClubsTopology : ParticleSwarmOptimizationTopology Inheritance object ParticleSwarmOptimizationTopology ClubsTopology Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Fixes (Divergences/ParticleSwarmTopologyTests.cs): the initial clubs are drawn in [0, totalClubs − 1], where QuantLib's draws in [1, totalClubs] and reads one past each particle's clubs; a particle's social best is its best club's best particle, where QuantLib's takes the club's index for a particle; each club's worst is weighed over every member, where QuantLib's tests it only on a member that isn't the new best, so a club whose values fall in order names particle 0 its worst, a member or not; and a best particle leaves a club only above the minimum and a worst one joins only below the maximum, as the class documents, where QuantLib's never tests either, so a particle that stays best leaves every club and its social best is then the largest double. A club none of whose members passes QuantLib's comparisons, one with no members or whose personal bests are all NaN, has no best, and a particle reads only its clubs with a best, or its own personal best where none has one, where QuantLib's reads particle 0, a member or not, for such a club; a minimum below 1 is refused, as a particle in no club has no club-mates and so no social best, where QuantLib's best particle leaves every club and keeps particle 0's position at the largest double. Its integers are std::uniform_int_distribution's on a std::mt19937 on the seed, drawn as MSVC draws them; the seed is required, QuantLib's default seeding from the clock. Each minimization starts the generator from the seed and the iterations from 0. Constructors ClubsTopology(int, int, int, int, int, long) Initializes a new instance of the ClubsTopology class. public ClubsTopology(int defaultClubs, int totalClubs, int maxClubs, int minClubs, int resetIteration, long seed) Parameters defaultClubs int The clubs each particle starts in. totalClubs int The clubs. maxClubs int The most clubs a particle joins. minClubs int The fewest clubs a particle keeps. resetIteration int The iterations between resets to the default. seed long The seed, in [1, 4294967295]. Exceptions ArgumentException The club counts are out of order, with QuantLib's texts. ArgumentOutOfRangeException minClubs is below 1, or seed is outside [1, 4294967295]. The other schedules are refused, where QuantLib returns no period and its swaps then refuse "no pricing periods" or price as expired: its two branches read a schedule two ways, monthly as periods of its own tenor and daily as monthly periods summing its quantity, and no QuantLib case or caller says which a weekly, quarterly or yearly schedule means, while a constant, window or hourly one has no tenor. A note on the conventions used: consider the currency pair EUR-USD. EUR is the base currency, while USD is the quote currency; the quote currency is the amount paid in that currency for one unit of base currency. Hence, for a cross-currency swap there is a base-currency leg and a quote-currency leg, and the instrument's parameters (collateral currency, basis, resetting or constant-notional legs) are defined relative to them. For example, for EUR-USD basis swaps the collateral is paid in the quote currency (USD), and the basis is given on the base-currency leg (EUR). For more details see N. Moreni, A. Pallavicini (2015), FX Modelling in Collateralized Markets: foreign measures, basis curves and pricing formulae. api/NanoQL.Experimental.ContinuousArithm.summary: Class ContinuousArithmeticAsianVecerEngine Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll Vecer's engine for continuous arithmetic average-price Asian options: the option's value as a one-dimensional PDE in the replicating strategy's variable, solved by Crank-Nicolson (see <http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~vecer/asian-vecer.pdf>); a put by the Asian put-call parity. [Experimental("NQL0001")] public static class ContinuousArithmeticAsianVecerEngine Inheritance object ContinuousArithmeticAsianVecerEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The engine reads every structure on one clock, the earliest reference date of the process's structures on the risk-free day counter, each at the instant a time denotes and nothing accrued before its own date, where QuantLib measures the time from the evaluation date on the risk-free day counter beside each curve's zero rate from its own date: each rate is the curve's own zero rate to the maturity times its own time over the clock's, and the volatility its own Black volatility at the maturity times the square root of its time over the clock's; on structures sharing the evaluation date and the day counter each factor is 1 and QuantLib's numbers stand. Where the initial point lies on the grid's upper end the price is the last node's value, the interpolation's own limit, where QuantLib reads one node past the grid. The operators are built per call. The averaging starts at the engine's start date, as QuantLib's; an option carrying a start date of its own that differs is refused, where QuantLib ignores it. QuantLib's current average is never read by its engine, nor here. api/NanoQL.Experimental.CumulativeBehren.summary: Class CumulativeBehrensFisher Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll The cumulative (generalized) Behrens-Fisher distribution: the exact distribution of a linear combination of any number of Student t variables of odd orders, adapted from Witkovsky's algorithm (Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference 94, 2001, 1-13). [Experimental("NQL0001")] public sealed class CumulativeBehrensFisher Inheritance object CumulativeBehrensFisher Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable. The characteristic function of a t of order ν = 2n + 1 is a polynomial of degree n times exp(−√ν|t|); the combination's is their product, and the Gil-Pelaez theorem inverts it term by term in closed form. The orders must be odd. A term of degree k divides (k − 1)!, or k! for the density, by the power k of a radius, and QuantLib's arithmetic overflows where either leaves the doubles: from 172 on, on the cumulative of two t's of order 173, it reads NaN, and its inverse refuses with "root not bracketed" (convolvedstudentt.cpp:124-127), where the series stays accurate. There nanoql scales the factorial and the power together, in logarithms; QuantLib's bits wherever its arithmetic doesn't overflow, through order 171, where the series is accurate to 2e-14 relative against 50 digits. A documented divergence (Divergences/BehrensFisherHighOrderTests.cs). [Experimental("NQL0001")] [WorkingType] public sealed class DiscretizedCallableFixedRateBond : DiscretizedAsset Inheritance object DiscretizedAsset DiscretizedCallableFixedRateBond Inherited Members DiscretizedAsset.Initialize(Lattice, double) DiscretizedAsset.Rollback(double) DiscretizedAsset.PartialRollback(double) DiscretizedAsset.PresentValue() DiscretizedAsset.PreAdjustValues() DiscretizedAsset.PostAdjustValues() DiscretizedAsset.AdjustValues() DiscretizedAsset.ReserveCapacity(int) DiscretizedAsset.StepValues(int) DiscretizedAsset.CommitStep(int, double) DiscretizedAsset.Time DiscretizedAsset.Values DiscretizedAsset.Method object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A working type (DiscretizedAsset), built for one calculation from the bond's arguments at the context's settlement date. Times are measured on the curve's day counter from its reference date. A callability within a week before a coupon date is moved to that coupon's time, its price carried there by the discount factor between the two dates, spread included, and that coupon is then added before the callabilities at its time; a callability on the date of a coupon so moved ahead gets that coupon added to its price. Prices are scaled from per 100 to the face amount. Each live callability is applied by its own type, as QuantLib's fix after v1.44 does (PR #2875), where QuantLib 1.44 read the i-th live callability's type from the i-th entry of the whole schedule, so that after a callability on or before the settlement date a call was applied as a put, or a put as a call. A call caps the values at its price, a put floors them.
