api/NanoQL.Experimental.SamplerVeryFastA.title: Class SamplerVeryFastAnnealing | nanoql
api/NanoQL.Experimental.SamplerVeryFastA.summary: Class SamplerVeryFastAnnealing Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll The very fast annealing's sampler, for the very fast annealing's temperature; the parameter space must be bounded above and below: QuantLib's SamplerVeryFastAnnealing. [Experimental("NQL0001")] [WorkingType] public sealed class SamplerVeryFastAnnealing : IAnnealingSampler<SamplerVeryFastAnnealing> Inheritance object SamplerVeryFastAnnealing Implements IAnnealingSampler<SamplerVeryFastAnnealing> Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Each coordinate is x + y(upper − lower), y = sign(u − ½)·T·((1 + 1/T)^|2u − 1| − 1), redrawn until inside its bounds. Its draws are std::uniform_real_distribution<Real> on a std::mt19937, as MSVC draws them, on the seed, which is required: QuantLib's default seeds from the clock. A working type. A step is at most the box's width w: below it for every draw that moves a point up, and w itself only at u = 0, which moves it down. So no draw brings in a point outside the box by w or more, nor one off a zero-width box's bound; and at T = 0 no draw but u = 0 moves a point at all. QuantLib's loop never ends there: such a point is refused, and so is a lower bound above its upper (Conventions/ExperimentalMathRefusalTests.cs). Fixed (Divergences/VeryFastAnnealingSamplerTests.cs): each coordinate is drawn at least once, where QuantLib's starts the loop from lower − 1, which rounds to the lower bound itself at every magnitude from 2⁵⁴ and at some from 2⁵³, and then returns that bound undrawn; and a temperature whose reciprocal overflows, below about 5.6e-309, takes y as sign·(T^(1 − |2u − 1|) − T), the same value rewritten, where QuantLib's y is infinite and never lands in the box, and its 0·∞ at T = 0 is NaN, which its loop returns. A temperature of 0 so holds the point, the distribution's limit. Above T 100, where 1 + 1/T loses the digits of 1/T (QuantLib's step is 2.3e-2 off at 1e14 and 0 from about 1e16, so the point is held), y is sign·T·expm1(|2u − 1|·log1p(1/T)), the same value. Elsewhere QuantLib's arithmetic. api/NanoQL.Experimental.SuoWangDoubleBar.summary: Class SuoWangDoubleBarrierEngine Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll Suo and Wang's analytic engine for European double barrier options ("Barrier Option Pricing"): the knock-out as an image series, the knock-in as the European less it. [Experimental("NQL0001")] public static class SuoWangDoubleBarrierEngine Inheritance object SuoWangDoubleBarrierEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The value, with QuantLib's additional results: "vanilla", the analytic European; "barrierOut" and "barrierIn", the knock-out and knock-in without their rebate; "rebateIn", QuantLib's own sum for a knock-in's rebate, unread by the value, as in QuantLib. Documented divergences (each leaving QuantLib's value and bits where it doesn't apply). The strike limits are clipped to the corridor on both sides, K↑ = max(min(H, K), L) and K↓ = min(max(L, K), H), where QuantLib clips one side and prices a knock-out call struck above H or a put struck below L negative (#2881's class); the image series runs from −series to series and on while the next pair of terms exceeds machine epsilon of the sum, where QuantLib sums from −series to series − 1, ten terms, unconverged on narrow corridors; QuantLib's sum stands wherever it agrees with that converged series within 1e-12 on the value's scale, max(|value|, 1), QuantLib's cases among them; where that sum isn't finite or disagrees with the analytic engine's knock-out within 1e-12 on the value's scale, as at low volatility, where QuantLib returns NaN once a term's power overflows and, at volatilities of 1% to 3%, sums that cancel, the knock-out is the analytic engine's, its terms taken in logs and its deterministic limit below machine-epsilon variance, the two one image series; and the rebate is priced, a knock-out's at the first touch of either barrier and a knock-in's at expiry where neither is touched, the analytic engine's value, where QuantLib's engine reads none (Divergences/SuoWangDoubleBarrierTests.cs). Each rate and discount is read to the residual time on the volatility's clock, the volatility at the strike, as the analytic engine reads them, where QuantLib reads every structure at the risk-free curve's time: equivalent-constant reads, as the analytic engine keeps them, no exact closed form existing for a first passage under general deterministic term structures. They are exact where (r − q)/σ² is constant over the option's life and the volatility depends on time alone, a knock-out's rebate, paid at the first touch, where r/σ² and q/σ² are each constant, as the analytic engine's are (Conventions/ClosedFormExactnessTests.cs). api/NanoQL.Experimental.TCopulaPolicy.ht.summary: Struct TCopulaPolicy Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll The Student t latent model's copula policy: independent t factors, each normalized to unit variance by √((ν − 2)/ν), so that a latent variable is a combination of t's (CumulativeBehrensFisher). [Experimental("NQL0001")] public readonly struct TCopulaPolicy : ICopulaPolicy<TCopulaPolicy, TCopulaPolicyInitTraits> Implements ICopulaPolicy<TCopulaPolicy, TCopulaPolicyInitTraits> Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.GetType() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks A readonly struct built by Create(ImmutableArray<ImmutableArray<double>>, TCopulaPolicyInitTraits), over immutable state; its zero value holds no distribution, and every member of default(TCopulaPolicy) throws InvalidOperationException. The orders must exceed 2 (finite variance) and, for a model with variables, be odd, as the convolution requires. The distributions are Boost.Math's students_t, ported: its cdf, pdf and quantile. At 4 and 6 degrees of freedom Boost's quantile takes Shaw's forms, which cancel near ½ (InverseCumulativeStudent's remarks); there, within 0.05 of ½, the policy takes one Newton step on Boost's cumulative function, as InverseCumulativeStudent does. Those orders are even, which the convolution refuses, so only a policy built without variables reads them. The target tenor must be a whole number of base tenors. A smile section is built per query, as QuantLib's, from the indexes' fixings and forecasts at the option date: its fixings are read in the context the structure was built with, which it keeps, since the smile-section and volatility queries take no context. The structure takes the base structure's reference date, calendar, convention and day counter. A volatility is the smile section's at the strike, the range checked once, by the query with its own extrapolation flag (Divergences/TenorOptionletExtrapolationTests.cs). QuantLib's builds the section through smileSection(optionTime), which checks the range again without extrapolation, so a query allowed to extrapolate past the base structure's last date refuses: QuantLib's own testTenoroptionletvts asks for its 30-year caplets from the base structure's reference date, two business days after the evaluation date, and on QuantLib 1.44 refuses ("time (30.0219) is past max curve time (30.0137)") on every evaluation date of 29 October to 11 November 2026 but the two Wednesdays. On its test runner's date, 16 September 2015, a Wednesday, the case passes, so QuantLib's own run doesn't refuse. QuantLib's swaption structure builds its section unchecked, as here; where QuantLib's doesn't refuse, the value is its. ExtrapolatorExtensions.DisableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) ExtrapolatorExtensions.EnableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) Remarks A target swaption's smile is the base smile at a strike mapped through the tenor basis spread, under an affine terminal swap rate model fitted to the base swaption's deterministic flows, scaled by the target swap's annuity against the final swap's. A smile section is built per query, as QuantLib's, from the swaps' fair rates on the discount curve; the swaps are built in the context the structure was built with, which it keeps. The target floating schedule is on the base index's calendar, as QuantLib's. QuantLib's empty UnitOfMeasure(), a placeholder whose members throw, is a UnitOfMeasure? null. QuantLib's units are presets: each reads its data from Current when it is built (ResolveUnitOfMeasure(string, Func<UnitOfMeasureData>)), QuantLib's unless a provider configures them, its code QuantLib's always. QuantLib keeps a process-wide registry keyed by name, so a second construction with a known name returns the first construction's data whatever it was given: UnitOfMeasure("Barrels", "B2", Mass) after ("Barrels", "BBL", Volume) has code BBL and type Volume (unitofmeasure.cpp:37-49). There is no registry here, so every unit holds the data it is given, a documented divergence (Divergences/CommodityRegistryTests.cs). Two units are equal when their codes are, compared ordinally, whatever their other data, as QuantLib's operator== compares them (unitofmeasure.hpp:130-132); the hash is the code's. The equality is sealed, so every subclass compares the same way. Every unit's rounding is QuantLib's default Rounding(), which leaves an amount as it is, where QuantLib's is Rounding(0), to the closest whole unit, which its public constructor can't change (unitofmeasure.hpp:82-86), so its automated conversions round a thousand-barrel quantity to thousands of barrels: 2 MB plus 1,500 BBL is 4 MB there, 3.5 MB here (Divergences/QuantityRoundingTests.cs). Default holds QuantLib's known factors between its petroleum units, which its manager holds at start and after clear(), with two of them stored the right way round: QuantLib stores one litre as worth 3.78541 gallons and one gallon as worth 42,000 thousand-barrels (unitofmeasureconversionmanager.cpp:115-122), where one gallon is 3.785 411 784 litres and, "by custom", 42 gallons a barrel (NIST Handbook 44, Appendix C), so a direct lookup converts 1,000 litres into 3,785.41 gallons there and 264.17 here (Divergences/CommodityKnownFactorsTests.cs). Add(UnitOfMeasureConversion) replaces a conversion of the same commodity type between the same two units, either way round, and puts the new one last, as QuantLib's add does. Lookup(CommodityType, UnitOfMeasure, UnitOfMeasure, UnitOfMeasureConversionType) finds a direct, triangulated or chained conversion in QuantLib's order. QuantLib's chained search forbids each unit it starts from to the searches below it, to avoid cycles, but drops the list when it recurses (:190), so a search whose first candidate leads back recurses without end: its known factors' first entry pairs thousand-barrels and barrels, so every chained search from either overflows the stack (barrels to metric tonnes, with or without a path). Here the list is passed down, as QuantLib's ExchangeRateManager passes its own; wherever QuantLib's search returns it never revisits a unit above it, so the answer is QuantLib's (Divergences/UnitConversionSearchTests.cs). api/NanoQL.Experimental.VannaVolgaBarrie.summary: Class VannaVolgaBarrierEngine Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll The Vanna-Volga engine for FX barrier options (Castagna and Mercurio, 2007): the analytic barrier price at the money, corrected by the vanna and volga of the 25-delta call and put, weighted by the probability of not touching the barrier, and bounded by the vanilla price the Vanna-Volga smile gives. [Experimental("NQL0001")] public static class VannaVolgaBarrierEngine Inheritance object VannaVolgaBarrierEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks QuantLib's method, its quote shifts for the barrier's vega, volga and vanna replayed on local values in QuantLib's order (each shift and set-back made on the value the quote holds, since a + s − s need not be a), its barrier prices the analytic engine's as nanoql fixes it. Its additional results carry QuantLib's tags: "Forward", "StrikeVol", "VanillaPrice", "BarrierInPrice", "BarrierOutPrice" and, inside the barriers, "lambda". Two changes, each a documented divergence that leaves QuantLib's bits where it doesn't apply. The engine reads each curve at the instant the quotes' time denotes on the volatility's clock (dated by the evaluation date on Actual/365F), nothing accrued before the curve's own date, where QuantLib reads each at that time on its own clock: its discount factors and the touch probability's zero rates (the logarithms of those discounts over the time). And a rebate is priced as each option pays it: an out option's price with its rebate is QuantLib's, but where QuantLib's bounds bind its rebate-free price, the bound plus the rebate's value at the hit; an in option is QuantLib's rebate-free in price plus the analytic engine's value of the rebate paid at expiry; at or beyond the barrier an out option is its rebate, due now. QuantLib prices a knock-in by parity with the knock-out's rebate and bounds the out price as though it had none. At a zero rebate every added term is 0. api/NanoQL.Experimental.VannaVolgaDouble.summary: Class VannaVolgaDoubleBarrierEngine Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll The Vanna-Volga engine for FX double barrier options (Castagna and Mercurio, 2007): a double-barrier engine's price at the money, corrected by the vanna and volga of the at-the-money, 25-delta call and put options, weighted by the probability of touching neither barrier, and bounded by the vanilla price the Vanna-Volga smile gives. [Experimental("NQL0001")] public static class VannaVolgaDoubleBarrierEngine Inheritance object VannaVolgaDoubleBarrierEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks QuantLib's template on its double-barrier engine as a delegate of the engines' Calculate form: the engine given, such as AnalyticDoubleBarrierEngine.Calculate or SuoWangDoubleBarrierEngine.Calculate, is called on the option's knock-out at each of QuantLib's quote shifts, built as QuantLib builds it, on a Black-Scholes process at the at-the-money volatility dated by the evaluation date on Actual/365F, with QuantLib's number of series terms. Its shifts for the barrier's vega, volga and vanna are replayed on local values in QuantLib's order (each shift and set-back made on the value the quote holds, since a + s − s need not be a). Its additional results carry QuantLib's tags: "VanillaPrice", "BarrierInPrice", "BarrierOutPrice" and, inside the barriers, "lambda". Documented divergences, each leaving QuantLib's bits where it doesn't apply (Divergences/VannaVolgaDoubleBarrierTests.cs). The Vanna-Volga smile's interpolation takes the domestic discount first, as its constructor's order and QuantLib's single-barrier engine take it, where QuantLib passes the foreign discount twice: the vanilla on the smile moves by up to 1.4e-4 at QuantLib's rates. The engine reads each curve at the instant the quotes' time denotes on the volatility's clock, nothing accrued before the curve's own date, where QuantLib reads each at that time on its own clock: its discount factors and the survival probability's zero rates. The already-out and already-in tests include a spot on a barrier, as the option's own Triggered(double), where QuantLib's strict tests send it to the inner engine's "barrier touched". And a rebate is priced as each option pays it: an out option's price with its rebate is QuantLib's, but where QuantLib's bounds bind its rebate-free price, the bound plus the rebate's value at the hit; an in option is QuantLib's rebate-free in price plus the inner engine's value of the rebate paid at expiry; on or beyond a barrier an out option is its rebate, due now. At a zero rebate every added term is 0. The inner engine's own fixes stand: the analytic engine and Suo-Wang price a rebate and converge their series. The method's equivalent-constant reads stand, QuantLib's: one volatility and the zero rates to the quotes' time. Its volatilities are quotes, flat in time, so its Black-Scholes legs are exact where r_d − r_f is constant, and an out option's rebate, paid at the hit, where r_d and r_f are each flat; the smile's correction is the method's approximation. api/NanoQL.Experimental.VarianceGammaEng.summary: Class VarianceGammaEngine Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll The analytic engine for European options under the variance gamma process: the Black-Scholes price conditional on the gamma time, integrated against the gamma density. [Experimental("NQL0001")] public static class VarianceGammaEngine Inheritance object VarianceGammaEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Each curve's discount is read by date, nothing accrued before its own date, and the time on the risk-free clock from its reference date, as QuantLib's. Documented divergences (Divergences/VarianceGammaEngineTests.cs). The gamma density is computed in logs where QuantLib's denominator, Γ(t/ν)·ν^(t/ν), isn't finite and nonzero (t/ν past about 170, ν at most 0.005 at a year), where QuantLib's product of an overflow and an underflow makes the integrand NaN and the integration throws; elsewhere QuantLib's form stands; and where ν < t/100 the integration's bound starts at t + 15√(νt), beyond the gamma time's mean, where QuantLib's 15√(νt) lies below it once ν < t/225 and misses the whole mass. Where 1 − θν − σ²ν/2 isn't positive the spot's mean is infinite and no risk-neutral price exists: the engine refuses, where QuantLib throws "forward (-nan(ind)) must be positive". [Experimental("NQL0001")] public sealed class VegaStressedBlackScholesProcess : GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess Inheritance object StochasticProcess StochasticProcess1D GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess VegaStressedBlackScholesProcess Inherited Members GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess.Drift(double, double) GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess.Apply(double, double) GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess.Expectation(double, double, double) GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess.Time(Date) GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess.X0 GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess.StateVariable GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess.DividendYield GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess.RiskFreeRate GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess.BlackVolatility GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess.LocalVolatility StochasticProcess1D.InitialValues() StochasticProcess1D.Drift(double, Vector) StochasticProcess1D.Diffusion(double, Vector) StochasticProcess1D.Expectation(double, Vector, double) StochasticProcess1D.StdDeviation(double, Vector, double) StochasticProcess1D.Covariance(double, Vector, double) StochasticProcess1D.Evolve(double, Vector, double, Vector) StochasticProcess1D.Apply(Vector, Vector) StochasticProcess1D.Size StochasticProcess.InitialValues(Span<double>) StochasticProcess.Evolve(double, ReadOnlySpan<double>, double, ReadOnlySpan<double>, Span<double>) StochasticProcess.Factors object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The diffusion inside the box [lower time, upper time] × [lower asset, upper asset], ends included, is the process's plus the stress level. QuantLib's setters, which change the process in place, return a copy here. With a nonzero stress the standard deviation, the variance and the step go through the discretization, QuantLib's own route for a strike-dependent volatility, so the stressed diffusion reaches them; QuantLib's take the exact forms from the term structures on a strike-independent volatility, which read no diffusion, so the stress never reaches a step there (Divergences/VegaStressedProcessTests.cs). The expectation keeps QuantLib's exact value from the curves, the mean of the asset reading no volatility, where the discretized route refuses ("not implemented"). With no stress the process is QuantLib's. api/NanoQL.Experimental.ZigguratRng.html.summary: Class ZigguratRng Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Assembly NanoQL.dll A generator of standard normal variates by the Ziggurat method over a 32-bit Mersenne Twister: QuantLib's ZigguratRng. [Experimental("NQL0001")] [WorkingType] public sealed class ZigguratRng : ISeedableRng<ZigguratRng>, IRng Inheritance object ZigguratRng Implements ISeedableRng<ZigguratRng> IRng Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The algorithm is Marsaglia and Tsang's (2000), "The Ziggurat Method for Generating Random Variables", Journal of Statistical Software 5 (8), with their right-most step; each draw uses the leftmost 24 bits of the twister's output for its acceptance, which avoids the correlation between the paper's steps 1 and 2, and its tail is sampled through the inverse cumulative normal. A working type, as the generators are: each draw changes it, and it is not thread-safe. The seed is required: QuantLib's default, 0, seeds the twister from the clock. Constructors ZigguratRng(long) Initializes a new instance of the ZigguratRng class. public ZigguratRng(long seed) Parameters seed long The twister's seed, in [1, 4294967295]. Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException seed is outside [1, 4294967295]. Methods Clone() Copies the generator deeply, its state and its buffers: the copy's next draw equals this generator's, into its own buffer. public ZigguratRng Clone() Returns ZigguratRng The copy. Next() Draws the next standard normal variate, changing the generator (QuantLib's next()). public Sample<double> Next() Returns Sample<double> The variate, with weight 1. Explicit Interface Implementations Create(long) Builds the generator from a seed. static ZigguratRng Create(long seed) Parameters seed long The seed, in [1, 4294967295]. Returns ZigguratRng The generator.

api/NanoQL.Experimental.html.summary: Namespace NanoQL.Experimental Classes AbcdAtmVolCurve The at-the-money volatility curve of the abcd function fitted to quoted volatilities at option tenors, each fitted value scaled by the adjustment factor that matches the quotes, interpolated linearly in time. AdaptedPathPayoff A path payoff that is an adapted function: each payment and exercise reads only the fixings up to its own time, which its AdaptedPathPayoffValuationData enforces. AdaptedPathPayoffValuationData One path's data for an AdaptedPathPayoff, QuantLib's AdaptedPathPayoff::ValuationData: the fixings and curves it reads and the payments and exercise data it writes, refusing a write earlier than the latest time read. AdaptiveInertia An adaptive inertia, after A. Lukic, "Approximating Kinetic Parameters Using Particle Swarm Optimization": halved, within its bounds, after more than sh iterations' net stalls, and doubled below sl: QuantLib's AdaptiveInertia. AnalyticContinuousGeometricAveragePriceAsianHestonEngine Kim and Wee's analytic engine for continuous geometric average-price Asian options under the Heston model ("Pricing of geometric Asian options under Heston's stochastic volatility model", Quantitative Finance 14:10, 2014): the joint characteristic function of the log geometric average and the log spot, Phi(Complex, Complex, double, double, int), inverted by a Fourier integral on 128 Gauss-Legendre points. AnalyticDiscreteGeometricAveragePriceAsianHestonEngine Kim, Kim, Kim and Wee's analytic engine for discrete geometric average-price Asian options under the Heston model: the joint characteristic function of the log geometric average, QuantLib's Phi, inverted by a Fourier integral. AnalyticHestonForwardEuropeanEngine Kruse's analytic engine for forward-starting, strike-reset European options under the Heston model ("On the Pricing of Forward Starting Options under Stochastic Volatility", 2003): the vanilla's probabilities from the characteristic function at each variance the reset may reach, integrated over that variance's law at the reset. AssetSwapHelper A risky-asset-swap helper for a default-probability curve's bootstrap: a payer swap of nominal 100 from the settlement date, whose fair spread on the curve under construction is the helper's quote. BankruptcyEvent A bankruptcy: a default event stronger than every other, which matches every contract event type. BarrelUnitOfMeasure Barrels: code BBL, a volume, the base unit of CommoditySettings by default. BaseCorrelationLossModel<TBaseModel, TInterpolator, TInitTraits> The base correlation loss model, its interpolation by the portfolio's (live) amount percentage: the tranche's expected loss is the difference of two equity tranches' to its attachment and detachment, each priced by a base model at the correlation the surface gives at its level. BaseCorrelationTermStructure<TInterpolator> The matrix-based base correlation term structure: a loss level against time interpolated scalar copula-type parametric correlation, the correlation of a given portfolio's credit loss at a loss level and time. Basket A credit basket: credit names, each with a notional, drawn from a pool of issuers, and a tranche of the pool's loss, with the default loss model that gives its loss statistics. BetaRisk A catastrophe risk whose events arrive as a Poisson process of a return period and whose losses follow a beta distribution of a mean and standard deviation, scaled to a maximum loss. BetaRiskSimulation The simulation of a BetaRisk: each path's events arrive as a Poisson process over the period, each event's loss the maximum loss times a beta draw, X / (X + Y) of two gamma draws. BinomialCRRDoubleBarrierEngine The binomial double-barrier engine on the Cox-Ross-Rubinstein tree and Derman and Kani's discretized double-barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialCRRDoubleBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine<CoxRossRubinstein, DiscretizedDermanKaniDoubleBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine The binomial engine for double barrier options: a discretized double-barrier asset rolled back on a Black-Scholes lattice over a binomial tree, built on the process's curves and volatility flattened at the option's maturity. BinomialEQPDoubleBarrierEngine The binomial double-barrier engine on the additive equal-probabilities tree and Derman and Kani's discretized double-barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialEQPDoubleBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine<AdditiveEQPBinomialTree, DiscretizedDermanKaniDoubleBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialJ4DoubleBarrierEngine The binomial double-barrier engine on the Joshi tree and Derman and Kani's discretized double-barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialJ4DoubleBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine<Joshi4, DiscretizedDermanKaniDoubleBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialJRDoubleBarrierEngine The binomial double-barrier engine on the Jarrow-Rudd tree and Derman and Kani's discretized double-barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialJRDoubleBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine<JarrowRudd, DiscretizedDermanKaniDoubleBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialLRDoubleBarrierEngine The binomial double-barrier engine on the Leisen-Reimer tree and Derman and Kani's discretized double-barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialLRDoubleBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine<LeisenReimer, DiscretizedDermanKaniDoubleBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialLossModel<TCopula, TInitTraits> The binomial defaultable basket loss model: the portfolio loss distribution approximated by an adjusted binomial, which fits the loss distribution's two moments and so allows the portfolio's inhomogeneity at little cost over the LHP. See Dominic O'Kane, "Approximating Independent Loss Distributions with an Adjusted Binomial Distribution", EDHEC Risk and Asset Management Research Centre, 2007, and "Modelling single name and multi-name credit derivatives", chapter 18.5.2, Wiley Finance, 2008. BinomialProbabilityOfAtLeastNEvents The binomial probability of at least n default events, as a function of the names' probabilities, the first read. BinomialTianDoubleBarrierEngine The binomial double-barrier engine on the Tian tree and Derman and Kani's discretized double-barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialTianDoubleBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine<Tian, DiscretizedDermanKaniDoubleBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialTrigeorgisDoubleBarrierEngine The binomial double-barrier engine on the Trigeorgis tree and Derman and Kani's discretized double-barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialTrigeorgisDoubleBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialDoubleBarrierEngine<Trigeorgis, DiscretizedDermanKaniDoubleBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BlackAtmVolCurve The base of Black at-the-money (no-smile) volatility curves. Volatilities are on an annual basis. BlackCallableFixedRateBondEngine The Black-formula engine for callable fixed-rate bonds with a single call or put date: the embedded European option follows the Black "European bond option" treatment of Hull, fourth edition, chapter 20. BlackCallableZeroCouponBondEngine The Black-formula engine for callable zero-coupon bonds with a single call or put date: QuantLib's subclass of the fixed-rate bonds' engine, which only adds constructors, so each overload is BlackCallableFixedRateBondEngine's. QuantLib notes it as yet untested. BlackCdsOptionEngine The Black-formula engine for options on credit default swaps: the underlying's fair spread against its running spread, discounted by its risky annuity, plus the front-end protection of a payer option that doesn't knock out. BlackIborQuantoCouponPricer A Black Ibor coupon pricer whose fixing is quanto-adjusted for an index paid in another currency: QuantLib's BlackIborQuantoCouponPricer. BlackVolSurface The base of Black volatility (smile) surfaces: a smile section at each time, the at-the-money volatility and variance read off it. Volatilities are on an annual basis. BoxMullerFactorSampler The members of BoxMullerFactorSampler<TUrng> that need more of their generator than the class does: its seed constructor. BoxMullerFactorSampler<TUrng> A Gaussian latent model's factor sampler by Box-Muller: a sequence of Box-Muller normal draws, bypassing the copula. QuantLib's LatentModel::FactorSampler specialized on RandomSequenceGenerator<BoxMullerGaussianRng>. CDO The collateralized debt obligation: a mezzanine CDO tranche, its loss given default between the attachment D₁ and the detachment D₂ > D₁. For purchased protection the value is the protection value V₁ less the premium value V₂. CDOResults The results of a CDO's calculation, signed by the protection side. CPICapFloorTermPriceSurface CPI cap and floor prices by maturity and strike, filled across all strikes by put-call parity: QuantLib's CPICapFloorTermPriceSurface. CallableBond The callable bond base class: a bond with a schedule of calls and puts, European or Bermudan (no American optionality), for fixed-rate and zero-coupon bonds. CallableBondConstantVolatility A constant callable-bond volatility, with no time, length or strike dependence. CallableBondResults The results a callable bond's engines return: a bond's, with nothing added, as QuantLib's CallableBond::results adds nothing. CallableBondVolatilityStructure The callable-bond volatility structure base class: forward yield volatilities by option time and bond length, or by option date or tenor and bond tenor, and their smile sections. CallableFixedRateBond A callable or puttable fixed-rate bond: simple annually compounded coupon rates on a schedule, and a single redemption. CallableZeroCouponBond A callable or puttable zero-coupon bond: a single redemption at maturity. CappedFlooredCmsSpreadCoupon A CMS spread coupon with a cap, a floor or both on its rate: a CappedFlooredCoupon over a CmsSpreadCoupon it builds. CatBond A catastrophe bond: a bond whose notional a catastrophe risk reduces, priced by simulating the risk's events. CatBondResults The results of a cat bond's calculation: the bond's, with the simulated loss statistics. CatRisk A catastrophe risk: a source of simulations of its events over a period. CatSimulation A simulation of catastrophe events over a period: each call to NextPath(List<KeyValuePair<Date, double>>) writes the next path's events, their dates and losses. CdsOption An option on a credit default swap. The side of the option is set by choosing the side of the swap: a receiver option is a right to buy an underlying swap selling protection and receiving a coupon, a payer option a right to buy one buying protection and paying a coupon. CdsOptionResults The results of a credit default swap option's calculation: its value and the underlying's risky annuity. ClaytonCopulaRng<TRng> A random-number generator of Clayton copula draws, by conditional inversion of uniform draws: QuantLib's ClaytonCopulaRng. ClubsTopology The clubs topology, after H. M. Emara, "Adaptive Clubs-based Particle Swarm Optimization": each particle belongs to a default number of clubs, and its social best is the best of its clubs' members; a club's best leaves a random club (down to a minimum) and its worst joins one (up to a maximum), and every reset iterations the others return to the default: QuantLib's ClubsTopology. CmsSpreadCoupon A CMS spread coupon: a floating-rate coupon fixing on a swap spread index. CmsSpreadCouponPricer The base of the CMS spread coupon pricers, which read the correlation of the two swap rates. CmsSpreadLeg A builder of a sequence of CMS spread coupons, capped, floored or not. Commodity The base of commodity instruments: an instrument with secondary costs. CommodityCashFlow An energy swap's payment for one pricing period, discounted and undiscounted, in the base currency and the payment's. CommodityCurve A commodity forward curve: prices at dates, forward-flat between them and flat before the first and after the last, optionally on a basis curve whose prices it adds. CommodityIndex A commodity index: its fixings, read from the context, and a forward curve priced in its own unit. CommodityPricingHelperFunctions QuantLib's CommodityPricingHelper, a class of static members: the conversion factors, a unit cost in the base currency and unit, and an energy swap's pricing periods. CommoditySettings The base currency and unit of measure the energy instruments value in: QuantLib's process-wide CommoditySettings, as a value that CommoditySettings holds. CommodityType A commodity type: its name and code, such as "Heating Oil" and "HO". CommodityUnitCost A cost per unit of a commodity: an amount of money per unit of measure, such as 0.1 USD a gallon. ConstNotionalCrossCurrencyBasisSwapRateHelper The rate helper for bootstrapping over constant-notional cross-currency basis swaps. ConstNotionalCrossCurrencySwapRateHelper The rate helper for bootstrapping fixed-vs-floating cross-currency par swaps. ConstantLossLatentModel<TCopula, TInitTraits> The constant-loss default latent model: each name's loss given default a deterministic constant, its recovery; integrable. QuantLib's ConstantLossLatentmodel. ConstantLossModel<TCopula, TInitTraits> The constant-loss latent model as a default loss model: it gives no loss distribution, having no integration of one, but prices digital products such as n-th-to-default swaps through its event probabilities, default correlations and recoveries. ConstantRecoveryModel A recovery-rate model returning its quote's value, whatever the date and the seniority. ContinuousArithmeticAsianVecerEngine Vecer's engine for continuous arithmetic average-price Asian options: the option's value as a one-dimensional PDE in the replicating strategy's variable, solved by Crank-Nicolson (see <http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~vecer/asian-vecer.pdf>); a put by the Asian put-call parity. CorrelationTermStructure The abstract correlation term structure, pretty much like the volatility term structure: the correlation's range is known in advance and there is no strike. Derived structures might hold correlations of any dimension. CrossCurrencyBasisSwapRateHelperBase The base of the cross-currency basis swap rate helpers. CrossCurrencySwapRateHelperBase The base of the cross-currency swap rate helpers: their conventions, collateral curve and dates. CumulativeBehrensFisher The cumulative (generalized) Behrens-Fisher distribution: the exact distribution of a linear combination of any number of Student t variables of odd orders, adapted from Witkovsky's algorithm (Journal of Statistical Planning and Inference 94, 2001, 1-13). DateInterval An interval of dates, from a start date to an end date, both held. DecreasingGaussianWalk A Gaussian random walk whose step decreases: after each round of the moved fireflies' walks, δ becomes δ²: QuantLib's DecreasingGaussianWalk. DecreasingInertia A decreasing inertia: each velocity times the optimizer's inertia times a factor falling linearly with the iterations to the threshold at the last: QuantLib's DecreasingInertia. DefaultEvent A credit event on the bonds of a seniority and currency, with its optional settlement: a realized event, of an atomic type, which the bonds of that seniority and currency suffer together. DefaultLatentModel<TCopula, TInitTraits> The default-event latent model: a latent model of a portfolio's joint default events, a name defaulting by a date when its latent variable falls below the inverse of its default probability. It models the events alone, no severity or exposure; the basket's names and the model's variables correspond by index. DefaultLossModel The abstract default loss model: IDefaultLossModel's contract with the binding written once, QuantLib's DefaultLossModel. DefaultProbKey The key that indexes market-implied credit curves: a proxy for the defaultable bond, or class of bonds, that sets a credit contract's conditions, grouping the atomic default types the contract is sensitive to with the obligation's currency and seniority. DefaultSettlement A default event's settlement: its date and the realized recovery rates of the seniorities it settled. QuantLib's DefaultEvent::DefaultSettlement. DefaultType An atomic credit-event type: one of ISDA's default contractual types and, for a restructuring, its restructuring type. DigitalCmsSpreadCoupon A CMS spread coupon with a digital call, a digital put or both: QuantLib's DigitalCmsSpreadCoupon. DigitalCmsSpreadLeg A builder of a sequence of digital CMS spread coupons: QuantLib's DigitalCmsSpreadLeg. DigitalNotionalRisk A digital notional risk: an event whose loss reaches a threshold takes the whole notional. DiscountingFxResetPricer The FX-reset pricer based on spot FX and two discount curves. DiscountingMtMCrossCurrencyBasisSwapEngine The discounting engine of mark-to-market cross-currency basis swaps. DiscretizedCallableFixedRateBond A callable fixed-rate bond discretized on a lattice: its redemption rolled back with its coupons added and its callabilities applied at their times. DiscretizedDermanKaniDoubleBarrierOption A double barrier option on a lattice with Derman, Kani, Ergener and Bardhan's correction ("Enhanced Numerical Methods for Options with Barriers", 1995): at the nodes straddling a barrier, the values interpolate between the rolled-back value and the knocked-in vanilla or knocked-out rebate by the nodes' distances from the barrier. DiscretizedDoubleBarrierOption A double barrier option on a lattice: knocked out to its rebate, or knocked in to its vanilla, at the nodes on or beyond either barrier, as its type says of each. Distribution A discretized probability density and cumulative probability: buckets of a range, each holding a density, an average and the cumulated and excess probabilities. DistributionRandomWalk<TDistribution> A random walk whose step's radius is drawn from a distribution, its direction isotropic and its sphere an ellipsoid over the problem's bounds, scaled by δ: QuantLib's DistributionRandomWalk. DoubleBarrierPathPricer The path pricer of a double barrier option: either barrier is checked at the path's points, a knock-out paying its rebate at the first hit's node and a knock-in its rebate at expiry where neither is hit. DynProgVPPIntrinsicValueEngine The intrinsic value of a VanillaVPPOption by dynamic programming over known fuel and power prices, one price of each per exercise step: the plant's step condition rolled back from the last step, undiscounted. EnergyBasisSwap An energy basis swap: one index's price against another's on each pricing day, plus a basis on one leg. EnergyCommodity The base of energy commodity instruments: the swaps and the future, priced without an engine. EnergyCommodityResults The results of an energy commodity's calculation: the NPV, in the base currency, with what QuantLib keeps on the instrument (its pricing errors, secondary cost amounts, daily positions and payment cash flows). EnergyDailyPosition An energy swap's position on one pricing day: QuantLib's EnergyDailyPosition. EnergyFuture An energy future: a quantity bought or sold at a trade price, valued at its index's quote. EnergySwap The base of energy swaps: a calendar, a pay and a receive currency, and pricing periods. EnergyVanillaSwap A vanilla energy swap: a fixed price against an index's price on each pricing day. EquityFXVolSurface The base of equity and FX volatility (smile) surfaces, with the at-the-money forward volatility and variance between two times. Volatilities are on an annual basis; only without a smile does the at-the-money forward volatility make sense. EuropeanPathMultiPathPricer The path basket's path pricer: the path payoff's payments at the fixing times, discounted and summed, its early exercise ignored. EventPaymentOffset The offset from a catastrophe event to the date its notional reduction is paid. EventSet A catastrophe risk given by a historical set of events, each path the events of one period of the set's years, shifted to the simulated period. EventSetSimulation The simulation of an EventSet: its paths are the set's events in successive periods as long as the simulated one, from the first such period starting in the set's first year, shifted to the simulated period, until the set runs out. EverestMultiPathPricer The Everest option's path pricer: the notional times one plus the worst asset's return plus the guarantee, discounted. EverestOption An Everest option on several assets: at expiry it pays the notional times one plus the worst of the assets' returns since inception plus a guaranteed return. EverestOptionResults The results of an EverestOption's engine: a multi-asset option's, with the yield the price implies, null where the engine doesn't compute it. ExchangeContract An exchange-traded contract: its code, its expiration date and its underlying's delivery dates, which a nearby commodity curve rolls on. ExponentialIntensity An exponentially decreasing intensity, (β₀ − β_min) e^(−γd) + β_min: QuantLib's ExponentialIntensity. ExtOUWithJumpsProcess Kluge's spot model, an extended Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process plus exponential jumps (an extension of Lucia and Schwartz's): S = e^(X + Y), dX = α(μ(t) − X)dt + σdW, dY = −βY dt + J dN, the jumps exponential with rate η. ExtendedAdditiveEQPBinomialTree The time-dependent additive equal-probabilities binomial tree: equal probabilities, the up move matching the step's first two moments with the drift at the step's time: QuantLib's ExtendedAdditiveEQPBinomialTree. ExtendedBinomialTree<T> The time-dependent binomial tree base: two branches from each node, node index of column i going to nodes index and index + 1, its moves read from the process at each step's time: QuantLib's ExtendedBinomialTree. ExtendedBlackScholesMertonProcess A Black-Scholes-Merton process on its Black volatility, stepped by a built-in scheme: QuantLib's ExtendedBlackScholesMertonProcess. ExtendedBlackVarianceCurve A Black variance curve on volatilities at dates: the variance interpolated in time (linearly by default) up to the last date, the last date's volatility flat beyond it. QuantLib's extension of BlackVarianceCurve to quoted volatilities. ExtendedBlackVarianceSurface A Black variance surface on volatilities at dates and strikes: the variance interpolated in time and strike (bilinearly by default) up to the last date, the last date's volatility flat beyond it. QuantLib's extension of BlackVarianceSurface to quoted volatilities. ExtendedCoxRossRubinstein The time-dependent Cox-Ross-Rubinstein binomial tree: equal jumps of one standard deviation of a step at the step's time, the probabilities carrying the drift: QuantLib's ExtendedCoxRossRubinstein. ExtendedEqualJumpsBinomialTree<T> A time-dependent binomial tree whose up and down moves are equal in the logarithm of the underlying, the probabilities carrying the drift at the step's time: QuantLib's ExtendedEqualJumpsBinomialTree. ExtendedEqualProbabilitiesBinomialTree<T> A time-dependent binomial tree with both branches' probabilities 1/2, its nodes at the drift plus a multiple of the up move at the step's time: QuantLib's ExtendedEqualProbabilitiesBinomialTree. ExtendedJarrowRudd The time-dependent Jarrow-Rudd (multiplicative) equal-probabilities binomial tree: its up move one standard deviation of a step at the step's time: QuantLib's ExtendedJarrowRudd. ExtendedJoshi4 The time-dependent Joshi binomial tree of order 4: centered on the strike, its probabilities from Joshi's expansion at the step's time, on an odd number of steps: QuantLib's ExtendedJoshi4. ExtendedLeisenReimer The time-dependent Leisen-Reimer binomial tree: centered on the strike, its probabilities from the Peizer-Pratt inversion at the step's time, on an odd number of steps: QuantLib's ExtendedLeisenReimer. ExtendedOrnsteinUhlenbeckProcess The extended Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process dx = a(b(t) − x)dt + σdW, its level b a function of time. ExtendedTian The time-dependent Tian binomial tree: its moves and probabilities matching the step's first three moments at the step's time: QuantLib's ExtendedTian. ExtendedTrigeorgis The time-dependent Trigeorgis (additive equal jumps) binomial tree: its move the root of the step's variance and squared drift at the step's time: QuantLib's ExtendedTrigeorgis. FFTEngine The fast-Fourier-transform engine for European options (Carr and Madan, 1998, "Option valuation using the fast Fourier transform", Journal of Computational Finance 2, 61-73): one transform prices every option of an expiry. FFTEngine.ExpiryState The model's state at one expiry: its characteristic function, its discount factors and the strip of exponents u with E[S^u] finite. FFTVanillaEngine The fast-Fourier-transform engine for European options under Black-Scholes, on a constant volatility: one transform prices every option of an expiry (FFTEngine). FFTVarianceGammaEngine The fast-Fourier-transform engine for European options under the variance gamma process: one transform prices every option of an expiry (FFTEngine). FactorSpreadedHazardRateCurve A default-probability structure with a multiplicative spread on the hazard rates of an original curve, whose reference date, calendar, day counter and range it takes. FailureToPay The failure-to-pay atomic event type, with its grace period and the amount required to trigger it. FailureToPayEvent A failure to pay: a default event with the amount defaulted, which matches a contract's FailureToPay type once its grace period has passed. FarlieGumbelMorgensternCopulaRng<TRng> A random-number generator of Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern copula draws, by conditional inversion of uniform draws: QuantLib's FarlieGumbelMorgensternCopulaRng. FdExtOUJumpVanillaEngine The two-dimensional finite-difference engine of a vanilla option on Kluge's spot e^(f(t) + X + Y): X's mesher from its extended Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, Y's an exponential jump mesher, and early exercise by the vanilla step conditions. FdKlugeExtOUSpreadEngine The three-dimensional finite-difference engine of a spread option between Kluge's power e^(f_p(t) + X + Y) and the gas price e^(f_g(t) + U) of a KlugeExtOUProcess: X's and U's meshers from their extended Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, Y's an exponential jump mesher, the basket payoff on power and gas, and early exercise by the vanilla step conditions. FdOrnsteinUhlenbeckVanillaEngine The one-dimensional finite-difference engine of a vanilla option on an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process: the payoff on the process's own value, discounted on a curve, with dividends and early exercise by the vanilla step conditions. FdSimpleExtOUJumpSwingEngine The three-dimensional finite-difference engine of a swing option on Kluge's spot e^(f(t) + X + Y): X's mesher from its extended Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, Y's an exponential jump mesher, and the exercises taken in the third direction by the simple swing condition. FdSimpleExtOUStorageEngine The two-dimensional finite-difference engine of a storage option on the spot e^(f(t) + X), X an extended Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process: the storage level in the second direction, on QuantLib's elevator mesher (the levels reached from empty and from full at the change rate) or a uniform one, and the injections and withdrawals by the simple storage condition at the exercise dates. FdSimpleKlugeExtOUVPPEngine The four-dimensional finite-difference engine of a VanillaVPPOption on a KlugeExtOUProcess: Kluge's power e^(f_p(t) + X + Y) and the fuel price e^(f_g(t) + G), X's and G's meshers from their extended Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes, Y's an exponential jump mesher, and the plant's states in the fourth direction, run by its step condition at the exercise dates. FdmDupire1dOp The Dupire local volatility pricing operator in the strike, ½σ²(K)·∂²/∂K², time reversed so that backward solvers work. FdmExpExtOUInnerValueCalculator The inner value of a payoff on e^(f(t) + u), u a mesher's location in one direction and f a seasonal shape read at the first of its times at or after t − √ε (0 without a shape). FdmExtOUJumpModelInnerValue The inner value of a payoff on Kluge's spot e^(f(t) + x + y), x and y a mesher's locations in directions 0 and 1 and f a seasonal shape read at the first of its times at or after t − √ε (0 without a shape). FdmExtOUJumpOp The finite-difference operator of Kluge's ExtOUWithJumpsProcess on a two-dimensional mesher, X in direction 0 and the jump component Y in direction 1: the extended Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator in X, Y's decay, and the jumps' integral by Gauss-Laguerre quadrature over the exponential jump sizes, linearly interpolated in Y. FdmExtOUJumpSolver The two-dimensional finite-difference solver of Kluge's ExtOUWithJumpsProcess, its jump integral at a Gauss-Laguerre order of 32, as QuantLib's. FdmExtendedOrnsteinUhlenbeckOp The finite-difference operator of an ExtendedOrnsteinUhlenbeckProcess in one direction of a mesher: its drift at the step's mid-time, its diffusion, and the discount at the forward rate over the step. FdmKlugeExtOUOp The finite-difference operator of a KlugeExtOUProcess on a three-dimensional mesher: the power process's operator (FdmExtOUJumpOp) in directions 0 and 1, the gas process's Ornstein-Uhlenbeck operator in direction 2 at a zero rate (the power operator discounts), and the correlation of X and the gas price as a mixed derivative. FdmKlugeExtOUSolver The finite-difference solver of a KlugeExtOUProcess on a mesher of three or more dimensions, its jump integral at a Gauss-Laguerre order of 16, as QuantLib's; directions past the third carried by the step conditions. FdmSimple2dExtOUSolver A two-dimensional finite-difference solver on an ExtendedOrnsteinUhlenbeckProcess's operator in direction 0, the second direction carried by the step conditions (a storage level, say). FdmSimple3dExtOUJumpSolver A three-dimensional finite-difference solver on Kluge's ExtOUWithJumpsProcess operator in directions 0 and 1, its jump integral at a Gauss-Laguerre order of 32, the third direction carried by the step conditions (a swing option's exercises, say). FdmSpreadPayoffInnerValue The inner value of a basket payoff on two inner values, a spread's two legs. FdmVPPStartLimitStepCondition A virtual power plant's step condition with its minimum up and down times and, optionally, a limit on its starts: a block of states per start left. FdmVPPStepCondition The step condition of a virtual power plant valued by dynamic programming: each step adds the running states' spark-spread earnings, at the minimum or the maximum output, then lets each point's states change as the plant's rules allow, at the gas price there. FdmVPPStepConditionFactory Builds a VanillaVPPOption's state mesher and step condition: the plain plant and the plant with a start limit, as QuantLib's; a running-hour limit, which QuantLib's factory classifies and refuses to build, is refused. FdmVPPStepConditionMesher The mesher a virtual power plant's step condition runs on, and the direction of the plant's states. FdmZabrOp The ZABR pricing operator on a mesher whose first direction is the forward F and second the volatility v: ½v²F2β·∂²/∂F² + ½ν²v2γ·∂²/∂v² + νρ|v|γ+1Fβ·∂²/∂F∂v; γ = 1 is SABR. FdmZabrUnderlyingPart The ZABR operator's forward part, ½v²F2β·∂²/∂F² on a mesher whose first direction is the forward F and second the volatility v. FdmZabrVolatilityPart The ZABR operator's volatility part, ½ν²v2γ·∂²/∂v² on a mesher whose first direction is the forward and second the volatility v. FireflyAlgorithm The firefly algorithm, with a differential evolution subpopulation: QuantLib's FireflyAlgorithm. FireflyAlgorithmIntensity The intensity with which fireflies attract each other, which moves each toward the brighter ones: QuantLib's FireflyAlgorithm::Intensity. A derived class implements IntensityImpl(double, double, double) only. FireflyAlgorithmRandomWalk The random walk that moves each firefly besides its attraction: QuantLib's FireflyAlgorithm::RandomWalk. A derived class implements WalkImpl(Vector) only. FloatingCatBond A floating-rate cat bond, possibly capped and/or floored: a floating-rate bond's leg under a notional risk. FrankCopulaRng<TRng> A random-number generator of Frank copula draws, by conditional inversion of uniform draws: QuantLib's FrankCopulaRng. FxResetCashFlowsFunctions QuantLib's free function setFxResetPricer, with a swap form. FxResetConvention The convention for creating FX-reset observations from accrual dates. FxResetCoupon A floating-rate coupon of an FX-resetting leg. FxResetNotionalExchange A netted notional exchange of an FX-resetting leg. FxResetPricer The interface for obtaining the rate of an FX-reset observation. GallonUnitOfMeasure US gallons: code GAL, a volume, converted through barrels. GaussNonCentralChiSquaredPolynomial The orthogonal polynomial of the non-central χ² distribution with ν degrees of freedom and non-centrality λ, for Gauss quadrature on that distribution: QuantLib's GaussNonCentralChiSquaredPolynomial. GaussianBinomialLossModel The binomial loss model on the Gaussian copula: QuantLib's typedef GaussianBinomialLossModel. GaussianConstantLossLM The constant-loss latent model on the Gaussian copula: QuantLib's typedef GaussianConstantLossLM. GaussianDefProbLM The default-event latent model on the Gaussian copula: QuantLib's typedef GaussianDefProbLM. GaussianLHPFlatBCLM The vanilla base correlation model: the Gaussian LHP base model on a bilinear surface, QuantLib's typedef GaussianLHPFlatBCLM. GaussianLHPLossModel The portfolio loss model of a large homogeneous pool on a Gaussian one-factor copula, its expected tranche loss analytic: Anna Kalemanova, Bernd Schmid, Ralf Werner, "The Normal Inverse Gaussian Distribution for Synthetic CDO pricing.", Journal of Derivatives, Vol. 14, No. 3, (Spring 2007), pp. 80-93. GaussianQuadLMIntegration A latent model's integration by a Gauss-Hermite rule per dimension: QuantLib's IntegrationBase<GaussianQuadMultidimIntegrator>, scalar and vector. GaussianQuadMultidimIntegrator Integrates a scalar or a vector function of a vector over ℝ^d with a Gauss-Hermite rule per dimension, the last dimension outermost. GaussianRandomDefaultLM The random default latent model simulation on the Gaussian copula, inverting a Sobol sequence: QuantLib's typedef GaussianRandomDefaultLM. GaussianRandomDefaultModel Random default times on a one-factor Gaussian copula. GaussianRandomLossLM The random spot recovery loss model simulation on the Gaussian copula, inverting a Sobol sequence: QuantLib's typedef GaussianRandomLossLM. GaussianSimulatedAnnealing The hybrid simulated annealing on the Gaussian sampler, the Boltzmann downhill probability, the exponential temperature and no reannealing: QuantLib's GaussianSimulatedAnnealing typedef. GaussianSpotLossLM The spot-recovery latent model on the Gaussian copula: QuantLib's typedef GaussianSpotLossLM. GaussianWalk A Gaussian random walk: the step's radius normal with standard deviation σ, its direction isotropic and its sphere an ellipsoid over the problem's bounds, scaled by δ: QuantLib's GaussianWalk. GemanRoncoroniProcess Geman and Roncoroni's electricity price process: a seasonal mean-reverting diffusion with upward jumps below a threshold over the mean and downward jumps above it: QuantLib's GemanRoncoroniProcess. GeneralizedHullWhite The generalized Hull-White model: d f(rₜ) = (θ(t) − α(t) f(rₜ))dt + σ(t) dWₜ, with α and σ interpolated over dates and f a function of the short rate, fitted to a yield curve: QuantLib's GeneralizedHullWhite. GeneralizedOrnsteinUhlenbeckProcess The Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process dx = a(t)(level − x)dt + σ(t)dW with time-dependent speed and volatility: QuantLib's GeneralizedOrnsteinUhlenbeckProcess. GenericCPI A generic consumer price index: family "CPI", region GenericRegion. GenericRegion A generic geographical or economic region: name "Generic", code "GENERIC". GlobalTopology The global topology: each particle's social best is the best of all the particles' personal bests: QuantLib's GlobalTopology. Glued1dMesher A one-dimensional mesher joining two: the left mesher's points, then the right one's, a point the two share kept once. HaganIrregularSwaptionEngine The engine for European irregular swaptions by super-replication with a basket of vanilla swaptions: QuantLib's HaganIrregularSwaptionEngine. HimalayaMultiPathPricer The Himalaya option's path pricer: at each fixing after the first node the best performer left joins the average and leaves; the payoff at the average, discounted. HimalayaOption A Himalaya option on a basket: at each fixing date the best performer since inception among the assets left joins the average and leaves the basket; at the last fixing the option pays the average's excess over the strike. HomogGaussPoolLossModel The homogeneous pool loss model on the Gaussian copula: QuantLib's typedef HomogGaussPoolLossModel. HomogTPoolLossModel The homogeneous pool loss model on the Student t copula: QuantLib's typedef HomogTPoolLossModel. HomogeneousPoolLossModel<TCopula, TInitTraits> The default loss distribution of a finite homogeneous pool by convolution: the conditional distributions of a one-factor constant-loss latent model integrated over the factor on a midpoint grid. HybridSimulatedAnnealing<TSampler, TProbability, TTemperature, TReannealing> The hybrid simulated annealing: a sampler draws each new point, a probability accepts it, a temperature schedule cools the dimensions and a reannealing rescales their steps, with a local optimizer at each new or best point: QuantLib's HybridSimulatedAnnealing. IHGaussPoolLossModel The inhomogeneous pool loss model on the Gaussian copula: QuantLib's typedef IHGaussPoolLossModel. IHStudentPoolLossModel The inhomogeneous pool loss model on the Student t copula: QuantLib's typedef IHStudentPoolLossModel. IborIborBasisSwapRateHelper A rate helper for bootstrapping over IBOR-IBOR basis swaps. IborLegCashFlows A floating leg mapped to deterministic cash flows under a tenor basis: the notional at the first remaining coupon's start, a spread coupon per remaining coupon, and the notional back at the end: QuantLib's IborLegCashFlows. InhomogeneousPoolLossModel<TCopula, TInitTraits> The default loss distribution of a finite inhomogeneous pool by Hull-White bucketing: the conditional distributions of a one-factor constant-loss latent model integrated over the factor on a midpoint grid. IntegralCDOEngine The integral engine for synthetic CDOs: each premium period integrated in steps of a given size from the later of its start and the evaluation date, the premium paid on the tranche's notional less the expected loss at each step. IntegralHestonVarianceOptionEngine The integral engine for variance options under Heston: the realized variance's law inverted by Bailey and Swarztrauber's fractional transform (see <http://www.econ.univpm.it/recchioni/finance/w4/>). IntegralNtdEngine The integral engine for n-th-to-default swaps: each premium period's default leg integrated in steps of a given size, the contract triggered by the basket's n-th default. InterestRateVolSurface The base of interest-rate volatility (smile) surfaces on an index: an option tenor's date is the index's fixing date for a start that tenor after the index's value date. Volatilities are on an annual basis. InterpolatedAffineHazardRateCurve<TInterpolator> A one-factor affine survival structure whose deterministic hazard rate is interpolated on nodes: the survival is that rate's, flat past the last node, times the model's bond price at its initial intensity. InterpolatedCPICapFloorTermPriceSurface<TInterpolator2D> A CPI cap and floor price surface interpolated over maturity times and quoted strikes: QuantLib's InterpolatedCPICapFloorTermPriceSurface. InterpolatedYoYCapFloorTermPriceSurface<TInterpolator2D, TInterpolator1D> A year-on-year inflation cap and floor price surface interpolated over maturity times and strikes, its at-the-money swap rates where the cap and floor prices meet, and its year-on-year curve bootstrapped on them: QuantLib's InterpolatedYoYCapFloorTermPriceSurface. InterpolatedYoYInflationOptionletStripper The year-on-year optionlet stripper on linear interpolation: QuantLib-Python's InterpolatedYoYInflationOptionletStripper. InterpolatedYoYInflationOptionletVolatilityCurve The year-on-year optionlet volatility curve on linear interpolation: QuantLib-Python's InterpolatedYoYInflationOptionletVolatilityCurve. InterpolatedYoYOptionletStripper<TInterpolator> Strips year-on-year optionlet volatilities along each strike by bootstrapping an interpolated curve on the price surface's caps or floors: QuantLib's InterpolatedYoYOptionletStripper. InterpolatedYoYOptionletVolatilityCurve<TInterpolator> A year-on-year optionlet volatility interpolated in time and flat in strike: QuantLib's InterpolatedYoYOptionletVolatilityCurve. InterpolatingCPICapFloorEngine Prices a CPI cap or floor off a CPI cap and floor price surface: QuantLib's InterpolatingCPICapFloorEngine. InterpolationParameter A parameter whose value is an interpolation of its parameters over fixed times, extrapolated past them: QuantLib's InterpolationParameter. InverseCumulativeBehrensFisher The inverse of CumulativeBehrensFisher, found by Brent's solver on the right half, the distribution being symmetric. InverseLawSquareIntensity An inverse-square-law intensity, (β₀ − β_min)/(d + ε) + β_min: QuantLib's InverseLawSquareIntensity. IrregularSwap An irregular swap: a fixed leg against a floating one, each given whole, their nominals and rates free to change from coupon to coupon: QuantLib's IrregularSwap. IrregularSwapResults The results an engine returns for an irregular swap: the swap's, with the fair fixed rate and the fair floating spread: QuantLib's IrregularSwap::results. IrregularSwaption An option to enter an irregular swap: QuantLib's IrregularSwaption. IrregularSwaptionFunctions The irregular swaption's free functions: QuantLib's stream operator on IrregularSettlementType, whose text differs from the one its ToString() gives. IsotropicRandomWalk<TDistribution> An isotropic random walk: a step whose radius is drawn from a distribution and whose direction on the d-dimensional sphere is uniform, every direction equally likely: QuantLib's IsotropicRandomWalk. Issuer A credit name: the default-probability curves of its bond collections, each keyed by the contract conditions it prices, and the history of its credit events. KInterpolatedYoYInflationOptionletVolatilitySurface The year-on-year optionlet volatility surface interpolating its stripped volatilities linearly in strike: QuantLib-Python's KInterpolatedYoYInflationOptionletVolatilitySurface. KInterpolatedYoYOptionletVolatilitySurface<TInterpolator> A year-on-year optionlet volatility surface stripped along each strike of a cap and floor price surface and interpolated across the strikes: QuantLib's KInterpolatedYoYOptionletVolatilitySurface. KNeighbors The K-neighbours topology: each particle's social best is the best of the K particles before and the K after it, the swarm a ring: QuantLib's KNeighbors. KilolitreUnitOfMeasure Kilolitres: code kl, a volume, converted through barrels. KlugeExtOUProcess Kluge's power model beside a correlated extended Ornstein-Uhlenbeck gas model: the power state (X, Y) of an ExtOUWithJumpsProcess, and the gas log-price U, dU = κ(μ(t) − U)dt + σdW_U, its Brownian motion correlated with X's by ρ. LMIntegration A latent model's integration over its systemic factors: QuantLib's LMIntegration, the common base of its two integrator families, so that an integrable model chooses its algorithm apart. LaplaceInterpolation The reconstruction of missing values on a grid by Laplace interpolation, in any number of dimensions n ≥ 1 and on non-equidistant grids: QuantLib's LaplaceInterpolation. LaplaceInterpolationFunctions The Laplace interpolation of a matrix's missing values: QuantLib's laplaceInterpolation. LatentModelFactorSampler The members of LatentModelFactorSampler<TCopula, TInitTraits, TUsng> that need more of their generator than the class does: its seed constructor. LatentModelFactorSampler<TCopula, TInitTraits, TUsng> A latent model's factor sampler by copula inversion: each draw of a uniform sequence generator, every factor's cumulative distribution inverted by the policy. QuantLib's default LatentModel::FactorSampler<USNG>. LatentModel<TCopula, TInitTraits> The generic multifactor latent variable model: latent variables Yᵢ = Σₖ aᵢₖMₖ + √(1 − Σₖ aᵢₖ²) Zᵢ over independent zero-mean, unit-variance systemic factors Mₖ and idiosyncratic factors Zᵢ, the Zᵢ all of one law, their distributions given by a copula policy. LevyFlightDistribution The Levy flight distribution, p(x) = α x_m^α / x^(α+1) on [x_m, ∞) with α > 0: QuantLib's LevyFlightDistribution. LevyFlightInertia A Levy flight inertia: while a particle keeps improving its personal best the inertia is a random one, and after more than threshold iterations without improvement its velocity is a Levy flight, u^(−1/α): QuantLib's LevyFlightInertia. LevyFlightWalk A Levy flight random walk: the step's radius from a Levy flight distribution, its direction isotropic, scaled by δ: QuantLib's LevyFlightWalk. LinearFlatInterpolation Linear interpolation between discrete points with flat extrapolation: QuantLib's LinearFlatInterpolation. LitreUnitOfMeasure Litres: code l, a volume, converted through barrels. LogNormalSimulatedAnnealing The hybrid simulated annealing on the lognormal sampler, the Boltzmann downhill probability, the exponential temperature and no reannealing: QuantLib's LogNormalSimulatedAnnealing typedef. LognormalCmsSpreadPricer The CMS spread coupon pricer of Brigo and Mercurio, 13.6.2, with the extensions for shifted lognormal and normal dynamics of http://ssrn.com/abstract=2686998: QuantLib's LognormalCmsSpreadPricer. LongstaffSchwartzMultiPathPricer The Longstaff-Schwartz path pricer for path payoffs (Longstaff and Schwartz, 2001, "Valuing American Options by Simulation: A Simple Least-Squares Approach", The Review of Financial Studies 14(1), 113-147): it stores the calibration paths, regresses the continuation value on each fixing's state, then prices on the fitted decisions. LossDist The loss distributions' base: a pool's distribution of losses from each name's volume and default probability, and the probabilities of n defaults. LossDistBinomial The binomial loss distribution: n names of one volume and one default probability. LossDistBucketing The loss distribution of varying volumes and default probabilities, independence assumed, by Hull-White bucketing: John Hull and Alan White, "Valuation of a CDO and nth to default CDS without Monte Carlo simulation", Journal of Derivatives 12, 2, 2004. LossDistHomogeneous The loss distribution of a homogeneous pool, equal volumes and varying default probabilities, built exactly by convolving one name at a time: Xiaofong Ma, "Numerical Methods for the Valuation of Synthetic Collateralized Debt Obligations", PhD Thesis, University of Toronto, 2007 (formula 2.1), avoiding the numerical instability of John Hull and Alan White, "Valuation of a CDO and nth to default CDS without Monte Carlo simulation", Journal of Derivatives 12, 2, 2004. LossDistMonteCarlo The loss distribution of varying volumes and default probabilities by a Monte Carlo simulation of independent defaults, each a Mersenne Twister draw at or below its probability. LossDistResult A homogeneous or binomial loss distribution with its by-products: the members QuantLib's LossDistBinomial and LossDistHomogeneous keep mutable and reset at each call. LotUnitOfMeasure A lot: QuantLib's LotUnitOfMeasure, code Lot, a count. MBUnitOfMeasure Thousands of barrels: code MB, a volume, converted through barrels. MCAmericanPathEngine<TRng, TStats> The Longstaff-Schwartz Monte Carlo engine for path options with early exercise on correlated processes. MCDoubleBarrierEngine The Monte Carlo pricing engine for double barrier options, the barriers checked at the path's points (DoubleBarrierPathPricer). MCEverestEngine The Monte Carlo engine for Everest options on correlated processes. MCHimalayaEngine The Monte Carlo engine for Himalaya options on correlated processes. MCLDDoubleBarrierEngine MCDoubleBarrierEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: MCLDDoubleBarrierEngine, named as QuantLib-Python names its siblings, QuantLib's MCDoubleBarrierEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDEverestEngine MCEverestEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDEverestEngine, QuantLib's MCEverestEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDHimalayaEngine MCHimalayaEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDHimalayaEngine, QuantLib's MCHimalayaEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDPagodaEngine MCPagodaEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: MCLDPagodaEngine, named as QuantLib-Python names its siblings, QuantLib's MCPagodaEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDPathBasketEngine MCPathBasketEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: MCLDPathBasketEngine, named as QuantLib-Python names its siblings, QuantLib's MCPathBasketEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLongstaffSchwartzPathEngine<TRng, TStats> The Longstaff-Schwartz Monte Carlo engine for path options (Longstaff and Schwartz, 2001): calibration paths fit the exercise decisions, then the pricing paths are valued on them. MCPRDoubleBarrierEngine MCDoubleBarrierEngine on pseudo-random draws with QuantLib's default statistics: MCPRDoubleBarrierEngine, named as QuantLib-Python names its siblings, QuantLib's MCDoubleBarrierEngine<PseudoRandom>, its calculations closed at PseudoRandom and GeneralStatistics. MCPREverestEngine MCEverestEngine on pseudo-random draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCPREverestEngine, QuantLib's MCEverestEngine<PseudoRandom>, its calculations closed at PseudoRandom and GeneralStatistics. MCPRHimalayaEngine MCHimalayaEngine on pseudo-random draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCPRHimalayaEngine, QuantLib's MCHimalayaEngine<PseudoRandom>, its calculations closed at PseudoRandom and GeneralStatistics. MCPRPagodaEngine MCPagodaEngine on pseudo-random draws with QuantLib's default statistics: MCPRPagodaEngine, named as QuantLib-Python names its siblings, QuantLib's MCPagodaEngine<PseudoRandom>, its calculations closed at PseudoRandom and GeneralStatistics. MCPRPathBasketEngine MCPathBasketEngine on pseudo-random draws with QuantLib's default statistics: MCPRPathBasketEngine, named as QuantLib-Python names its siblings, QuantLib's MCPathBasketEngine<PseudoRandom>, its calculations closed at PseudoRandom and GeneralStatistics. MCPagodaEngine The Monte Carlo engine for Pagoda options on correlated processes. MCPathBasketEngine The Monte Carlo engine for path options on correlated processes, their early exercise ignored. MTUnitOfMeasure Metric tonnes: code MT, a mass. MakeMCAmericanPathEngine<TRng, TStats> A builder of the Monte Carlo American path engine, with QuantLib's defaults but the seed. MakeMCDoubleBarrierEngine<TRng, TStats> A builder of the Monte Carlo double-barrier engine, with QuantLib's defaults but the seed. MakeMCEverestEngine<TRng, TStats> A builder of the Monte Carlo Everest engine, with QuantLib's defaults but the seed. MakeMCHimalayaEngine<TRng, TStats> A builder of the Monte Carlo Himalaya engine, with QuantLib's defaults but the seed. MakeMCPagodaEngine<TRng, TStats> A builder of the Monte Carlo Pagoda engine, with QuantLib's defaults but the seed. MakeMCPathBasketEngine<TRng, TStats> A builder of the Monte Carlo path basket engine, with QuantLib's defaults but the seed. ManipulateDistribution Operations on Distributions. MidPointCDOEngine The mid-point engine for synthetic CDOs: each premium period's loss taken at its midpoint, the premium paid on the tranche's notional less the expected loss at the period's end. MirrorGaussianSimulatedAnnealing The hybrid simulated annealing on the mirrored Gaussian sampler, the Boltzmann downhill probability, the exponential temperature and no reannealing: QuantLib's MirrorGaussianSimulatedAnnealing typedef. MonteCarloCatBondEngine The Monte Carlo cat bond engine: each simulated path of the catastrophe risk's events writes the bond's notional path, whose cash flows, each scaled by the notional left on its date, are discounted and averaged. MoorePenroseInverseFunctions The Moore-Penrose inverse of a real matrix: QuantLib's moorePenroseInverse. MtMCrossCurrencyBasisSwap A mark-to-market cross-currency basis swap. MtMCrossCurrencyBasisSwapRateHelper The rate helper for bootstrapping over mark-to-market cross-currency basis swaps. MtMCrossCurrencyBasisSwapResults The results an engine returns for a mark-to-market cross-currency basis swap: the cross-currency swap's, with each leg's fair spread and the FX rates and notionals of the resettable coupons. MultidimIntegral Integrates a scalar function of a vector over a box, one one-dimensional integrator per dimension, the last dimension outermost: it generalizes TwoDimensionalIntegral to any number of dimensions up to 15. MultidimLMIntegration A latent model's integration by one-dimensional integrators over a box [a, b] in every dimension: QuantLib's IntegrationBase<MultidimIntegral>, scalar only. NoArbSabrInterpolatedSmileSection A smile section whose volatilities are a no-arbitrage SABR fit to market volatilities at given strikes. NoArbSabrInterpolation The no-arbitrage SABR smile fitted to discrete volatilities: α, β, ν and ρ fitted to the lognormal volatilities at the strikes, interpolated by the volatility of the no-arbitrage SABR section at the fitted parameters. NoArbSabrModel Doust's no-arbitrage SABR model (Paul Doust, "No-arbitrage SABR", The Journal of Computational Finance, 2012): the SABR density with the absorption at zero read off a simulated table, its option and digital prices the density's integrals, the forward adjusted so the density reprices it. NoArbSabrSmileSection A smile section on Doust's no-arbitrage SABR model: its prices, digitals and density are the model's, its volatilities those prices' implied Black volatilities, the SABR expansion's where none is found. NoArbSabrSwaptionVolatilityCube The no-arbitrage SABR swaption volatility cube: QuantLib's NoArbSabrSwaptionVolatilityCube, the XABR cube on Doust's no-arbitrage SABR model, whose smiles are NoArbSabrInterpolation fits and whose sections are NoArbSabrSmileSections. NoOffset No offset: a notional reduction is paid on its event's date. NormalCLVModel The collocating local volatility (CLV) model with a normally distributed kernel process, an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, collocated to a Black-Scholes process's distribution at given maturities: QuantLib's NormalCLVModel. NormalRandomWalkDistribution The normal distribution as a random walk's radius, std::normal_distribution<Real>(mean, sigma) drawn as MSVC 14.44 draws it: the distribution of QuantLib's GaussianWalk. NorthAmericaCorpDefaultKey ISDA's standard default contractual key for US corporate debt: a failure to pay, a bankruptcy and, unless it is NoRestructuring, one restructuring type. NotionalPath A path of a cat bond's notional: the fraction of the original notional left, from the reductions added in date order. NotionalRisk A cat bond's notional risk: how a path's events reduce its notional. NthToDefault An n-th-to-default swap: protection against the n-th default in a basket of credits, for premium payments on the protected notional. Priced as a credit default swap whose default probability is the basket's probability of n defaults or more (Hull and White, "Valuation of a CDO and nth to default CDS without Monte Carlo simulation", Journal of Derivatives 12, 2, 2004). NthToDefaultResults The results an engine returns for an NthToDefault: the instrument's, with its legs' values and its fair premium. NullCommodityType The commodity type of conversions that hold for any commodity: name and code "<NULL>", the type of QuantLib's known unit conversions. OneFactorAffineSurvivalStructure The survival probability term structure of a one-factor stochastic model of the default intensity: the model's bond price at its initial intensity, conditional on survival to a prior time and the intensity realized there. OneFactorCopula The one-factor copula models' base: John Hull and Alan White, "The Perfect Copula", June 2006. The variables Yᵢ = a·M + √(1 − a²)·Zᵢ, M and Zᵢ independent of zero mean and unit variance, their correlation a² the copula's; a name's default by t is Yᵢ below F_Y⁻¹(Qᵢ(t)), so that, given M = m, it defaults with probability F_Z((F_Y⁻¹(p) − a·m)/√(1 − a²)). The densities of M and Z are the derived models'; F_Y is tabulated by them unless it is analytic, and the integrals over M are Euler sums on a midpoint grid. OneFactorGaussianCopula The one-factor Gaussian copula: M, Z and Y standard normal, φ(x) = exp(−x²/2)/√(2π), its distribution of Y analytic.
