OneFactorGaussianStudentCopula The one-factor Gaussian-Student t copula: Yᵢ = a·M + √(1 − a²)·Zᵢ, M Gaussian and Zᵢ Student t of N_z degrees of freedom, each Student variable scaled by √((ν − 2)/ν) to unit variance. Y's distribution is tabulated at construction on 201 points of [−10, 10], each a double Euler sum of the convolution on [−10, 10] in 400 steps, QuantLib's loop order. OneFactorStudentCopula The one-factor double Student t copula: Yᵢ = a·M + √(1 − a²)·Zᵢ, M and Zᵢ Student t of N_m and N_z degrees of freedom, each Student variable scaled by √((ν − 2)/ν) to unit variance. Y's distribution is tabulated at construction on 201 points of [−10, 10], each a double Euler sum of the convolution on [−10, 10] in 400 steps, QuantLib's loop order. OneFactorStudentGaussianCopula The one-factor Student t-Gaussian copula: Yᵢ = a·M + √(1 − a²)·Zᵢ, M Student t of N_m degrees of freedom and Zᵢ Gaussian, each Student variable scaled by √((ν − 2)/ν) to unit variance. Y's distribution is tabulated at construction on 201 points of [−10, 10], each a double Euler sum of the convolution on [−10, 10] in 400 steps, QuantLib's loop order. OvernightIborBasisSwapRateHelper A rate helper for bootstrapping over overnight-IBOR basis swaps. OvernightIndexedFundingRateHelper A rate helper quoting the funding margin over a compounded overnight rate: QuantLib's OvernightIndexedFundingRateHelper. OvernightOvernightBasisSwapRateHelper A rate helper for bootstrapping over overnight-overnight basis swaps. PagodaMultiPathPricer The Pagoda option's path pricer: a fraction of the portfolio's average performance over the periods, capped at the roof and floored at 0, discounted. PagodaOption A Pagoda option on a portfolio: at expiry it pays a fraction of the portfolio's performance over the fixing periods, capped at a roof and floored at 0. ParticleSwarmOptimization Particle swarm optimization: QuantLib's ParticleSwarmOptimization. ParticleSwarmOptimizationInertia The inertia that alters the swarm's velocities each iteration: QuantLib's ParticleSwarmOptimization::Inertia. ParticleSwarmOptimizationTopology The topology that sets each particle's social best from the swarm's personal bests each iteration: QuantLib's ParticleSwarmOptimization::Topology. PathMultiAssetOption An option on several assets' paths, its payoff a PathPayoff at fixing dates. PathPayoff A payoff on the assets' whole paths at the fixing dates: its payments and early-termination values, and the state on which a Longstaff-Schwartz regression decides an exercise. PaymentTerm A payment term, such as "Pricing end + 5 days": an offset in days from an event, on a calendar. PerturbativeBarrierOptionEngine The perturbative engine for up-and-out put options on time-dependent Black-Scholes markets (Fatone, Recchioni and Zirilli): the barrier price on the market's averages, corrected to first or second order in the drift and variance's departures from them. PiecewiseFunctionFunctions A piecewise constant function: QuantLib's QL_PIECEWISE_FUNCTION macro. PiecewiseIntegral The integral of a piecewise well-behaved function, each piece integrated by a given integrator, optionally over intervals that strictly exclude the critical points: QuantLib's PiecewiseIntegral. PiecewiseYoYOptionletVolatilityCurve<TInterpolator, TBootstrap, TTraits> A year-on-year optionlet volatility curve bootstrapped at one strike on optionlet helpers, flat in strike and interpolated in time: QuantLib's PiecewiseYoYOptionletVolatilityCurve. PolarStudentTFactorSampler The members of PolarStudentTFactorSampler<TUrng> that need more of their generator than the class does: its seed constructor. PolarStudentTFactorSampler<TUrng> A Student t latent model's factor sampler by polar Student t draws, bypassing the copula: one generator per systemic factor, and one for every idiosyncratic factor. QuantLib's LatentModel::FactorSampler specialized on RandomSequenceGenerator<PolarStudentTRng>. PolarStudentTRng The members of PolarStudentTRng<TUrng> that need more of their uniform generator than the class does: its seed constructor. PolarStudentTRng<TUrng> The polar Student t random-number generator: Bailey's polar method ("Polar Generation of Random Variates With the t-Distribution", Mathematics of Computation 62-206, 1994), in the variant of "Random Number Generation and Monte Carlo Methods" (Springer, 2003, page 185), with uniforms remapped to [−1, 1] so that no draw sets the sign. Polynomial2DSpline A two-dimensional interpolation, parabolic in the y direction and a spline in the x direction: QuantLib's Polynomial2DSpline. Pool A pool of issuers by name, each with the default key it enters with and a time. PricingError A message a commodity's calculation records: QuantLib's PricingError. PricingPeriod A pricing period of an energy swap: its dates, its payment date and the quantity it delivers. ProbabilityAlwaysDownhill A probability that accepts only the points that improve on the current one: depending on the problem, the optimizer is then very unlikely to escape a local optimum: QuantLib's ProbabilityAlwaysDownhill. ProbabilityBoltzmann A probability from a Boltzmann distribution: a point is accepted where 1/(1 + e^(−(current − new)/T)) is above a uniform draw, T the largest temperature: QuantLib's ProbabilityBoltzmann. ProbabilityBoltzmannDownhill A Boltzmann probability that always accepts a point that improves on the current one: QuantLib's ProbabilityBoltzmannDownhill. ProbabilityOfAtLeastNEvents The probability of at least n default events, as a function of the names' probabilities. ProbabilityOfNEvents The probability of exactly n default events, as a function of the names' probabilities. ProportionalNotionalRisk A proportional notional risk: the cumulated losses above an attachment reduce the notional linearly, to nothing at the exhaustion. ProxyIbor An Ibor index whose forecast is another index's fixing, geared and spread: QuantLib's ProxyIbor. QuantityFunctions QuantLib's free functions of quantity.hpp: the closeness of two quantities. QuantitySettings The settings that say how Quantity amounts in different units combine: QuantLib's static Quantity::conversionType and Quantity::baseUnitOfMeasure, as a value that QuantitySettings holds. QuantoDoubleBarrierOption A quanto double barrier option: a double barrier option on an asset in a foreign currency, paid in the domestic one. RandomDefaultLM<TCopula, TInitTraits, TUsng> The default-only latent model simulation with fixed recoveries: each path's defaults, by name, on a default latent model's variables. RandomDefaultModel The base class of random default models: sequences of random default times, one for each name in the pool. RandomLM<TCopula, TInitTraits, TUsng> The base of the latent models' Monte Carlo simulations, independent of the copula and of the generator: it draws the factors and the variables and finds each default's day; the derived models say what a sample's events are. Its statistics read the stored paths. RandomLossLM<TCopula, TInitTraits, TUsng> The random spot recovery rate loss model simulation for any copula: each path's defaults and their recoveries, on a spot-recovery latent model's default and recovery variables. ReannealingFiniteDifferences A reannealing by finite differences, which raises the temperature the more sensitive dimensions see so the search concentrates on them: QuantLib's ReannealingFiniteDifferences. ReannealingTrivial No reannealing: QuantLib's ReannealingTrivial. RecoveryRateModel A model of the recovery rate: the future value of a recovery rate in the event of a default. RecoveryRateQuote A recovery-rate market quote and the seniority it is quoted for. RecursiveGaussLossModel The recursive loss model on the Gaussian copula: QuantLib's typedef RecursiveGaussLossModel. RecursiveLossModel<TCopula, TInitTraits> The recursive STCDO default loss model of a heterogeneous pool: names heterogeneous in their default probabilities, notionals and recoveries, their correlations given by the latent model. The recursive pricing algorithm is Andersen, Sidenius and Basu's, "All your hedges in one basket", Risk, November 2003, pages 67-72. RiskyAssetSwap A risky asset swap: a risky fixed-rate bond bought at par and swapped into the floating rate plus a spread, the bond's value from the default-probability curve with its recovery integrated over the default density. RiskyAssetSwapOption An option on a risky asset swap: Bachelier's formula on the swap's spread against the market's, its annuity the swap's float annuity times its nominal. RiskyAssetSwapResults The results of a RiskyAssetSwap's calculation. SABRVolTermStructure A Black volatility term structure of SABR smiles on a forward growing at a constant rate: at time t the SABR volatility (Hagan's 2002 expansion) at the forward s₀e^(rt). SabrVolSurface An interest-rate volatility surface of SABR smiles: at each time, the SABR section fitted to the at-the-money curve's volatility plus volatility spreads at strike spreads around the index's fixing, the spreads interpolated linearly between the option tenors. SaddlePointLossModel<TCopula, TInitTraits> The saddle-point portfolio credit default loss model: the saddle-point expansion's integrations of several default risk metrics, the dependence dealt with through a latent model that makes the integrals conditional on its factor, the latent variables integrated indirectly. SaddlePointTailLossModel<TCopula, TInitTraits> The saddle-point loss model with its expected tranche loss read from its own tail: the probability of losing each amount in the tranche or more, ProbOverPortfLoss(Date, double), integrated over the tranche, where the base reads the tranche of the conditional expected loss, a large-pool reading. SamplerCauchy A sampler from the Cauchy distribution, x + T·c: for lower dimensions it can be faster than the Gaussian sampler, especially with the Cauchy temperature: QuantLib's SamplerCauchy. SamplerGaussian A sampler from the normal distribution, x + √T·z, so the parameter space must have support on the whole real line: QuantLib's SamplerGaussian. SamplerLogNormal A sampler from the lognormal distribution, x·e^(√T·z), so the parameter space must have support on the positive side of the real line only: QuantLib's SamplerLogNormal. SamplerMirrorGaussian A sampler from the normal distribution constrained to lie within the boundaries: a value beyond one is reflected back: QuantLib's SamplerMirrorGaussian. SamplerRingGaussian A sampler from the normal distribution constrained to lie within the boundaries: a value beyond one comes back from the other side, as on a ring: QuantLib's SamplerRingGaussian. SamplerVeryFastAnnealing The very fast annealing's sampler, for the very fast annealing's temperature; the parameter space must be bounded above and below: QuantLib's SamplerVeryFastAnnealing. SimpleRandomInertia A random inertia: each velocity times the optimizer's inertia times a uniform draw in (threshold, 1): QuantLib's SimpleRandomInertia. SpotRecoveryLatentModel<TCopula, TInitTraits> The random spot recovery rate latent variable portfolio model: N. Bennani and J. Maetz, "A Spot Stochastic Recovery Extension of the Gaussian Copula", MPRA July 2009; H. Li, "Extension of Spot Recovery model for Gaussian Copula", MPRA October 2009; adapted to many factors and any copula. Its variables are the n names' defaults, then their n recoveries. SpreadedHazardRateCurve A default-probability structure with an additive spread on the hazard rates of an original curve, whose reference date, calendar, day counter and range it takes. SquareRootCLVModel The collocating local volatility (CLV) model with a square-root kernel process, its distribution non-central χ², collocated to a Black-Scholes process's distribution at given maturities: QuantLib's SquareRootCLVModel. StrippedCappedFlooredCoupon The option embedded in a capped or floored coupon, stripped from it: QuantLib's StrippedCappedFlooredCoupon. StrippedCappedFlooredCouponLeg A leg whose capped or floored coupons are replaced by their stripped options: QuantLib's StrippedCappedFlooredCouponLeg, whose conversion to a leg is ToLeg(). StrippedYoYOptionlets Year-on-year optionlet volatilities stripped along each strike: a volatility curve per strike, what QuantLib's YoYOptionletStripper holds after its initialize. SuoWangDoubleBarrierEngine Suo and Wang's analytic engine for European double barrier options ("Barrier Option Pricing"): the knock-out as an image series, the knock-in as the European less it. SviInterpolatedSmileSection A smile section whose volatilities are an SVI fit to market volatilities at given strikes. SviInterpolation The SVI smile fitted to discrete volatilities: SVI's five parameters a, b, σ, ρ and m fitted to the lognormal volatilities at the strikes, interpolated by the volatility of the SVI smile section at the fitted parameters. SviInterpolationFunctions QuantLib's SVI free functions: the parameters' check and the total variance. SviSmileSection The stochastic-volatility-inspired (SVI) smile section: the volatility whose total variance at a log-moneyness k is a + b(ρ(k − m) + √((k − m)² + σ²)). SwapCashFlows A fixed-versus-floating swap mapped to deterministic cash flows under a tenor basis: the floating leg's (IborLegCashFlows) and the fixed coupons that start on or after the discount curve's reference date, with their annuity weights: QuantLib's SwapCashFlows. SwapSpreadIndex A swap-rate spread index: gearing₁ times one swap index's rate plus gearing₂ times another's. SwaptionCashFlows A swaption mapped to deterministic fixed and floating cash flows under a tenor basis, with its exercise times after the discount curve's reference date: QuantLib's SwaptionCashFlows. SyntheticCDO A synthetic collateralized debt obligation: protection on a basket's tranche between its attachment D₁ and detachment D₂, against a running premium on the tranche's notional, reduced by the expected protection payments, and an upfront. SyntheticCDOResults A synthetic CDO's results: its legs, its fair rates and the expected tranche losses. TBinomialLossModel The binomial loss model on the Student t copula: QuantLib's typedef TBinomialLossModel. TConstantLossLM The constant-loss latent model on the Student t copula: QuantLib's typedef TConstantLossLM. TDefProbLM The default-event latent model on the Student t copula: QuantLib's typedef TDefProbLM. TRandomDefaultLM The random default latent model simulation on the Student t copula, inverting a Sobol sequence: QuantLib's typedef TRandomDefaultLM. TRandomLossLM The random spot recovery loss model simulation on the Student t copula, inverting a Sobol sequence: QuantLib's typedef TRandomLossLM. TSpotLossLM The spot-recovery latent model on the Student t copula: QuantLib's typedef TSpotLossLM. TemperatureBoltzmann A temperature for the Gaussian sampler, T₀/ln k: QuantLib's TemperatureBoltzmann. TemperatureCauchy A temperature for the Cauchy sampler, T₀/k: QuantLib's TemperatureCauchy. TemperatureCauchy1D A temperature for the Cauchy sampler, T₀/k^(1/n): QuantLib's TemperatureCauchy1D. TemperatureExponential An exponential temperature, T₀·p^k: QuantLib's TemperatureExponential. TemperatureVeryFastAnnealing The very fast annealing's temperature, T₀·e^(−c·k^(1/n)), for the very fast annealing's sampler: QuantLib's TemperatureVeryFastAnnealing. TenorOptionletVTS A normal optionlet volatility on a longer target tenor transformed from one on a shorter base tenor: QuantLib's TenorOptionletVTS. TenorOptionletVTSCorrelationStructure The correlation between two forward rates by their start times, which TenorOptionletVTS reads: QuantLib's TenorOptionletVTS::CorrelationStructure, by its typedef's name. TenorSwaptionVTS A normal swaption volatility on a target floating tenor and fixed frequency transformed from one on a base floating tenor and fixed frequency: QuantLib's TenorSwaptionVTS. TokyoKilolitreUnitOfMeasure Tokyo kilolitres: code KL_tk, a volume, converted through barrels. TreeCallableFixedRateBondEngine The numerical lattice engine for callable fixed-rate bonds: the bond rolled back on a short-rate model's tree. TreeCallableZeroCouponBondEngine The numerical lattice engine for callable zero-coupon bonds: QuantLib's subclass of the fixed-rate bonds' engine, which only adds constructors, so each overload is TreeCallableFixedRateBondEngine's. TrivialInertia A constant inertia: each velocity times the optimizer's inertia: QuantLib's TrivialInertia. TwoParameterCorrelation The two-parameter correlation ρ = ρ∞ + (1 − ρ∞)·exp(−β|t₂ − t₁|), its parameters interpolated in the first start time: QuantLib's TenorOptionletVTS::TwoParameterCorrelation. UnitOfMeasure A unit of measure specification: its name, code and type. UnitOfMeasureConversion A conversion factor between two units of measure, for a commodity type: a unit of the source is worth ConversionFactor units of the target. UnitOfMeasureConversions The registry of conversion factors between units of measure: QuantLib's process-wide UnitOfMeasureConversionManager, renamed, as an immutable value that UnitOfMeasureConversions holds. UnitOfMeasureData A unit of measure preset's data, which ResolveUnitOfMeasure(string, Func<UnitOfMeasureData>) returns. VanillaVPPOption A virtual power plant: the right to run a gas-fired plant at each exercise date, earning power less gas at its heat rate, within its output range, minimum up and down times, start costs and, optionally, a limit on its starts or running hours. VannaVolgaBarrierEngine The Vanna-Volga engine for FX barrier options (Castagna and Mercurio, 2007): the analytic barrier price at the money, corrected by the vanna and volga of the 25-delta call and put, weighted by the probability of not touching the barrier, and bounded by the vanilla price the Vanna-Volga smile gives. VannaVolgaDoubleBarrierEngine The Vanna-Volga engine for FX double barrier options (Castagna and Mercurio, 2007): a double-barrier engine's price at the money, corrected by the vanna and volga of the at-the-money, 25-delta call and put options, weighted by the probability of touching neither barrier, and bounded by the vanilla price the Vanna-Volga smile gives. VannaVolgaInterpolation The Vanna-Volga interpolation of a smile between three volatilities in strike space: the at-the-money call's Black price corrected by the three quoted calls' market premia over their at-the-money ones, weighted by each strike's vega, and turned back into a volatility. VarianceGammaEngine The analytic engine for European options under the variance gamma process: the Black-Scholes price conditional on the gamma time, integrated against the gamma density. VarianceGammaModel The variance gamma model (Madan, Carr and Chang, 1998, "The variance gamma process and option pricing", European Finance Review 2, 79-105): its process's three parameters. VarianceGammaProcess The variance gamma process: a Brownian motion with drift θ and volatility σ, db = θ dt + σ dW, evaluated at the times of a gamma process with mean 1 and variance rate ν. VarianceOption An option on realized variance: at maturity it pays the notional times the payoff of the variance realized from the start date. VegaStressedBlackScholesProcess A Black-Scholes process whose volatility is stressed by a level inside a box of times and asset values: QuantLib's VegaStressedBlackScholesProcess. VolatilityCube A volatility cube of interest-rate volatility surfaces and abcd at-the-money curves on one reference date. YYGenericCPI A quoted year-on-year generic consumer price index, not a ratio: family "YY_CPI", region GenericRegion. YoYCapFloorTermPriceSurface Year-on-year inflation cap and floor prices by maturity and strike, with the at-the-money year-on-year swap rates and the year-on-year curve they imply: QuantLib's YoYCapFloorTermPriceSurface. YoYInflationCapFloorTermPriceSurface The year-on-year cap and floor price surface on bicubic interpolation of its prices and cubic interpolation of its swap rates: QuantLib-Python's YoYInflationCapFloorTermPriceSurface. YoYOptionletHelper A year-on-year inflation volatility bootstrap helper: a cap or floor priced off the volatility under construction, quoting its price: QuantLib's YoYOptionletHelper. YoYOptionletStripper Strips year-on-year optionlet volatilities from a cap and floor price surface along each strike: QuantLib's YoYOptionletStripper. ZigguratRng A generator of standard normal variates by the Ziggurat method over a 32-bit Mersenne Twister: QuantLib's ZigguratRng. Structs AffineHazardRate The affine hazard-rate curve traits: a deterministic hazard rate interpolated on the nodes, added to a one-factor affine model of the default intensity, bootstrapped so that the model's curve reprices the market. FdmVPPStepConditionParams A virtual power plant's operating parameters, as its step conditions read them. FxReset The contractual observation used to reset a cross-currency notional. GaussianCopulaPolicy The Gaussian latent model's copula policy: standard normal systemic and idiosyncratic factors, so that the latent variables are standard normal too, by the Gaussian's stability under convolution. GaussianCopulaPolicyInitTraits The Gaussian copula policy's initialization parameters: none, QuantLib's int placeholder. LinearFlat The linear interpolation with flat extrapolation's factory and traits: QuantLib's LinearFlat. Loss A loss's time and amount, ordered by time. NoArbSabr The no-arbitrage SABR interpolation factory: builds a NoArbSabrInterpolation with its parameters over given points. Global: a change to one point changes the whole fit. Polynomial The Polynomial2DSpline interpolation's factory: QuantLib's Polynomial. Quantity An amount of a commodity, in a unit of measure. Svi The SVI interpolation's factory and traits: an SviInterpolation fitted with its parameters. SwaptionVolCubeNoArbSabrModel The XABR cube's model for Doust's no-arbitrage SABR: QuantLib's SwaptionVolCubeNoArbSabrModel with its traits' specialization, the smiles NoArbSabrInterpolation fits, the sections NoArbSabrSmileSections, no γ. TCopulaPolicy The Student t latent model's copula policy: independent t factors, each normalized to unit variance by √((ν − 2)/ν), so that a latent variable is a combination of t's (CumulativeBehrensFisher). TCopulaPolicyInitTraits The Student t copula policy's initialization parameters: the orders of the factors' t distributions, the systemic factors' and then one for every idiosyncratic factor. VannaVolga The Vanna-Volga interpolation's factory and traits: a VannaVolgaInterpolation on a market. YoYInflationVolatilityTraits The bootstrap traits of a year-on-year optionlet volatility curve: QuantLib's YoYInflationVolatilityTraits. Ziggurat Random-number traits for the Ziggurat generator: QuantLib's Ziggurat. Interfaces IAnnealingProbability<TSelf> The hybrid simulated annealing's probability, which decides whether a new point is accepted: QuantLib's Probability template parameter. IAnnealingReannealing<TSelf> The hybrid simulated annealing's reannealing, which rescales each dimension's steps to raise the temperature the more sensitive dimensions see: QuantLib's Reannealing template parameter. IAnnealingSampler<TSelf> The hybrid simulated annealing's sampler, which draws a new point from a density on the current one: QuantLib's Sampler template parameter. IAnnealingTemperature<TSelf> The hybrid simulated annealing's temperature, a schedule T(k) over each dimension's steps: QuantLib's Temperature template parameter. IBaseCorrelationModel<TInitTraits> A base model of the base-correlation loss model: a loss model of one correlation, built per correlation the surface gives, QuantLib's setupModels specialisations. ICopulaPolicy<TSelf, TInitTraits> The concept of a latent model's copula policy: the distributions of the systemic factors, the idiosyncratic factors and the latent variables they combine into, which LatentModel<TCopula, TInitTraits> takes as its template parameter. IDefaultLossModel A default loss model: the basket's contract with the algorithms that give its joint loss statistics (latent models, top-down models). QuantLib's DefaultLossModel, whose abstract class form is DefaultLossModel. IDiscretizedDoubleBarrierAsset<TSelf> A discretized double-barrier asset a binomial double-barrier engine builds: the constructor QuantLib's engine template calls, D(arguments, process, grid) (binomialdoublebarrierengine.hpp:119), as a static factory (IDiscretizedBarrierAsset's form). IRandomWalkDistribution A distribution an isotropic random walk draws its step's radius from, over a 32-bit Mersenne Twister: QuantLib's Distribution template parameter, "compatible with std::mt19937". Enums AtomicDefaultType An atomic default event, a single contractual event: QuantLib's AtomicDefault::Type. EnergyCommodityDeliverySchedule When an energy commodity is delivered: QuantLib's EnergyCommodity::DeliverySchedule. EnergyCommodityPaymentSchedule When an energy commodity is paid for: QuantLib's EnergyCommodity::PaymentSchedule. EnergyCommodityQuantityPeriodicity The period a quantity is given per: QuantLib's EnergyCommodity::QuantityPeriodicity. ExtendedBlackScholesMertonProcessDiscretization The extended Black-Scholes-Merton process's built-in schemes: QuantLib's ExtendedBlackScholesMertonProcess::Discretization. ExtendedBlackVarianceSurfaceExtrapolation How an ExtendedBlackVarianceSurface extrapolates beyond its strikes. ExtendedOrnsteinUhlenbeckProcessDiscretization How an ExtendedOrnsteinUhlenbeckProcess integrates its time-dependent level over a step. HybridSimulatedAnnealingLocalOptimizeScheme When the hybrid simulated annealing runs its local optimizer: QuantLib's HybridSimulatedAnnealing::LocalOptimizeScheme. HybridSimulatedAnnealingResetScheme Where the hybrid simulated annealing resets its current point: QuantLib's HybridSimulatedAnnealing::ResetScheme. IrregularSettlementType How an irregular swaption settles on exercise: QuantLib's IrregularSettlement::Type. LatentModelIntegrationType A latent model's integration algorithm over its systemic factors. MtMCrossCurrencyBasisSwapType Whether a mark-to-market cross-currency basis swap pays or receives its FX base-currency leg: QuantLib's MtMCrossCurrencyBasisSwap::Type. PaymentTermEventType The event a payment term counts from: QuantLib's PaymentTerm::EventType. PricingErrorLevel How serious a pricing error is: QuantLib's PricingError::Level. QuantityConversionType How quantities in different units are combined: QuantLib's Quantity::ConversionType, read from ConversionType. RestructuringType A restructuring type: QuantLib's Restructuring::Type. Seniority The seniority of a bond; also the ISDA tiers and seniorities of CDS conventional spreads. UnitOfMeasureConversionType Where a unit conversion comes from: QuantLib's UnitOfMeasureConversion::Type. UnitOfMeasureType What a unit of measure measures: QuantLib's UnitOfMeasure::Type. Delegates MultidimIntegrand A scalar function of a vector, QuantLib's std::function<Real (const std::vector<Real>&)>: the integrand of a multidimensional integration. Any other value's fields are written out, its parts that equal no preset under generated names, name/1, name/2, which a user's name takes only beside its name in one snapshot, as this output does. A day counter that carries a trade's data (Actual/Actual (ISMA) with a schedule, 30/360 (ISDA) with a termination date) is no convention and is refused. A currency is one of QuantLib's by its code, its name and numeric code QuantLib's, since the three are its identity: one that differs from the set's in its other fields is described as an override of its code, the set holding one record per code, and one whose name or numeric code isn't QuantLib's is refused. An instrument convention is records already: it is described as its record with every field its base chain gives, under the name, its names those of the set it was resolved in. A unit of measure of a preset's class is described as an override of the set's preset where its data differ, the set holding one record per preset, and an alias of it; QuantLib's null commodity type as no record, a field left out. api/NanoQL.Extensions.Conventions.Conven.summary: Class ConventionSet Namespace NanoQL.Extensions.Conventions Assembly NanoQL.Extensions.dll An immutable set of convention records, layered snapshot on snapshot, and the ConventionProvider that answers from them: QuantLib's shipped presets (QuantLib) or none (Empty), with a user's files on top. public sealed class ConventionSet : ConventionProvider, IEquatable<ConventionSet> Inheritance object ConventionProvider ConventionSet Implements IEquatable<ConventionSet> Inherited Members ConventionProvider.Use(ConventionProvider) ConventionProvider.Default ConventionProvider.Current object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks QuantLib is the shipped records; Default, Current and Use(ConventionProvider) are the provider's, so a set configures the system as ConventionProvider.Default = ConventionSet.QuantLib.With(...). A lookup builds a new object each time, inside the set's scope, so a preset comes out as its own class with the set's values, and an index keeps the set as its provider. A field comes from its record, then the record's base chain, then QuantLib's reference. Calendars, day counters and currencies are code kinds: a name the set doesn't define, but a coded preset has, resolves to QuantLib's preset, with no edits, even on Empty. A record named after a coded preset must be one the preset's class can take, since a coded construction can't become another kind: a calendar preset takes its own preset record or a calendar record based on itself, a day counter or currency preset a record of its own kind based on itself, and an alias between two presets only where QuantLib shares their implementation. With(ConventionSnapshot) refuses any other, and resolves every record of the new set, so a name a later layer breaks, a cycle or a value the core refuses fails when the file is loaded. Two sets are equal when they hold equal snapshots in the same order on the same base. BespokeCalendarRecord A bespoke calendar (BespokeCalendar): weekend days and holidays given as data, its name the calendar's own. CalendarPresetRecord A calendar preset (CalendarPreset): one of QuantLib's calendars by its type and market, its rules code, with QuantLib's name and the holiday edits the preset's constructor applies through the set. api/NanoQL.Extensions.Instruments.Amorti.summary: Class AmortizingBond Namespace NanoQL.Extensions.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.Extensions.dll A fixed-rate bond held at amortised cost: the effective rate of its purchase, and its carrying amount over its life, the difference between its cost and its face amount amortised by the effective interest method. public sealed class AmortizingBond : Bond Inheritance object Instrument Bond AmortizingBond Inherited Members Bond.IsExpired(EvaluationContext) Bond.SetupExpired() Bond.Validate() Bond.FetchResults(InstrumentResults) Bond.Notional(EvaluationContext, Date?) Bond.DirtyPrice(double, DayCounter, Compounding, Frequency, EvaluationContext, Date?) Bond.Yield(BondPrice, DayCounter, Compounding, Frequency, EvaluationContext, Date?, double, int, double) Bond.AccruedAmount(EvaluationContext, Date?) Bond.NextCouponRate(EvaluationContext, Date?) Bond.PreviousCouponRate(EvaluationContext, Date?) Bond.NextCashFlowDate(EvaluationContext, Date?) Bond.PreviousCashFlowDate(EvaluationContext, Date?) Bond.SettlementDays Bond.Calendar Bond.Notionals Bond.Cashflows Bond.Redemptions Bond.IssueDate object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The effective rate is solved on the trade date, at initial recognition, as IFRS 9 and ASC 310-20's interest method require: the rate, simple within each coupon period and compounded at each coupon date, at which the bond's remaining coupons and redemption are worth the price paid, the cost plus the accrued interest purchased (Yield(ImmutableArray<CashFlow>, double, DayCounter, Compounding, Frequency, EvaluationContext, bool?, Date?, Date?, double, int, double), settled on the trade date). Each coupon date after the trade books an amortisation (Amortizations): the interest at the effective rate on the carrying amount, over the yield's own time, less the coupon (less the accrued interest purchased, in the first period), rounded to the cent, positive when the carrying amount accretes toward a face above it; the last closes the carrying amount to the face amount. AmortizationValue(Date) is the carrying amount, without accrued interest, at any date of the bond's life: the cost on the trade date, continuous, and the face amount at maturity. Ported from QLNet. Its departures from QLNet: the rate is solved at the trade date with the accrued interest purchased, where QLNet solves at the coupon date on or before the trade (or at its global evaluation date, with no coupon before it) and its carrying amount jumps at the first coupon date; a partial period accrues on the carrying amount at its start, where QLNet's accrues on the cost; the coupon is the leg's own, day-counted, where QLNet's amortisation pays the face amount times the rate over the frequency; an amortisation's sign is its interest less its coupon, where QLNet's is the bond's being at a premium; the last amortisation closes to the face amount, where QLNet's cents leave it off; a given yield of 0 is taken, where QLNet solves instead; the bond's calendar is the one given, where QLNet's base uses TARGET; and the bond's cash flows are its coupons and redemption, where QLNet's hold the accounting entries and coupons whose amounts it overrides. api/NanoQL.Extensions.Instruments.PSACur.summary: Class PSACurve Namespace NanoQL.Extensions.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.Extensions.dll The Public Securities Association's prepayment benchmark at a multiple of its speed: a CPR rising by 0.2% a month from 0.2% in the first month to 6% in the thirtieth, and 6% from then on, times the multiplier. public sealed class PSACurve : IPrepayModel Inheritance object PSACurve Implements IPrepayModel Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The rates follow SIFMA's standard formula (Uniform Practices, Chapter SF, SF-6: CPR = min{100, PSA/100 · 0.2 · max{1, min{MONTH, 30}}}), MONTH "the accrual period during which the age of the mortgage loans increases from MONTH – 1 to MONTH": the whole calendar months from the curve's start, plus one, so that a date's MONTH is k + 1 from the start's k-month anniversary until the next. Three departures from QLNet follow it. QLNet counts the month as the 30/360 Bond Basis days from the start over 30, plus one, which from a start on the 29th to the 31st repeats a month at February's anniversary and skips the next, and counts a 31st a month ahead from a start on the 1st; the CPR is capped at 100%, where QLNet's passes it above 1,666⅔% PSA and its SMM is NaN; and every month before the first counts as the first ("MONTH equals 1 for all prior months"), where QLNet's falls to 0 and below. Elsewhere the rates are QLNet's, bit for bit. The SMM is the CPR's monthly equivalent, 1 − (1 − CPR)^(1/12) (SF-5). It has tenor one week, is fixed weekly on Wednesdays and is applied with a one-day fixing gap from Thursdays on for one week. Initializes a new instance of the BMAIndex class. public BMAIndex(YieldTermStructure? h = null) Parameters h YieldTermStructure The forwarding curve, or null for none. Returns Schedule The schedule. Exceptions ArgumentException A date is default(Date), or the schedule can't be built. Returns double The forecast. Exceptions ArgumentNullException context is null. ArgumentException fixingDate is default(Date). NanoQLException The index has no forwarding curve, or the curve can't give the rate. IsValidFixingDate(Date) Whether a date is a valid fixing date: a Wednesday that is a business day, or the first business day after a run of holidays starting on a Wednesday. public override bool IsValidFixingDate(Date fixingDate) Parameters fixingDate Date The date. Returns bool true when it is. Exceptions ArgumentException fixingDate is default(Date). MaturityDate(Date) The maturity date of a value date: the business day after the Wednesday following the value date's fixing date. public override Date MaturityDate(Date valueDate) Parameters valueDate Date The value date. api/NanoQL.Indexes.CPI.html.summary: Class CPI Namespace NanoQL.Indexes Assembly NanoQL.dll Observations of inflation indexes with a lag, flat or interpolated: QuantLib's CPI struct, with its interpolation type as CPIInterpolationType. public static class CPI Inheritance object CPI Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks An inflation coupon observes its index with a lag, interpolating between fixings or not; QuantLib's indexes no longer interpolate, the coupons do, through these functions. Methods LaggedFixing(ZeroInflationIndex, Date, Period, CPIInterpolationType, EvaluationContext) An inflation index's fixing observed with a lag, flat or interpolated. public static double LaggedFixing(ZeroInflationIndex index, Date date, Period observationLag, CPIInterpolationType interpolationType, EvaluationContext context) Parameters index ZeroInflationIndex The index. date Date The date without lag, usually the payment date of an inflation coupon. observationLag Period The lag subtracted from the date: with a date in May and a three-month lag, the fixing of February is observed (and of March, when interpolating). interpolationType CPIInterpolationType The interpolation type. context EvaluationContext The evaluation context. Returns double The fixing of the lagged date's period; or, interpolated, the line between it and the next period's fixing, at the date's position in its own period. Exceptions ArgumentNullException index or context is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException interpolationType isn't a member of its type. NanoQLException A fixing it reads is missing or can't be forecast. LaggedYoYRate(YoYInflationIndex, Date, Period, CPIInterpolationType, EvaluationContext) A year-on-year inflation index's rate observed with a lag, flat or interpolated. public static double LaggedYoYRate(YoYInflationIndex index, Date date, Period observationLag, CPIInterpolationType interpolationType, EvaluationContext context) Parameters index YoYInflationIndex The index. date Date The date without lag, usually the payment date of an inflation coupon. observationLag Period The lag subtracted from the date. interpolationType CPIInterpolationType The interpolation type. context EvaluationContext The evaluation context. Returns double The rate of the lagged date's period; or, interpolated, the line between it and the next period's. For a ratio index whose fixings are past, the interpolated underlying fixing over the one a year earlier, less one: the convention is to interpolate the underlying first, which differs from interpolating the ratios, and it needs past fixings, since forecasts go through the year-on-year curve. Remarks QuantLib chooses between the two interpolated forms by whether the unlagged date needs a forecast, though the fixings it reads are those of the lagged date's period and the next one, so a fixing it never reads can change the rate it returns; and where the lag is shorter than the index's period, it can take the ratio form on a fixing not yet published and forecast the underlying index, which its own comment rules out. Here the choice reads the latest fixing the ratio form uses: the next period's first day, or the lagged period's own when the date starts its period. The first case gets QuantLib's value with that fixing added, the second the ratios forecast through the year-on-year curve: a documented divergence that changes no QuantLib case. Exceptions ArgumentNullException index or context is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException interpolationType isn't a member of its type. NanoQLException A fixing it reads is missing or can't be forecast.

api/NanoQL.Indexes.EquityIndex.html.summary: Class EquityIndex Namespace NanoQL.Indexes Assembly NanoQL.dll Base class for equity indexes. public class EquityIndex : FinancialIndex Inheritance object FinancialIndex EquityIndex Inherited Members FinancialIndex.HasHistoricalFixing(Date, EvaluationContext) FinancialIndex.PastFixing(Date, EvaluationContext) FinancialIndex.TimeSeries(EvaluationContext) FinancialIndex.FixingDates(Date) FinancialIndex.AllowsNativeFixings object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The equity index object allows to retrieve past fixings, as well as project future fixings using either both the risk free interest rate term structure and the dividend term structure, or just the interest rate term structure in which case one can provide a term structure of equity forwards implied from, e.g. option prices. In case of the first method, the forward is calculated as I(t, T) = I(t, t) P_D(t, T) / P_R(t, T), where I(t, t) is today's value of the index, P_D(t, T) is a discount factor of the dividend curve at future time T, and P_R(t, T) is a discount factor of the risk free curve at future time T. In case of the latter method, the forward is calculated as I(t, T) = I(t, t) / P_F(t, T), where P_F(t, T) is a discount factor of the equity forward term structure. To forecast future fixings, the user can provide the current index spot. If the spot is null, today's fixing will be used instead. Each discount factor is read from the evaluation date t: P(t, T) is the curve's discount at T over its discount at t, nothing accruing before the curve's own reference date. QuantLib reads each curve's discount at T from its own reference date (equityindex.cpp:84-88), which is the formula's only where the curve is dated on or after the evaluation date; on such a curve the forecast is QuantLib's bit for bit, and on a curve dated before it a documented divergence. api/NanoQL.Indexes.IndexFixings.html.title: Class IndexFixings | nanoql
api/NanoQL.Indexes.IndexFixings.html.summary: Class IndexFixings Namespace NanoQL.Indexes Assembly NanoQL.dll The stored fixings of indexes, by index name: QuantLib's IndexManager, as an immutable value that Fixings holds. public sealed class IndexFixings : IEquatable<IndexFixings> Inheritance object IndexFixings Implements IEquatable<IndexFixings> Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks Every change returns a new store, as .NET's immutable collections do. The writers take the index, whose name keys its history and whose IsValidFixingDate(Date) and AllowsNativeFixings QuantLib's checks read; an index reads its fixings through PastFixing(Date, EvaluationContext), HasHistoricalFixing(Date, EvaluationContext) and TimeSeries(EvaluationContext). Names compare as QuantLib's do: ASCII letters upper-cased, every other character as it is, so "Euribor6M" and "EURIBOR6M" share a history. The first spelling stored is the one Histories() gives, in the order of that comparison. Two stores are equal when they hold the same names, by that comparison, each with an equal history; which spelling was kept doesn't count. The hash combines one hash per history, each computed when its series was built. Three divergences from QuantLib: a refused batch changes nothing, where QuantLib stores its valid fixings, and a null entry at the refused date, before it throws; reading never writes, where QuantLib's reads insert null entries and empty histories; and a fixing equal to QuantLib's null sentinel Null<Real>() (3.4028234663852886e38) is stored as a value, where QuantLib reads it as no fixing. Properties Empty Gets the store with no fixings, QuantLib's state after clearHistories(). public static IndexFixings Empty { get; } Property Value IndexFixings Methods AddFixing(FinancialIndex, Date, double, bool) A store with one more fixing, written on every date the index gives for it. public IndexFixings AddFixing(FinancialIndex index, Date fixingDate, double fixing, bool forceOverwrite = false) Parameters index FinancialIndex The index the fixing is for. fixingDate Date The actual calendar date of the fixing, with no settlement days applied. fixing double The fixing. forceOverwrite bool Whether a fixing already stored on those dates is replaced. Returns IndexFixings The new store; this one is unchanged. Remarks The fixing is written on each date of the index's FixingDates(Date): the date alone, or for an inflation index every day of the date's inflation period, as QuantLib's InflationIndex::addFixing writes it. The dates are written together, through the same checks as AddFixings(FinancialIndex, IEnumerable<Date>, IEnumerable<double>, bool), all or nothing. Exceptions ArgumentException A date isn't a valid fixing date, or a different fixing is stored on one and forceOverwrite is false. NanoQLException The index allows no native fixings. AddFixings(FinancialIndex, TimeSeries<double>, bool) A store with more fixings, taken from a series. public IndexFixings AddFixings(FinancialIndex index, TimeSeries<double> fixings, bool forceOverwrite = false) Parameters index FinancialIndex The index the fixings are for. fixings TimeSeries<double> The fixings, on the actual calendar dates of the fixings. forceOverwrite bool Whether fixings already stored on those dates are replaced. Returns IndexFixings The new store; this one is unchanged. Exceptions ArgumentException A date isn't a valid fixing date, or a different fixing is stored on it and forceOverwrite is false. Nothing is stored then. NanoQLException The index allows no native fixings. api/NanoQL.Indexes.InflationIndex.html.title: Class InflationIndex | nanoql
api/NanoQL.Indexes.InflationIndex.html.summary: Class InflationIndex Namespace NanoQL.Indexes Assembly NanoQL.dll The base class of inflation indexes, whose fixings cover a period: a month, a quarter, a year. public abstract class InflationIndex : FinancialIndex Inheritance object FinancialIndex InflationIndex Derived YoYInflationIndex ZeroInflationIndex Inherited Members FinancialIndex.HasHistoricalFixing(Date, EvaluationContext) FinancialIndex.TimeSeries(EvaluationContext) FinancialIndex.AllowsNativeFixings object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A fixing stored through AddFixing(FinancialIndex, Date, double, bool) is written on every day of its date's inflation period, as QuantLib's addFixing writes it, through FixingDates(Date); the reads key on the period's first day. The store's bulk writers store the dates they are given, as QuantLib's non-virtual addFixings does. Inflation indexes aren't associated with a day but with a period, so they have no fixing calendar: QuantLib's NullCalendar stands in, and every date is a valid fixing date. An extension point. O'Kane, "Introduction to Asset Swaps", Lehman Brothers European Fixed Income Research, January 2000. public sealed class AssetSwap : Swap Inheritance object Instrument Swap AssetSwap Inherited Members Swap.IsExpired(EvaluationContext) Swap.Validate() Swap.StartDate() Swap.MaturityDate() Swap.Leg(int) Swap.Payer(int) Swap.NumberOfLegs Swap.Legs object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The bond's clean price is its (forward) price at the floating schedule's start, the upfront date. On an overnight index the floating schedule must be given, and the floating coupons are overnight-indexed. QuantLib warns that the fair prices are wrong with indexed coupons. A non-par repayment is per 100 of the bond's notional at the upfront date, as the fair repayment reads it, and paid as that share of the notional, where QuantLib's pays the number given as an amount (assetswap.cpp:125-134); with none given the swap repays the bond's redemption, and its repayment is that redemption per 100 of notional, where QuantLib's stores 100 whatever the redemption (:130). On a bond of 100 redeemed at 100 the two agree. The swap is priced by DiscountingSwapEngine's asset swap overload, its fair values derived from the swap's results; QuantLib's AssetSwap::arguments, which no QuantLib engine reads, aren't ported. api/NanoQL.Instruments.Bond.html.summary: Class Bond Namespace NanoQL.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.dll The base bond class: a leg of cash flows, its redemptions among them, with a settlement rule. public class Bond : Instrument Inheritance object Instrument Bond Derived CallableBond CatBond AmortizingBond MBSFixedRateBond AmortizingCmsRateBond AmortizingFixedRateBond AmortizingFloatingRateBond CPIBond CmsRateBond ConvertibleBond FixedRateBond FloatingRateBond ZeroCouponBond Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Most members assume that the cash flows are sorted by date, the redemptions after any cash flow on the same date; with a single redemption, it is the last cash flow. Prices are per 100 of the notional at the settlement date, as QuantLib's are: for a bond whose notional isn't 100, the cash price is the quote times the notional over 100, and the yield and Z-spread functions take their prices per 100 too. Unsealed, an extension point, as QuantLib's concrete base: the fixed-rate, floating-rate, zero-coupon and amortizing bonds derive from it, and later bonds will. Its public constructors are QuantLib's two, which sort the cash flows they are given (stably: equal-dated cash flows keep their order) and check the issue date against the first payment. The construction contract is QuantLib's protected interface: a derived constructor calls the protected Bond(int, Calendar?, Date?), which builds no leg, then writes the protected cashflows, maturityDate and, for a bond with its own redemptions, redemptions, and calls the helpers that fill the notional schedule and the redemptions: AddRedemptionsToCashflows(IEnumerable<double>?), SetSingleRedemption(double, double, Date), SetSingleRedemption(double, CashFlow) or CalculateNotionalsFromCashflows(). That path keeps QuantLib's omissions: no issue-date check, and no sort of a leg already sorted. The protected state and the helpers are written while the bond is built, by a derived constructor, or on a fresh copy (WithCashflows(ImmutableArray<CashFlow>)), and never after: a convention the base can't enforce, since a derived class's every member can reach them, on which the bond's immutability rests. The members that read the evaluation date, directly or through the settlement date or a coupon's fixing, take the context, QuantLib's default date becoming null: the settlement date, the notional, tradability, the accrued amount, the coupon rates, the cash-flow dates, and the prices and yields from a yield. The members that read QuantLib's attached engine (cleanPrice(), dirtyPrice(), settlementValue() and the theoretical yield) take that engine's results instead, with the context: they recompute the settlement date and the accrued amount from it, as QuantLib's recompute them from its one evaluation date, so the results and the context must be the same call's. Results read under another context mix two settlement dates, which nothing here can detect. api/NanoQL.Instruments.BondForward.html.summary: Class BondForward Namespace NanoQL.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.dll A forward contract on a bond: the bond's dirty price at spot, less its coupons paid before delivery, carried to the delivery date; a repo, for instance, at its repurchase price. public sealed class BondForward : Forward Inheritance object Instrument Forward BondForward Inherited Members Forward.SettlementDate(EvaluationContext) Forward.IsExpired(EvaluationContext) Forward.ImpliedYield(double, double, Date, Compounding, DayCounter, EvaluationContext) Forward.SetupExpired() Forward.FetchResults(InstrumentResults) Forward.DayCounter Forward.Calendar Forward.BusinessDayConvention Forward.SettlementDays Forward.Payoff Forward.ValueDate Forward.MaturityDate Forward.DiscountCurve Forward.IncomeDiscountCurve Instrument.Validate() object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks QuantLib's spotValue() is the bond's dirty price on the bond's own engine; here Calculate(EvaluationContext, Func<Bond, EvaluationContext, BondResults>) takes the bond's engine, and CleanForwardPrice(ForwardResults, EvaluationContext) and ForwardPrice(ForwardResults) read its results. The income, the coupons paid after the settlement date and up to the delivery date discounted on the income curve, is per 100 of the bond's notional at its settlement date, as the dirty price is, where QuantLib's sums the coupons' amounts on the bond's face (bondforward.cpp:59-83), so on a face other than 100 delivering after a coupon its forward value mixes the two. The forward value and the prices are then per 100. The spot value, the bond's dirty price, is a value at the bond's settlement date: it is carried back to the discount curve's reference date before the income, discounted to that date, is netted and the rest carried to delivery, where QuantLib's grows the settlement-date price from the reference date (bondforward.cpp:86-87, forward.cpp:61-65), so for a bond that doesn't settle on the curve's reference date its forward is high by 1/P(ref, settlement). On a bond settling on the reference date the two agree. The clean forward price takes the accrued amount at delivery on the forward's basis, per 100 of the notional at settlement, where QuantLib's subtracts it per 100 of the notional at delivery (bondforward.cpp:49-51), another basis once the bond amortizes between the two. api/NanoQL.Instruments.CPISwap.html.summary: Class CPISwap Namespace NanoQL.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.dll A zero-inflation-indexed swap: a CPI leg, fixed rates inflated by a zero-inflation index with an inflated notional at the end, against a floating leg paying an Ibor rate plus a spread, with a notional flow where it is needed. public sealed class CPISwap : Swap Inheritance object Instrument Swap CPISwap Inherited Members Swap.IsExpired(EvaluationContext) Swap.Validate() Swap.StartDate() Swap.MaturityDate() Swap.Leg(int) Swap.Payer(int) Swap.NumberOfLegs Swap.Legs object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The type, payer or receiver, refers to the floating leg. The CPI leg is the first leg, CPILeg's; the floating leg is the second, Ibor coupons on the floating schedule when it has more than one date, then a notional flow when the schedule has a single date, when the inflation nominal isn't subtracted, or when it differs from the nominal: the nominal less the inflation nominal where it is subtracted, else the nominal, paid with the last coupon or on the single date. Accrual adjustments and calendars are in the schedules. The constructor builds the Ibor leg with the index's default pricer, which reads the context's at-par switch, so it takes the context; a null floating index is accepted where the schedule has a single date, since QuantLib never reads it then. A type that isn't a member of SwapType is refused, where QuantLib takes it as a receiver. An engine's results are a CPISwapResults: its fair rate is the swap engine's (see its remarks), and its fair spread is derived from the floating leg's BPS. QuantLib's own arguments, results and engine classes aren't ported. api/NanoQL.Instruments.CPISwapResults.ht.summary: Class CPISwapResults Namespace NanoQL.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.dll The results an engine returns for a CPISwap: the swap's, with the fair fixed rate of the CPI leg and the fair spread over the floating leg. public sealed record CPISwapResults : SwapResults, IEquatable<InstrumentResults>, IEquatable<SwapResults>, IEquatable<CPISwapResults> Inheritance object InstrumentResults SwapResults CPISwapResults Implements IEquatable<InstrumentResults> IEquatable<SwapResults> IEquatable<CPISwapResults> Inherited Members SwapResults.Equals(InstrumentResults) SwapResults.LegNPV SwapResults.LegBPS SwapResults.StartDiscounts SwapResults.EndDiscounts SwapResults.NpvDateDiscount InstrumentResults.Result<T>(string) InstrumentResults.NPV InstrumentResults.ErrorEstimate InstrumentResults.ValuationDate InstrumentResults.AdditionalResults object.GetType() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks QuantLib's swap stores these from its own results class, or derives them from the swap's results; here they are members of the results FetchResults(InstrumentResults) returns. The CPI leg is the first leg and the floating leg the second. The fair rate is the engine's: DiscountingSwapEngine's CPISwap overload gives it, where QuantLib derives it from the CPI leg's BPS, which leaves out the index ratio that a CPI coupon's sensitivity to its rate carries, so the swap repriced at QuantLib's fair rate isn't worth zero (a documented divergence). The fair spread is derived from the floating leg's BPS, as QuantLib derives it. A result QuantLib refuses to read ("result not available") is null: the fair rate when the engine gives none or the CPI leg has no live coupon, the fair spread when the floating leg's BPS is zero or unknown, both for an expired swap, and a leg's NPV when it is unknown. Equality compares the per-leg arrays element by element, and the fair rate and spread by value. api/NanoQL.Instruments.CompositeInstrume.summary: Class CompositeInstrument Namespace NanoQL.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.dll An aggregate of other instruments: its value is the sum of its components' values, each times its multiplier, QuantLib's CompositeInstrument. public sealed class CompositeInstrument : Instrument Inheritance object Instrument CompositeInstrument Inherited Members Instrument.SetupExpired() Instrument.Validate() Instrument.FetchResults(InstrumentResults) object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable: Add(Instrument, Func<EvaluationContext, InstrumentResults>, double) and Subtract(Instrument, Func<EvaluationContext, InstrumentResults>, double) return a new composite with the component added, where QuantLib's change the composite. Each component carries the engine that prices it, a delegate from the evaluation context, as nanoql's instruments carry none; QuantLib's composite reads the engines its components carry. It is priced without an engine: Calculate(EvaluationContext) runs QuantLib's steps, its value the components' values summed in the order they were added, each from its engine's results under the context, an expired component's 0 without its engine, as QuantLib's instrument gives it. It has expired when every component has, an empty composite included, as QuantLib's. Its error estimate is null, as QuantLib's is on a composite never expired. QuantLib's deepUpdate has no counterpart. api/NanoQL.Instruments.CreditDefaultSwap.summary: Class CreditDefaultSwap Namespace NanoQL.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.dll A credit default swap: a premium leg of running-spread coupons against protection on a reference entity's default, with an optional upfront and an accrual rebate. public sealed class CreditDefaultSwap : Instrument Inheritance object Instrument CreditDefaultSwap Inherited Members Instrument.FetchResults(InstrumentResults) object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The instrument assumes that the issuer hasn't defaulted by the evaluation date. With IncludeReferenceDateEvents set, payments at the swap's settlement date may count in its NPV and its fair spread. The implied quantities price with the mid-point engine by default, which isn't ISDA conformant. QuantLib's constructors read no evaluation date: the trade date, when not given, is deduced from the protection start and the schedule's rule, and the cash settlement date from the trade date. An empty schedule is refused before its first date is read, where QuantLib, given no protection start, reads it first for one, an undefined read (a documented divergence). The accrual rebate reads its first live coupon's amount or accrued amount through the coupon's context-free forms. The engines are static (MidPointCdsEngine, IsdaCdsEngine), and the results are a CreditDefaultSwapResults. An expired swap's results are all 0, its accrual rebate's NPV included, where QuantLib leaves that one unset and reads an uninitialized value, a documented divergence. Equality is by reference. ImpliedHazardRate(double, YieldTermStructure, DayCounter, EvaluationContext, double, double, CreditDefaultSwapPricingModel) and ConventionalSpread(double, YieldTermStructure, DayCounter, EvaluationContext, CreditDefaultSwapPricingModel) refuse an expired swap ("instrument expired"), where QuantLib returns its solver's guess or a sentinel; the conventional spread also refuses where the engine leaves the fair spread null, with QuantLib's "fair spread not available". Under the ISDA model their flat curve is dated on the evaluation date, which the ISDA engine requires, where QuantLib's rolls a weekend to Monday and its engine then refuses it: documented divergences. api/NanoQL.Instruments.DiscreteAveraging.summary: Class DiscreteAveragingAsianOption Namespace NanoQL.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.dll A discrete-averaging Asian option: its payoff reads the arithmetic or geometric average of the underlying's fixings on given dates. public sealed class DiscreteAveragingAsianOption : OneAssetOption Inheritance object Instrument Option OneAssetOption DiscreteAveragingAsianOption Inherited Members OneAssetOption.IsExpired(EvaluationContext) OneAssetOption.SetupExpired() OneAssetOption.FetchResults(InstrumentResults) Option.Validate() Option.Payoff Option.Exercise object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable. Two constructors, as in QuantLib: one taking the running sum or product of the past fixings and their number beside the future fixing dates; one taking every fixing date with the past fixings' values, which an engine splits by the evaluation context's date, the dates before it past (QuantLib's setupArguments on its global evaluation date). Both sort their fixing dates, a stable sort, where QuantLib's second constructor keeps the caller's order and its engines then read unsorted dates (Divergences/AsianUnsortedDatesTests.cs); the past values are taken by count, as QuantLib takes them. A geometric option's past fixings are carried as QuantLib's running product and, beside it, their log-sum, which the geometric engines read where the product leaves double's range: 120 past fixings at 1,000 multiply to ∞, where QuantLib's analytic engine prices ∞ (Divergences/GeometricAsianProductRangeTests.cs). A derived swap passes QuantLib's arguments and the builder of its floating leg to the protected constructor, which checks its terms and builds the fixed leg first and then calls the builder, in QuantLib's order: QuantLib's base constructor runs before the derived constructor's body builds the floating leg. api/NanoQL.Instruments.ForwardRateAgreem.title: Class ForwardRateAgreement | nanoql
api/NanoQL.Instruments.ForwardRateAgreem.summary: Class ForwardRateAgreement Namespace NanoQL.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.dll A forward rate agreement (FRA). public sealed class ForwardRateAgreement : Instrument Inheritance object Instrument ForwardRateAgreement Inherited Members Instrument.Validate() object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Unlike the forward contract conventions on carryable financial assets (stocks, bonds, commodities), the value date for a FRA is taken to be the day when the forward loan or deposit begins and when full settlement takes place (based on the NPV of the contract on that date). The maturity date is the date when the forward loan or deposit ends. In fact, the FRA settles and expires on the value date, not on the (later) maturity date. It follows that the time from the value date to the maturity date is the tenor or term of the underlying loan or deposit. Choose Long for an "FRA purchase" (future long loan, short deposit, the borrower), and Short for an "FRA sale" (future short loan, long deposit, the lender). Immutable. QuantLib's FRA computes in the instrument, with no engine: Calculate(EvaluationContext) does, running Instrument::calculate's steps and returning the NPV, the payoff and the forward rate (ForwardRateAgreementResults). Nothing is cached: each call computes again. QuantLib's to-do list: preconditions and tests, and the BBA (British), AFB (French, assumed here) and ABA (Australian) banker conventions told apart in the calculations. QuantLib warns that the class still needs to be rigorously tested. Constructors ForwardRateAgreement(IborIndex, Date, PositionType, double, double, YieldTermStructure?) Initializes a new instance of the ForwardRateAgreement class whose forward rate the index forecasts: its fixing for the value date, its maturity the index's. This corresponds to useIndexedCoupon = true in FraRateHelper. public ForwardRateAgreement(IborIndex index, Date valueDate, PositionType position, double strikeForwardRate, double notionalAmount, YieldTermStructure? discountCurve = null) Parameters index IborIndex The index, which holds the forecasting curve. valueDate Date The date the underlying loan or deposit starts accruing and the FRA settles. position PositionType Long for an FRA purchase, short for an FRA sale. strikeForwardRate double The contract rate, simple on the index's day counter. notionalAmount double The notional amount. discountCurve YieldTermStructure The curve discounting the payoff; the index's forecasting curve when null, QuantLib's empty handle. Exceptions ArgumentNullException index is null. ArgumentException The notional isn't positive, or the value date isn't before the maturity date. ArgumentOutOfRangeException position isn't a member of its enum. ForwardRateAgreement(IborIndex, Date, Date, PositionType, double, double, YieldTermStructure?) Initializes a new instance of the ForwardRateAgreement class whose forward rate is the par approximation: the simple rate from the value date to the maturity date on the index's forecasting curve. This corresponds to useIndexedCoupon = false in FraRateHelper. public ForwardRateAgreement(IborIndex index, Date valueDate, Date maturityDate, PositionType position, double strikeForwardRate, double notionalAmount, YieldTermStructure? discountCurve = null) Parameters index IborIndex The index, which holds the forecasting curve. valueDate Date The date the underlying loan or deposit starts accruing and the FRA settles. maturityDate Date The date the underlying loan or deposit ends, adjusted on the index's fixing calendar by its convention. position PositionType Long for an FRA purchase, short for an FRA sale. strikeForwardRate double The contract rate, simple on the index's day counter. notionalAmount double The notional amount. discountCurve YieldTermStructure The curve discounting the payoff; the index's forecasting curve when null, QuantLib's empty handle. Exceptions ArgumentNullException index is null. ArgumentException The notional isn't positive, or the value date isn't before the adjusted maturity date. ArgumentOutOfRangeException position isn't a member of its enum. ToCapFloor(EvaluationContext) builds the instrument, in place of QuantLib's conversion operators. The leg is the floating leg of the MakeVanillaSwap the builder holds, built at 0% with a yearly Actual/365 (Fixed) fixed leg, which only spares that builder its currency's default fixed tenor; the first caplet is excluded unless a forward start or the effective date's flag keeps it, and an optionlet keeps the last coupon alone. With no strike, the instrument is struck at the money: at the leg's at-the-money rate on a discount curve, at the curve's reference date and without the flows paid on it. QuantLib reads that curve out of the Black or Bachelier engine given to withPricingEngine; an engine here is a function, which hides its curve, so the builder takes the curve itself through WithDiscountingTermStructure(YieldTermStructure?), which computes the strike and is never stored. WithPricingEngine(Func<CapFloor, EvaluationContext, InstrumentResults>?) is kept and changes nothing: the instrument holds no engine. The strike comes before the instrument is built, so a Collar is refused by the instrument's constructor after the at-the-money rate, as QuantLib refuses it. A builder has no value equality. An option the builder isn't given that QuantLib's builder fixes takes the builder's provider's default (Defaults(ConventionProvider)), read when the instrument is built: QuantLib's values with nothing configured. A builder has no value equality. An option the builder isn't given that QuantLib's builder fixes takes the builder's provider's default (Defaults(ConventionProvider)), read when the swaption is built: QuantLib's values with nothing configured. api/NanoQL.Instruments.MakeYoYInflationC.summary: Class MakeYoYInflationCapFloor Namespace NanoQL.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.dll A builder of standard year-on-year inflation caps and floors. public sealed record MakeYoYInflationCapFloor : IEquatable<MakeYoYInflationCapFloor> Inheritance object MakeYoYInflationCapFloor Implements IEquatable<MakeYoYInflationCapFloor> Inherited Members object.GetType() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks An immutable builder: each method returns a modified copy, so a builder kept and reused never changes under its holder. ToYoYInflationCapFloor(EvaluationContext) builds the instrument, in place of QuantLib's conversion operators. The leg is YoYInflationLeg's on an annual schedule over the given number of years, from the effective date or, without one, from the spot date (the evaluation date advanced by the fixing days) plus the forward start; the fixing days move the start only. An optionlet keeps the last coupon alone. Its defaults are QuantLib's: a nominal of 1,000,000, 30/360 (Bond Basis), ModifiedFollowing, no fixing days. With no strike, the instrument is struck at the money: at the leg's at-the-money rate on the nominal curve given to WithAtmStrike(YieldTermStructure?), at its reference date and without the flows paid on it; with neither, the conversion refuses with QuantLib's empty-handle text. QuantLib's withFirstCapletExcluded is declared and never defined, so it isn't ported. WithPricingEngine(Func<YoYInflationCapFloor, EvaluationContext, InstrumentResults>?) is kept and changes nothing: the instrument holds no engine. A Collar is refused by the instrument's constructor after the strike, as QuantLib refuses it. A builder has no value equality. An option the builder isn't given that QuantLib's builder fixes takes the builder's provider's default (Defaults(ConventionProvider)), read when the instrument is built: QuantLib's values with nothing configured. api/NanoQL.Instruments.NonstandardSwap.h.summary: Class NonstandardSwap Namespace NanoQL.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.dll A vanilla swap, but possibly with period-dependent nominals, fixed rates, gearings and spreads. public sealed class NonstandardSwap : Swap Inheritance object Instrument Swap NonstandardSwap Inherited Members Swap.IsExpired(EvaluationContext) Swap.SetupExpired() Swap.Validate() Swap.FetchResults(InstrumentResults) Swap.StartDate() Swap.MaturityDate() Swap.Leg(int) Swap.Payer(int) Swap.NumberOfLegs Swap.Legs object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The constructors build the legs, as QuantLib's do: a fixed leg, and an Ibor leg with the index's default pricer, which reads the context's at-par switch, so they take the context; or, for an overnight index, a compounded overnight leg. A zero gearing becomes QuantLib's machine epsilon, so that the floating leg is built of floating coupons. With the capital exchanges, a redemption follows each coupon whose nominal changes after it, and the last, the nominals and fixed rates repeated (the rate as 0) beside each, as QuantLib's inspectors give them. The fixed leg is paid by a payer swap. Converted from a fixed-versus-floating swap, it keeps an overnight-indexed swap's observation conventions, as QuantLib's does, and its rounding precision, which QuantLib's conversion drops, so a rounded swap's coupons would differ from the source's: the converted swap is worth the source's, QuantLib's own identity (testNonstandardSwapConversionPreservesObservationConventions). api/NanoQL.Instruments.ZeroCouponInflati.summary: Class ZeroCouponInflationSwap Namespace NanoQL.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.dll A zero-coupon inflation-indexed swap, quoted as a fixed rate K: at maturity it exchanges the notional's growth at K, N[(1 + K)^T - 1], against its inflation growth, N[I(T)/I(0) - 1], where T is the time from the start to the maturity. public sealed class ZeroCouponInflationSwap : Swap Inheritance object Instrument Swap ZeroCouponInflationSwap Inherited Members Swap.IsExpired(EvaluationContext) Swap.SetupExpired() Swap.Validate() Swap.FetchResults(InstrumentResults) Swap.Leg(int) Swap.Payer(int) Swap.NumberOfLegs Swap.Legs object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The type, payer or receiver, refers to the inflation leg. The fixed leg is the first leg, one simple cash flow; the inflation leg is the second, one ZeroInflationCashFlow paying the growth only. Inflation is available on every day, holidays and weekends included, so the observation dates are the start and the maturity less the lag, unadjusted. The standard DiscountingSwapEngine prices it; QuantLib's own arguments and engine classes aren't ported, since no engine uses them. The constructor reads no evaluation date and forecasts nothing. It refuses a type that isn't a member of SwapType on entry, where QuantLib refuses it after building the legs. The inflation leg pays on the inflation calendar and convention, the fixed leg's when they aren't given. QuantLib's default convention is BusinessDayConvention(), Following, which it replaces with the fixed leg's, so an inflation leg asked to pay Following pays on the fixed convention; here a null convention takes the fixed leg's and an explicit one is kept, a documented divergence. AdjustObservationDates is stored and exposed, as QuantLib's is, and read by nothing. The results-dependent members take the engine's SwapResults. QuantLib's fairRate is the rate that pays the inflation growth, growth^(1/T) - 1, which zeroes the swap only when both legs pay on the same day; where they pay on different days, FairRate(EvaluationContext, SwapResults?) scales the growth's excess by the ratio of the legs' end discounts from the results, so the swap rebuilt at it is worth zero, a documented divergence. api/NanoQL.Instruments.ZeroCouponSwap.ht.summary: Class ZeroCouponSwap Namespace NanoQL.Instruments Assembly NanoQL.dll A zero-coupon interest-rate swap: at maturity a fixed amount N[(1 + R)^α(T₀, T_K) − 1], or a given one, is swapped for the floating amount N[∏(1 + α(T_k, T_{k+1}) L(T_k, T_{k+1})) − 1], the index's fixings compounded over its own periods. public sealed class ZeroCouponSwap : Swap Inheritance object Instrument Swap ZeroCouponSwap Inherited Members Swap.IsExpired(EvaluationContext) Swap.Validate() Swap.Leg(int) Swap.Payer(int) Swap.NumberOfLegs Swap.Legs object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The legs carry one cash flow each, on unadjusted dates; only the payment date is adjusted, the payment delay's business days after maturity. The fixed leg is the first, the floating leg the second. An engine's results are a ZeroCouponSwapResults, whose fair payment DiscountingSwapEngine's overload gives at the fixed flow's payment date, where QuantLib's reads the discount at the fixed leg's maturity date, the accrual end for the fixed-rate constructor's coupon, so with a payment delay its fair payment fed back leaves a non-zero NPV. The volatility is the model's constant one, read at the strike e^x; the inverse reads it at e^p, the probability as QuantLib passes it, which a constant volatility doesn't see. The dividend curve and the volatility are read at the instant a time denotes, each on its own clock, the variance accrued from the risk-free curve's reference date, where QuantLib reads them at the risk-free curve's time (the mismatched-dates class); structures that share the curve's times keep QuantLib's bits. api/NanoQL.Methods.CEVRNDCalculator.html.summary: Class CEVRNDCalculator Namespace NanoQL.Methods Assembly NanoQL.dll The risk-neutral density of the constant elasticity of variance (CEV) process df = α·f^β·dW with an absorbing boundary at f = 0, by the non-central chi-squared distribution (D. R. Brecher and A. E. Lindsay, "Results on the CEV Process, Past and Present"), with the probability mass absorbed at zero. public sealed class CEVRNDCalculator : RiskNeutralDensityCalculator Inheritance object RiskNeutralDensityCalculator CEVRNDCalculator Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks QuantLib refuses β = 1, where δ = (1 − 2β)/(1 − β) divides by zero, and near it Boost's non-central chi-squared refuses or runs for seconds. Here β = 1 is the lognormal density of the driftless forward, the CEV density's limit, with no mass at zero; for 0 < |β − 1| < 1e-3 the constructor refuses. A documented divergence (Divergences/CevNearOneTests.cs). The inverse first solves Sankaran's approximation by Brent's method for its guess; where that fails, QuantLib's catch (...) starts from the forward instead, here on NanoQLException, the type of every failure QuantLib's solver and Boost's distribution raise there. That second Brent can step below zero, where QuantLib's distribution reads X(f) = f^(2(1 − β)) as NaN and Boost refuses it, so QuantLib throws at a quantile that exists (β 0.95, σ 200%, five years, the median); here the density and distribution are 0 below zero, the absorbing boundary, and QuantLib's values at and above it stand. A documented divergence (a run find, Divergences/CevDensityBelowZeroTests.cs), checked by the quantile's own distribution.
