api/NanoQL.Models.SwaptionHelper.html.summary: Class SwaptionHelper Namespace NanoQL.Models Assembly NanoQL.dll A calibration helper for interest-rate swaptions: a European swaption on a swap of the index, quoted by a volatility. public sealed class SwaptionHelper : BlackCalibrationHelper Inheritance object CalibrationHelper BlackCalibrationHelper SwaptionHelper Inherited Members BlackCalibrationHelper.CalibrationError(ICalibratedModel, EvaluationContext) BlackCalibrationHelper.ImpliedVolatility(double, double, int, double, double, EvaluationContext) BlackCalibrationHelper.Volatility BlackCalibrationHelper.VolatilityType BlackCalibrationHelper.MarketValue object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable. Each constructor builds what QuantLib's helper builds at its first calculation, under the context it is given: the exercise and start dates, the schedules, a swap at a zero rate whose fair rate is the forward (priced on the term structure, without the settlement date's flows), the exercise rate (the strike, or the forward when none is given) and the swap's type (a receiver, unless the strike is above the forward), the swap at that rate, the European swaption, and the market value. So the at-par choice of the swaps' Ibor coupons is the context's at construction, where QuantLib's reads its global switch whenever the helper recalculates. An overnight index builds an overnight-indexed swap, which model-based engines treat as a vanilla swap: at best a decent proxy, at worst simply wrong; use with caution. Its value dates are QuantLib's telescopic ones, which nanoql builds in full. The model value is the pricing engine's, set by SetPricingEngine<TModel>(Func<Swaption, EvaluationContext, TModel, InstrumentResults>?), which takes the model being calibrated as its last argument; with no engine, pricing a swaption that hasn't expired refuses with QuantLib's "null pricing engine". The settlement days' value is never read, as in QuantLib: any non-null value takes the start date the index's fixing days after the exercise date, where null takes the index's value date. An outer path allocates, as QuantLib's does: a curve-state copy a step and a callable clone an inner simulation. One departure from QuantLib (Divergences/VolatilityInterpolationSpecifierOffsetTests.cs): a short rate between two long rates resets at its own index, i + j·period + offset, where QuantLib's resets at i + j·period, an earlier rate's, at an offset other than 0 (volatilityinterpolationspecifierabcd.cpp:169-170). A period of 0, which QuantLib divides by, no long rates, whose last QuantLib reads, no short rate times, and long rates' times past the short ones, which QuantLib reads past, are refused. api/NanoQL.Models.html.title: Namespace NanoQL.Models | nanoql
api/NanoQL.Models.html.summary: Namespace NanoQL.Models Classes AbcdVol The abcd-interpolated volatility market model: each rate's instantaneous volatility its own multiple k of a common abcd function of the time to its fixing, correlated by a piecewise-constant correlation, each step's pseudo-root the rank-reduced square root of its covariance. AccountingEngine The engine that values a market-model product along an evolver's paths: on each path it steps the evolver and the product together, converts each cash flow into numeraire bonds at its step, rolls the holding into the next step's numeraire, and adds the products' values, in units of the initial numeraire, to the caller's statistics. AlphaFinder The α of an alpha form, and the multipliers a and b, at which a swap rate's volatilities give a caplet its target variance: by the form's α at the initial guess where it works, by a bisection on the quadratic's turning point otherwise, or, with SolveWithMaxHomogeneity(double, int, ReadOnlySpan<double>, ReadOnlySpan<double>, ReadOnlySpan<double>, double, double, double, double, double, double, int, out double, out double, out double, Span<double>), at the α of the most homogeneous volatilities among those that work. AlphaForm A one-parameter family of each rate's volatility multiplier, the alpha calibration's form: SetAlpha(double) chooses the member, Evaluate(int) reads its value at a rate. AlphaFormInverseLinear The alpha form 1/(1 + α t_i). AlphaFormLinearHyperbolic The alpha form √(1 + α t_i (atan(α t_i) − π/2)). BatesDetJumpModel The Bates model with a deterministic jump intensity, mean-reverting at κ_λ to θ_λ: dλ(t) = κ_λ(θ_λ − λ) dt. BatesDoubleExpDetJumpModel The Heston model with double-exponential jumps at a deterministic intensity, mean-reverting at κ_λ to θ_λ. BatesDoubleExpModel The Heston model with double-exponential jumps: an up-jump with probability p, its size exponential with mean η_u (NuUp), and a down-jump otherwise, with mean η_d (NuDown), at intensity λ. BatesModel The Bates stochastic-volatility model: the Heston model with log-normal jumps, calibrated. BermudanSwaptionExerciseValue The exercise value of a Bermudan swaption into the coterminal swaps: at rate time i, the coterminal swap's annuity times its payoff on the coterminal swap rate, floored at 0, paid at rate time i. BlackCalibrationHelper A liquid market instrument used during calibration, quoted by a Black (or Bachelier) volatility: its market value is the Black price at the quoted volatility. BlackKarasinski The standard Black-Karasinski model: d ln rₜ = (θ(t) − α ln rₜ)dt + σ dWₜ, with constant α and σ, fitted to a yield curve. BrownianGenerator An incremental generator of Brownian increments: each path's draws, step by step, for a number of factors. BrownianGeneratorFactory A factory of BrownianGenerators. Burley2020SobolBrownianGenerator The Brownian generator on Burley's scrambled Sobol sequence for market-model simulations: each path a scrambled Sobol sequence of the factors times the steps, turned into Gaussian variates by the inverse cumulative normal and Brownian-bridged by the base's ordering. Burley2020SobolBrownianGeneratorFactory The factory of Burley2020SobolBrownianGenerators, each on the factory's ordering, seeds and direction integers. CMSMMDriftCalculator The drifts μΔt of a displaced log-normal constant-maturity swap market model's swap rates over a step, under the step's numeraire: Mark Joshi, "Rapid Computation of Drifts in a Reduced Factor Libor Market Model", Wilmott Magazine, May 2003. CMSwapCurveState The curve state of constant-maturity swap market models: set on the swap rates spanning a fixed number of forwards, from a first valid index on. CTSMMCapletAlphaFormCalibration The alpha-form coterminal swap market model caplet calibration: each caplet fitted by scaling the next swap rate's volatilities before the caplet's reset by a times the alpha form at an α the solver finds, and after it by b, its swaption variance kept. CTSMMCapletCalibration A coterminal swap market model's calibration to caplet volatilities, the swaption volatilities given: each pass fits the swap rates' pseudo-roots to the caplet volatilities in use, then rescales those by the market's over the model's, until the caplets' root-mean-square error is within the tolerance or the passes run out. CTSMMCapletCalibrationResults A coterminal swap market model caplet calibration's results: QuantLib's inspectors of a calibrated CTSMMCapletCalibration, the fit's errors, the swap rates' pseudo-roots and the model's caplet and swaption volatilities. CTSMMCapletCalibrationStep One pass of a coterminal swap market model's caplet calibration: the swap rates' pseudo-roots and the failures, and what the calibration computes besides (the alpha form's α, a and b; the max-homogeneity calibration's deformation size and swaption error). CTSMMCapletCalibration's hook returns it, and the calibrations' static functions return it in place of QuantLib's out-parameters. CTSMMCapletMaxHomogeneityCalibration The maximally homogeneous coterminal swap market model caplet calibration: each caplet fitted by moving the next swap rate's volatilities to the point closest to its given ones on the sphere of its swaption variance and the cylinder of the caplet's, the caplet or the swaption favoured where they don't meet. CTSMMCapletOriginalCalibration The original coterminal swap market model caplet calibration: the swap variances made time-inhomogeneous by 1/(1 + α s)² and rescaled to their totals, then each swap rate's variance before the previous rate's reset scaled by a² and after it by b², a and b solving the caplet approximation's quadratic. CalibratedModel The calibrated model class: ICalibratedModel over QuantLib's arguments and constraint. CalibratedModelExtensions QuantLib's members of CalibratedModel that return a new model, for any ICalibratedModel. CalibrationHelper The abstract base class for calibration helpers: an instrument whose error a calibration minimizes. CalibrationResults<TModel> A calibration's result: the calibrated model, and QuantLib's record of the calibration that produced it, which QuantLib's CalibratedModel keeps in the model it calibrates. CallSpecifiedMultiProduct A callable product: the underlying's cash flows until the strategy calls it at an exercise time, the rebate's from then on; without a rebate, a cash rebate of 0 at the exercise times. CallSpecifiedPathwiseMultiProduct A callable pathwise product: the underlying's cash flows and derivatives until the strategy calls it at an exercise time, the rebate's from then on; without a rebate, a pathwise cash rebate of 0 at the exercise times. CapHelper A calibration helper for at-the-money caps: a cap on the index, struck at the fair rate of a swap on it. CapPseudoDerivative A cap's implied volatility in a market model, the flat undisplaced Black volatility that reprices the model's displaced caplets, and the derivatives of its price and its implied volatility with respect to the pseudo-roots' elements, step by step, for market vegas. CapletCoterminalPeriodicFunctions The periodic caplet and swaption calibration: a coterminal swap market model on short rates fitted to the short caplets and to the swaptions on long rates, each spanning a period of the short ones. CapletSwaptionPeriodicCalibrationResults The periodic caplet and swaption calibration's results, QuantLib's return value and out-parameters. CollectNodeDataFunctions The node-data collection for a market-model callable product's exercise: QuantLib's free function. ConstantEstimator The constant-estimator volatility model: at each date past the first size, the dispersion of the size values before it. Volatilities are assumed to be expressed on an annual basis. ConstantParameter The standard constant parameter: a(t) = a. ConstrainedEvolver A constrained market-model evolver: an evolver whose rates can be fixed by importance sampling, for the Fries-Joshi proxy simulation approach to Greeks. CotSwapFromFwdCorrelation The coterminal swap rates' correlation implied by a forward-rate correlation on a curve: each period's the correlation of the coterminal Z matrix times the forwards' correlation times its transpose, the expired rates' coefficients zero. CotSwapToFwdAdapter A coterminal swap-rate market model as a forward-rate one, in the frozen-coefficient approximation: its initial rates the forwards of the coterminal model's curve, each step's pseudo-root the inverse of the coterminal Z matrix times the coterminal model's, the expired rates' rows zero. CotSwapToFwdAdapterFactory The factory of CotSwapToFwdAdapters, each on a coterminal swap-rate model its coterminal factory creates. CoterminalSwapCurveState The curve state of coterminal swap market models: set on coterminal swap rates, from a first valid index on. CoxIngersollRoss The Cox-Ingersoll-Ross model: dr(t) = k(θ − r(t))dt + σ√r(t) dW(t). CurveState The curve state of a market-model simulation: the yield curve at the simulation's fixed rate times, the workhorse discounting object a product reads, so that a product runs on any kind of model (LIBOR, coterminal swap or constant-maturity swap). CurveStateFunctions The curve-state conversions of curvestate.hpp: forward, coterminal swap and constant-maturity swap rates from discount ratios, each written into the caller's buffers from the first valid index on. EvolutionDescription A market-model evolution's description: the rate times defining the rates evolved, the evolution times at which the rates need to be known, and which rates are relevant at each step. EvolutionDescriptionFunctions The numeraire functions of an evolution: the measures and the numeraires' checks. ExerciseAdapter An exercise value as a product: stepped at the exercise value's times, it pays the exercise value at its first exercise time and is done there. ExpCorrelationsFunctions The exponential correlation matrix of forward rates. ExponentialForwardCorrelation The exponential forward correlation, piecewise constant: at γ = 1 time-homogeneous on the rate times, otherwise each period's matrix the exponential correlation at the period's midpoint. ExtendedCoxIngersollRoss The extended Cox-Ingersoll-Ross model: r(t) = φ(t) + y(t), y a standard Cox-Ingersoll-Ross process, dy(t) = k(θ − y(t))dt + σ√y(t) dW(t), and φ the deterministic parameter fitting the curve. FlatVol The flat-volatility market model: each rate with a constant volatility until its fixing, correlated by a piecewise-constant correlation, each step's pseudo-root the rank-reduced square root of its covariance. FlatVolFactory The factory of FlatVol models on a yield curve: the initial rates the curve's simple forwards, the volatilities interpolated linearly in the rates' fixing times and displaced, and the exponential correlation made time-homogeneous. FlatVolFunctions The flat-volatility model's covariance function. ForwardForwardMappings The mappings between forward rates of a multiple tenor and the forward rates of the curve state's: the Jacobian of the long forwards in the short ones, the Y matrix that switches a model's base from short to long forwards, and the curve state restricted to the long forwards' times. FwdPeriodAdapter A forward-rate market model on short forwards as one on long forwards, each spanning a period of the short ones from an offset: its curve the short model's restricted to the long rate times, its evolution the short model's to the last long reset, each step's pseudo-root the Y matrix times the short model's, the expired rates' rows zero. FwdToCotSwapAdapter A forward-rate market model as a coterminal swap-rate one, in the frozen-coefficient approximation: its initial rates the coterminal swap rates of the forward model's curve, each step's pseudo-root the coterminal Z matrix times the forward model's, the expired rates' rows zero. FwdToCotSwapAdapterFactory The factory of FwdToCotSwapAdapters, each on a forward-rate model its forward factory creates. G2 The two-additive-factor Gaussian model: rₜ = φ(t) + xₜ + yₜ, with dxₜ = −a xₜ dt + σ dW¹ₜ, x₀ = 0, dyₜ = −b yₜ dt + η dW²ₜ, y₀ = 0, and dW¹ₜdW²ₜ = ρ dt, fitted to a yield curve. GJRGARCHModel The GJR-GARCH model for the stochastic volatility of an asset: its six arguments ω, α, β, γ, λ and v₀ over a GJRGARCHProcess. GJRGARCHModelVolatilityConstraint The constraint β + γ ≥ 0 on a GJR-GARCH model's parameters, read from β and γ, the third and fourth of GJRGARCHModel's: QuantLib's GJRGARCHModel::VolatilityConstraint. Garch11 The GARCH(1,1) volatility model: σ²ₜ = ω + α u²ₜ₋₁ + β σ²ₜ₋₁, ω = γ V_L with γ = 1 − α − β and V_L the long-term variance. Volatilities are assumed to be expressed on an annual basis. Garch11Calibration A GARCH(1,1) calibration to squared returns, QuantLib's calibrate_r2: the parameters it writes through its references and the minimization it returns. GarmanKlassAbstract The Garman-Klass volatility models, based on high-low formulas using the method of Garman and Klass in their paper "On the Estimation of the Security Price from Historical Data": at each date, √(|f(p)|/y) for a point estimator f of the interval's prices p and a year fraction y. Volatilities are assumed to be expressed on an annual basis. GarmanKlassSigma1 Garman and Klass's first estimator: the overnight jump beside the simple estimator. GarmanKlassSigma3 Garman and Klass's third estimator: the overnight jump beside Parkinson's. GarmanKlassSigma4 Garman and Klass's fourth estimator, on the interval's open, close, high and low. GarmanKlassSigma5 Garman and Klass's fifth estimator, on the interval's open, close, high and low. GarmanKlassSigma6 Garman and Klass's sixth estimator: the overnight jump beside the fourth. GarmanKlassSimpleSigma The simple Garman-Klass estimator: the squared log of the interval's close over its open. Gaussian1dModel The interface of one-factor interest-rate models whose state is Gaussian: a derived model implements the numeraire and the zero bond for a value of the state variable y, the standardized (zero mean, unit variance) form of the model's state x. Gsr The one-factor GSR model, formulated in the forward measure of its numeraire time: piecewise constant volatilities on the step dates, and a constant reversion or piecewise constant reversions on the same dates. HestonModel The Heston model for the stochastic volatility of an asset: its process's five parameters, calibrated. HestonModelFellerConstraint The Feller constraint on a Heston model's parameters, σ ≥ 0 and σ² < 2κθ, read from θ, κ and σ, the first three of HestonModel's: QuantLib's HestonModel::FellerConstraint. HestonModelHelper A calibration helper for the Heston model: a European plain-vanilla option, a period after the risk-free curve's reference date, quoted by a Black volatility. HestonSLVFDMModel The Heston stochastic-local volatility model calibrated by the Fokker-Planck forward equation: the leverage function L(t, S) that makes the model's spot follow the local volatility's marginals, σ_LV(t, S)²/E[v | S], solved step by step on the joint density of the log spot and the variance. HestonSLVFDMModelLogEntry A step of a HestonSLVFDMModel's calibration: the joint density of the log spot and the variance at a time, on its mesher. HestonSLVFokkerPlanckFdmParams The Fokker-Planck finite-difference calibration's settings for a HestonSLVFDMModel. HestonSLVMCModel The Heston stochastic-local volatility model calibrated by Monte Carlo: at each time step the calibration paths' spots are sorted into bins, and the leverage at each bin's midpoint is the local volatility over the root of the bin's mean variance. HistoricalForwardRatesAnalysis The outcome of a statistical analysis of historical forward rates: the dates skipped and failed, their messages, and the forwards' fixing periods. HistoricalForwardRatesAnalysisFunctions The statistical analysis of historical forward rates: QuantLib's free function template historicalForwardRatesAnalysis<Traits, Interpolator>. HistoricalForwardRatesAnalysisImpl<TTraits, TInterpolator> The statistical analysis of historical forward rates on a curve of the given traits and interpolator, run at construction into the statistics it is given (HistoricalForwardRatesAnalysis<TTraits, TInterpolator>(SequenceStatistics, Date, Date, Period, InterestRateIndex, Period, Period, ReadOnlySpan<IborIndex>, ReadOnlySpan<SwapIndex>, DayCounter, EvaluationContext, double, TInterpolator)). HistoricalForwardRatesAnalysisResults What HistoricalForwardRatesAnalysis<TTraits, TInterpolator>(SequenceStatistics, Date, Date, Period, InterestRateIndex, Period, Period, ReadOnlySpan<IborIndex>, ReadOnlySpan<SwapIndex>, DayCounter, EvaluationContext, double, TInterpolator) leaves in QuantLib's reference outputs: the dates skipped, where a fixing was missing or refused, the dates failed, where the curve or a forward rate failed, each with its error's message, and the forwards' fixing periods. HistoricalRatesAnalysis The statistical analysis of historical rates, run at construction: the relative changes of the indexes' fixings between successive dates, added to the statistics it is given (HistoricalRatesAnalysis(SequenceStatistics, Date, Date, Period, ReadOnlySpan<InterestRateIndex>, EvaluationContext)). HistoricalRatesAnalysisFunctions The statistical analysis of historical rates: QuantLib's free function historicalRatesAnalysis. HistoricalRatesAnalysisResults What HistoricalRatesAnalysis(SequenceStatistics, Date, Date, Period, ReadOnlySpan<InterestRateIndex>, EvaluationContext) leaves in QuantLib's reference outputs: the dates skipped, where a fixing was missing or refused, each with its error's message. HullWhite The single-factor Hull-White (extended Vasicek) model: drₜ = (θ(t) − αrₜ)dt + σ dWₜ, with constant α and σ, fitted to a yield curve. LMMCurveState The curve state of LIBOR market models: set on forward rates or discount ratios, from a first valid index on. LMMDriftCalculator The drifts μΔt of a displaced log-normal LIBOR market model's forwards over a step, under the step's numeraire: Mark Joshi, "Rapid Computation of Drifts in a Reduced Factor Libor Market Model", Wilmott Magazine, May 2003. LMMNormalDriftCalculator The drifts μΔt of a normal LIBOR market model's forwards over a step, under the step's numeraire: Mark Joshi, "Rapid Computation of Drifts in a Reduced Factor Libor Market Model", Wilmott Magazine, May 2003, modified for normal forward-rate dynamics. LogNormalCmSwapRatePc The predictor-corrector evolver of a displaced log-normal constant-maturity swap market model: the model's rates are the swap rates spanning a fixed number of forwards, each step predicted with the drifts at its start and corrected with the average of those and the drifts on the predicted curve. LogNormalCotSwapRatePc The predictor-corrector evolver of a displaced log-normal coterminal swap market model: the model's rates are the coterminal swap rates, each step predicted with the drifts at its start and corrected with the average of those and the drifts on the predicted curve. LogNormalFwdRateBalland Balland's predictor-corrector evolver of a displaced log-normal LIBOR market model: each step's drifts corrected with the drifts at the geometric mean of the step's predicted end forwards and its start forwards. LogNormalFwdRateEuler The Euler evolver of a displaced log-normal LIBOR market model: each step's drifts at its start, the log forwards stepped by them and the step's correlated Brownian increments. LogNormalFwdRateEulerConstrained The constrained Euler evolver of a displaced log-normal LIBOR market model, for the Fries-Joshi proxy simulation of Greeks: at each step whose constraint is active, the log forwards are shifted along the constrained rate's covariances so that it lands on its constraint, and the step's weight takes the likelihood ratio of the shift. LogNormalFwdRateIpc The iterative predictor-corrector evolver of a displaced log-normal LIBOR market model under the terminal measure: the forwards stepped from the last to the first, each corrected with the drift its later forwards' new values give. LogNormalFwdRatePc The predictor-corrector evolver of a displaced log-normal LIBOR market model: each step's log forwards predicted with the drifts at its start, then corrected with the average of those and the drifts at the predicted forwards. LogNormalFwdRateiBalland Balland's iterative predictor-corrector evolver of a displaced log-normal LIBOR market model under the terminal measure: the forwards stepped from the last to the first, each drift from the later forwards' geometric means. LongstaffSchwartzExerciseStrategy The Longstaff-Schwartz exercise strategy: at each exercise, exercises where the exercise value, in units of the numeraire portfolio, reaches the continuation value the regression's coefficients estimate on the basis functions, plus the control's value. MTBrownianGenerator The Mersenne-twister Brownian generator for market-model simulations: each path a uniform sequence of the factors times the steps, drawn eagerly, each step's slice turned into Gaussian variates by the inverse cumulative normal. MTBrownianGeneratorFactory The factory of MTBrownianGenerators, each on the factory's seed. MarketModel A market model: for each evolution step, the pseudo-square root of the rates' covariance over the step. MarketModelBasisSystem The basis functions a Longstaff-Schwartz regression reads at each exercise: a node-data provider whose data are the functions' values. MarketModelCashRebate The receipt of a fixed cash amount, once: each step pays each product its amount for that step, at the step's payment time, and finishes the path. Mainly the rebate received when another product is cancelled. MarketModelComposite A market-model product composed of one or more products on the same rate times, each with a multiplier: its evolution steps at every part's evolution times, and each part steps at its own. MarketModelDifferencesFunctions The differences between two market models on the same initial rates and evolution: their rates' volatilities and instantaneous volatilities. QuantLib's free functions in marketmodeldifferences.hpp. MarketModelDiscounter The number of numeraire bonds a unit paid at a time is worth on a curve state: the discount ratio of the rate times bracketing the payment, log-linearly interpolated between them. MarketModelEvolver A market-model evolver: the gritty work of evolving the rates from one evolution time to the next, path by path. MarketModelExerciseValue The value of exercising a market-model callable product: stepped along a path at its evolution's times, it gives at each exercise time the cash flow exercising pays. MarketModelFactory A factory of MarketModels on given evolutions. MarketModelMultiProduct A market-model product, or several on the same rate times: the information of its term sheet, and, for a callable product, its exercise strategy. At each step of an evolution it generates the cash flows of that step for the state of the curve. MarketModelNodeDataProvider The data a market-model callable product's exercise decision reads at each exercise: stepped along a path at its evolution's times, it fills the current exercise's values. MarketModelParametricExercise A parametric exercise rule on a market model: a node-data provider whose data are the rule's variables, and the rule. MarketModelPathwiseCashRebate The receipt of a fixed cash amount, once, for the pathwise engines: each step pays each product its amount for that step, its derivatives 0, and finishes the path. MarketModelPathwiseCoterminalSwaptionsDeflated The coterminal payer swaptions for the pathwise engines, one product a rate: swaption i pays, at rate i's reset, (Sᵢ − Kᵢ) Aᵢ in its first bond where positive, Sᵢ the coterminal swap rate and Aᵢ its annuity, with its analytic derivatives with respect to the forwards from fᵢ. MarketModelPathwiseCoterminalSwaptionsNumericalDeflated The coterminal payer swaptions for the pathwise engines with numerical derivatives: as MarketModelPathwiseCoterminalSwaptionsDeflated, each derivative a central difference of the swaption's value on the state's forwards bumped up and down by the bump size. MarketModelPathwiseDiscounter The number of units of the discretely compounding money-market account a unit paid at a time buys on a step's rates, and its derivative with respect to each forward rate, for the pathwise Greeks: the discount factors of the rate times bracketing the payment, log-linearly interpolated between them. MarketModelPathwiseInverseFloater An inverse floater for the pathwise engines: MultiStepInverseFloater's cash flows, with each coupon's derivative with respect to its rate's forward. MarketModelPathwiseMultiCaplet Caplets for the pathwise engines, one product a rate: caplet i pays (fᵢ − Kᵢ) aᵢ at its payment time where positive, with its derivative aᵢ with respect to fᵢ; mainly a test product. MarketModelPathwiseMultiDeflatedCap Caps for the pathwise engines, already deflated: cap k is the deflated caplets on one strike from its start rate to before its end rate, each caplet's cash flow and derivatives its cap's. MarketModelPathwiseMultiDeflatedCaplet Caplets for the pathwise engines, already deflated: caplet i pays (fᵢ − Kᵢ) aᵢ P(Tᵢ₊₁)/P(T₀), in units of the money-market numeraire, where positive, with its derivatives with respect to each forward up to fᵢ. MarketModelPathwiseMultiProduct A market-model product, or several on the same rate times, that also gives each cash flow's derivatives with respect to each forward rate, for the pathwise Greeks: MarketModelMultiProduct's contract with MarketModelPathwiseMultiProductCashFlow cash flows. MarketModelPathwiseMultiProductCashFlow A cash flow a MarketModelPathwiseMultiProduct generates at a step: the index of its payment time and its amount followed by the amount's derivatives with respect to each forward rate. QuantLib's nested MarketModelPathwiseMultiProduct::CashFlow, made top-level. MarketModelPathwiseSwap A swap for the pathwise engines: at each rate's reset, (fᵢ − Kᵢ) τᵢ times the multiplier, paid at the period's end, with its derivative τᵢ times the multiplier with respect to fᵢ. MarketModelVolProcess A volatility process for a displaced-diffusion LIBOR market model with an uncorrelated stochastic volatility, the "shifted BGM" with Heston volatility of Brace's "Engineering BGM": it scales each evolution step's variance. MarkovFunctional The one-factor Markov-functional model, its numeraire calibrated to a swaption or a caplet smile: see http://ssrn.com/abstract_id=2183721 and http://quantlib.org/slides/qlws13/caspers.pdf. MarkovFunctionalCustomSmileFactory The factory of the custom smile sections the Markov-functional model calibrates to. MarkovFunctionalCustomSmileSection A smile section of one's own for the Markov-functional model's calibration, which inverts digital prices to market rates itself. MarkovFunctionalModelOutputs The Markov-functional model's diagnostics: per calibration point in date order, its expiry, tenor, at-the-money level and annuity, the numeraire's adjustment factors, the yield curve's fit and the smile's fit on the moneyness grid, and the calibration's messages. MarkovFunctionalModelSettings The Markov-functional model's numerical settings: the state grid, the Gauss-Hermite integration, the digitals' gap, the market rates' accuracy and bounds, and the adjustments and smile pretreatments. MergedTimes The result of MergeTimes(ReadOnlySpan<ImmutableArray<double>>): QuantLib's mergeTimes outputs, the merged times and each set's presence among them. MultiProductComposite A composite of market-model products whose products stay apart: its products are each part's products in turn, each part's cash flows scaled by its multiplier. MultiProductMultiStep A market-model product evaluated in more than one step (Rebonato's long jump): its evolution steps at every rate time but the last, each step's relevant rates the one resetting there. MultiProductOneStep A market-model product evaluated in one step (Rebonato's very long jump): its evolution steps once, at the last rate's reset, every rate relevant. MultiProductPathwiseWrapper A pathwise product as an ordinary one: its cash flows' amounts without their derivatives, so the product is written once for both kinds of engine. MultiStepCoinitialSwaps The coinitial payer swaps, one product a rate: swap i, from the first rate to rate i, pays at each of its rates' resets the fixed coupon −K τᶠⁱˣ and the floating coupon f τᶠˡᵒᵃᵗ, at the period's payment time. MultiStepCoterminalSwaps The coterminal payer swaps, one product a rate: swap i, from rate i to the last, pays at each of its rates' resets the fixed coupon −K τᶠⁱˣ and the floating coupon f τᶠˡᵒᵃᵗ, at the period's payment time. MultiStepCoterminalSwaptions The coterminal swaptions, one product a rate: swaption i pays, at rate i's reset, its payoff of the coterminal swap rate from rate i times the swap's annuity in its first bond, at its payment time. MultiStepForwards Forward-rate agreements, one product a rate: product i pays (fᵢ − Kᵢ) τᵢ at its payment time, fixed at the rate's reset. MultiStepInverseFloater An inverse floater: at each rate's reset, the inverse floating coupon max(Kᵢ − mᵢ fᵢ, 0) τᶠⁱˣᵢ less the floating coupon (fᵢ + sᵢ) τᶠˡᵒᵃᵗᵢ, received, or paid by a payer. MultiStepNothing Products that pay nothing, its path finished once it has stepped past a given index: the underlying of a Bermudan option on MarketModelMultiProduct's callable framework, and a placeholder. MultiStepOptionlets Optionlets, one product a rate: product i pays its payoff of the forward fᵢ times τᵢ at its payment time, fixed at the rate's reset. MultiStepPeriodCapletSwaptions The caplets and coterminal swaptions on the long forwards made of a period of rates each, from an offset: at each long forward's reset, a caplet on the long forward and a swaption on the long coterminal swap from it, the first half of the products the caplets and the second the swaptions. MultiStepRatchet A full ratchet: at each rate's reset, the coupon max(g_floor · floor + s_floor, g_fixing · f + s_fixing) times the accrual, the floor then the coupon, from the initial floor. MultiStepSwap A swap on the forward rates: at each rate's reset, the fixed coupon −K τᶠⁱˣᵢ and the floating coupon fᵢ τᶠˡᵒᵃᵗᵢ, each paid at the period's payment time, signed for a payer (−1 on the floating leg for a receiver). MultiStepSwaption A swaption on a contiguous run of the rates: at the swap's start its payoff of the swap rate times the annuity, paid at the start, the path finished. It steps through every rate time up to the swap's start; mainly a test product. MultiStepTarn A targeted redemption note: at each rate's reset it receives the floating coupon (f + s) τᶠˡᵒᵃᵗ and pays the inverse floating coupon max(K − m f, 0) τ, until the coupons paid reach the total coupon or the last rate, when it pays what is left of the total and ends. NormalFwdRatePc The predictor-corrector evolver of a normal LIBOR market model: each step's forwards predicted with the drifts at its start, then corrected with the average of those and the drifts at the predicted forwards. NothingExerciseValue An exercise value of nothing: at each exercise time a cash flow of 0, paid at the current rate time. NullParameter A parameter which is always zero: a(t) = 0, with no parameters. OneFactorAffineModel The single-factor affine base class: a model whose discount bond is P(t, T, r) = A(t, T)·exp(−B(t, T)·r), for derived classes implementing A(double, double) and B(double, double). OneFactorModel The single-factor short-rate model abstract class: its short rate a function of one state variable. OneFactorModelShortRateDynamics The base class describing a one-factor model's short-rate dynamics: the short rate and its state variable. OneFactorModelShortRateTree A recombining trinomial tree discretizing a one-factor model's state variable. OneStepCoinitialSwaps The coinitial payer swaps valued in one step: at the last rate's reset, swap i, from the first rate to rate i, pays each of its periods' fixed coupon −K τᶠⁱˣ and floating coupon f τᶠˡᵒᵃᵗ at the period's payment time. OneStepCoterminalSwaps The coterminal payer swaps valued in one step: at the last rate's reset, swap i, from rate i to the last, pays each of its periods' fixed coupon −K τᶠⁱˣ and floating coupon f τᶠˡᵒᵃᵗ at the period's payment time. OneStepForwards Forward-rate agreements valued in one step: at the last rate's reset, product i pays (fᵢ − Kᵢ) τᵢ at its payment time. OneStepOptionlets Optionlets valued in one step: at the last rate's reset, product i pays its payoff of fᵢ times τᵢ at its payment time where the payoff is positive. OrthogonalizedBumpFinder Pseudo-root bumps that each move one instrument's implied volatility by one percent and leave the others fixed: the instruments' one-percent bumps projected orthogonally to each other, an instrument too correlated with the others discarded. Parameter The base class for model arguments: a function of time defined by an array of parameters. Parameter.Impl The base class for a parameter's implementation: its value at a time from the parameters. ParametricExerciseAdapter An exercise strategy from a parametric exercise rule and its parameters: at each exercise, the rule on the exercise's parameters and the variables the rule reads in the state. ParkinsonSigma Parkinson's estimator: the squared log range of the interval over 4 ln 2. PathwiseAccountingEngine The engine that values pathwise market-model products and their deltas along a log-normal Euler evolver's paths, by Giles and Glasserman's smoking adjoints: on each path it gathers the products' cash flows and their derivatives, then carries the derivatives back to the initial forward rates through the Euler step's Jacobian. PathwiseVegasAccountingEngine The engine that values pathwise market-model products, their deltas and their vegas along given bumps of the pseudo-roots, along a log-normal Euler evolver's paths, by Giles and Glasserman's smoking adjoints: the delta engine's recursion, with each step's rates differentiated along the bumps as the path goes and combined with the derivatives as early as possible. PathwiseVegasOuterAccountingEngine The engine that values pathwise market-model products, their deltas and their vegas along a log-normal Euler evolver's paths, by Giles and Glasserman's smoking adjoints: PathwiseVegasAccountingEngine's values, with the derivatives taken with respect to every pseudo-root element and combined into the bumps' vegas as late as possible, after the paths' means. PiecewiseConstantAbcdVariance The piecewise-constant variance of the rate resetting at a given rate time under an abcd volatility: each step to the reset the abcd function's variance over the step, 0 after it. PiecewiseConstantCorrelation A piecewise-constant correlation of the rates: one correlation matrix per period between its times, which must include every rate time but the last. PiecewiseConstantParameter A piecewise-constant parameter: a(t) = aᵢ for tᵢ₋₁ ≤ t < tᵢ, one parameter per piece, so a time equal to a breakpoint takes the next piece. This kind of parameter is usually used to enhance the fitting of a model. PiecewiseConstantVariance A rate's variance, piecewise constant over the steps between its rate times: each step's variance and volatility, and their totals from time zero. PiecewiseTimeDependentHestonModel The Heston model with piecewise time-dependent parameters on a time grid, calibrated. ProxyGreekEngine The engine that values market-model products and their Greeks by Fries and Joshi's partial proxy simulation: each path is valued on the original evolver, which records each step's constrained rate, then on each bumped constrained evolver pinned to those rates, its weights the likelihood ratio; finite-difference weights combine the original and the bumped values into each Greek's path value. PseudoRootFacade A market model given by its pseudo-roots, one per rate time but the last: its evolution the rate times', its initial rates and displacements given; the coterminal swap market model a caplet calibration builds. RatePseudoRootJacobian The derivative of a log-normal Euler step's end rates along given bumps of its pseudo-root, analytically, for the pathwise vegas (Giles and Glasserman's B, a row per bump): the step in the discretely compounding money-market account. RatePseudoRootJacobianAllElements The derivative of each end rate of a log-normal Euler step with respect to each element of its pseudo-root, analytically, for the pathwise vegas: the step in the discretely compounding money-market account. RatePseudoRootJacobianNumerical The change in a log-normal Euler step's rates when its pseudo-root is bumped, by revaluing the step on each bumped pseudo-root: the numerical form RatePseudoRootJacobian is tested against. RoughHestonModel The rough Heston model for the stochastic volatility of an asset: the Heston parameters and the variance's Hurst exponent, calibrated. SMMDriftCalculator The drifts μΔt of a displaced log-normal coterminal swap market model's swap rates over a step, under the step's numeraire: Mark Joshi and Lorenzo Liesch, "Effective Implementation Of Generic Market Models". SVDDFwdRatePc The predictor-corrector evolver of a displaced-diffusion LIBOR market model with an uncorrelated stochastic volatility: each step's variance scaled by its volatility process's step multiplier, the process drawn from some of each step's variates. ShortRateModel The abstract short-rate model class: a calibrated model that builds a lattice on a time grid. SimpleLocalEstimator The local-estimator volatility model: at each date after the first, |ln(Sᵢ/Sᵢ₋₁)|/√y for a year fraction y between quotes. Volatilities are assumed to be expressed on an annual basis. SingleProductComposite A composite of market-model products as one product: every part's products' cash flows, scaled by the part's multiplier, are the one product's. SobolBrownianGenerator The Sobol Brownian generator for market-model simulations: each path a Sobol sequence of the factors times the steps, turned into Gaussian variates by the inverse cumulative normal and Brownian-bridged by the base's ordering. SobolBrownianGeneratorBase The incremental Brownian generator on a low-discrepancy sequence: each path's Gaussian variates, of the factors times the steps, assigned to the factors and steps by an ordering and Brownian-bridged along each factor's path. SobolBrownianGeneratorFactory The factory of SobolBrownianGenerators, each on the factory's ordering, seed and direction integers. SquareRootAndersen A square-root (CIR) variance process stepped by Andersen's quadratic-exponential scheme, sub-stepping each evolution step, its step's standard deviation multiplier the weighted average of the variance at the sub-steps' ends. SwapBasisSystem The basis functions 1, the next forward rate and the coterminal swap rate after it, at each exercise; at an exercise on the last rate, 1 and the forward rate. SwapForwardBasisSystem The quadratic basis functions in the next forward rate x, the coterminal swap rate after it y and the discount ratio to the last rate time z at each exercise: 1, x, y, z, xy, yz, zx, x², y², z²; at an exercise on the second-to-last rate, 1, x, the last forward y, x², xy, y²; on the last, 1, x, x². SwapForwardMappings The mappings between swap rates and forward rates: annuities, the swap rates' derivatives and Jacobians in the forwards, the Z matrices that switch a model's base from forwards to swap rates, and a swaption's implied volatility by frozen coefficients. SwapRateTrigger An exercise strategy on swap-rate triggers: at each exercise, exercises where the coterminal swap rate from the next rate is above the exercise's trigger. SwaptionHelper A calibration helper for interest-rate swaptions: a European swaption on a swap of the index, quoted by a volatility. SwaptionPseudoDerivative A swaption's implied volatility in a market model, by frozen coefficients, and its derivatives with respect to the pseudo-roots' elements, step by step, for market vegas. TermStructureFittingParameter A deterministic time-dependent parameter used for yield-curve fitting, with no parameters of its own. TermStructureFittingParameter.NumericalImpl The numerical implementation: the fitted values at the times a tree sets them. TimeHomogeneousForwardCorrelation A time-homogeneous forward correlation: in the k-th period, between rate times k and k + 1, the alive rates i and j correlate as rates i − k and j − k do at time zero. TriggeredSwapExercise A parametric exercise on a swap-rate trigger: one variable, the coterminal swap rate from the next rate at each exercise, and one parameter, the trigger, exercised when the rate reaches it; the strikes are the triggers' guesses. TwoFactorModel The abstract two-factor short-rate model class: its short rate a function of two state variables. TwoFactorModelShortRateDynamics The class describing the dynamics of a two-factor model's state variables: the short rate rₜ = f(t, xₜ, yₜ), with dxₜ = μₓ(t, xₜ)dt + σₓ(t, xₜ)dWˣₜ, dyₜ = μᵧ(t, yₜ)dt + σᵧ(t, yₜ)dWʸₜ and dWˣₜdWʸₜ = ρ dt. TwoFactorModelShortRateTree A recombining two-dimensional tree discretizing a two-factor model's state variables. UpperBoundEngine The Andersen-Broadie upper bound of a callable product: on each outer path the hedged portfolio's maximum over the exercise dates, the hedge's unexercised value at each date from an inner simulation of the hedge's call-specified product. UtilitiesFunctions The market models' time utilities: merging sets of times, subset tests and the times' checks. Vasicek The Vasicek model: drₜ = a(b − rₜ)dt + σ dWₜ, with constant a, b and σ, and a risk premium λ. VegaBumpCluster A block of pseudo-root elements bumped together for a vega: the factors, rates and steps in three half-open ranges. VegaBumpCollection The clusters a model's alive pseudo-root elements are bumped in, too many to bump one by one: by default each alive element alone, or each alive rate's factors together. VolatilityBumpInstrumentJacobian The derivatives of swaptions' and caps' implied volatilities along a collection's vega bumps, and for each instrument the smallest combination of the bumps that moves its implied volatility by one percent. VolatilityInterpolationSpecifier How the volatility structure of synthetic short rates interleaved between long rates is decided: the short rates' variances interpolated from the long rates', each long rate's scaled, the last short rate's matching a caplet volatility. VolatilityInterpolationSpecifierabcd The volatility interpolation of synthetic short rates on abcd curves: each long rate's a, b and d scaled, each short rate between two long ones on the mean of their a, b, c and d, those before the first and after the last on the nearest long rate's, the last rescaled to match the last caplet's volatility. Structs AbcdCoefficients An abcd function's four parameters, GetABCD()'s result: QuantLib's getABCD out-parameters. MarketModelMultiProductCashFlow A cash flow a MarketModelMultiProduct generates at a step: its amount and the index of its payment time in the product's PossibleCashFlowTimes(). QuantLib's nested MarketModelMultiProduct::CashFlow, made top-level. VolatilityBumpInstrumentJacobianCap A cap whose implied volatility VolatilityBumpInstrumentJacobian bumps: the caplets from the start index to the end index at a strike. QuantLib's nested VolatilityBumpInstrumentJacobian::Cap, made top-level. VolatilityBumpInstrumentJacobianSwaption A swaption whose implied volatility VolatilityBumpInstrumentJacobian bumps: on the swap from the start index to the end index. QuantLib's nested VolatilityBumpInstrumentJacobian::Swaption, made top-level. Interfaces IAffineModel An affine model: the base for analytically tractable models, which engines test for with is. ICalibratedModel A model that can be calibrated: what a calibration and the calibration helpers read of it, which QuantLib's CalibratedModel declares. ITermStructureConsistentModel A term-structure consistent model: one that can reprice exactly any discount bond of its curve. Enums BlackCalibrationHelperCalibrationErrorType How a Black calibration helper measures its error: QuantLib's BlackCalibrationHelper::CalibrationErrorType. Garch11Mode The initial guess of a GARCH(1,1) calibration, QuantLib's Garch11::Mode. MarkovFunctionalModelSettingsAdjustments The Markov-functional model's adjustments and smile pretreatments, flags combined with |. SobolBrownianGeneratorBaseOrdering How a SobolBrownianGeneratorBase assigns the Sobol sequence's variates to the factors and steps.

api/NanoQL.Money.html.summary: Struct Money Namespace NanoQL Assembly NanoQL.dll An amount of cash in a given currency. public readonly struct Money : IEquatable<Money> Implements IEquatable<Money> Inherited Members object.GetType() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks A value: its zero value, default(Money), is QuantLib's Money(), 0.0 in the empty currency, a null Currency. The operators combine amounts in one currency as QuantLib's do, and never convert: QuantLib's operators read the global Money::Settings, and these see no context, so they behave as under its NoConversion. On a currency mismatch every operator but == and != throws QuantLib's "currency mismatch and no conversion specified"; == returns false and != true, where QuantLib's throw. The conversion modes are methods that take the context, which holds the settings (MoneySettings) and the exchange rates (ExchangeRates): Add(Money, EvaluationContext), Subtract(Money, EvaluationContext), Divide(Money, EvaluationContext), Equals(Money, EvaluationContext), LessThan(Money, EvaluationContext), LessThanOrEqual(Money, EvaluationContext), GreaterThan(Money, EvaluationContext), GreaterThanOrEqual(Money, EvaluationContext), and MoneyFunctions' Close and CloseEnough. Equals(Money) and GetHashCode() compare the currency and the value, the value by Equals(double), so that equality is reflexive, as .NET's own double keeps == IEEE's. api/NanoQL.Numerics.AliMikhailHaqCopula..summary: Class AliMikhailHaqCopula Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The Ali-Mikhail-Haq copula, C(x, y) = xy/(1 − θ(1 − x)(1 − y)). public sealed class AliMikhailHaqCopula Inheritance object AliMikhailHaqCopula Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable. On the unit square's edges it returns the boundary values, C(u, 0) = C(0, v) = 0, C(u, 1) = u and C(1, v) = v, before its formula, as every copula here does: QuantLib's is NaN at (0, 0) at θ 1. Where θ(1 − x)(1 − y) exceeds 1/2 the denominator is computed as (1 − θ) + θ(x + y − xy), which doesn't cancel as θ nears 1 and x and y near 0, where QuantLib's loses its digits (at θ 1, C(1e-14, 1e-14) 8e-4 off, and ∞ below about 1.1e-16); QuantLib's formula elsewhere, so its bits at θ in [−1, 1/2]. In the rewritten region, where xy is below the normal range, the product is formed last. api/NanoQL.Numerics.BFGS.html.summary: Class BFGS Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno method (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BFGS_method), adapted from Numerical Recipes in C, 2nd edition. public sealed class BFGS : LineSearchBasedMethod Inheritance object OptimizationMethod LineSearchBasedMethod BFGS Inherited Members OptimizationMethod.Minimize(Problem, EndCriteria) OptimizationMethod.Minimize(ProblemState, EndCriteria) object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The user has to provide a line-search method and optimization end criteria. Immutable: each minimization runs on a new line search and a new inverse Hessian, the identity at its start (SciPy's hess_inv0). QuantLib's method keeps its inverse Hessian as a member, built on its first minimization only, so a second minimization on one object starts from the first's Hessian, and one of another dimension reads it out of range: a documented divergence (Divergences/BFGSTests.cs). The update is QuantLib's, on the search direction before the line search's step scales it, not on the step, which QuantLib's Armijo search, starting each iteration from the previous step and only shrinking it, compensates; kept as it is: the textbook update fails to converge with the same searches. api/NanoQL.Numerics.BSpline.html.summary: Class BSpline Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The B-spline basis functions N_{i,p}(x) of degree p, i = 0, 1, …, n, over a knot vector of p + n + 2 nondecreasing points (x_0, x_1, …, x_{n+p+1}). Follows the treatment and notation of Weisstein, Eric W. "B-Spline." From MathWorld, a Wolfram Web Resource, http://mathworld.wolfram.com/B-Spline.html. public sealed class BSpline Inheritance object BSpline Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A linear B-spline has p = 1, a quadratic one p = 2, a cubic one p = 3; n + 1 is the number of control points. The basis functions are defined recursively: N_{i,0}(x) is 1 if x_i ≤ x < x_{i+1} and 0 otherwise, and N_{i,p}(x) = N_{i,p−1}(x)·(x − x_i)/(x_{i+p} − x_i) + N_{i+1,p−1}(x)·(x_{i+p+1} − x)/(x_{i+p+1} − x_{i+1}). Immutable: the knots are copied. On a repeated knot one of those spans is zero, and QuantLib's recursion divides by it, giving NaN, so a cubic B-spline fit on knots with a repeat throws. Here a term whose span is zero reads 0, the Cox–de Boor convention, the limit of QuantLib's own values as the repeated knots close up; on distinct knots it is QuantLib's arithmetic and bits. A documented divergence. Exceptions ArgumentNullException knots is null. ArgumentException The degree is below 1, n is below 1 or below the degree, the number of knots isn't p + n + 2, or the knots decrease. Methods Evaluate(int, double) The i-th basis function at a point. public double Evaluate(int i, double x) Parameters i int The basis function's index, from 0 to n. x double The point. Returns double N_{i,p}(x). Exceptions ArgumentOutOfRangeException The index is negative or greater than n.

Each row is a natural cubic spline in x (Spline, not monotonic, a second derivative of 0 at both ends), built with the interpolation; a value is the natural cubic spline in y through the rows' values at x, built at each call, each spline extrapolating outside its range. The x and y values must be sorted. The five derivatives follow QuantLib's: DerivativeX(double, double) and SecondDerivativeX(double, double) differentiate the spline in x through the values at the x nodes, DerivativeY(double, double) and SecondDerivativeY(double, double) the spline in y of the value, and DerivativeXY(double, double) the spline in x of DerivativeY(double, double) at the nodes. As in QuantLib, they skip the range check Evaluate(double, double, bool) makes, and the spline they differentiate refuses a point outside its own range, whatever the extrapolation flag. A matrix larger than the grid is read in its first rows and columns, as QuantLib reads it; a smaller one, which QuantLib reads past its end, is refused. api/NanoQL.Numerics.ClaytonCopula.html.title: Class ClaytonCopula | nanoql
api/NanoQL.Numerics.ClaytonCopula.html.summary: Class ClaytonCopula Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The Clayton copula, C(x, y) = max(x^−θ + y^−θ − 1, 0)^(−1/θ). public sealed class ClaytonCopula Inheritance object ClaytonCopula Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable. On the unit square's edges it returns the boundary values, C(u, 0) = C(0, v) = 0, C(u, 1) = u and C(1, v) = v, before its formula, as every copula here does. Below θ 0 the base is taken at 0 before the power, the copula's definition, where QuantLib takes the maximum after it, so a negative base gives NaN or, at an even exponent, a positive value: at θ −0.5, C(0.2, 0.2) 0 for QuantLib's 0.0111. Near independence, |θ| below 0.1, the base is computed as (x^−θ − 1) + (y^−θ − 1) by expm1 and the power by log1p, where QuantLib's cancels (4e-8 relative at θ 1e-8, on points within 1e-8 of the edges); above θ 0.1 QuantLib's formula, but where x^−θ or y^−θ would overflow (θ·(−ln min(x, y)) above 709, where QuantLib's gives 0): there m(1 + (m/M)^θ − m^θ)^(−1/θ), with m and M the smaller and larger argument. Each form is within 5e-15 relative of a 50-digit evaluation of QuantLib's formula on points within 1e-12 of the edges; at θ −1 the copula is max(x + y − 1, 0), whose cancellation near x + y = 1 no form avoids. Standard (μ/μ_w, λ)-CMA-ES with positive recombination weights. Reference: N. Hansen, "The CMA Evolution Strategy: A Tutorial", 2016, arXiv:1604.00772. Immutable: each minimization draws from a new Mersenne Twister built from the seed, so a second minimization repeats the first's draws, where QuantLib's optimizer keeps its generator and continues its stream (Divergences/CmaesTests.cs). The samples are ranked by a stable sort of their costs, so equal costs keep QuantLib's order up to a population of 32 (MSVC's insertion sort) and their own beyond, where MSVC's introsort reorders them. A NaN cost is refused before the ranking, where QuantLib's sort reads it and breaks its ordering. api/NanoQL.Numerics.ConvexMonotoneInterp.summary: Class ConvexMonotoneInterpolation Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The convex-monotone interpolation of instantaneous forward rates from their section averages: QuantLib's ConvexMonotoneInterpolation, Hagan and West's method ("Interpolation Methods for Curve Construction", Applied Mathematical Finance 13(2), 2006) with QuantLib's enhancements. public sealed class ConvexMonotoneInterpolation : Interpolation Inheritance object Extrapolator Interpolation ConvexMonotoneInterpolation Inherited Members Interpolation.XValues() Interpolation.YValues() Interpolation.IsInRange(double) Interpolation.Evaluate(double, bool) Interpolation.Primitive(double, bool) Interpolation.Derivative(double, bool) Interpolation.SecondDerivative(double, bool) Interpolation.XMin Interpolation.XMax Extrapolator.AllowsExtrapolation object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Extension Methods ExtrapolatorExtensions.DisableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) ExtrapolatorExtensions.EnableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) Remarks The y values are the sections' averages, the first ignored: the section from xi−1 to xi averages yi, and the primitive at xi is the sum of the sections' averages times their lengths. A monotonicity of 1 and a quadraticity of 0 is Hagan and West's basic method; a monotonicity below 1 or a quadraticity above 0 gives smoother curves. Forcing positivity keeps the forwards non-negative where the averages are. Past the last node the interpolation is flat at its last value; with a flat final period, the last section is flat at its average, as the local bootstrap builds the curve a section at a time. Immutable: the section helpers are computed at construction. The derivatives aren't implemented, as in QuantLib. Three fixes of QuantLib's sections (documented divergences in Divergences/ConvexMonotoneTests.cs): a section's quadratic is split to stay non-negative only where it dips below 0 inside the section, and a discriminant that rounds a hair below 0 is taken as 0, so every section keeps its average and the forwards their continuity; and positivity isn't forced on a section whose average is negative, nor is an end forward beside one floored at 0, so a negative-rate curve keeps its averages. Everywhere else QuantLib's values, bit for bit. Local schemes (fourth-order, parabolic, modified parabolic, Fritsch–Butland, Akima, Kruger) use only the values near xi to calculate each derivative there; the non-local spline schemes, with different boundary conditions, use all the values and solve a linear system. Local schemes produce C¹ interpolants, the spline schemes C² ones. Hyman's monotonicity-constrained filter is also implemented: it can be applied to every scheme to ensure that, in the regions of local monotonicity of the input (three successive increasing or decreasing values), the interpolating cubic remains monotonic. A cubic already monotonic is left unchanged. For the C² interpolants the filter ensures local monotonicity at the expense of the second derivative, which is no longer continuous where it applies. Some non-linear schemes (modified parabolic, Fritsch–Butland, Kruger) are locally monotonic as they stand; the others must be filtered, at the expense of their linearity. See R. L. Dougherty, A. Edelman and J. M. Hyman, "Nonnegativity-, Monotonicity-, or Convexity-Preserving Cubic Spline and Quintic Hermite Interpolation", Mathematics of Computation, v. 52, n. 186, April 1989, pp. 471-494. Not yet implemented in QuantLib: the fourth-order and modified parabolic schemes, and the periodic boundary condition. Immutable: the coefficients are computed at construction, and UpdateLeftConditionValue(double) and UpdateRightConditionValue(double) return a new interpolation, where QuantLib's change the boundary value for a later update(). An extension point, as in QuantLib: the named interpolations derive from it. api/NanoQL.Numerics.CumulativeStudentDis.summary: Class CumulativeStudentDistribution Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The Student t-distribution's cumulative distribution function for n degrees of freedom (see mathworld.wolfram.com): F(x) = ½ + ½·sgn(x)·[I(1; n/2, ½) − I(n/(n + x²); n/2, ½)], I(z; a, b) the regularized incomplete beta function. public sealed class CumulativeStudentDistribution Inheritance object CumulativeStudentDistribution Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable. QuantLib's formula loses digits in two places, which nanoql computes otherwise (Divergences/StudentDistributionTests.cs). Where n/(n + x²) exceeds ½, near the centre and everywhere as n grows, its incomplete beta takes its complement at 1 − n/(n + x²), losing the argument's digits (6.4e-10 relative at n 1e6 and 4.6e-9 at 1e8, at x 1.5); there nanoql takes I(x²/(n + x²); ½, n/2), the same value by the beta function's reflection, its argument computed directly. And below the centre, ½ − ½·(1 − I) cancels as F(x) falls, to 0 where F(x) is below about 1e-16 (at n 30, x −30); there nanoql takes ½·I(n/(n + x²); n/2, ½), or its reflection's complement, directly. Both routes take Boost's regularised incomplete beta (ibeta, ported for the quantile), as QuantLib's own loses digits in its log-gamma prefactor as n grows (7.6e-10 at n 1e6 with the complementary argument alone): within 8e-14 relative of a high-precision evaluation for n from 1 to 1e9. At n 1 below the centre Boost's complement is its arcsine form on 1 − z, which rounds 1 − z, so there nanoql takes ½·(1 − I(z; ½, ½)), F lying in [¼, ½]: within 2.9e-14 of the Cauchy distribution's ½ + atan(x)/π, where QuantLib's value is 0.5 at x −1e-8, 6.4e-9 off. QuantLib's formula above the centre where n/(n + x²) is at most ½, bit for bit. Three basic crossover types are also available. Immutable, with QuantLib's defaults: each With… method returns a modified copy, where QuantLib's setters change the configuration and return it. api/NanoQL.Numerics.FactorReductionFunct.title: Class FactorReductionFunctions | nanoql
api/NanoQL.Numerics.FactorReductionFunct.summary: Class FactorReductionFunctions Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The reduction of a correlation matrix to a single factor's loadings by the principal factor iteration (Harman, Modern Factor Analysis, 1976, chapter 9): the diagonal replaced by the communalities, the loadings the principal eigenvector scaled by the root of its eigenvalue, until they settle. public static class FactorReductionFunctions Inheritance object FactorReductionFunctions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks It assumes the reduction is possible: where the dependence isn't one factor's, loadings may exceed 1. QuantLib reads the loadings from the matrix's row at the largest eigenvalue's index, the input's first row, where its own commented-out eigenvectors belong: on a one-factor matrix with loadings (0.9, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3, 0.8) it returns (0.546, 0.63, 0.45, 0.27, 0.72). Here the loadings are the principal eigenvector, its sign the decomposition's (the first loading positive), times the root of its eigenvalue, on the diagonal patched with their squares, which returns the one-factor matrix's loadings exactly; the relative change that stops the iteration divides by the previous loading's magnitude, so a negative loading converges too, and a loading of exactly 0 counts its successor's magnitude, where 0/0 would stop the iteration at its first pass whenever the first loading is 0. And QuantLib refuses a reduction that converges on its last allowed pass; here only one that hasn't converged is refused (a documented divergence). A matrix below 2 × 2, where QuantLib's initial guess divides by 0, is refused. Methods FactorReduction(Matrix, int) The single factor's loadings of the correlation matrix mtrx. public static ImmutableArray<double> FactorReduction(Matrix mtrx, int maxIters = 25) Parameters mtrx Matrix The correlation matrix, square, at least 2 × 2; it is copied. maxIters int The most iterations after the first. Returns ImmutableArray<double> The loadings, one per variable. Exceptions ArgumentNullException mtrx is null. ArgumentException mtrx isn't square, or is below 2 × 2. ArgumentOutOfRangeException maxIters is negative. NanoQLException The loadings haven't converged after the iterations allowed.

api/NanoQL.Numerics.FaureRsg.html.summary: Class FaureRsg Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The Faure low-discrepancy sequence generator. It is based on existing Fortran and C algorithms to calculate the Pascal matrix and gray transforms: E. Thiemard, Economic generation of low-discrepancy sequences with a b-ary gray code; Algorithms 659, 647, http://www.netlib.org/toms/647, http://www.netlib.org/toms/659. [WorkingType] public sealed class FaureRsg : IRsg Inheritance object FaureRsg Implements IRsg Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A mutable working type: each draw changes it, and it is not thread-safe. A draw returns a view of its buffer, valid until its next draw. The correctness of the returned values is tested by reproducing known good values. Its integers are QuantLib's long under MSVC, 32 bits wide, which also sets the number of base-b digits the sequence carries, ⌊ln(2^31 − 1)/ln b⌋: 30 in two dimensions (base 2), 4 in a hundred (base 101). Once its counter carries past them the generator refuses ("Error processing Faure sequence."), after 2^30 − 1 draws in base 2 and 101^4 − 1 in base 101, where QuantLib built with a 64-bit long (Linux) draws other numbers and refuses after about 10^18. These are the Python wheel's numbers. Below |θ| 1.7 nanoql takes their Taylor series to 14 terms (α = 2θ³/45 − 2θ⁵/315 + …, β = 2/3 + 2θ²/15 − …, γ = 4/3 − 2θ²/15 + …), within 3.3e-16 of a 50-digit evaluation there, and Simpson's rule at θ 0; from 1.7, where they are within 1e-15 of it, QuantLib's closed forms, bit for bit. A documented divergence. Zero intervals are refused: QuantLib accepts them and divides by 0. QuantLib's integrator counts none of its evaluations and sets no error estimate, so a result's number of evaluations is 0 and its error null. api/NanoQL.Numerics.FractionalKernelAppr.summary: Class FractionalKernelApproximation Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The sum-of-exponentials approximation Kⁿ(t) = Σ cᵢ e^{−xᵢt} of the fractional kernel K(t) = t^{α−1}/Γ(α), α in (0, 1]. public sealed class FractionalKernelApproximation Inheritance object FractionalKernelApproximation Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks K is completely monotone, K(t) = ∫₀^∞ e^{−xt} μ(dx) with μ(dx) = x^{−α}/(Γ(α)Γ(1 − α)) dx (Abi Jaber), and a partition 0 = η₀ < η₁ < … < ηₙ gives non-negative cᵢ and xᵢ, so a completely monotone Kⁿ, by collapsing each interval's mass onto its barycentre: cᵢ = ∫ μ(dx) and xᵢ = (1/cᵢ) ∫ x μ(dx) over [ηᵢ₋₁, ηᵢ]. api/NanoQL.Numerics.FrankCopula.html.summary: Class FrankCopula Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The Frank copula, C(x, y) = −(1/θ)·ln(1 + (e^(−θx) − 1)(e^(−θy) − 1)/(e^(−θ) − 1)). public sealed class FrankCopula Inheritance object FrankCopula Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable. On the unit square's edges it returns the boundary values, C(u, 0) = C(0, v) = 0, C(u, 1) = u and C(1, v) = v, before its formula, as every copula here does. QuantLib's formula loses digits wherever the logarithm's argument nears 1 (near the edges, about 1e-7 relative at every θ on points 1e-8 from them, and everywhere as θ nears 0) and overflows from |θ| about 700; nanoql writes z = (e^(−θx) − 1)(e^(−θy) − 1)/(e^(−θ) − 1) with expm1, the quotient first, and the logarithm with log1p. Above θ 0, where z falls to −1/2 or below, 1 + z is (A + B)/(1 − e^(−θ)) with A = e^(−θx)(1 − e^(−θy)) and B = e^(−θy)(1 − e^(−θ(1 − y))), two positive terms, summed in logarithms; below θ 0 the quotient takes the larger argument, at most 1, so it stays normal where the other factor is small; and below θ −700 the logarithm of z is summed from its factors'. Within 6e-16 relative of a high-precision evaluation of QuantLib's formula on points within 1e-12 of the edges at θ from 1e-8 to 2000, and within 2e-15 at θ from −1e-8 to −30, the error growing as |θ|·ε below that (5.6e-14 at θ −700, 1.8e-13 at −2000), the rounding of θx's own amplification. api/NanoQL.Numerics.GMRES.html.title: Class GMRES | nanoql
api/NanoQL.Numerics.GMRES.html.summary: Class GMRES Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The generalized minimal residual method for a linear system A·x = b, A given as its product with a vector, with an optional preconditioner. References: Y. Saad, Iterative methods for sparse linear systems (1996), http://www-users.cs.umn.edu/~saad/books.html; R. Barrett et al., Templates for the Solution of Linear Systems: Building Blocks for Iterative Methods, 2nd edition, SIAM (1994), http://www.netlib.org/templates/templates.pdf; C. Kanzow, Numerik linearer Gleichungssysteme, chapter 6. public sealed class GMRES Inheritance object GMRES Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks QuantLib stops at a breakdown, the new Krylov vector's norm below ε², without rotating the column that found it, and solves with the columns before it (gmres.cpp:101-131). At the first step there are none: the back-substitution writes before its array, undefined (the process crashes on diag(2, 3) with b = (1, 0), an eigenvector). At a later step the column dropped turns a solved system into a refusal: with A = diag(1, 1, 3, 3) and b = (1, 1, 1, 1), the vector is exactly zero at the second step, and solve throws "could not converge" where solveWithRestart(5) returns (1, 1, 1/3, 1/3). Here, as the method defines the breakdown, the Krylov space holds the solution: the column is rotated and the system solved with it. A documented divergence. A restart count of zero is refused: QuantLib's bound restart - 1 wraps to unlimited restarts (gmres.cpp:54), where every positive count bounds them, and it refuses a zero bound on the iterations. Constructors GMRES(Func<Vector, Vector>, int, double, Func<Vector, Vector>?) Initializes a new instance of the GMRES class. public GMRES(Func<Vector, Vector> A, int maxIter, double relTol, Func<Vector, Vector>? preConditioner = null) Parameters A Func<Vector, Vector> The matrix's product with a vector. maxIter int The maximum number of steps, positive. relTol double The tolerance on the residual's norm relative to the right-hand side's. preConditioner Func<Vector, Vector> The preconditioner's product with a vector, or null for none. Exceptions ArgumentNullException A is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException maxIter is negative. ArgumentException maxIter is zero. Methods Solve(Vector, Vector?) Solves A·x = b in at most the maximum number of steps. public GMRESResult Solve(Vector b, Vector? x0 = null) Parameters b Vector The right-hand side. x0 Vector The initial guess, or null or empty for zero. Returns GMRESResult The solution, with the relative residual after each step. Exceptions ArgumentNullException b is null. NanoQLException The last residual doesn't meet the tolerance. SolveWithRestart(int, Vector, Vector?) Solves A·x = b, restarting from the last solution at most restart − 1 times while the residual doesn't meet the tolerance. public GMRESResult SolveWithRestart(int restart, Vector b, Vector? x0 = null) Parameters restart int The maximum number of solves, positive. b Vector The right-hand side. x0 Vector The initial guess, or null or empty for zero. Returns GMRESResult The last solution, with the relative residuals of every solve. Exceptions ArgumentNullException b is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException restart is negative. ArgumentException restart is zero. NanoQLException The last residual doesn't meet the tolerance.

api/NanoQL.Numerics.GalambosCopula.html.summary: Class GalambosCopula Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The Galambos copula, C(x, y) = xy·exp(((−ln x)^−θ + (−ln y)^−θ)^(−1/θ)). public sealed class GalambosCopula Inheritance object GalambosCopula Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable. On the unit square's edges it returns the boundary values, C(u, 0) = C(0, v) = 0, C(u, 1) = u and C(1, v) = v, before its formula, as every copula here does: QuantLib's is NaN at (0, 0). Above θ 19, where (−ln x)^−θ can overflow (from θ 19.3 at the largest x below 1, so QuantLib's is ∞ from θ about 50 on points 1e-8 from the edge), the smaller logarithm m is factored out, xy·exp(m(1 + r^θ)^(−1/θ)) with r the ratio of the two; QuantLib's formula to θ 19, where no power leaves the doubles' normal range. Where xy is below the normal range the product is formed last, and where e^(…) overflows (x and y both subnormal) as e^(… + ln x + ln y), where QuantLib's is NaN. Returns double C(x, y). Exceptions ArgumentException x or y is outside [0, 1].

api/NanoQL.Numerics.GaussKronrodAdaptive.summary: Class GaussKronrodAdaptive Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll The adaptive Gauss-Kronrod integration: the 15-point Kronrod rule against its 7-point Gauss rule on an interval, halved, each half to half the tolerance, until the two agree; more robust than the non-adaptive rule on functions that are less smooth, though singular functions need dedicated algorithms, and less efficient, since it doesn't reuse earlier points. public sealed class GaussKronrodAdaptive : Integrator Inheritance object Integrator GaussKronrodAdaptive Inherited Members Integrator.SetAbsoluteAccuracy(double) Integrator.SetMaxEvaluations(int) Integrator.Integrate(Func<double, double>, double, double) Integrator.IntegrateWithStatistics(Func<double, double>, double, double) Integrator.IntegrationSuccess(IntegrationResult) Integrator.AbsoluteAccuracy Integrator.MaxEvaluations object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks References: Gauss-Kronrod Integration (http://mathcssun1.emporia.edu/~oneilcat/ExperimentApplet3/ExperimentApplet3.html); NMS - Numerical Analysis Library (http://www.math.iastate.edu/burkardt/f_src/nms/nms.html). The correctness of the result is tested by checking it against known good values. QuantLib halves the interval by recursion, bounded only by its evaluations, so a tight tolerance overflows a default stack before the bound refuses (kronrodintegral.cpp:386-439), which in .NET ends the process uncaught. The rule iterates over an explicit stack instead, in QuantLib's order: the left half before the right, each interval's value the sum of its halves' as QuantLib's recursion adds them, and the evaluation bound checked before each split. So its values, counts and refusals are QuantLib's on a stack deep enough for QuantLib's recursion. It computes no error estimate, as QuantLib's doesn't: AbsoluteError is null. api/NanoQL.Numerics.GeneralLinearLeastSq.summary: Class GeneralLinearLeastSquares Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Assembly NanoQL.dll General linear least-squares regression: the coefficients of a linear combination of basis functions that best fits samples, through the singular value decomposition ("Numerical Recipes in C", 2nd edition, Press, Teukolsky, Vetterling, Flannery). public sealed class GeneralLinearLeastSquares Inheritance object GeneralLinearLeastSquares Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The fit is computed by Create<TX>(IReadOnlyList<TX>, IReadOnlyList<double>, IReadOnlyList<Func<TX, double>>), QuantLib's templated constructor, and the object is immutable: its members return copies. Singular values below n·ε times the largest are dropped, as QuantLib drops them. The standard errors are the modelling uncertainty times the residuals' standard deviation over n − p degrees of freedom, p the coefficients the fit estimates (the singular values it keeps: the basis' size at full rank), as R's lm computes them. QuantLib divides by n − 2 whatever the basis (generallinearleastsquares.hpp:144), which is R's only for a straight line, infinite at n = 2 and undefined at n = 1, where n − 2 wraps: a documented divergence (Divergences/LeastSquaresStandardErrorTests.cs); at p = 2 the errors are QuantLib's. Samples and values of different sizes are refused, with QuantLib's text, where QuantLib checks the values' size against itself and writes the samples past the matrix's column, or leaves it partly unset.
