api/NanoQL.Numerics.html.summary: Namespace NanoQL.Numerics Classes AbcdInterpolation The abcd interpolation between discrete points: an AbcdCalibration fitted to the volatilities by their times, interpolated by the fitted abcd Black volatility. AbcdMathFunction The abcd functional form, f(t) = (a + b·t)·e−c·t + d, in Rebonato's notation; 0 at a negative time. AdaptiveRungeKutta<T> The adaptive Runge-Kutta integrator of an ordinary differential equation f'(x) = F(x, f(x)), F from ℝ × Kⁿ to Kⁿ, K the real or the complex numbers: Cash and Karp's embedded fifth-order step, whose fourth-order error estimate sets the next step's size (Numerical Recipes in C, chapter 16.2). AkimaCubicInterpolation Cubic interpolation with Akima's first-derivative approximation; at least 4 points. AliMikhailHaqCopula The Ali-Mikhail-Haq copula, C(x, y) = xy/(1 − θ(1 − x)(1 − y)). ArmijoLineSearch The Armijo line search. ArrayFunctions The free functions of QuantLib's array.hpp over a Vector: the dot product, the norm, and the element-by-element mathematical functions, each returning a new vector. AutocovarianceFunctions Convolutions, autocovariances and autocorrelations of a sequence, by the fast Fourier transform: the data's transform, its squared modulus, and that transformed again. BFGS The Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno method (http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BFGS_method), adapted from Numerical Recipes in C, 2nd edition. BSpline The B-spline basis functions N_{i,p}(x) of degree p, i = 0, 1, …, n, over a knot vector of p + n + 2 nondecreasing points (x_0, x_1, …, x_{n+p+1}). Follows the treatment and notation of Weisstein, Eric W. "B-Spline." From MathWorld, a Wolfram Web Resource, http://mathworld.wolfram.com/B-Spline.html. BackwardFlatInterpolation Backward-flat interpolation between discrete points: on each interval (xi, xi+1] the value is yi+1, and below x0 it is y0. BackwardflatLinearInterpolation A 2-D interpolation backward flat in x and linear in y: between two x values the value is the next x value's, at an x value its own, and between two y values it is interpolated linearly. BasisIncompleteOrdered An orthonormal basis built by Gram-Schmidt from vectors added in order, each kept where it is independent of those before it. BernsteinPolynomial The Bernstein polynomials B_{i,n}(x) = C(n, i)·x^i·(1 − x)^(n−i). See Weisstein, Eric W. "Bernstein Polynomial." From MathWorld, a Wolfram Web Resource, http://mathworld.wolfram.com/BernsteinPolynomial.html. BetaFunctions The beta function and the incomplete beta function. The implementation of the algorithm was inspired by "Numerical Recipes in C", 2nd edition, Press, Teukolsky, Vetterling, Flannery, chapter 6. BiCGstab The biconjugate gradient stabilized method for a linear system A·x = b, A given as its product with a vector, with an optional preconditioner. BicubicSpline Bicubic-spline interpolation between discrete points. BilinearInterpolation Bilinear interpolation between discrete points. BinomialDistribution The binomial probability distribution: the probability of k successes in n trials of probability p. BinomialDistributionFunctions The binomial coefficients and Peizer-Pratt's second inversion. Bisection The bisection one-dimensional solver. BivariateCumulativeNormalDistributionDr78 The cumulative bivariate normal distribution by Drezner's 1978 algorithm, to six decimal places: the probability that two standard normals of correlation ρ fall below a and b. BivariateCumulativeNormalDistributionWe04DP The cumulative bivariate normal distribution by West (2004), to near double precision: the probability that two standard normals of correlation ρ fall below x and y. QuantLib's default bivariate normal. BivariateCumulativeStudentDistribution The bivariate cumulative Student t-distribution, implemented following the formulas from Dunnett, C.W. and Sobel, M. (1954). A bivariate generalization of Student t-distribution with tables for certain special cases. Biometrika 41, 153–169. BoundaryConstraint A constraint imposing all arguments to be in [low, high]. BoxMullerGaussianRng<TRng> The Gaussian random-number generator by the well-known Box-Muller transformation: normally distributed deviates with average 0.0 and standard deviation 1.0, from uniform deviates in (0, 1) supplied by TRng. BoxMullerKnuthGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's BoxMullerKnuthGaussianRng: BoxMullerGaussianRng<TRng> over KnuthUniformRng, standard Gaussian deviates. BoxMullerLecuyerGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's BoxMullerLecuyerGaussianRng: BoxMullerGaussianRng<TRng> over LecuyerUniformRng, standard Gaussian deviates. BoxMullerMersenneTwisterGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's BoxMullerMersenneTwisterGaussianRng: BoxMullerGaussianRng<TRng> over MersenneTwisterUniformRng, standard Gaussian deviates. BoxMullerXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's BoxMullerXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRng: BoxMullerGaussianRng<TRng> over Xoshiro256StarStarUniformRng, standard Gaussian deviates. Brent Brent's 1-D solver: inverse quadratic interpolation, falling back to bisection. Burley2020SobolBrownianBridgeRsg The Brownian-bridge sequence generator on Burley's scrambled Sobol sequence: each sequence a path of Burley2020SobolBrownianGenerator's, its steps' Gaussian variates one after another, the factors of each step together. Burley2020SobolRsg The Sobol sequence scrambled after Brent Burley, "Practical Hash-based Owen Scrambling", Journal of Computer Graphics Techniques, Vol. 9, No. 4, 2020: each sample's index and each dimension's integers through a nested uniform scramble seeded per group of four dimensions. CLGaussianRng<TRng> The Gaussian random-number generator by the well-known fact that the sum of 12 uniform deviates in (−0.5, 0.5) is approximately a Gaussian deviate with average 0 and standard deviation 1; the uniform deviates are supplied by TRng. CeilingTruncation Ceiling truncation: Ceiling. CentralLimitKnuthGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's CentralLimitKnuthGaussianRng: CLGaussianRng<TRng> over KnuthUniformRng, standard Gaussian deviates. CentralLimitLecuyerGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's CentralLimitLecuyerGaussianRng: CLGaussianRng<TRng> over LecuyerUniformRng, standard Gaussian deviates. CentralLimitMersenneTwisterGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's CentralLimitMersenneTwisterGaussianRng: CLGaussianRng<TRng> over MersenneTwisterUniformRng, standard Gaussian deviates. CentralLimitXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's CentralLimitXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRng: CLGaussianRng<TRng> over Xoshiro256StarStarUniformRng, standard Gaussian deviates. ChebyshevInterpolation Chebyshev interpolation on [−1, 1]: the Lagrange interpolation of values at the Chebyshev nodes (S. A. Sarra, "Chebyshev Interpolation: An Interactive Tour"). CholeskyDecompositionFunctions The Cholesky decomposition of a symmetric matrix, and the solve it gives. ClaytonCopula The Clayton copula, C(x, y) = max(x^−θ + y^−θ − 1, 0)^(−1/θ). ClosestRounding Closest rounding: Closest. Cmaes The Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES). CmaesConfiguration The CMA-ES optimizer's configuration, QuantLib's Cmaes::Configuration. ComparisonFunctions QuantLib's floating-point comparisons (comparison.hpp), after Knuth's advice. CompositeConstraint A constraint enforcing both given sub-constraints: its bounds are the tighter of theirs. ConjugateGradient The multi-dimensional conjugate gradient method. Constraint The base class of an optimization's constraints on its parameters. ConvergenceStatistics<TStats, TRule> A one-dimensional statistics with a convergence table: the mean, stored each time the number of samples reaches the next of the sampling rule's sizes. ConvexMonotoneInterpolation The convex-monotone interpolation of instantaneous forward rates from their section averages: QuantLib's ConvexMonotoneInterpolation, Hagan and West's method ("Interpolation Methods for Curve Construction", Applied Mathematical Finance 13(2), 2006) with QuantLib's enhancements. CostFunction The cost function of an optimization problem: a vector of values, and the cost they give. CovarianceDecomposition A covariance matrix decomposed into its variances, standard deviations and correlation matrix. Only the covariance's lower part is used. CubicInterpolation Cubic interpolation between discrete points: on each interval, the cubic matching the values at its ends and the first derivatives there, which the derivative approximation gives. CubicNaturalSpline The natural cubic spline: the spline approximation with a zero second derivative at both ends. CubicSplineOvershootingMinimization1 The cubic spline minimizing the overshooting of the first derivative. CubicSplineOvershootingMinimization2 The cubic spline minimizing the overshooting of the second derivative. CumulativeBinomialDistribution The cumulative binomial distribution: the probability of at most k successes in n trials of probability p, through the incomplete beta function. CumulativeChiSquareDistribution The cumulative chi-squared distribution with df degrees of freedom: P(df/2, x/2), the gamma CDF. CumulativeGammaDistribution The cumulative gamma distribution of shape a and unit scale: the regularized lower incomplete gamma function P(a, x), by its series below a + 1 and its continued fraction from there. CumulativeNormalDistribution The cumulative normal distribution: for average μ and standard deviation σ, the probability of a value below x, from the error function, with the normal density as its derivative. CumulativePoissonDistribution The cumulative Poisson distribution: the probability of an integer up to k for a mean μ, 1 − P(k + 1, μ), from the incomplete gamma function. CumulativeStudentDistribution The Student t-distribution's cumulative distribution function for n degrees of freedom (see mathworld.wolfram.com): F(x) = ½ + ½·sgn(x)·[I(1; n/2, ½) − I(n/(n + x²); n/2, ½)], I(z; a, b) the regularized incomplete beta function. DifferentialEvolution The differential evolution optimization method. DifferentialEvolutionConfiguration The differential evolution's configuration, QuantLib's DifferentialEvolution::Configuration. DiscrepancyStatistics Statistics of N-dimensional samples with the L² discrepancy: SequenceStatistics with Discrepancy(), updated with each sample added. DiscreteSimpsonIntegral Simpson's rule on given points, unevenly spaced: the integral of a function known at abscissas x, each pair of intervals by the parabola through its three points, an odd last interval by the trapezoid rule. DiscreteSimpsonIntegrator Simpson's rule on a fixed number of evenly spaced evaluations of a function over [a, b], the ends included, an odd number of intervals closed by QuantLib's end correction. DiscreteTrapezoidIntegral The trapezoid rule on given points: the integral of a function known at abscissas x, ½ Σ (x_{i+1} − x_i)(f_i + f_{i+1}). DiscreteTrapezoidIntegrator The trapezoid rule on a fixed number of evenly spaced evaluations of a function over [a, b], the ends included. DownRounding Down-rounding: Down. EndCriteria The criteria that end an optimization: the maximum number of iterations, and the minimum number of iterations around a stationary point; a stationary point of x, the independent variable; a stationary value of y = f(x), the dependent variable; and a stationary gradient. ErrorFunction The error function, erf(x) = (2/√π) ∫₀ˣ exp(−t²) dt, from FDLIBM's erf; it gives the cumulative normal distribution. ExpSinhIntegral The exp-sinh quadrature of Boost.Math, a rapidly convergent integration scheme for holomorphic integrands on half-infinite intervals. The tolerance is used against the error estimate for the L1 norm of the integral. Expm1Functions The complex versions of expm1 and log1p, accurate near zero. ExpmFunctions The matrix exponential by the ordinary differential equations method (Moler and Van Loan 1978, "Nineteen Dubious Ways to Compute the Exponential of a Matrix"): each column of exp(t·M) solves x' = M·x from a unit vector, by adaptive Runge-Kutta. ExponentialIntegralsFunctions The sine, cosine and exponential integrals, QuantLib's ExponentialIntegral namespace: Si and Ci, real and complex; E1 and Ei, complex. References: B. Rowe et al., "GALSIM: The modular galaxy image simulation toolkit", https://arxiv.org/abs/1407.7676; V. Pegoraro, P. Slusallek, "On the Evaluation of the Complex-Valued Exponential Integral", https://www.sci.utah.edu/~vpegorar/research/2011_JGT.pdf. Extrapolator The base class of objects that may allow extrapolation. ExtrapolatorExtensions Extrapolator's modifiers, which return a modified copy of the receiver, keeping its static type, where QuantLib's change the object. FactorReductionFunctions The reduction of a correlation matrix to a single factor's loadings by the principal factor iteration (Harman, Modern Factor Analysis, 1976, chapter 9): the diagonal replaced by the communalities, the loadings the principal eigenvector scaled by the root of its eigenvalue, until they settle. Factorial Factorial numbers: n! and ln(n!), tabulated up to 27! and from the gamma function above. FalsePosition The false-position one-dimensional solver. FarlieGumbelMorgensternCopula The Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern copula, C(x, y) = xy + θxy(1 − x)(1 − y). FastFourierTransform The fast Fourier transform of order k: the radix-2 Cooley-Tukey transform of 2ᵏ points. FaureRsg The Faure low-discrepancy sequence generator. It is based on existing Fortran and C algorithms to calculate the Pascal matrix and gray transforms: E. Thiemard, Economic generation of low-discrepancy sequences with a b-ary gray code; Algorithms 659, 647, http://www.netlib.org/toms/647, http://www.netlib.org/toms/659. FilonIntegral Filon's sine and cosine integrals: the integral of f(x)·sin(tx) or f(x)·cos(tx) over [a, b] on a given even number of intervals (Abramowitz and Stegun, pp. 890-891). FiniteDifferenceNewtonSafe The safe (bracketed) Newton 1-D solver with finite-difference derivatives: Newton's steps on the slope between the last two evaluations, falling back to bisection. FlatExtrapolator A 1-D interpolation extrapolated flat: a decorator that reads another interpolation inside its range and its boundary values outside it. FlatExtrapolator2D A 2-D interpolation extrapolated flat: a decorator that reads another interpolation at the point moved onto its grid's edges. FloorTruncation Floor truncation: Floor. ForwardFlatInterpolation Forward-flat interpolation between discrete points: on each interval [xi, xi+1) the value is yi, and from the last x on it is the last y. FourierIntegration The Fourier integration of characteristic-function pricing engines: a quadrature or an adaptive integrator, with the change of variables that maps the semi-infinite integration range onto the domain the algorithm expects. The decay rate c_∞ of the characteristic function along the integration contour drives the mapping. FractionalAdamsFunctions The free functions of QuantLib's fractionaladams.hpp. FractionalAdams<T> The fractional Adams-Bashforth-Moulton predictor-corrector scheme for the fractional initial value problem D^α y(t) = f(t, y(t)), y(0) = y₀, α in (0, 1], D^α the Caputo derivative; at α = 1, the classical one-step Adams-Bashforth-Moulton method. FractionalKernelApproximation The sum-of-exponentials approximation Kⁿ(t) = Σ cᵢ e^{−xᵢt} of the fractional kernel K(t) = t^{α−1}/Γ(α), α in (0, 1]. FrankCopula The Frank copula, C(x, y) = −(1/θ)·ln(1 + (e^(−θx) − 1)(e^(−θy) − 1)/(e^(−θ) − 1)). FritschButlandCubic Cubic interpolation with the Fritsch–Butland first-derivative approximation and Hyman's monotonicity filter. FritschButlandLogCubic Log-cubic interpolation with the Fritsch–Butland first-derivative approximation of the logarithms. FrobeniusCostFunction The cost of a parametrized pseudo-root against a target correlation matrix in the Frobenius norm: the strict lower triangle of P·Pᵀ − target as the values, their squares' sum as the value. FunctionalFunctions Functionals and combinators not included in the standard library. GMRES The generalized minimal residual method for a linear system A·x = b, A given as its product with a vector, with an optional preconditioner. References: Y. Saad, Iterative methods for sparse linear systems (1996), http://www-users.cs.umn.edu/~saad/books.html; R. Barrett et al., Templates for the Solution of Linear Systems: Building Blocks for Iterative Methods, 2nd edition, SIAM (1994), http://www.netlib.org/templates/templates.pdf; C. Kanzow, Numerik linearer Gleichungssysteme, chapter 6. GalambosCopula The Galambos copula, C(x, y) = xy·exp(((−ln x)^−θ + (−ln y)^−θ)^(−1/θ)). GammaFunction The gamma function, Γ(z) = ∫₀^∞ t^(z−1) e^(−t) dt, and its logarithm. GaussChebyshev2ndIntegration The Gauss-Chebyshev integration of the second kind of ∫₋₁¹ f(x) dx, with weight w(x) = (1 − x²)^(½). GaussChebyshev2ndIntegrator The integral over [a, b] by the Gauss-Chebyshev (second kind) quadrature of a given order, mapped from [−1, 1]: QuantLib's detail::GaussianQuadratureIntegrator<GaussChebyshev2ndIntegration>. It counts no evaluation, as QuantLib's doesn't. GaussChebyshev2ndPolynomial The Gauss-Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind: Jacobi's with α = β = ½, weight (1 − x²)^(½) on [−1, 1]. GaussChebyshevIntegration The Gauss-Chebyshev integration of ∫₋₁¹ f(x) dx, with weight w(x) = (1 − x²)^(−½). GaussChebyshevIntegrator The integral over [a, b] by the Gauss-Chebyshev quadrature of a given order, mapped from [−1, 1]: QuantLib's detail::GaussianQuadratureIntegrator<GaussChebyshevIntegration>. It counts no evaluation, as QuantLib's doesn't. GaussChebyshevPolynomial The Gauss-Chebyshev polynomial: Jacobi's with α = β = −½, weight (1 − x²)^(−½) on [−1, 1]. GaussGegenbauerIntegration The Gauss-Gegenbauer integration of ∫₋₁¹ f(x) dx, with weight w(x) = (1 − x²)^(λ − ½). GaussGegenbauerPolynomial The Gauss-Gegenbauer polynomial: Jacobi's with α = β = λ − ½, weight (1 − x²)^(λ − ½) on [−1, 1]. GaussHermiteIntegration The generalized Gauss-Hermite integration of ∫ f(x) dx over ℝ, with weight w(x; μ) = |x|^(2μ)·e^(−x²), μ > −0.5. GaussHermitePolynomial The generalized Gauss-Hermite polynomial, with weight w(x; μ) = |x|^(2μ)·e^(−x²) on ℝ, μ > −0.5. GaussHyperbolicIntegration The Gauss hyperbolic integration of ∫ f(x) dx over ℝ, with weight w(x) = 1/cosh(x). GaussHyperbolicPolynomial The Gauss hyperbolic polynomial, with weight w(x) = 1/cosh(x) on ℝ. GaussJacobiIntegration The Gauss-Jacobi integration of ∫₋₁¹ f(x) dx, with weight w(x; α, β) = (1 − x)^α·(1 + x)^β. GaussJacobiPolynomial The Gauss-Jacobi polynomial, with weight w(x; α, β) = (1 − x)^α·(1 + x)^β on [−1, 1], α, β > −1. Unsealed: QuantLib's Legendre, Chebyshev and Gegenbauer polynomials derive from it. GaussKronrodAdaptive The adaptive Gauss-Kronrod integration: the 15-point Kronrod rule against its 7-point Gauss rule on an interval, halved, each half to half the tolerance, until the two agree; more robust than the non-adaptive rule on functions that are less smooth, though singular functions need dedicated algorithms, and less efficient, since it doesn't reuse earlier points. GaussKronrodNonAdaptive The non-adaptive Gauss-Kronrod integration: QuantLib's 10-, 21-, 43- and 87-point rules in succession, each reusing its predecessors' points, until an estimate is within the absolute or the relative accuracy; for fast integration of smooth functions. GaussLaguerreCosinePolynomial The Gauss-Laguerre cosine polynomial: orthogonal under the weight w(x; u) = e^(−x)·(1 + cos(ux))/m₀ on [0, ∞), m₀ = 1 + 1/(1 + u²) normalising it, for the Gaussian quadrature of ∫₀^∞ f(x) dx. GaussLaguerreIntegration The generalized Gauss-Laguerre integration of ∫₀^∞ f(x) dx, with weight w(x; s) = x^s·e^(−x), s > −1. GaussLaguerrePolynomial The generalized Gauss-Laguerre polynomial, with weight w(x; s) = x^s·e^(−x) on [0, ∞), s > −1. GaussLaguerreSinePolynomial The Gauss-Laguerre sine polynomial: orthogonal under the weight w(x; u) = e^(−x)·(1 + sin(ux))/m₀ on [0, ∞), m₀ = 1 + u/(1 + u²) normalising it, for the Gaussian quadrature of ∫₀^∞ f(x) dx. GaussLaguerreTrigonometricBase The base of the Gauss-Laguerre cosine and sine polynomials: the moments of e^(−x) times cos(ux) or sin(ux), by their recurrence mₙ = (2n·mₙ₋₁ − n(n − 1)·mₙ₋₂)/(1 + u²), and the factorials. GaussLegendreIntegration The Gauss-Legendre integration of ∫₋₁¹ f(x) dx, with weight w(x) = 1. GaussLegendreIntegrator The integral over [a, b] by the Gauss-Legendre quadrature of a given order, mapped from [−1, 1]: QuantLib's detail::GaussianQuadratureIntegrator<GaussLegendreIntegration>. It counts no evaluation, as QuantLib's doesn't. GaussLegendrePolynomial The Gauss-Legendre polynomial: Jacobi's with α = β = 0, weight 1 on [−1, 1]. GaussLobattoIntegral The integral of a one-dimensional function by the adaptive Gauss-Lobatto formula: W. Gander and W. Gautschi, "Adaptive Quadrature - Revisited", BIT 40(1):84-101, March 2000, after Gander's MATLAB adaptlob. GaussianCopula The Gaussian copula, C(x, y) = Φ₂(Φ⁻¹(x), Φ⁻¹(y); ρ). GaussianKernel The Gaussian kernel: the normal density of the given average and standard deviation, times √(2π). GaussianOrthogonalPolynomial An orthogonal polynomial for Gaussian quadratures, defined by the three-term recurrence P_{k+1}(x) = (x − α_k)·P_k(x) − β_k·P_{k−1}(x) and μ₀ = ∫ w(x) dx: G.H. Golub and J.H. Welsch, "Calculation of Gauss quadrature rules", Math. Comput. 23 (1969), 221-230; "Numerical Recipes in C", 2nd edition, Press, Teukolsky, Vetterling, Flannery. GaussianQuadrature A Gaussian quadrature: the nodes and weights of an orthogonal polynomial's rule of a given order, from the eigen-decomposition of its recurrence's Jacobi matrix (G.H. Golub and J.H. Welsch, "Calculation of Gauss quadrature rules", Math. Comput. 23 (1969), 221-230), and the weighted sum of a function at the nodes. GaussianStatisticsExtensions The Gaussian-assumption risk measures (value-at-risk, expected shortfall, …), from the mean and standard deviation of a statistics tool: QuantLib's GenericGaussianStatistics<Stat>, which derives from its type parameter, as C# 14 extension members over any ISummaryStatistics. GeneralLinearLeastSquares General linear least-squares regression: the coefficients of a linear combination of basis functions that best fits samples, through the singular value decomposition ("Numerical Recipes in C", 2nd edition, Press, Teukolsky, Vetterling, Flannery). GeneralStatistics A statistics tool: it accumulates a set of data and returns their statistics (mean, variance, skewness, kurtosis, error estimation, percentile, …) based on the empirical distribution, with no Gaussian assumption. GenericSequenceStatisticsExtensions The members of GenericSequenceStatistics<TStats> that need more of its type parameter than its class does, lifted over the components: the empirical risk measures, where each component's statistics keeps its samples (IEmpiricalStatistics, with the members of RiskStatisticsExtensions), and the downside variance and deviation of IncrementalStatistics, its own. QuantLib's template compiles a lifted member only where its type parameter has it; C# 14 extension members with these constraints keep that. GenericSequenceStatistics<TStats> Statistics of N-dimensional samples: each component's one-dimensional statistics, kept by a TStats per component, and the samples' covariance and correlation. GetCovarianceFunctions The free functions of QuantLib's getcovariance.hpp. GoldsteinLineSearch Goldstein and Price's line search: the step is bracketed until the Goldstein conditions hold. GumbelCopula The Gumbel copula, C(x, y) = exp(−((−ln x)^θ + (−ln y)^θ)^(1/θ)). Halley Halley's 1-D solver: Halley's steps from the guess, falling back to NewtonSafe when a step leaves the bracket. HaltonRsg The Halton low-discrepancy sequence generator. For more details see chapter 8, paragraph 2 of "Monte Carlo Methods in Finance", by Peter Jäckel. HarmonicCubic Cubic interpolation with the weighted harmonic mean as the first-derivative approximation. HarmonicLogCubic Log-cubic interpolation with the weighted harmonic mean as the first-derivative approximation of the logarithms. Histogram The histogram of a data set. The caller can specify the number of bins, the breaks, or the algorithm for determining these quantities in computing the histogram. HouseholderReflection The Householder reflection onto a unit vector e: the transformation that maps a vector a to |a|e. HouseholderTransformation The Householder transformation of a vector v: x ↦ x − 2(v·x)v. HuslerReissCopula The Hüsler-Reiss copula, C(x, y) = x^Φ(1/θ + θ/2·ln(ln x/ln y))·y^Φ(1/θ + θ/2·ln(ln y/ln x)). IncompleteGammaFunctions The regularized lower incomplete gamma function P(a, x), and its series and continued-fraction representations (incompletegamma.hpp). IncrementalStatistics A statistics tool based on incremental accumulation: it accumulates a set of data and returns their statistics (mean, variance, skewness, kurtosis, error estimation, …) from running sums, keeping no sample. IndependentCopula The independent copula, C(x, y) = x·y. Integrator The base of the one-dimensional integrators: QuantLib's absolute accuracy and maximum number of evaluations, and the integral of a function over an interval. Interpolation The base class for 1-D interpolations: interpolated values from two sequences of equal length, the discretized values of a variable and of a function of it. Interpolation2D The base class for 2-D interpolations: interpolated values from two sequences of lengths N and M, the discretized values of the x and y variables, and a matrix of the tabulated function values. InvCumulativeBurley2020SobolGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's InvCumulativeBurley2020SobolGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over Burley2020SobolRsg and InverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian low-discrepancy sequences on Burley's 2020 scrambling of Sobol's. InvCumulativeHaltonGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's InvCumulativeHaltonGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over HaltonRsg and InverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian low-discrepancy sequences. InvCumulativeKnuthGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's InvCumulativeKnuthGaussianRng: InverseCumulativeRng<TRng, TIc> over KnuthUniformRng and InverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian deviates. InvCumulativeKnuthGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's InvCumulativeKnuthGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> and InverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian pseudo-random sequences. InvCumulativeLecuyerGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's InvCumulativeLecuyerGaussianRng: InverseCumulativeRng<TRng, TIc> over LecuyerUniformRng and InverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian deviates. InvCumulativeLecuyerGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's InvCumulativeLecuyerGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> and InverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian pseudo-random sequences. InvCumulativeMersenneTwisterGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's InvCumulativeMersenneTwisterGaussianRng: InverseCumulativeRng<TRng, TIc> over MersenneTwisterUniformRng and InverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian deviates. InvCumulativeMersenneTwisterGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's InvCumulativeMersenneTwisterGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> and InverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian pseudo-random sequences. InvCumulativeSobolGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's InvCumulativeSobolGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over SobolRsg and InverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian low-discrepancy sequences. InvCumulativeXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's InvCumulativeXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRng: InverseCumulativeRng<TRng, TIc> over Xoshiro256StarStarUniformRng and InverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian deviates. InvCumulativeXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's InvCumulativeXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> and InverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian pseudo-random sequences. InverseCumulativeRng<TRng, TIc> The inverse cumulative random-number generator: it uses a uniform deviate in (0, 1), supplied by TRng, as the source of cumulative distribution values, then the inverse cumulative distribution TIc to calculate the distribution deviate. InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> The inverse cumulative random sequence generator: it uses a sequence of uniform deviates in (0, 1), supplied by TUsg, as the source of cumulative distribution values, then the inverse cumulative distribution TIc to calculate the distribution deviates. InverseCumulativeStudent The Student t-distribution's inverse cumulative distribution function for n degrees of freedom. The implementation delegates the calculation to Boost.Math's quantile, ported (NanoQL.Numerics.StudentsTFunctions). InverseNonCentralCumulativeChiSquareDistribution The inverse of the cumulative non-central chi-squared distribution: the bracket's right end doubled from df + ncp until the distribution reaches the probability, then Brent's solver within the evaluations left. KernelFunction A kernel function in the statistical sense: a nonnegative, real-valued function which integrates to one and is symmetric. An extension point. KernelInterpolation Kernel interpolation between discrete points (Hakala and Wystup, Foreign Exchange Risk, p. 256): the value at x is Σᵢ αᵢ·K(|x − xᵢ|) / Σᵢ K(|x − xᵢ|), the weights α solving y = M·α with Mᵢⱼ = K(|xᵢ − xⱼ|)/Σₖ K(|xᵢ − xₖ|). KernelInterpolation2D Two-dimensional kernel interpolation (Hakala and Wystup, Foreign Exchange Risk, p. 256): the value at X = (x, y) is Σₖ αₖ·K(‖X − Xₖ‖) / Σₖ K(‖X − Xₖ‖) over the grid's points Xₖ, the weights α solving z = M·α. KnuthUniformRng The uniform random-number generator by Knuth. For more details see Knuth, Seminumerical Algorithms, 3rd edition, Section 3.6. KnuthUniformRsg QuantLib-Python's KnuthUniformRsg: RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> over KnuthUniformRng, uniform sequences in (0, 1). KrugerCubic Cubic interpolation with Kruger's first-derivative approximation. KrugerLogCubic Log-cubic interpolation with Kruger's first-derivative approximation of the logarithms. LBFGSB Limited-memory BFGS for bound-constrained optimization (L-BFGS-B). LagrangeInterpolation Barycentric Lagrange interpolation (J.-P. Berrut and L. N. Trefethen, "Barycentric Lagrange interpolation", SIAM Review 46(3), 2004): the polynomial through every point, evaluated by the barycentric formula. LatticeRsg The rank-1 lattice-rule low-discrepancy sequence generator: its i-th point is (i·z_j/N mod 1) in each dimension j, z a generating vector (LatticeRule) and N the number of points. LatticeRule The generating vectors of the rank-1 lattice rules of Cools, Kuo and Nuyens (SIAM J. Sci. Comp., 2006), for LatticeRsg: four rules, each of 3,600 dimensions, for 2^10 to 2^20 points. LeastSquareFunction The cost function of a least-squares problem: r(x) = |f(x)|², f(x) = b − φ(x), its gradient −2 f′(x)ᵀ f(x). LeastSquareProblem A least-squares problem: a target vector b and a function φ(x) to fit to it, f(x) = b − φ(x). LecuyerUniformRng The uniform random-number generator of L'Ecuyer with added Bays-Durham shuffle (known as ran2 in Numerical Recipes). For more details see Section 7.1 of Numerical Recipes in C, 2nd Edition, Cambridge University Press (available at http://www.nr.com/). LecuyerUniformRsg QuantLib-Python's LecuyerUniformRsg: RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> over LecuyerUniformRng, uniform sequences in (0, 1). LevenbergMarquardt The Levenberg–Marquardt optimization method, minimizing the sum of the squares of the cost function's values. LineSearch The base class for line searches. LineSearchBasedMethod A line-search-based optimization method. LineSearchBasedMethodState A line-search method's state through one minimization, which QuantLib's methods keep as members across minimizations (BFGS's inverse Hessian). LinearInterpolation Linear interpolation between discrete points. LinearLeastSquaresRegression General linear least-squares regression on given basis functions: QuantLib's interface kept for backward compatibility, which QuantLib asks callers to replace with GeneralLinearLeastSquares directly. LinearRegression Linear regression, yᵢ = a₀ + a₁·xᵢ,₀ + … + aₙ·xᵢ,ₙ₋₁ + ε, by general linear least squares: QuantLib's LinearRegression, a GeneralLinearLeastSquares on the linear basis. LogCubicInterpolation Log-cubic interpolation between discrete points: the exponential of a CubicInterpolation of the logarithms of the y values, which must be positive. LogCubicNaturalSpline Log-cubic interpolation by the natural cubic spline of the logarithms. LogLinearInterpolation Log-linear interpolation between discrete points: the exponential of the linear interpolation of the logarithms of the y values, which must be positive. LogMixedLinearCubicInterpolation Log-mixed-linear-cubic interpolation between discrete points: the exponential of a MixedLinearCubicInterpolation of the logarithms of the y values, which must be positive. LogMixedLinearCubicNaturalSpline Log-mixed-linear-cubic interpolation whose cubic part is the natural cubic spline of the logarithms. LogParabolic Log-cubic interpolation with the parabolic first-derivative approximation of the logarithms. MaddockCumulativeNormal Maddock's cumulative normal distribution, Boost.Math's normal cdf: for average μ and standard deviation σ, the probability of a value below x. MarshallOlkinCopula The Marshall-Olkin copula, C(x, y) = min(y·x^(1 − a₁), x·y^(1 − a₂)). Matrix A matrix used in linear algebra, stored by rows. It implements the concept of a matrix as used in linear algebra, and is not meant to be used as a container. MatrixFunctions The free functions of QuantLib's matrix.hpp over a Matrix: the transpose, the outer product, and the inverse and determinant through Boost uBLAS's LU factorization with partial pivoting. MaxCopula The max copula, C(x, y) = min(x, y), the Fréchet-Hoeffding upper bound. MersenneTwisterUniformRng The Mersenne Twister uniform random-number generator, MT19937, of period 2^19937 − 1. MersenneTwisterUniformRsg QuantLib-Python's MersenneTwisterUniformRsg: RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> over MersenneTwisterUniformRng, uniform sequences in (0, 1). MinCopula The min copula, C(x, y) = max(x + y − 1, 0), the Fréchet-Hoeffding lower bound. MixedLinearCubicInterpolation Mixed linear/cubic interpolation between discrete points: linear before the switch point, the n-th point, and cubic from it on. MixedLinearCubicNaturalSpline Mixed linear/cubic interpolation whose cubic part is the natural cubic spline. MixedLinearFritschButlandCubic Mixed linear/cubic interpolation whose cubic part takes the Fritsch–Butland derivative approximation. MixedLinearKrugerCubic Mixed linear/cubic interpolation whose cubic part takes Kruger's derivative approximation. MixedLinearMonotonicCubicNaturalSpline Mixed linear/cubic interpolation whose cubic part is the natural cubic spline with Hyman's monotonicity filter. MixedLinearMonotonicParabolic Mixed linear/cubic interpolation whose cubic part takes the parabolic derivative approximation with Hyman's monotonicity filter. MixedLinearParabolic Mixed linear/cubic interpolation whose cubic part takes the parabolic derivative approximation. ModifiedBesselFunctions The modified Bessel functions of the first and second kind, I_ν(x) and K_ν(x), real and complex, by the series expansions in e.g. http://www.mhtlab.uwaterloo.ca/courses/me755/web_chap4.pdf; the exponentially weighted versions return the function's value times e^(−x) (I) and e^(x) (K). MomentBasedGaussianPolynomial An orthogonal polynomial defined by the moments of its distribution: the three-term recurrence's coefficients α and β computed from the moments (Golub and Welsch 1969; Morandi Cecchi and Redivo Zaglia 1993), so that a Gaussian quadrature follows from the moments alone. An extension point: a derived class gives Moment(int) and W(double). MonotonicCubicNaturalSpline The natural cubic spline with Hyman's monotonicity filter. MonotonicLogCubicNaturalSpline Log-cubic interpolation by the natural cubic spline of the logarithms, with Hyman's monotonicity filter. MonotonicLogParabolic Log-cubic interpolation with the parabolic first-derivative approximation of the logarithms and Hyman's monotonicity filter. MonotonicParabolic Cubic interpolation with the parabolic first-derivative approximation and Hyman's monotonicity filter. MoroInvCumulativeBurley2020SobolGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's MoroInvCumulativeBurley2020SobolGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over Burley2020SobolRsg and MoroInverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian low-discrepancy sequences on Burley's 2020 scrambling of Sobol's. MoroInvCumulativeHaltonGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's MoroInvCumulativeHaltonGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over HaltonRsg and MoroInverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian low-discrepancy sequences. MoroInvCumulativeKnuthGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's MoroInvCumulativeKnuthGaussianRng: InverseCumulativeRng<TRng, TIc> over KnuthUniformRng and MoroInverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian deviates. MoroInvCumulativeKnuthGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's MoroInvCumulativeKnuthGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> and MoroInverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian pseudo-random sequences. MoroInvCumulativeLecuyerGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's MoroInvCumulativeLecuyerGaussianRng: InverseCumulativeRng<TRng, TIc> over LecuyerUniformRng and MoroInverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian deviates. MoroInvCumulativeLecuyerGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's MoroInvCumulativeLecuyerGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> and MoroInverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian pseudo-random sequences. MoroInvCumulativeMersenneTwisterGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's MoroInvCumulativeMersenneTwisterGaussianRng: InverseCumulativeRng<TRng, TIc> over MersenneTwisterUniformRng and MoroInverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian deviates. MoroInvCumulativeMersenneTwisterGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's MoroInvCumulativeMersenneTwisterGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> and MoroInverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian pseudo-random sequences. MoroInvCumulativeSobolGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's MoroInvCumulativeSobolGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over SobolRsg and MoroInverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian low-discrepancy sequences. MoroInvCumulativeXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's MoroInvCumulativeXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRng: InverseCumulativeRng<TRng, TIc> over Xoshiro256StarStarUniformRng and MoroInverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian deviates. MoroInvCumulativeXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's MoroInvCumulativeXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRsg: InverseCumulativeRsg<TUsg, TIc> over RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> and MoroInverseCumulativeNormal, standard Gaussian pseudo-random sequences. MultiCubicSpline N-dimensional cubic spline interpolation between discrete points, in 1 to 15 dimensions. MultiDimGaussianIntegration The tensor product of one-dimensional Gaussian quadratures: a quadrature of the given order in each dimension, each order's built once, and the weighted sum of a function at the product's nodes. Newton The Newton 1-D solver: Newton's steps from the guess, falling back to NewtonSafe when a step leaves the bracket. NewtonSafe The safe (bracketed) Newton 1-D solver: Newton's steps, falling back to bisection. NoConstraint No constraint: every point satisfies it, and it has no bounds. NonCentralCumulativeChiSquareDistribution The cumulative non-central chi-squared distribution with df degrees of freedom and non-centrality ncp, by the series of Poisson-weighted central terms (Ding's algorithm, as R's pnchisq sums it). NonCentralCumulativeChiSquareSankaranApprox Sankaran's approximation of the cumulative non-central chi-squared distribution, through the normal distribution. NonLinearLeastSquare Non-linear least squares: min r(x) over x ∈ Rⁿ, r(x) = |f(x)|² for f(x) = b − φ(x), by an optimization method (by default the conjugate gradient), under a constraint. NonLinearLeastSquareResults The results of a non-linear least-squares fit, QuantLib's NonLinearLeastSquare inspectors. NonhomogeneousBoundaryConstraint A constraint imposing the i-th argument to be in [lowᵢ, highᵢ], for every i. NormalDistribution The normal distribution's density: for average μ and standard deviation σ, f(x) = exp(−(x − μ)²/(2σ²)) / (σ√(2π)), with its first derivative. OptimizationMethod The base class of constrained optimization methods. OrthogonalProjections Given vectors w_i, the vectors x_i with x_i orthogonal to every w_j but w_i and ⟨x_i, w_i⟩ = ⟨w_i, w_i⟩: Gram-Schmidt on the others, then the projection onto their orthogonal space, each vector valid where its multiplier is below the cut-off and the others independent to the tolerance. Parabolic Cubic interpolation with the parabolic first-derivative approximation. ParametersTransformation A transformation of an optimization's parameters, and its inverse: an extension point, as in QuantLib, for the calibrations that optimize over transformed parameters. PascalTriangle Pascal's triangle: the binomial coefficients C(n, k) of each order n. PlackettCopula The Plackett copula, C(x, y) = (s − √(s² − 4xyθ(θ − 1)))/(2(θ − 1)), s = 1 + (θ − 1)(x + y). PoissonDistribution The Poisson distribution: the probability of an integer k for a mean μ. PolynomialFunction A polynomial f(t) = Σᵢ cᵢ·tⁱ, i from 0 to n, with its derivative and primitive. PositiveConstraint A constraint imposing positivity on all arguments. PrimeNumbers The prime numbers, by index: 2, 3, 5, 7, … Taken from "Monte Carlo Methods in Finance", by Peter Jäckel. Problem A constrained optimization problem: a cost function, a constraint and an initial value. ProblemResults The results of a minimization: what QuantLib's minimize leaves in the Problem it changes, and the end criterion it returns. ProblemState The working state of a minimization: QuantLib's Problem, with its cost function and constraint, its current value, and the function value, gradient norm and evaluation counts a method leaves in it. ProjectedConstraint A constraint on the free parameters of a Projection: a constraint on all the parameters, tested and bounded with the fixed ones included. ProjectedCostFunction A cost function of a subset of another's parameters, the others fixed: the cost function evaluated at the fixed values with the free ones replaced. Projection A parameter projection: a set of parameters, some of them fixed, mapped to its free parameters and back. PseudoSqrtFunctions The pseudo square root of a real symmetric matrix, and its rank-reduced form. QRDecompositionFunctions The QR decomposition and the least-squares solve built on MINPACK's qrfac and qrsolv (http://www.netlib.org/minpack): Householder transformations with optional column pivoting. QRDecompositionResult A QR decomposition with column pivoting, A·P = Q·R: what QuantLib's qrDecomposition writes into the caller's matrices and returns. Quadratic The quadratic a x² + b x + c: its value, turning point, discriminant and real roots. RandomSequenceGenerator The members of QuantLib's RandomSequenceGenerator<RNG> that need more of their generator than RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> does: C++ instantiates only the members a caller uses, so each is a generic method here, with its own constraint. RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> A random sequence generator based on a pseudo-random number generator TRng: each sequence is the generator's next Dimension draws. RandomizedLDS QuantLib's seed constructors of RandomizedLDS<TLds, TPrng>, which build its generators from seeds: C++ instantiates them only where a caller uses them, so each is a generic method here, with its own constraints. Its pseudo-random generator is QuantLib's default, a RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng>. RandomizedLDS<TLds, TPrng> The randomized (random shift) low-discrepancy sequence: it random-shifts a uniform low-discrepancy sequence of dimension N by adding, modulo 1 in each coordinate, a pseudo-random uniform deviate in (0, 1)^N. It is used for implementing randomized quasi-Monte Carlo. Ranlux3UniformRng QuantLib's Ranlux3UniformRng, Ranlux64UniformRng<223, 24>: the "luxury" uniform random-number generator keeping 24 of every 223 draws of its engine, where any theoretically possible correlations have a very small chance of being observed. Ranlux4UniformRng QuantLib's Ranlux4UniformRng, Ranlux64UniformRng<389, 24>: the "luxury" uniform random-number generator keeping 24 of every 389 draws of its engine, the highest possible luxury. Ranlux64UniformRng M. Luescher's "luxury" uniform random-number generator, at the luxury level its derived class sets: Ranlux3UniformRng (any theoretically possible correlations have a very small chance of being observed) or Ranlux4UniformRng (the highest possible luxury). RichardsonExtrapolation Richardson extrapolation, a sequence acceleration for f(Δh) = f₀ + α·(Δh)ⁿ + O((Δh)ⁿ⁺¹): f extrapolated to Δh → 0 from its values at Δh and at Δh scaled down. Ridder Ridder's 1-D solver: the bracket's midpoint and an exponential fit through it. RiemannLiouvilleWeights The quadrature weights of the product-trapezoidal Riemann-Liouville integral, which depend only on the order α and the number of grid steps: built once, they serve every integration on that grid, as the rough Heston characteristic function's at each quadrature node. RiskStatisticsExtensions The empirical risk measures (semi-variance, regret, value-at-risk, expected shortfall, …), from the samples of a statistics tool that keeps them: QuantLib's GenericRiskStatistics<S>, which derives from its type parameter, as C# 14 extension members over any IEmpiricalStatistics. Rounding A basic rounding class that supports rounding to up to 16 decimal places, by one of the methods of RoundingType. RungeKutta QuantLib-Python's RungeKutta: an AdaptiveRungeKutta<T> over real values. SABRInterpolation The SABR smile fitted to discrete volatilities: SABR's four parameters fitted to the volatilities at the strikes, interpolated by the SABR volatility at the fitted parameters. SVD The singular value decomposition of a real matrix, M = U·S·Vᵀ. Secant The secant one-dimensional solver. SegmentIntegral The integral of a one-dimensional function over a number N of intervals, by the trapezoid formula ∫ₐᵇ f dx = (½f(x₀) + f(x₁) + … + f(x_{N−1}) + ½f(x_N))·Δx, x₀ = a, x_N = b, xᵢ = a + iΔx, Δx = (b − a)/N. SequenceStatistics The default statistics of N-dimensional samples, each component a GeneralStatistics, which keeps its samples: QuantLib's SequenceStatistics, GenericSequenceStatistics<Statistics>, with the empirical risk measures of GenericSequenceStatisticsExtensions. SequenceStatisticsInc Statistics of N-dimensional samples, each component an IncrementalStatistics, which keeps running sums and no samples: QuantLib's SequenceStatisticsInc, GenericSequenceStatistics<IncrementalStatistics>. The market-model accounting engines add their paths' values into it. SimpleCostFunction A cost function whose values a function gives, with every other member CostFunction's default. Simplex The multi-dimensional downhill simplex method of Nelder and Mead. SimpsonIntegral The integral of a one-dimensional function by Simpson's formula: the trapezoid's refinements, each pair combined as (4·I₂ₙ − Iₙ)/3, until two combined estimates differ by at most the accuracy, after at least six refinements. SimulatedAnnealing<TRng> Simulated annealing: Numerical Recipes in C (second edition), Chapter 10.9, with the original exit criterion in f(x) replaced by one in x (as the simplex method's). SobolBrownianBridgeRsg The Sobol Brownian-bridge sequence generator: each sequence a path of SobolBrownianGenerator's, its steps' Gaussian variates one after another, the factors of each step together. SobolRsg The Sobol low-discrepancy sequence generator. A Gray code counter and bitwise operations are used for very fast sequence generation. Solver1DBracket What a solver's bracketing hands its implementation, QuantLib's protected members as they stand before solveImpl: XMin and XMax form a valid bracket; FxMin and FxMax are the function's values there; Root is a valid initial guess. Solver1D<TSelf, TFunction> The base class of 1-D solvers: QuantLib's curiously recurring Solver1D<Impl>. It brackets the zero of a function, then hands the bracket to the solver's SolveCore<TF>(TF, double, Solver1DBracket). SparseILUPreconditioner A preconditioner by the incomplete LU factorisation ILU(k) of a sparse matrix (Saad 1996, Iterative Methods for Sparse Linear Systems): A ≈ L·U, the fill kept to the given level, applied by a forward and a backward solve. SparseMatrix A sparse matrix in compressed row storage: QuantLib's SparseMatrix, uBLAS's compressed_matrix<Real>. A mutable working type, as Matrix is. SparseMatrixFunctions The product of a sparse matrix and a vector. SphereCylinderFunctions QuantLib's free functions of spherecylinder.hpp. SphereCylinderOptimizer The point closest to a point Z of the intersection, in R³, of the sphere of radius r centred at the origin and the vertical cylinder of radius s centred at (α, 0): by projection onto the cylinder, or by a golden-section search along the intersection. The intersection may be empty. StatsHolder A helper class for precomputed distributions: a mean and a standard deviation, to which the Gaussian risk measures of GaussianStatisticsExtensions apply, as QuantLib's GenericGaussianStatistics<StatsHolder>. SteepestDescent The multi-dimensional steepest-descent method: the search direction is −f′(x). StochasticCollocationInvCDF The stochastic collocation inverse cumulative distribution function: an inverse cumulative function approximated by a Lagrange polynomial in a standard normal deviate, collocated at the Gauss-Hermite nodes. StudentDistribution The Student t-distribution's probability density for n degrees of freedom (see mathworld.wolfram.com or wikipedia.org): f(x) = Γ((n + 1)/2) / (√(nπ) Γ(n/2)) · (1 + x²/n)^(−(n + 1)/2). SymmetricSchurDecomposition The eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a real symmetric matrix, by the symmetric threshold Jacobi algorithm. TabulatedGaussLegendre The tabulated Gauss-Legendre quadratures of orders 6, 7, 12 and 20 on [−1, 1], their abscissas and weights from Abramowitz and Stegun to 15 decimals. TanhSinhIntegral The tanh-sinh quadrature of Boost.Math, a rapidly convergent integration scheme for holomorphic integrands. The tolerance is used against the error estimate for the L1 norm of the integral. TapCorrelationsFunctions The triangular angles parametrization of correlation matrices (Rapisarda, Brigo and Mercurio, "Parameterizing correlations: a geometric interpretation"): a pseudo-root of the correlation matrix whose rows are unit vectors in spherical coordinates. TqrEigenDecomposition The eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix by QR steps with an explicit shift (Wilkinson): J.H. Wilkinson and C. Reinsch, Linear Algebra, vol. II of Handbook for Automatic Computation (Springer, 1971); "Numerical Recipes in C", 2nd edition, Press, Teukolsky, Vetterling, Flannery. TrapezoidIntegral<TIntegrationPolicy> The integral of a one-dimensional function by the trapezoid formula, its number of intervals refined until two estimates differ by at most the accuracy. TwoDimensionalIntegral The integral of a two-dimensional function f(x, y) between (aₓ, a_y) and (bₓ, b_y), by two nested one-dimensional integrations: the outer over x, the inner over y at each x. UpRounding Up-rounding: Up. Vector A 1-D array used in linear algebra: QuantLib's Array, renamed. It implements the concept of a vector as used in linear algebra, and is not meant to be used as a container. Xoshiro256StarStarUniformRng The xoshiro256** uniform random-number generator, of period 2^256 − 1. For more details see https://prng.di.unimi.it/ and its reference implementation https://prng.di.unimi.it/xoshiro256starstar.c. Xoshiro256StarStarUniformRsg QuantLib-Python's Xoshiro256StarStarUniformRsg: RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> over Xoshiro256StarStarUniformRng, uniform sequences in (0, 1). ZabrInterpolation<TEvaluation> The ZABR smile fitted to discrete volatilities: ZABR's five parameters fitted to the lognormal volatilities at the strikes, interpolated by the volatility of the ZABR smile section at the fitted parameters. ZigguratGaussianRng<TRng> The Gaussian random-number generator by the ziggurat transformation: normally distributed deviates with average 0.0 and standard deviation 1.0, from random integers in the [0, 0xffffffffffffffff] interval supplied by TRng. ZigguratXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRng QuantLib-Python's ZigguratXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRng: ZigguratGaussianRng<TRng> over Xoshiro256StarStarUniformRng, standard Gaussian deviates. ZigguratXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRsg QuantLib-Python's ZigguratXoshiro256StarStarGaussianRsg: RandomSequenceGenerator<TRng> over ZigguratGaussianRng<TRng> over Xoshiro256StarStarUniformRng, standard Gaussian pseudo-random sequences. Structs Abcd The abcd interpolation's factory and traits: an AbcdInterpolation fitted with its parameters. BackwardFlat The backward-flat interpolation factory and traits. BackwardflatLinear The factory of the 2-D interpolation backward flat in x and linear in y. BiCGStabResult BiCGstab's solution: the number of iterations, the relative residual and the solution. Bicubic The bicubic-spline-interpolation factory. Bilinear The bilinear-interpolation factory. ConvexMonotone The convex-monotone interpolation factory and traits: QuantLib's ConvexMonotone. Cubic The cubic-interpolation factory and traits. Default QuantLib's default trapezoid policy: each refinement halves the intervals, adding the integrand at their midpoints. DoublingConvergenceSteps The default sampling rule of ConvergenceStatistics<TStats, TRule>: the mean is stored at 1 sample, then at 2n + 1 after n, so at 1, 3, 7, 15, … (2ᵏ − 1) samples. QuantLib's comment says 2ⁿ⁻¹; its code, which its test asserts and this follows, gives 2ⁿ − 1. Its zero value is QuantLib's default construction. EndCriteriaCheck The outcome of one of EndCriteria's checks that counts stationary iterations: whether the optimization stops, why, and the count after the check. It replaces QuantLib's Size& and EndCriteria::Type& arguments. ForwardFlat The forward-flat interpolation factory and traits. GMRESResult GMRES's solution: the relative residual after each step, and the solution. GenericLowDiscrepancy<TUrsg, TIc> Random-number traits for low-discrepancy generation: sequences of a uniform sequence generator TUrsg, mapped through the inverse cumulative TIc. api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.AmericanPayoff.summary: Class AmericanPayoffAtExpiry Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The analytic formula for American exercise with the payoff at expiry: a cash-or-nothing or asset-or-nothing payoff paid at expiry if the underlying has reached the strike (knock-in: an up-and-in call or a down-and-in put), or if it hasn't (knock-out: an up-and-out call or a down-and-out put). public sealed class AmericanPayoffAtExpiry Inheritance object AmericanPayoffAtExpiry Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks An immutable calculator over the spot, the discount and dividend discount to expiry and the variance to expiry, as QuantLib's; its value. QuantLib's master after the pin keeps the price at low volatility (#2855, taken as a fix): where N(D₂) underflows or the power it multiplies overflows, their finite product is taken in logs, through log N's asymptotic tail. Only where N(D₂) is the formula's: with the strike on the spot, a knock-out is already knocked out and QuantLib sets N(D₂) to 0, which #2855's test reads as an underflow, pricing −D·K·N(D₂) where QuantLib 1.44 prices 0; here 1.44's 0 stands, a documented divergence (Divergences/AmericanPayoffAtExpiryKnockedOutTests.cs). Below a variance of ε, QuantLib takes the spot's side of the strike for both probabilities (americanpayoffatexpiry.cpp:112-121), so a call whose forward passes the strike is worth nothing; here the underlying follows its forward, which reaches the strike by expiry where the forward is past it, and the payoff is paid at expiry if it did (knock-in) or didn't (knock-out): a documented divergence (Divergences/AmericanPayoffZeroVarianceTests.cs). A payoff other than a cash-or-nothing or asset-or-nothing one is refused, where QuantLib leaves the paid amount unset. Exceptions ArgumentNullException payoff is null. ArgumentException The spot, the discount or the dividend discount isn't positive, the variance is negative, or the payoff is neither cash-or-nothing nor asset-or-nothing. Methods Value() The value. public double Value() Returns double The value.

api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.AmericanPayoff.title: Class AmericanPayoffAtHit | nanoql
api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.AmericanPayoff.summary: Class AmericanPayoffAtHit Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The analytic formula for American exercise with the payoff at hit: a cash-or-nothing or asset-or-nothing payoff paid when the underlying first reaches the strike, an up-and-in call or a down-and-in put. public sealed class AmericanPayoffAtHit Inheritance object AmericanPayoffAtHit Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks An immutable calculator over the spot, the discount and dividend discount to expiry and the variance to expiry, as QuantLib's; its value and its delta, gamma and rho. Two documented divergences, each leaving QuantLib's arithmetic where it doesn't apply. Where the closed form has no real λ (λ² = μ² − 2 ln D / σ²T < 0, at negative rates), QuantLib's square root is NaN (americanpayoffathit.cpp:75); here the value and its Greeks are the payoff's present value at the hit integrated over the first-passage density of the log-price to the strike, which is the closed form where λ is real (as the barrier engines' rebate; Divergences/AmericanPayoffAtHitNegativeRateTests.cs). Below a variance of ε, QuantLib divides by the variance (:87-102), NaN out of the money; here the underlying follows its forward, ln S(τ) = ln S + τ ln(D_q/D) over the fraction τ of the time to expiry, and the payoff is paid at the τ* where that path reaches the strike, if it does by expiry, with the Greeks of that value (Divergences/AmericanPayoffZeroVarianceTests.cs). A payoff other than a cash-or-nothing or asset-or-nothing one is refused, where QuantLib leaves the paid amount unset. api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.AnalyticAmeric.summary: Class AnalyticAmericanMargrabeEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The analytic engine for an American Margrabe option: the exchange priced as an American call on Q₁S₁ struck at Q₂S₂, on the first asset's yield as dividend, the second's as rate and their spread's volatility, by BjerksundStenslandApproximationEngine; E. G. Haug, "The Complete Guide to Option Pricing Formulas", 2nd edition (2007). public static class AnalyticAmericanMargrabeEngine Inheritance object AnalyticAmericanMargrabeEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The value alone, as QuantLib's. The second asset's yield is read on the first process's risk-free curve, its yield plus the first rate less the second, where QuantLib reads no risk-free rate, so two risk-free curves price as QuantLib's engine on the market restated onto the first (Divergences/TwoAssetTwoRiskFreeCurvesTests.cs). The flat market runs on the clock across both processes (NanoQL.Methods.FdmBlackScholesOp.ClockAcross(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{NanoQL.Processes.GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess})), each structure read by date, accruing nothing before its date, where QuantLib builds it from the evaluation date with rates over the risk-free curve's time; on structures dated at the evaluation date alike the market is QuantLib's (Divergences/TwoAssetMismatchedTimesTests.cs). api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.AnalyticBSMHul.summary: Class AnalyticBSMHullWhiteEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The analytic European option pricer including stochastic interest rates: the Black-Scholes engine on the equity variance shifted by the Hull-White rate's variance and its covariance with the equity (Brigo and Mercurio, "Interest Rate Models"). public static class AnalyticBSMHullWhiteEngine Inheritance object AnalyticBSMHullWhiteEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The engine reports the analytic European engine's results on the shifted variance. The correctness of the returned value is tested by reproducing results available in web and literature. QuantLib's offset takes the Hull-White terms over the risk-free curve's time and the equity volatility as its own structure quotes it (analyticbsmhullwhiteengine.cpp:86-102), which differ where the two are counted differently; here the equity volatility in the covariance is its variance per unit of the risk-free curve's time, the offset's own, QuantLib's where they share their times (Divergences/BsmHullWhiteMismatchedTimesTests.cs). Below a·t = 1e-2 the offset is its series to (a·t)⁴, QuantLib's three terms first, where QuantLib's closed form, used above (a·t)⁴ = ε, cancels to a relative error of about 3ε/(a·t)³ (Divergences/BsmHullWhiteSmallReversionTests.cs). api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.AnalyticBarrie.title: Class AnalyticBarrierEngine | nanoql
api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.AnalyticBarrie.summary: Class AnalyticBarrierEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The analytic engine for European barrier options: Haug's closed forms ("Option pricing formulas", 1998, pp. 69-72) on a Black-Scholes process. public static class AnalyticBarrierEngine Inheritance object AnalyticBarrierEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks QuantLib's formulas, with four changes, each a documented divergence that leaves QuantLib's bits where it doesn't apply. At a variance below machine epsilon the underlying follows its forward, as QuantLib's master prices it (e29c64126): a knock-out pays its rebate at the hit or the vanilla payoff, a knock-in the vanilla payoff or its rebate at expiry, a spot on the barrier a hit. A negative rebate is priced, where QuantLib's E and F test rebate > 0 and drop it. Each rate is read on the volatility's clock, the curve's zero rate times its own time over the volatility's, nothing accrued before a structure's reference date, so curves on other day counters or dates price as QuantLib's engine does on the same market restated on the volatility's (a factor of 1.0, and QuantLib's bits, where the clocks agree; 1.0 where the volatility's time is 0). A knock-out's rebate whose closed form has no real λ (λ² = μ² + 2r/σ² < 0, at negative rates), where QuantLib's is NaN, is the rebate's present value at the hit, integrated over the barrier's first-passage density. The formulas are first-passage closed forms in one equivalent-constant carry and volatility, the variance and discounts to expiry: no exact closed form exists for a first passage under general deterministic term structures, and on shaped markets they miss QuantLib's finite-difference barrier engine by -2.4% to +0.6%. They are exact where (r − q)/σ² is constant over the option's life and the volatility depends on time alone, the price then a time change of a constant market's, so a smile breaks it; a knock-out's rebate, paid at the hit, where r/σ² and q/σ² are each constant (Conventions/ClosedFormExactnessTests.cs). The term-structure-exact route is FdBlackScholesBarrierEngine; the Monte Carlo engines monitor the barrier at their grid's dates. QuantLib's references: Haug's formulas, and its testHaugValues table. Methods Calculate(BarrierOption, EvaluationContext, GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess) Prices a barrier option. public static OneAssetOptionResults Calculate(BarrierOption option, EvaluationContext context, GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess process) Parameters option BarrierOption The option. context EvaluationContext The evaluation context. process GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess The Black-Scholes process. Returns OneAssetOptionResults The option's results: the value; the expired results when the option has expired. Exceptions ArgumentNullException An argument is null. NanoQLException The payoff isn't a plain vanilla one or its strike isn't positive, the exercise isn't European, the spot isn't positive, or it lies beyond the barrier ("barrier touched").

api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.AnalyticBinary.summary: Class AnalyticBinaryBarrierEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The analytic engine for binary barrier options: a cash-or-nothing or asset-or-nothing payoff at expiry, knocked in or out at a barrier, by Haug's formulas ("The complete guide to option pricing formulas", 2nd ed., p. 176 and following). public static class AnalyticBinaryBarrierEngine Inheritance object AnalyticBinaryBarrierEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The option's exercise is American with its payoff at expiry, its window open from the start, as in QuantLib. The engine reads its discounts and its variance by date, so curves on other day counters or dates price as on one clock. The formulas are first-passage closed forms in one equivalent-constant carry and volatility, the variance and discounts to expiry: no exact closed form exists for a first passage under general deterministic term structures, and on shaped markets they miss QuantLib's finite-difference barrier engine or a Monte Carlo by -3.6% to +1.7%. They are exact where (r − q)/σ² is constant over the option's life and the volatility depends on time alone, the price then a time change of a constant market's; a knock-out's rebate, paid at the hit, where r/σ² and q/σ² are each constant (Conventions/ClosedFormExactnessTests.cs). The term-structure-exact route is FdBlackScholesBarrierEngine; the Monte Carlo engines monitor the barrier at their grid's dates. Two documented divergences. api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.AnalyticCapFlo.title: Class AnalyticCapFloorEngine | nanoql
api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.AnalyticCapFlo.summary: Class AnalyticCapFloorEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The analytic cap/floor engine: each optionlet an option on a discount bond of an affine model. public static class AnalyticCapFloorEngine Inheritance object AnalyticCapFloorEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A static class: Calculate runs QuantLib's four steps (playbook §2.1) on the model, an argument where QuantLib's engine holds it. An optionlet whose payment is past (or on the reference date, unless the context includes that day's payments) is skipped; one fixed on or before the reference date pays its known amount, discounted on the model; any other is (1 + Kτ) times the model's option on the discount bond from its start to its payment, struck at 1/(1 + Kτ), a put for a caplet and a call for a floorlet. The option's expiry: QuantLib's option expires at the optionlet's start (analyticcapfloorengine.cpp:94-112), where the instrument fixes its rate and QuantLib's Monte Carlo engine reads it at the fixing date, so an optionlet with a fixing lag is priced on the variance to its start. On a HullWhite model, an optionlet fixed before its start is the option expiring at its fixing on the bond from its start to its payment, QuantLib's own five-argument bond option, as its Jamshidian engine prices one; one fixed on its start is QuantLib's value, bit for bit. The other models keep QuantLib's expiry at the start, since QuantLib has no such option for them: its affine model's five-argument option ignores the bond's start. A divergence (Divergences/CapletFixingExpiryTests.cs). An in-arrears caplet still to be fixed, fixed after its start, is refused, on every model, since no closed form values it: QuantLib prices it as the caplet in advance, on its start and its accrual period, reading neither its fixing nor its index's period (Divergences/CapletInArrearsTests.cs). The tree and Monte Carlo engines value it at its fixing. The term structure is needed only when the model can't provide one: a model that is an ITermStructureConsistentModel reads its own curve's reference date and day counter, as QuantLib's engine does, whatever curve is given. Methods Calculate(CapFloor, EvaluationContext, IAffineModel, YieldTermStructure?) Prices a cap, floor or collar on an affine model. public static InstrumentResults Calculate(CapFloor capFloor, EvaluationContext context, IAffineModel model, YieldTermStructure? termStructure = null) Parameters capFloor CapFloor The cap, floor or collar. context EvaluationContext The evaluation context. model IAffineModel The affine model. termStructure YieldTermStructure The curve that gives the reference date and day counter of the times, for a model that has no curve of its own; null, QuantLib's empty handle, by default. Returns InstrumentResults The instrument's results: the expired results when it has expired. Exceptions ArgumentNullException The cap, the context or the model is null. NanoQLException The cap's terms are inconsistent, a cash flow isn't a floating-rate coupon, a forward can't be computed, the model has no curve and none is given, or a caplet still to be fixed is fixed after its start (in arrears).

QuantLib evaluates the formula on one zero rate, dividend yield and volatility per maturity, its critical value on the times between the dates, so it is exact only on flat markets; here each term reads the variances to each date at the call's strike, the correlations from their ratios and the discounts by date, and the critical spot solves the forward Black values from the choosing date (Divergences/ComplexChooserTermStructureTests.cs, against the exact integral at the choosing date within the critical value's accuracy). api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.AnalyticCompou.summary: Class AnalyticCompoundOptionEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The analytic engine for a compound option: Geske's formula, the critical spot at the mother's maturity where the daughter is worth the mother's strike, and a bivariate term for the daughter. public static class AnalyticCompoundOptionEngine Inheritance object AnalyticCompoundOptionEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Stateless. QuantLib solves its critical spot on the volatility at a date as far from the curves' start as the daughter's maturity from the mother's and on the discounts over that span, then reads the daughter's volatility at its maturity and the mother's at the mother's strike, so it is exact only on flat markets; here Geske's formula reads the variances to each maturity at the daughter's strike, the correlation √(V_M/V_D) and the discounts by date, and the critical spot solves the daughter's forward Black value over the mother's period (Divergences/CompoundTermStructureTests.cs, against the exact integral at the mother's maturity within Brent's accuracy), with QuantLib's solver, bracket and accuracy. The Greeks are the form's: the delta and gamma with the critical spot held, the vega under a parallel shift of the volatilities, and the theta with each date's zero rate and volatility held as the times shorten, where QuantLib's take the vega on the daughter's volatility alone and discount the mother's strike at the daughter's rate in the theta. The bivariate normal is West's, QuantLib's default, where its engine reads Drezner's. Where the daughter is a put whose largest value, K_D·D(T_M, T_D), doesn't exceed the mother's strike, there is no critical spot and QuantLib's Brent refuses ("root not bracketed"); the mother is then never exercised (a call on the put is worth 0) or always (a put on the put is worth K_M·D(T_M) less the put), and those limits are priced (Divergences/CompoundNoCriticalSpotTests.cs). Every structure is read by date, accruing nothing before its own date (Divergences/ExoticMismatchedTimesTests.cs); a date before the process's clock keeps QuantLib's "negative time" refusal. The average is priced exactly under deterministic term structures: ln G is normal with mean (1/N)(the past fixings' log-sum + Σ[ln F(tᵢ) − V(tᵢ)/2]) and variance (1/N²)ΣΣV(min(tᵢ, tⱼ)) over the future fixings, F the forward and V the Black variance at the strike, each read by date, where QuantLib reads one volatility at the exercise date and the zero rates to it for every fixing, +37.4% and −18.9% off on shaped markets (Divergences/GeometricAsianTermStructureTests.cs). A fixing dated from the evaluation date to the clock's origin, where the structures settle after the evaluation date, is taken at the origin, the spot with no variance and no discount accrued, so as a past fixing at the spot (Divergences/AsianLateSettlementTests.cs), where QuantLib drops it from the average. api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.AnalyticDouble.summary: Class AnalyticDoubleBarrierBinaryEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The analytic engine for double barrier binary options: cash-or-nothing knock-outs and knock-ins paid at expiry by Hui's eigenfunction series ("One-touch double barrier binary option values", Applied Financial Economics 6/1996), and KIKO and KOKI options paid at the hit, by the same series' sums. public static class AnalyticDoubleBarrierBinaryEngine Inheritance object AnalyticDoubleBarrierBinaryEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The knock-out and knock-in take a European exercise; KIKO and KOKI an American one paying at the hit, its window open from the start. Each rate is read on the volatility's clock and each time is the volatility's, as AnalyticBarrierEngine reads them, where QuantLib reads every structure at the risk-free curve's times. Documented divergences. The knock-out integrates the killed density over the payoff's region, [max(K, L), U] for a call and [L, min(K, U)] for a put, where QuantLib's series integrates over the whole corridor whatever the payoff's strike and type, so a put struck at 0 pays (Divergences/DoubleBinaryStrikeTests.cs); the knock-in is the European cash-or-nothing less the knock-out, and one already knocked in is that European, where QuantLib pays the cash undiscounted (Divergences/DoubleBinaryKnockedInTests.cs). QuantLib's value stands for a call at K ≤ L, its own cases. Hui's series is taken where a bound on its dropped tail free of its sines, the terms' envelope, is within 1e-11 of its sum, where QuantLib checks its last term, which carries a sine and passes unconverged at x/Z = j/99 (Divergences/DoubleBinaryHuiCheckTests.cs); elsewhere, where QuantLib refuses ("serie did not converge sufficiently fast") among them, the knock-out is the cash-or-nothing part of QuantLib's double-barrier image series, AnalyticDoubleBarrierEngine's callKO and putKO, which converges fastest there, its terms in logs (Divergences/DoubleBinarySmallVarianceTests.cs). The rebate is priced as the double barrier engine prices it, a knock-out's at the first touch of either barrier, now where one is already touched, a knock-in's at expiry where neither is touched, where QuantLib's engine reads none; a KIKO's or KOKI's, for which no convention fixes the payment, is refused (Divergences/DoubleBinaryRebateTests.cs). KIKO and KOKI are QuantLib's 999-term sums where Abel's bound on their dropped tail is within 1e-11 of the sum, QuantLib's value and bits there; elsewhere, where QuantLib's 999 terms run unconverged or it refuses, the absorption flux of QuantLib's own image-series killed density at the barrier, integrated in log time between the roots that bound its mass (Divergences/DoubleBinaryKikoTests.cs). Below machine-epsilon variance the underlying follows its forward. The degenerate branches, where a barrier is already touched, set the value, delta, gamma, vega and rho as QuantLib does, and no theta or dividend rho; one already knocked in takes those of the European cash-or-nothing it is. The series are first-passage closed forms in equivalent-constant rates and a volatility, the variance and discounts to expiry: no exact closed form exists for a first passage under general deterministic term structures, and on shaped markets an independent Monte Carlo finds a knock-out +0.66% and +1.78% off, within two of its standard errors. Its knock-in and knock-out are exact where (r − q)/σ² is constant over the option's life and the volatility depends on time alone, the price then a time change of a constant market's; its KIKO and KOKI, paid at the hit, and a knock-out's rebate, where r/σ² and q/σ² are each constant (Conventions/ClosedFormExactnessTests.cs). The term-structure-exact route is a Monte Carlo on the process, which monitors the barriers at its grid's dates. Where a term's power overflows, as at low volatility, it is taken in logs with its normal difference, QuantLib's own technique in the binary barrier engine, where QuantLib's product is NaN and its max(0, ·) prices 0; each difference of two normal probabilities whose arguments share a sign is taken from the small tail, ½erfc, where the plain difference cancels (Divergences/DoubleBarrierLowVolatilityTests.cs). It is exact where (r − q)/σ² is constant over the option's life and the volatility depends on time alone, the price then a time change of a constant market's; a knock-out's rebate, paid at the first touch, where r/σ² and q/σ² are each constant (Conventions/ClosedFormExactnessTests.cs). The term-structure-exact route is a Monte Carlo on the process, which monitors the barriers at its grid's dates. Margrabe, "The Value of an Option to Exchange One Asset for Another", Journal of Finance 33 (1978), 177-186; with E. G. Haug, "The Complete Guide to Option Pricing Formulas", 2nd edition (2007), for the Greeks. public static class AnalyticEuropeanMargrabeEngine Inheritance object AnalyticEuropeanMargrabeEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The value, each asset's delta and gamma, and the theta; the rho is 0 and the other Greeks are left null, as QuantLib's. Each forward reads its own process's curves and the payoff is discounted on the first process's risk-free curve, where QuantLib builds the second forward on the first process's discount; the theta reads the second asset's carry on the first process's curve (its yield plus the first rate less the second), as QuantLib's engine on that market restated (Divergences/TwoAssetTwoRiskFreeCurvesTests.cs).
