api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.Gaussian1dCapF.summary: Class Gaussian1dCapFloorEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The Gaussian1d cap/floor engine: each optionlet's payoff in the model's state at its fixing, deflated by the numeraire and integrated over the state grid. public static class Gaussian1dCapFloorEngine Inheritance object Gaussian1dCapFloorEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A static class: Calculate runs QuantLib's four steps (playbook §2.1) on the model, an argument where QuantLib's engine holds it. The coupons must carry no spread. The results add each optionlet's price and its at-the-money forward, the coupon's (optionletsPrice, optionletsAtmForward). Seven of QuantLib's defects are fixed. The strike's leg is discounted on the discount curve, as the floating leg and the swaption engine's are, where QuantLib's reads the model curve (:86-89, :158-161); the at-the-money forwards are the coupons', where QuantLib's are left 0; a caplet fixed before today is the known payoff discounted to its payment, where QuantLib's is undiscounted; a curve on another clock is read at a caplet's fixing date; a CMS coupon's rate is the model's swap rate at its fixing, and a CMS spread coupon's the geared spread of its two indexes' swap rates, the float-float engine's estimates, where QuantLib's prices the coupon period's simple forward; flat payoff extrapolation's right tail reads the last node. And a compounded overnight coupon, which QuantLib prices on its last day's rate times the whole accrual, is a Black call on its window's compounding factor on GSR: each daily factor is a zero bond affine in the state, so the factor is lognormal given the state at the window's start, exactly for plain compounding and an observation shift and to second order for a lookback without the shift and a lockout, its log-variance the discrete sum's over the fixing dates; fixings already made come from the index's history, and a payment after the window's end is handled statically, the window end's forward deflated by the payment date's bond. On a Markov-functional model, which defines no short rate, such a coupon is refused. Methods Calculate(CapFloor, EvaluationContext, Gaussian1dModel, int, double, bool, bool, YieldTermStructure?) api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.Gaussian1dJams.summary: Class Gaussian1dJamshidianSwaptionEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The Jamshidian swaption engine on a Gaussian1d model: a European swaption decomposed into options on the coupon bond's zero bonds, struck at the state y* where the bond is worth the nominal. public static class Gaussian1dJamshidianSwaptionEngine Inheritance object Gaussian1dJamshidianSwaptionEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A static class (the playbook's engine row): Calculate runs QuantLib's four steps (playbook §2.1). Only the fixed coupons whose start is on or after the exercise date are part of the bond, which pays the nominal at the floating leg's accrual end. A floating coupon paid after its accrual end (an overnight swap with a payment lag) has the difference its delay makes frozen at time zero and folded into the nominal at the value date, as QuantLib's does. One call shares one memo of the model's terms. Two documented divergences (Divergences/JamshidianBracketTests.cs and Divergences/JamshidianNoFixedCouponTests.cs). QuantLib solves for y* on the fixed bracket [−8, 8] and refuses short-dated swaptions away from the money; the bracket here is QuantLib's first and is doubled only where it doesn't bracket the root, so QuantLib's solver path and bits stand wherever it prices. And with no fixed coupon starting on or after the exercise, QuantLib reads the fixed reset dates past their end as the bond's value date; here the value date is the first floating reset on or after the exercise, the start of the coupons QuantLib's Gaussian1d swaption engine exercises into, and with none the swaption is worth 0, as that engine values it. api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.Gaussian1dSwap.summary: Class Gaussian1dSwaptionEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The one-factor model swaption engine: a European or Bermudan swaption rolled back over a grid of a Gaussian1d model's state, each step integrating the next exercise's values' cubic spline against the state's Gaussian density. public static class Gaussian1dSwaptionEngine Inheritance object Gaussian1dSwaptionEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A static class (the playbook's engine row): Calculate runs QuantLib's four steps (playbook §2.1), the model and QuantLib's settings arguments. Every fixed coupon whose start is on or after an exercise date is part of the swap exercised into there. An overnight-indexed underlying is supported: a compounded coupon's daily compounding telescopes to a zero bonds' ratio over its rate period, over the shifted value dates under an observation shift, normalised by the coupon's own rate accrual, which is exact for plain compounding and a lookback with the shift; a lookback without the shift and a lockout are priced as if they weren't there. A payment delay is handled statically. Cash-settled swaptions and arithmetically averaged overnight coupons aren't supported. One call shares one memo of the model's terms, built inside it. QuantLib's OpenMP branch, which warms the model's caches before a parallel loop, isn't ported: the loop runs in sequence, as QuantLib's default build does. Two documented divergences. A discount or forwarding curve on another clock than the model's is read at the instants QuantLib's arguments denote: the exercise's date in the numeraire's read and the Digital probabilities' discount, the coupons' dates where QuantLib passes them; QuantLib's reads where the curves share a clock (Divergences/Gaussian1dMismatchedTimesTests.cs). With flatPayoffExtrapolation, the right tail integrates the payoff's last node, where QuantLib's integrates its second-last (Divergences/FlatPayoffExtrapolationTests.cs). Morgan CDX model ISDA adopted in 2009, which integrates the protection and the default accrual exactly between the curves' nodes. public static class IsdaCdsEngine Inheritance object IsdaCdsEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks References: [1] The Pricing and Risk Management of Credit Default Swaps, with a Focus on the ISDA Model, OpenGamma Quantitative Research, version as of 15 October 2013; [2] ISDA CDS Standard Model Proposed Numerical Fix, Markit, 15 November 2012; [3] Markit Interest Rate Curve XML Specifications, version 1.16, 15 October 2013. According to [1] the options matching the standard model's C code are HalfDayBias and Flat before its version 1.8.2, and NoBias and Flat from it; the theoretically correct setting is NoBias and Piecewise. The curves must be ISDA compliant: Actual/365 (Fixed), dated on the evaluation date, a discount curve log-linear in its discounts or flat in its forwards, and a credit curve log-linear in its survival probabilities or flat in its hazard rates. QuantLib casts the curves to its interpolated curve types; here a curve qualifies by the IInterpolatedCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator> it implements, which the interpolated and the piecewise curves of those kinds both do, or by being a FlatForward or a FlatHazardRate. For precise consistency with the specification, Ibor coupons should be at par and the rate helpers' Ibor index should not provide the evaluation date's fixing; neither is checked. The protection leg runs to the maturity: the maturity joins the curves' nodes when their last one is before it. QuantLib adds the maturity only when the curves have no nodes, so on curves that end before the maturity it drops the protection from their last node to the maturity, a documented divergence. A static class: an expired swap's results are SetupExpired()'s. api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.JumpDiffusionE.summary: Class JumpDiffusionEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The jump-diffusion engine for vanilla options (Merton 1976): the Poisson-weighted sum of Black-Scholes prices conditional on the number of jumps, each on a constant rate and volatility. public static class JumpDiffusionEngine Inheritance object JumpDiffusionEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The engine reports the value, delta, gamma, theta, vega, rho and dividend rho. The correctness of the returned value is tested by reproducing results available in literature, and of the Greeks by reproducing numerical derivatives. QuantLib builds each term's flat curve and constant volatility on the risk-free curve's reference date with the volatility's time from its own (jumpdiffusionengine.cpp:62-67, :113-114); here both are built on the volatility's reference date, so the time and the structures agree: QuantLib's where the two dates coincide (Divergences/JumpDiffusionReferenceDateTests.cs). The terms' curve runs over the volatility's time, so their rho is per unit of its rate; the engine's rho is per unit of the risk-free curve's own rate over its own time, and theta's risk-free term runs over that time, as the analytic European engine's: QuantLib's where the two times agree. With no diffusive volatility the no-jump term's vega weight √(variance/t)/v and its theta's jump term are 0/0 (:110, :123-127); here they are their limits, 1 and 0, the values they take at any positive volatility (Divergences/JumpDiffusionZeroVolatilityTests.cs). TPath The path type. TStats The statistics accumulator. Inheritance object McSimulation<TPath, TStats> MCDiscreteAveragingAsianEngineBase<TMc, TPath, TStats> Inherited Members McSimulation<TPath, TStats>.Value(MonteCarloModel<TPath, TStats>, double, int, int) McSimulation<TPath, TStats>.ValueWithSamples(MonteCarloModel<TPath, TStats>, int) McSimulation<TPath, TStats>.Calculate(double?, int?, int, PathPricer<TPath>) McSimulation<TPath, TStats>.PathPricer() McSimulation<TPath, TStats>.PathGenerator() McSimulation<TPath, TStats>.TimeGrid() McSimulation<TPath, TStats>.ControlPathPricer() McSimulation<TPath, TStats>.ControlPathGenerator() McSimulation<TPath, TStats>.ControlVariateValue() McSimulation<TPath, TStats>.MaxError(double) McSimulation<TPath, TStats>.AntitheticVariate McSimulation<TPath, TStats>.ControlVariate object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks An extension point and an immutable object (over McSimulation<TPath, TStats>): a concrete engine's static Calculate builds one per call from the option, the context, the process and QuantLib's settings, implements the path pricer, and reads Run()'s model and results. QuantLib's arguments are the option's own, split by the context's date where it holds every past fixing, read once the engine prices: AverageType, RunningAccumulator, PastFixings, FixingDates and the past fixings' log-sum, RunningLog. The control variate's value comes from ControlPricingEngine(), an engine delegate of the engines' form, on the option; a controlled value is clamped at 0, and the grid is the additional result "TimeGrid", as QuantLib's. Every fixing in the past, or the one left today, is refused with QuantLib's "all fixings are in the past". The process is the engine's: the Black-Scholes and Heston engines pass the process on their clock, whose times run from the earliest structure's reference date, so TimeGrid()'s times are that clock's. A fixing dated from the evaluation date to the clock's origin, where the structures settle after the evaluation date, is taken at the origin, the spot with no variance and no discount accrued, so as a past fixing at the spot (Divergences/AsianLateSettlementTests.cs), where QuantLib's grid drops it from the average. The most samples for a tolerance, or null for no limit. seed long The seed, in [1, 4294967295]. timeSteps int? The number of time steps, or null for the fixing times alone. timeStepsPerYear int? The number of time steps per year, or null. includeExerciseDate bool Whether the exercise time joins the grid where it follows the last fixing. Exceptions ArgumentNullException The option, the context or the process is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException requiredSamples or maxSamples is negative, or seed is outside its range. TimeSteps { get; } Property Value int? TimeStepsPerYear Gets the number of time steps per year, or null. protected int? TimeStepsPerYear { get; } Property Value int? ControlVariateValue() The control variate's value: the control engine's NPV on the option. protected override double? ControlVariateValue() Returns double? The value. Exceptions NanoQLException The engine gives no control engine, or the control engine no NPV. Returns ImmutableArray<int> The indices, in the fixings' order. FixingMultiplicities(TimeGrid) The number of fixings at each node of a grid, its fixing dates to come counted by the node their time falls on, so a date given twice, or two dates on one time, counts twice, where QuantLib's grid keeps each time once and its pricers count it once. protected ImmutableArray<int> FixingMultiplicities(TimeGrid grid) Parameters grid TimeGrid The engine's grid. Returns ImmutableArray<int> The count at each node, 0 at a node that isn't a fixing. PathGenerator() The path generator: the traits' sequence generator, of the process's factors per step, and paths on the grid. protected override IPathGenerator<TPath> PathGenerator() Returns IPathGenerator<TPath> A new path generator. Run() QuantLib's calculate: runs the simulation and returns its model and QuantLib's results, the mean as the value, at least 0 under a control variate, the error estimate where the traits allow one, and the grid. protected (MonteCarloModel<TPath, TStats> Model, OneAssetOptionResults Results) Run() Returns (MonteCarloModel<TPath, TStats> Model, OneAssetOptionResults Results) The call's model and results. Exceptions NanoQLException Every fixing is in the past, the simulation refuses, or the samples can't reach the tolerance. TimeGrid() The time grid: the fixing times to come, the exercise time after them where it joins, in the steps given or the steps per year where either is. protected override TimeGrid TimeGrid() Returns TimeGrid The grid. api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.MCEuropeanBask.summary: Class MCEuropeanBasketEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The Monte Carlo engine for European basket options on correlated processes. public static class MCEuropeanBasketEngine Inheritance object MCEuropeanBasketEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The paths run on the clock spanning every Black-Scholes process's structures, from their earliest reference date on the first process's risk-free day counter, each process read at the instants those times denote and accruing nothing before its own date, where QuantLib evolves every process on the first's times (Divergences/McBasketMismatchedTimesTests.cs); a market on one clock keeps QuantLib's draws and arithmetic. The payoff is discounted on the first process's risk-free curve to the exercise date. The draw-price-add loop allocates nothing per sample after its first batch: the paths step through StochasticProcessArray's in-place pair and the path pricer passes its buffer (Conventions/McBasketAllocationTests.cs). The seed is explicit and required (the playbook's SeedGenerator row). The correctness of the returned value is tested by reproducing results available in literature. The type parameters, the traits and the accumulator, are QuantLib's template parameters, whose defaults are PseudoRandom and GeneralStatistics (QuantLib's Statistics). The payoff must be plain vanilla. The paths run on the engine's clock, from the earliest reference date of the process's structures on the risk-free curve's day counter, each structure read at the instants the grid's times denote and the payoff discounted there (Divergences/McMismatchedTimesTests.cs); QuantLib's grid runs from the risk-free curve's date, reading the other structures at its times. Where every structure shares the risk-free curve's clock, the bits are QuantLib's. The seed is explicit: QuantLib's default, 0, a seed from the clock, is refused. Run() builds the pricer, adds the calibration samples on the calibration traits' generator, calibrates, prices on the same pricer and returns the model with the call's exercise probability: QuantLib's mutable pricer and calibration model are the call's working state, and the pricer reaches the pricing model as the call's argument, not as a member, so two calls can share one engine object. The calibration samples default to 2,048, and the calibration's Brownian bridge and antithetic variates to the pricing's. The calibration seed defaults to the pricing seed plus 1,768,237,423, modulo 2³² as MSVC's 32-bit unsigned long computes it, as QuantLib's documentation says; QuantLib's code compares the narrowed Null<Size>() with Null<Real>(), so its default is always the narrowed null: a documented divergence (Divergences/LongstaffSchwartzCalibrationSeedTests.cs); QuantLib's engine with that seed passed reproduces this one's default. Where that default is 0, at the pricing seed 2,526,729,873, it is refused, since QuantLib reads 0 as a seed from the clock. The pricer exercises only at the exercise times on the grid (ExerciseTimes(TimeGrid)): a Bermudan option's dates, and an American option's grid times from its earliest exercise. api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.MCLookbackEngi.summary: Class MCLookbackEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The Monte Carlo pricing engine for the four continuous lookback options, the extremum read at the path's points. public static class MCLookbackEngine Inheritance object MCLookbackEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A static class with one Calculate overload per lookback instrument, QuantLib's template parameter I and its four pricer overloads, over one private simulation deriving McSimulation<TPath, TStats> directly; QuantLib's four .cpp-local path pricers are two private classes here, a partial pricer the full one over its window's nodes. The full-period overloads refuse a partial-time option held as the full-period type with QuantLib's "wrong argument type". The seed is explicit. Documented divergences. The paths and the discount run on the engine's clock, Clock(GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess, FdmQuantoHelper?), from the earliest reference date of the structures, where QuantLib's run on the risk-free curve's (Divergences/McLookbackMismatchedTimesTests.cs). The extremum observed so far is folded into the path's, where QuantLib's pricers take the extremum from the path's second node alone and price a seasoned option as a new one (Divergences/McLookbackSeasonedTests.cs), and it is read as the spot where it lies beyond it, the spot being observed. A partial option's window date is a time of the grid, its start node included, where QuantLib's pricers snap it to the closest time of a regular grid and the partial fixed pricer drops the window's first node (Divergences/McLookbackWindowTests.cs). A partial fixed window opened before the evaluation date is refused, as the analytic engine refuses it, where QuantLib's pricer starts it today, and a partial floating window closed before the evaluation date takes the extremum as given, neither the spot nor a path's node folded in, where QuantLib's folds today's spot into it; a window dated from the evaluation date to the clock's origin opens or closes at the path's start (Divergences/LookbackPartialWindowTodayTests.cs). And the partial floating option pays the terminal spot less λ times the minimum, or λ times the maximum less the terminal spot, as the instrument and the analytic engine have it, where QuantLib's pricer drops λ (Divergences/McLookbackLambdaTests.cs). TStats The statistics accumulator, QuantLib's S. Inheritance object McSimulation<TPath, TStats> Derived MCLongstaffSchwartzPathEngine<TRng, TStats> MCDiscreteAveragingAsianEngineBase<TMc, TPath, TStats> MCForwardVanillaEngine<TMc, TPath, TStats> MCLongstaffSchwartzEngine<TOption, TMc, TMcCalibration, TPath, TState, TStats> MCVanillaEngine<TMc, TPath, TStats> Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks An extension point and an immutable object: an engine derives from it, holds its settings and its call's instrument and context, and implements the hooks, each returning a new object per call. Calculate(double?, int?, int, PathPricer<TPath>?) builds a new MonteCarloModel<TPath, TStats>, runs QuantLib's value or valueWithSamples loop on it and returns it, so QuantLib's mutable mcModel_ is the call's result and two calculations can share one engine; its errorEstimate() and sampleAccumulator() read the returned model's accumulator. QuantLib's controlPricingEngine(), which the base never reads, is declared by the engines that read it, with their own engine delegate's type. A NaN error estimate is refused, where QuantLib's tolerance check skips it and returns the mean; and so is a next-batch estimate past the samples' range (a tolerance of 0 makes it infinite), where QuantLib's conversion to Size is undefined: documented divergences (Divergences/McSimulationUndefinedTests.cs). api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.MidPointCdsEng.summary: Class MidPointCdsEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The mid-point engine for credit default swaps: each coupon period's default falls at its middle, from the later of its start and the evaluation date. public static class MidPointCdsEngine Inheritance object MidPointCdsEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A static class: Calculate(CreditDefaultSwap, EvaluationContext, DefaultProbabilityTermStructure?, double, YieldTermStructure?, bool?) takes the engine's inputs and returns the results, in place of QuantLib's engine object. An expired swap's results are SetupExpired()'s, as QuantLib's instrument gives them before it calls the engine; otherwise the swap is validated and priced. A curve accrues nothing before its reference date: the discount at a default date before the discount curve's reference date is 1, and the survival at a payment date before the probability curve's reference date is 1, its default probability over a period ending before it 0, where QuantLib's reads refuse them ("negative time"): on a curve that settles after the evaluation date, and on curves dated the evaluation date for a live coupon whose period ended before it (one paid after the weekend that ended it). No default before the reference date is QuantLib's own premise for its two-date default probability, which excuses the period's start and not its end (defaulttermstructure.cpp:112-120). A documented divergence; wherever QuantLib's reads succeed, its values, bit for bit. api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.QuantoEngine.h.summary: Class QuantoEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The quanto engine: an option's own engine run on the underlying's process with its dividend curve carrying the quanto adjustment, with the quanto sensitivities added. public static class QuantoEngine Inheritance object QuantoEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks QuantLib's QuantoEngine<Instr, Engine> as a static class over a delegate in the engines' form: each overload runs the instrument's steps, builds QuantLib's quanto process (QuantoTermStructure as its dividend curve, at the drift's strike and the exchange rate's at-the-money level 1) and calls the engine on the instrument's terms as the inner engine's own instrument, QuantLib's arguments copy; the generic core takes any one-asset instrument and its terms, so later engines and a user's own quanto instruments plug in. Qvega and Qlambda read the underlying's volatility at the drift's strike, where QuantLib reads it at the spot, so on a smile they are the derivatives of the price the drift gives (Divergences/QuantoSmileTests.cs); on a flat volatility, QuantLib's. A quanto forward-start option's drift is read at the moneyness times the spot, the strike its forward engine prices at, where QuantLib reads it at the payoff's strike, which the forward engine ignores. The rho, vega, Qrho, Qvega and Qlambda come from the inner dividend rho through each input's change to the quanto curve's log discount, by date, at the dates the inner engine reads: at expiry, and for a forward-start option at the reset too. QuantLib's assume the input moves the quanto zero rate by one factor at expiry, which misses where a structure counts or dates its time apart from the dividend curve, whose clock the quanto curve keeps, and for a forward-start option where an input's contribution varies between the reset and expiry, as on a volatility term structure (Divergences/QuantoGreeksTermStructureTests.cs). Where every structure shares the dividend curve's times and the factor is one, QuantLib's formula. Returns QuantoOptionResults The option's results, with the quanto sensitivities where the double-barrier engine gives a dividend rho. Remarks The double-barrier engine prices the option's terms as a DoubleBarrierOption of its own; QuantLib's analytic double-barrier engine gives no Greeks, so with it the derived sensitivities are absent, as QuantLib's are. Exceptions ArgumentNullException An argument is null. NanoQLException The spot isn't positive, or the inner engine refuses. Remarks The derived Greeks (rho, vega, qrho, qvega, qlambda) take each input's change to the quanto curve at the underlying's expiry alone: they assume the inner engine reads the quanto curve's dividend discount there and nowhere earlier, as a European, barrier or double-barrier engine does. api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.ReplicatingVar.title: Class ReplicatingVarianceSwapEngine | nanoql
api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.ReplicatingVar.summary: Class ReplicatingVarianceSwapEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The pricing engine for variance swaps by the cost of their replicating portfolio of out-of-the-money calls and puts, as Demeterfi, Derman, Kamal and Zou describe it ("A Guide to Volatility and Variance Swaps", 1999). public static class ReplicatingVarianceSwapEngine Inheritance object ReplicatingVarianceSwapEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The portfolio replicates the log contract piecewise linearly between the strikes given, each option priced by the analytic European engine on the process. The fair variance is the drift's, less the log contract's adjustment at the forward, plus the portfolio's value carried to maturity; the NPV is the notional times the fair variance less the strike, discounted on the risk-free curve, and signed by the position. The additional result "optionWeights" holds each option's payoff and weight, calls first. The drift is 2·(z_r − z_q) and the forward S·D_q/D_r, with z_q and D_q the dividend curve's zero rate and discount read by the maturity date. QuantLib's drift is 2·z_r and its forward S/D_r, as if the dividend yield were zero, which misprices the fair variance at any other yield; its value is that of a zero-dividend process whose risk-free discount is D_r/D_q, which is the check (Divergences/ReplicatingVarianceSwapDividendTests.cs). At a zero dividend yield the value is QuantLib's. A put strike at or below the strike step refuses: the portfolio's added end strike is then 0, whose log payoff QuantLib divides into a NaN or an infinite variance (Divergences/ReplicatingVarianceSwapRefusalTests.cs). The variance is per year of the swap's time on the risk-free curve's day counter from the earliest reference date of the process's structures, each accruing nothing before its own. QuantLib's time is the risk-free curve's own, so where a later risk-free curve beside an earlier volatility shortens it, QuantLib divides the volatility's variance by the shorter time: 1.1% high at a year on a curve dated four days after the volatility, 2.3 times at a week. Where no structure is dated before the risk-free curve, the time is QuantLib's (Divergences/VarianceSwapMismatchedTimesTests.cs). Methods Calculate(VarianceSwap, EvaluationContext, GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess, double, ReadOnlySpan<double>, ReadOnlySpan<double>) Prices a variance swap. public static VarianceSwapResults Calculate(VarianceSwap swap, EvaluationContext context, GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess process, double dk = 5, ReadOnlySpan<double> callStrikes = default, ReadOnlySpan<double> putStrikes = default) Parameters swap VarianceSwap The variance swap. context EvaluationContext The evaluation context. process GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess The Black-Scholes process the options are priced on. dk double The strike step beyond the outermost strikes. callStrikes ReadOnlySpan<double> The call strikes. putStrikes ReadOnlySpan<double> The put strikes. Returns VarianceSwapResults The swap's results: its NPV, its fair variance, and the additional result "optionWeights". Exceptions ArgumentNullException The swap, the context or the process is null. ArgumentException No call or no put strike is given, the lowest put strike isn't positive, the lowest call strike and the highest put strike differ, or a put strike is at or below dk. NanoQLException The swap's strike or notional isn't positive, or a curve or the volatility can't be read at the maturity.

api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.RiskyBondEngin.title: Class RiskyBondEngine | nanoql
api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.RiskyBondEngin.summary: Class RiskyBondEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The risky engine for bonds: each future cash flow is weighted by its survival probability, and each coupon period adds the recovery on its nominal, paid at the period's midpoint, weighted by its default probability. public static class RiskyBondEngine Inheritance object RiskyBondEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The engine prices a bond on a default-probability curve and a recovery rate: each cash flow's amount is weighted by the probability of survival to its date and discounted; in each coupon period, from the later of the curve's reference date and the leg's start, the coupon's nominal times the recovery rate is weighted by the probability of default in the period and discounted from its midpoint. The settlement value counts the cash flows after the settlement date, discounted to it. A static class: Calculate(Bond, EvaluationContext, DefaultProbabilityTermStructure, double, YieldTermStructure) takes the engine's inputs and returns the results, in place of QuantLib's engine object, as DiscountingBondEngine does. An expired bond's results are SetupExpired()'s. Methods Calculate(Bond, EvaluationContext, DefaultProbabilityTermStructure, double, YieldTermStructure) Prices a bond. public static BondResults Calculate(Bond bond, EvaluationContext context, DefaultProbabilityTermStructure defaultTS, double recoveryRate, YieldTermStructure yieldTS) Parameters bond Bond The bond. context EvaluationContext The evaluation context, which gives the bond's settlement date. defaultTS DefaultProbabilityTermStructure The default-probability curve. recoveryRate double The recovery rate. yieldTS YieldTermStructure The discount curve. Returns BondResults The bond's results: the NPV at the discount curve's reference date, its valuation date, and the settlement value; no error estimate. The expired results when the bond has expired. Exceptions ArgumentNullException An argument is null. ArgumentException The bond has no cash flows, or a curve refuses a date. NanoQLException The bond takes other engines' arguments, or its settlement date can't be computed on QuantLib's empty calendar.

api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.SingleFactorBs.summary: Class SingleFactorBsmBasketEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The engine for European average-basket options whose assets are all driven by one stochastic factor: each asset's deviation is its Black volatility at the spot, signed, times the square root of the time. public static class SingleFactorBsmBasketEngine Inheritance object SingleFactorBsmBasketEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks J. Choi, "Sum of all Black-Scholes-Merton Models: An efficient Pricing Method for Spread, Basket and Asian Options", https://arxiv.org/pdf/1805.03172. The price is closed form at the root of a sum of exponentials, found by Brent's solver, and the root's d is returned among the additional results as "d", as QuantLib's. The processes must discount alike: QuantLib's check that every risk-free discount is close enough to the first's ("interest rates need to be the same for all underlyings"). The structures are read by date, accruing nothing before their dates, where QuantLib's reads throw for an option expiring before a later structure's date (Divergences/BasketExpiryBeforeReferenceDateTests.cs). Methods Calculate(BasketOption, EvaluationContext, ImmutableArray<GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess>, double) Prices a European average-basket option. public static MultiAssetOptionResults Calculate(BasketOption option, EvaluationContext context, ImmutableArray<GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess> processes, double xTol = 2.220446049250313E-12) Parameters option BasketOption The basket option, on an average-basket payoff of a plain vanilla. context EvaluationContext The evaluation context. processes ImmutableArray<GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess> The assets' processes, one per weight. xTol double The root solver's accuracy. Returns MultiAssetOptionResults The value, and the root's d among the additional results where a deviation isn't 0. Exceptions ArgumentNullException An argument is null. NanoQLException The payoff isn't an average basket of a plain vanilla, the weights aren't one per process, the exercise isn't European, the processes discount differently, or the root can't be found.

Each structure is read by date and accrues nothing before its reference date (the playbook's row for structures on another clock), where QuantLib's read throws for an option expiring before a later structure's date; on structures dated alike the reads are QuantLib's (Divergences/TwoAssetMismatchedTimesTests.cs). api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.StulzEngine.ht.title: Class StulzEngine | nanoql
api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.StulzEngine.ht.summary: Class StulzEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll Stulz's engine for a European option on the minimum or the maximum of two assets: R. Stulz, "Options on the Minimum or the Maximum of Two Risky Assets", Journal of Financial Economics 10 (1982), 161-185. public static class StulzEngine Inheritance object StulzEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The bivariate normal is QuantLib's default, BivariateCumulativeNormalDistributionWe04DP. Each forward reads its own process's curves and the payoff is discounted on the first process's risk-free curve, where QuantLib builds the second forward on the first process's discount (Divergences/TwoAssetTwoRiskFreeCurvesTests.cs); each structure is read by date and accrues nothing before its reference date (Divergences/TwoAssetMismatchedTimesTests.cs). Where the assets move together, a combined deviation of zero (a correlation of 1 with equal volatilities, or two zero volatilities), the minimum is the asset of the smaller forward and the maximum that of the larger, each priced by Black's formula, where QuantLib's derived correlations are NaN or infinite and refused; an asset of zero volatility reads the bivariate normal at an infinite bound, its limit (Divergences/StulzDegenerateTests.cs). At a negative strike the payoffs are linear: a call is the call struck at zero less the discounted strike, a put is worth nothing, where QuantLib takes the log of a negative ratio (Divergences/StulzNegativeStrikeTests.cs). Methods Calculate(BasketOption, EvaluationContext, GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess, GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess, double) Prices a European option on the minimum or the maximum of two assets: QuantLib's calculate. public static MultiAssetOptionResults Calculate(BasketOption option, EvaluationContext context, GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess process1, GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess process2, double correlation) Parameters option BasketOption The option, on a MinBasketPayoff or MaxBasketPayoff over a plain vanilla payoff. context EvaluationContext The evaluation context. process1 GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess The first asset's process. process2 GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess The second asset's process. correlation double The correlation of the two assets. Returns MultiAssetOptionResults The option's results: the value; the expired results when it has expired. Exceptions ArgumentNullException An argument is null. NanoQLException The exercise isn't European, or the payoff isn't a minimum or maximum basket over a plain vanilla payoff.

api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.TreeSwaptionEn.summary: Class TreeSwaptionEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll The numerical lattice engine for swaptions: a DiscretizedSwaption rolled back on a short-rate model's lattice. public static class TreeSwaptionEngine Inheritance object TreeSwaptionEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A static class: each Calculate overload runs QuantLib's four steps (playbook §2.1), the model an argument where QuantLib's engine holds it. QuantLib's constructors are its overloads: on a number of time steps, the lattice built per call on a grid through the swaption's mandatory times; on a time grid, the model's lattice on it, which QuantLib's engine builds once and nanoql builds per call; and on a built lattice, which a caller reuses by passing it in. The swaption is rolled back to its first exercise time on or after the reference date, and its value is its present value there. The engine is not guaranteed to work if the underlying swap has a start date in the past, before the reference date: prune the swap's initial part so that it starts at t ≥ 0. The term structure is needed only when the model can't provide one: a model that is an ITermStructureConsistentModel gives the reference date and day counter of the times from its own curve, as QuantLib's engine does, whatever curve is given. api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.TurnbullWakema.summary: Class TurnbullWakemanAsianEngine Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Assembly NanoQL.dll Turnbull and Wakeman's engine for discrete arithmetic average-price Asian options: the average matched to a log-normal by its first two moments, priced by Black's formula. public static class TurnbullWakemanAsianEngine Inheritance object TurnbullWakemanAsianEngine Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The value, delta and gamma, and QuantLib's additional results ("accrued", "discount", "strike", "effective_strike", "forward", "exp_A_2", "tte", "sigma", "times", "spotVols", "forwards"). An effective strike at or below zero is the certain exercise, priced in closed form (Haug, "Option Pricing Formulas", 2nd ed., p. 193). Documented divergences. With every fixing past, the known payoff discounted, as Choi's engine prices it, where QuantLib's reads the last of no fixing times and crashes the process (Divergences/TurnbullWakemanPastFixingsTests.cs); QuantLib's master prices it so after 1.44 (#2954), its branch ahead of the certain exercise's, as here. A seasoned option reads its variances and spot volatilities at the future average's own strike, K_f = (K − A/m)·m/f for f of m fixings to come, so it prices as (f/m) times the unseasoned option at K_f, where QuantLib reads them at K − A/m, +42% and +1,302% off on a smile varying with maturity (Divergences/SeasonedAsianSmileTests.cs). The last fixing on the evaluation date, at time 0, is priced with a zero standard deviation and σ, its delta discount · α · E[A] / S, as QuantLib's master prices it after 1.44 (#2954, Divergences/AsianUpstreamFixesTests.cs), where QuantLib 1.44 divides by the last time and refuses the NaN standard deviation; the standard deviation is the master's, √log(E[A²]/E[A]²), and each spot volatility the structure's volatility, so the price's last bits differ from 1.44's. A fixing dated from the evaluation date to the latest structure's date, where the structures settle after the evaluation date, is taken there, the spot with no variance and no discount accrued, so as a past fixing at the spot (Divergences/AsianLateSettlementTests.cs), where QuantLib reads its negative time and refuses it. Methods Calculate(DiscreteAveragingAsianOption, EvaluationContext, GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess) Prices a discrete arithmetic average-price Asian option. public static OneAssetOptionResults Calculate(DiscreteAveragingAsianOption option, EvaluationContext context, GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess process) Parameters option DiscreteAveragingAsianOption The option. context EvaluationContext The evaluation context. process GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess The Black-Scholes process. Exceptions ArgumentNullException An argument is null. NanoQLException The exercise isn't European, the average isn't arithmetic, the payoff isn't plain vanilla, or the option's past fixings fail its checks.
