api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.html.title: Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines | nanoql
api/NanoQL.PricingEngines.html.summary: Namespace NanoQL.PricingEngines Classes AmericanBasketPathPricer The early-exercise path pricer of a basket option for the Longstaff-Schwartz engine: the assets' prices at a step, scaled by the strike, as the regression's state, and its basis, the polynomials of several variables with the payoff appended. AmericanPathPricer The American early-exercise path pricer: the payoff of the underlying at a time step, the state the underlying scaled by the strike, and a polynomial basis of the state with the payoff as one more function. AmericanPayoffAtExpiry The analytic formula for American exercise with the payoff at expiry: a cash-or-nothing or asset-or-nothing payoff paid at expiry if the underlying has reached the strike (knock-in: an up-and-in call or a down-and-in put), or if it hasn't (knock-out: an up-and-out call or a down-and-out put). AmericanPayoffAtHit The analytic formula for American exercise with the payoff at hit: a cash-or-nothing or asset-or-nothing payoff paid when the underlying first reaches the strike, an up-and-in call or a down-and-in put. AnalyticAmericanMargrabeEngine The analytic engine for an American Margrabe option: the exchange priced as an American call on Q₁S₁ struck at Q₂S₂, on the first asset's yield as dividend, the second's as rate and their spread's volatility, by BjerksundStenslandApproximationEngine; E. G. Haug, "The Complete Guide to Option Pricing Formulas", 2nd edition (2007). AnalyticBSMHullWhiteEngine The analytic European option pricer including stochastic interest rates: the Black-Scholes engine on the equity variance shifted by the Hull-White rate's variance and its covariance with the equity (Brigo and Mercurio, "Interest Rate Models"). AnalyticBarrierEngine The analytic engine for European barrier options: Haug's closed forms ("Option pricing formulas", 1998, pp. 69-72) on a Black-Scholes process. AnalyticBinaryBarrierEngine The analytic engine for binary barrier options: a cash-or-nothing or asset-or-nothing payoff at expiry, knocked in or out at a barrier, by Haug's formulas ("The complete guide to option pricing formulas", 2nd ed., p. 176 and following). AnalyticBlackVasicekEngine The pricing of vanilla European options under a stochastic Vasicek interest rate: Black's formula on the Vasicek bond with the total variance of the equity, the rate and their covariance (the Black-Scholes-Vasicek model, http://hsrm-mathematik.de/WS201516/master/option-pricing/Black-Scholes-Vasicek-Model.pdf). AnalyticCEVEngine The pricing engine for European vanilla options on the constant elasticity of variance (CEV) process df = α·f^β·dW, with an absorbing boundary at f = 0: CEVCalculator's value, discounted. AnalyticCapFloorEngine The analytic cap/floor engine: each optionlet an option on a discount bond of an affine model. AnalyticCliquetEngine The analytic engine for a European cliquet option: each period a forward-start option struck at the moneyness times the spot, by Black's formula on the period's forward variance, weighted by the dividend discount to its start. AnalyticComplexChooserEngine The analytic engine for a complex chooser option: Rubinstein's formula, the critical spot at the choosing date where the call and the put are worth the same, and bivariate terms for each. AnalyticCompoundOptionEngine The analytic engine for a compound option: Geske's formula, the critical spot at the mother's maturity where the daughter is worth the mother's strike, and a bivariate term for the daughter. AnalyticContinuousFixedLookbackEngine The analytic engine for continuous fixed-strike lookback options: Conze and Viswanathan's closed form, as in Haug, "Option Pricing Formulas" (1998), pp. 63-64. AnalyticContinuousFloatingLookbackEngine The analytic engine for continuous floating-strike lookback options: Goldman, Sosin and Gatto's closed form, as in Haug, "Option Pricing Formulas" (1998), pp. 61-62. AnalyticContinuousGeometricAveragePriceAsianEngine The analytic engine for continuous geometric average-price Asian options, averaging from the evaluation date: the continuous geometric average of a log-normal process is log-normal (Haug, "Option Pricing Formulas", 1998, pp. 96-97). AnalyticContinuousPartialFixedLookbackEngine The analytic engine for continuous partial-time fixed-strike lookback options: Heynen and Kat's closed form, as in Haug, "The Complete Guide to Option Pricing Formulas" (2007), pp. 148-149. AnalyticContinuousPartialFloatingLookbackEngine The analytic engine for continuous partial-time floating-strike lookback options: Heynen and Kat's closed form, as in Haug, "The Complete Guide to Option Pricing Formulas" (2007), pp. 146-147. AnalyticDigitalAmericanEngine The analytic pricing engine for American vanilla options with a digital payoff: cash-or-nothing or asset-or-nothing, paid at the hit (AmericanPayoffAtHit) or at expiry (AmericanPayoffAtExpiry, knock-in). AnalyticDigitalAmericanKOEngine The analytic pricing engine for American knock-out options with a digital payoff at expiry: a cash-or-nothing or asset-or-nothing payoff paid at expiry if the underlying never reached the strike (an up-and-out call or a down-and-out put). AnalyticDiscreteGeometricAveragePriceAsianEngine The analytic engine for discrete geometric average-price Asian options: the geometric average of log-normal fixings is log-normal, priced by Black's formula on its forward and variance (Clewlow and Strickland, "Implementing Derivatives Models", 1998, pp. 118-123). AnalyticDiscreteGeometricAverageStrikeAsianEngine The analytic engine for discrete geometric average-strike Asian options: the option to exchange the geometric average of log-normal fixings for the terminal spot, both log-normal, priced in closed form. AnalyticDividendEuropeanEngine The analytic pricing engine for European options with discrete dividends: the Black-Scholes formulas on the spot less the present value of the dividends paid from the settlement date to the exercise date. AnalyticDoubleBarrierBinaryEngine The analytic engine for double barrier binary options: cash-or-nothing knock-outs and knock-ins paid at expiry by Hui's eigenfunction series ("One-touch double barrier binary option values", Applied Financial Economics 6/1996), and KIKO and KOKI options paid at the hit, by the same series' sums. AnalyticDoubleBarrierEngine The analytic engine for European double barrier options: Ikeda and Kunitomo's image series ("Pricing Options with Curved Boundaries", Mathematical Finance 2/1992) as Haug gives it ("The complete guide to option pricing formulas", 2nd ed., p. 156 and following), for flat barriers. AnalyticEuropeanEngine The pricing engine for European vanilla options by the analytic Black-Scholes formulas, through BlackCalculator, for plain vanilla, cash-or-nothing, asset-or-nothing and gap payoffs. AnalyticEuropeanMargrabeEngine The analytic engine for a European Margrabe option: W. Margrabe, "The Value of an Option to Exchange One Asset for Another", Journal of Finance 33 (1978), 177-186; with E. G. Haug, "The Complete Guide to Option Pricing Formulas", 2nd edition (2007), for the Greeks. AnalyticGJRGARCHEngine The analytic GJR-GARCH(1,1) engine for European options: Duan, Gauthier, Simonato and Sasseville's Edgeworth approximation, from the first four moments of the log return over the option's days. AnalyticH1HWEngine The analytic Heston-Hull-White engine on Grzelak and Oosterlee's H1-HW approximation: the equity correlated with the short rate, ρ_Sr ≥ 0, the variance independent of it. AnalyticHestonEngine The analytic Heston engine: European plain-vanilla options under the Heston model, by the Fourier transform of the model's characteristic function, integrated by a FourierIntegration. AnalyticHestonEngineAPHelper The integrand of AnalyticHestonEngine's control-variate forms and the control variate's value: QuantLib's AnalyticHestonEngine::AP_Helper. AnalyticHestonEngineOptimalAlpha The damping exponent α that minimizes the Fourier integrand's size at the origin, for the engine's control variates: Andersen and Lake's choice, QuantLib's AnalyticHestonEngine::OptimalAlpha. AnalyticHestonHullWhiteEngine The analytic Heston engine with a Hull-White short rate independent of the equity and its variance: dS = (r − d)S dt √v S dW₁, dv = κ(θ − v) dt + σ√v dW₂, dr = (θ(t) − ar) dt + η dW₃, dW₁dW₂ = ρ dt, dW₁dW₃ = dW₂dW₃ = 0. AnalyticHolderExtensibleOptionEngine The analytic engine for a holder-extensible option: Longstaff's formula, the vanilla to the first maturity and bivariate terms over the region where the holder extends, between two critical prices. AnalyticPDFHestonEngine The Heston engine for European options on any payoff: the payoff integrated against HestonRNDCalculator's density of the log spot at expiry. AnalyticPTDHestonEngine The analytic engine for European plain-vanilla options under PiecewiseTimeDependentHestonModel: the characteristic function's recursion across the model's time grid, integrated by Gatheral's form or Andersen and Piterbarg's. AnalyticPartialTimeBarrierOptionEngine The analytic engine for partial-time barrier options: Haug's formulas ("Option Pricing Formulas"), a put priced by the put-call symmetry from the call. AnalyticPerformanceEngine The analytic engine for a European performance option: a cliquet whose periods pay their returns, each by Black's formula on the period's forward variance, discounted to its start. AnalyticRoughHestonEngine The analytic engine for European plain-vanilla options under RoughHestonModel: the characteristic function's fractional Riccati equation solved by the Adams scheme, the Padé approximation or the lifted approximation, and the price by Andersen and Piterbarg's Fourier integral with a Black-Scholes control variate. AnalyticSimpleChooserEngine The analytic engine for a simple chooser option: Rubinstein's decomposition at the choosing date, the call to maturity and the put to the choosing date at the strike carried there. AnalyticSoftBarrierEngine The analytic engine for European soft barrier options: Haug's closed form ("The Complete Guide to Option Pricing Formulas", 2nd ed., after Hart and Ross, 1994), and the soft barrier's definition, the average of the single-barrier options with barriers in [L, U], where that form doesn't hold. AnalyticTwoAssetBarrierEngine The analytic engine for a barrier option on two assets: the first asset's payoff, knocked in or out by the second asset at the barrier (Haug, "The Complete Guide to Option Pricing Formulas", 2nd ed.). AnalyticTwoAssetCorrelationEngine The analytic engine for a European two-asset correlation option: M. Zhang, "Exotic Options", World Scientific (1998); E. G. Haug, "The Complete Guide to Option Pricing Formulas", 2nd edition (2007). AnalyticWriterExtensibleOptionEngine The analytic engine for a writer-extensible option: Longstaff's formula, the vanilla to the first exercise and a bivariate term for the extension, on West's bivariate normal. ArithmeticAPOHestonPathPricer The path pricer of a discrete arithmetic average-price Asian option on a Heston path: the discounted payoff at the average of the asset's values at the fixing indices and the past fixings. ArithmeticAPOPathPricer The path pricer of a discrete arithmetic average-price Asian option: the discounted payoff at the average of the path's fixings and the past ones. ArithmeticASOPathPricer The path pricer of a discrete arithmetic average-strike Asian option: the discounted payoff of the path's last value struck at the average of its fixings and the past ones. BachelierCalculator The Bachelier calculator: the value and sensitivities of a striked payoff on a forward with a normal distribution of a given standard deviation (in price units), discounted. It supports plain vanilla, cash-or-nothing, asset-or-nothing and gap payoffs. BachelierCapFloorEngine The Bachelier-Black-formula cap/floor engine: normal volatilities. BachelierSwaptionEngine The normal Bachelier-formula swaption engine. BaroneAdesiWhaleyApproximationEngine The Barone-Adesi and Whaley pricing engine for American options (1987). BarrierPathPricer The path pricer of a barrier option with the Brownian bridge correction for the barrier's crossings between the path's points: each step's extreme is drawn from its bridge, given a uniform number of its own (Beaglehole, Dybvig and Zhou, "Going to Extremes: Correcting Simulation Bias in Exotic Option Valuation", Financial Analysts Journal, Jan/Feb 1997; El Babsiri and Noel, "Simulating path-dependent options: A new approach", Journal of Derivatives, Winter 1998). BasketGeneratingEngine The base of the pricing engines that generate a calibration basket: per live exercise date, a standard swaption matching the underlying's value, delta and gamma in the model's state, or the at-the-money coterminal one. BatesDetJumpEngine The analytic Bates engine with a deterministic jump intensity: the log-normal jumps' term at the intensity's average over the maturity, which mean-reverts at κ_λ from λ to θ_λ. BatesDoubleExpDetJumpEngine The analytic engine of the Heston model with double-exponential jumps at a deterministic intensity: the double-exponential jumps' term at the intensity's average over the maturity. BatesDoubleExpEngine The analytic engine of the Heston model with double-exponential jumps: the jumps' term tλ(p/(1 − gη_u) + q/(1 + gη_d) − 1 − g(p/(1 − η_u) + q/(1 + η_d) − 1)) added to the Heston exponent, q = 1 − p. BatesEngine The analytic Bates engine: European plain-vanilla options under the Heston model with log-normal jumps, by the Fourier transform of the characteristic function, the jumps' term added to the Heston exponent. BiasedBarrierPathPricer The biased path pricer of a barrier option: the barrier is checked at the path's points only, so crossings between them are missed. BinomialBarrierEngine The binomial engine for barrier options: a discretized barrier asset rolled back on a Black-Scholes lattice over a binomial tree, built on the process's curves and volatility flattened at the option's maturity. For Cox-Ross-Rubinstein trees the number of steps is raised to Boyle and Lau's optimum ("Bumping up against the barrier with the binomial method", Journal of Derivatives, 1/1994). BinomialCRRBarrierEngine The binomial barrier engine on the Cox-Ross-Rubinstein tree and Derman and Kani's discretized barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialCRRBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialBarrierEngine<CoxRossRubinstein, DiscretizedDermanKaniBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialCRRConvertibleEngine The binomial convertible engine on the Cox-Ross-Rubinstein tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialCRRConvertibleEngine, QuantLib's BinomialConvertibleEngine<CoxRossRubinstein>. BinomialCRRVanillaEngine The binomial engine on the Cox-Ross-Rubinstein tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialCRRVanillaEngine, QuantLib's BinomialVanillaEngine<CoxRossRubinstein>. BinomialConvertibleEngine The binomial Tsiveriotis-Fernandes engine for convertible bonds: the bond rolled back on a Tsiveriotis-Fernandes lattice over a binomial tree, built on the process's curves and volatility flattened at the last exercise date, the dividends' present values taken from the spot. BinomialEQPBarrierEngine The binomial barrier engine on the additive equal-probabilities tree and Derman and Kani's discretized barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialEQPBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialBarrierEngine<AdditiveEQPBinomialTree, DiscretizedDermanKaniBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialEQPConvertibleEngine The binomial convertible engine on the additive equal-probabilities tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialEQPConvertibleEngine, QuantLib's BinomialConvertibleEngine<AdditiveEQPBinomialTree>. BinomialEQPVanillaEngine The binomial engine on the additive equal-probabilities tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialEQPVanillaEngine, QuantLib's BinomialVanillaEngine<AdditiveEQPBinomialTree>. BinomialJ4BarrierEngine The binomial barrier engine on the Joshi tree and Derman and Kani's discretized barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialJ4BarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialBarrierEngine<Joshi4, DiscretizedDermanKaniBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialJ4ConvertibleEngine The binomial convertible engine on the Joshi tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialJ4ConvertibleEngine, QuantLib's BinomialConvertibleEngine<Joshi4>. BinomialJ4VanillaEngine The binomial engine on Joshi's fourth-order tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialJ4VanillaEngine, QuantLib's BinomialVanillaEngine<Joshi4>. BinomialJRBarrierEngine The binomial barrier engine on the Jarrow-Rudd tree and Derman and Kani's discretized barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialJRBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialBarrierEngine<JarrowRudd, DiscretizedDermanKaniBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialJRConvertibleEngine The binomial convertible engine on the Jarrow-Rudd tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialJRConvertibleEngine, QuantLib's BinomialConvertibleEngine<JarrowRudd>. BinomialJRVanillaEngine The binomial engine on the Jarrow-Rudd tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialJRVanillaEngine, QuantLib's BinomialVanillaEngine<JarrowRudd>. BinomialLRBarrierEngine The binomial barrier engine on the Leisen-Reimer tree and Derman and Kani's discretized barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialLRBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialBarrierEngine<LeisenReimer, DiscretizedDermanKaniBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialLRConvertibleEngine The binomial convertible engine on the Leisen-Reimer tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialLRConvertibleEngine, QuantLib's BinomialConvertibleEngine<LeisenReimer>. BinomialLRVanillaEngine The binomial engine on the Leisen-Reimer tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialLRVanillaEngine, QuantLib's BinomialVanillaEngine<LeisenReimer>. BinomialTianBarrierEngine The binomial barrier engine on the Tian tree and Derman and Kani's discretized barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialTianBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialBarrierEngine<Tian, DiscretizedDermanKaniBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialTianConvertibleEngine The binomial convertible engine on the Tian tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialTianConvertibleEngine, QuantLib's BinomialConvertibleEngine<Tian>. BinomialTianVanillaEngine The binomial engine on the Tian tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialTianVanillaEngine, QuantLib's BinomialVanillaEngine<Tian>. BinomialTrigeorgisBarrierEngine The binomial barrier engine on the Trigeorgis tree and Derman and Kani's discretized barrier option: QuantLib-Python's BinomialTrigeorgisBarrierEngine, QuantLib's BinomialBarrierEngine<Trigeorgis, DiscretizedDermanKaniBarrierOption>, the wheel's closing. BinomialTrigeorgisConvertibleEngine The binomial convertible engine on the Trigeorgis tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialTrigeorgisConvertibleEngine, QuantLib's BinomialConvertibleEngine<Trigeorgis>. BinomialTrigeorgisVanillaEngine The binomial engine on the Trigeorgis tree: QuantLib-Python's BinomialTrigeorgisVanillaEngine, QuantLib's BinomialVanillaEngine<Trigeorgis>. BinomialVanillaEngine The binomial pricing engine for vanilla options: the option rolled back on a Black-Scholes lattice over a binomial tree, built on the process's curves and volatility flattened at the option's maturity. BjerksundStenslandApproximationEngine The Bjerksund and Stensland approximation engine for American options (1993), puts by the put-call symmetry. BjerksundStenslandSpreadEngine Bjerksund and Stensland's engine for a European spread option on two futures: P. Bjerksund and G. Stensland, "Closed form spread option valuation", Quantitative Finance 14 (2014), pp. 1785–1794. BlackCalculator The Black (1976) calculator: the value and sensitivities of a striked payoff on a forward with a log-normal distribution of a given standard deviation, discounted. It supports plain vanilla, cash-or-nothing, asset-or-nothing and gap payoffs. BlackCapFloorEngine The Black-formula cap/floor engine. BlackDeltaCalculator Black-Scholes deltas and strikes under FX markets' delta conventions: the delta of a strike, the strike of a delta, and the at-the-money strike of each convention. BlackFormulaFunctions Black and Bachelier formulas: prices, derivatives, in-the-money probabilities and implied volatilities. BlackScholesCalculator The Black-Scholes (1973) calculator: BlackCalculator on the forward of a spot, its growth and discount factors, with the spot sensitivities at that spot. BlackSwaptionEngine The shifted lognormal Black-formula swaption engine. BondFunctions Bond adapters of the CashFlows functions: each passes the bond's cash flows, its settlement date and includeSettlementDateFlows = false, and gives prices per 100 of the notional at the settlement date. CEVCalculator The undiscounted value of a European option on the constant elasticity of variance (CEV) process df = α·f^β·dW with an absorbing boundary at f = 0, by the non-central chi-squared distribution (D. R. Brecher and A. E. Lindsay, "Results on the CEV Process, Past and Present"). COSHestonEngine The COS-method Heston engine, on efficient Fourier-cosine series expansions. CashDividendEuropeanEngine The (semi-)analytic engine for European options on an underlying paying cash dividends: J. Healy, "The Pricing of Vanilla Options with Cash Dividends as a Classic Vanilla Basket Option Problem" (2021), https://arxiv.org/pdf/2106.12971. ChoiAsianEngine Choi's engine for discrete arithmetic average-price Asian options: the average replicated by a basket of the future fixings, priced by Choi's basket engine ("Sum of all Black-Scholes-Merton Models: An efficient Pricing Method for Spread, Basket and Asian Options", 2018). ChoiBasketEngine The engine for European basket and spread options on several assets by Choi's method: the basket's projection on one factor priced in closed form, integrated over the others by Gauss-Hermite quadrature. ContinuousArithmeticAsianLevyEngine Levy's engine for continuous arithmetic average-price Asian options: the average matched to a log-normal by its first two moments (Haug, "Option Pricing Formulas"). CounterpartyAdjSwapEngine The bilateral counterparty-risk adjusted swap engine: the swap's NPV less the counterparty's expected loss on its exposure, plus the investor's, each exposure a sequence of swaptions at the swap's fixed rate, one per fixed period, weighted by the party's default probability over the period. DengLiZhouBasketEngine Deng, Li and Zhou's engine for a European basket or spread option on several assets: S. Deng, M. Li and J. Zhou, "Multi-asset Spread Option Pricing and Hedging" (2008), https://mpra.ub.uni-muenchen.de/8259/1/MPRA_paper_8259.pdf, with the typo in formula (37) for J² corrected. DigitalPathPricer The path pricer of an American cash-or-nothing option paid at the hit or at expiry: the strike's crossing within each step is detected by the Brownian bridge's maximum (or minimum), drawn from a uniform sequence of its own. DiscountingBondEngine The discounting engine for bonds: it discounts the future cash flows to the curve's reference date, its NPV, and to the bond's settlement date, its settlement value. DiscountingConstNotionalCrossCurrencySwapEngine The discounting engine of constant-notional swaps whose legs involve two currencies: each leg is discounted on its currency's curve, and the NPV is expressed in the domestic currency. DiscountingFxForwardEngine The discounting engine for FxForward: each leg discounted on its currency's curve from the settlement date to maturity, the target leg converted at the spot rate, and the result discounted to each curve's reference date. DiscountingPerpetualFuturesEngine The discounting engine for perpetual futures: the spot times the funding payments' discounted sum (a linear payoff), or over it (an inverse payoff), the funding rates and interest-rate differences interpolated in time and flat past the last, the sum to a horizon on a grid and its tail in closed form. DiscountingSwapEngine The discounting engine for swaps: it discounts the future cash flows to the curve's reference date. DiscretizedBarrierOption A barrier option on a lattice: knocked out to its rebate, or knocked in to its vanilla, at the nodes beyond the barrier. DiscretizedCapFloor A discretized cap, floor or collar: its value on a lattice, each optionlet added as the rollback reaches it. DiscretizedConvertible A convertible bond on a Tsiveriotis-Fernandes lattice: its redemption rolled back with its coupons added, its callabilities applied and its conversion taken where it pays more, with each node's conversion probability and the blended rate it is discounted at. DiscretizedDermanKaniBarrierOption A barrier option on a lattice with Derman and Kani's correction: at the nodes straddling the barrier, the values interpolate between the rolled-back value and the knocked-in vanilla or knocked-out rebate by the nodes' distances from the barrier. DiscretizedSwap A discretized fixed-versus-floating swap: its value on a lattice, its coupons added as the rollback reaches them. DiscretizedSwaption A discretized swaption: an option, exercised at its exercise times, on a discretized swap. DiscretizedVanillaOption A vanilla option on a lattice: worth the larger of its rolled-back value and its payoff at each exercise time. EuropeanGJRGARCHPathPricer The European path pricer of a GJR-GARCH multi-path: a plain vanilla payoff on the first asset's last value, discounted. EuropeanHestonPathPricer The European path pricer of a Heston-like multi-path: a plain vanilla payoff on the first asset's last value, discounted. EuropeanMultiPathPricer The European basket option's path pricer: the basket payoff at the paths' final prices, discounted. EuropeanPathPricer The European path pricer: a plain vanilla payoff on the path's last value, discounted. ExponentialFittingHestonEngine The analytic Heston engine on an exponentially fitted Gauss-Laguerre quadrature: the integrand of AnalyticHestonEngineAPHelper's control variate summed on 64 nodes fitted to the option's moneyness. Fd2dBlackScholesVanillaEngine The two-dimensional finite-difference Black-Scholes engine for basket options on two assets: European, American and Bermudan exercises. FdBatesVanillaEngine The partial-integro finite-difference Bates pricing engine for vanilla options, European, American or Bermudan, with cash dividends: FdmBatesSolver on the finite-difference Heston engine's grid. FdBlackScholesAsianEngine The finite-difference Black-Scholes engine for discrete arithmetic average-price Asian options, on a mesher of the log spot and the log average with the average's step condition at each fixing. FdBlackScholesBarrierEngine The finite-difference engine for European barrier options: a knock-out on a grid bounded by the barrier, its rebate the Dirichlet boundary value; a knock-in as the vanilla option, plus the rebate, less the knock-out. FdBlackScholesRebateEngine The finite-difference engine for a barrier option's rebate: the value of the rebate paid at the hit, on a grid bounded by the barrier, with the rebate as its Dirichlet boundary value and a zero payoff at expiry. FdBlackScholesShoutEngine The finite-difference pricing engine for shout options under the Black-Scholes process, with cash dividends by the escrowed model: the holder may once lock in the intrinsic value, paid at maturity, and keep the option on the rest of the move (FdmShoutLogInnerValueCalculator), the shout window the option's exercise. FdBlackScholesVanillaEngine The finite-difference pricing engine for vanilla options under the Black-Scholes process, European, American or Bermudan, with cash dividends by the spot or the escrowed model, on the Black or local volatility, and optionally quanto. FdCEVVanillaEngine The finite-difference pricing engine for vanilla options, European, American or Bermudan, on the constant elasticity of variance (CEV) process df = α·f^β·dW, absorbed at f = 0: on FdmCEV1dMesher's grid, concentrating at the strike, with the analytic CEV value at the upper end and, where the process can reach zero (δ < 2), the payoff at the lower end discounted from maturity. FdCIRVanillaEngine The finite-difference pricing engine for vanilla options, European, American or Bermudan, on a Black-Scholes equity under a Cox-Ingersoll-Ross short rate, with cash dividends and optionally quanto: FdmCIRSolver on FdmBlackScholesMesher's grid of the log spot by a uniform grid of the short rate. FdG2SwaptionEngine The finite-difference G2 swaption engine: the swaption rolled back on a two-dimensional mesh of the model's factors, its exercise value the swap's inner value on the model's curves (FdmAffineModelSwapInnerValue<TModel>). FdHestonBarrierEngine The finite-difference Heston pricing engine for barrier options: FdmHestonSolver on a log-spot grid bounded at the barrier, the rebate its Dirichlet value, by FdmHestonLocalVolatilityVarianceMesher's grid of the variance; a knock-in by in-out parity on the vanilla and the rebate engines. FdHestonDoubleBarrierEngine The finite-difference Heston pricing engine for double barrier options: FdmHestonSolver on a log-spot grid bounded at both barriers, the rebate their Dirichlet value, paid at the first touch. FdHestonHullWhiteVanillaEngine The finite-difference Heston-Hull-White pricing engine for vanilla options, European, American or Bermudan, with cash dividends optional: FdmHestonHullWhiteSolver on the log spot, the variance and the Hull-White short rate's state, with a control variate, the analytic Heston engine's price less the finite-difference Heston engine's, optional. FdHestonRebateEngine The finite-difference Heston pricing engine for a barrier option's rebate: the rebate paid at the barrier, its Dirichlet value, or at expiry where the barrier is never hit, the knock-in leg of FdHestonBarrierEngine. FdHestonVanillaEngine The finite-difference Heston pricing engine for vanilla options, European, American or Bermudan, with cash dividends, a quanto adjustment and a leverage function optional: FdmHestonSolver on FdmBlackScholesMesher's grid of the log spot, sized by the variance mesher's volatility estimate, by FdmHestonLocalVolatilityVarianceMesher's grid of the variance. FdHullWhiteSwaptionEngine The finite-difference Hull-White swaption engine: the swaption rolled back on a mesh of the model's factor, its exercise value the swap's inner value on the model's curves (FdmAffineModelSwapInnerValue<TModel>). FdSabrVanillaEngine The finite-difference pricing engine for vanilla options, European, American or Bermudan, on the SABR model dF = α·F^β·dW₁, dα = ν·α·dW₂, d⟨W₁, W₂⟩ = ρ·dt: on FdmCEV1dMesher's grid of the forward, at the volatility's upper quartile, by a grid of the log volatility over ε-quantiles, with the payoff at both ends of the forward discounted from maturity. FdSimpleBSSwingEngine The finite-difference pricing engine for swing options under the Black-Scholes process: the Black-Scholes operator on a grid of the log spot by the rights used, the swing condition at each exercise time (FdmSimpleSwingCondition). FdndimBlackScholesVanillaEngine The n-dimensional finite-difference Black-Scholes engine for basket options on up to four assets: the problem in the principal components of the assets' log prices, rolled back on FdmWienerOp. FordeHestonExpansion Forde, Jacquier and Lee's small-time expansion of the Heston model's implied variance. ForwardEuropeanBSPathPricer The forward-start European path pricer: a plain vanilla payoff on the path's last value, struck at the moneyness times its value at the reset, discounted. ForwardEuropeanHestonPathPricer The forward-start European path pricer on a Heston multi-path: a plain vanilla payoff on the first asset's last value, struck at the moneyness times its value at the reset, discounted. ForwardPerformanceVanillaEngine The forward-start performance engine for vanilla options: the forward engine's inner option, its value per unit of the spot and discounted on the risk-free curve to the reset date. ForwardVanillaEngine The forward-start engine for vanilla options: a vanilla engine run on the forward process from the reset date, at the moneyness times the spot, its results discounted on the dividend curve to the reset date. G2SwaptionEngine The G2 swaption engine: a European swaption priced by G2's analytic formula. Gaussian1dCapFloorEngine The Gaussian1d cap/floor engine: each optionlet's payoff in the model's state at its fixing, deflated by the numeraire and integrated over the state grid. Gaussian1dFloatFloatSwaptionEngine The Gaussian1d float-float swaption engine: the swaption's value rolled back on the model's state grid from its last event, each coupon fixing and exercise date, to today, each leg's coupons estimated at their fixing (an Ibor index's forward rate, a swap index's rate, a swap spread index's two rates geared), capped and floored. Gaussian1dJamshidianSwaptionEngine The Jamshidian swaption engine on a Gaussian1d model: a European swaption decomposed into options on the coupon bond's zero bonds, struck at the state y* where the bond is worth the nominal. Gaussian1dNonstandardSwaptionEngine The one-factor model nonstandard swaption engine: a Bermudan or European exercise into a nonstandard swap, rolled back on the model's state grid. Gaussian1dSwaptionEngine The one-factor model swaption engine: a European or Bermudan swaption rolled back over a grid of a Gaussian1d model's state, each step integrating the next exercise's values' cubic spline against the state's Gaussian density. GaussianCopulaSpreadEngine The Gaussian copula engine for a European spread option, max(S₁ − S₂ − K, 0) and its put, with smile-implied marginals: nested Gauss-Hermite quadrature over a Gaussian copula of the two risk-neutral densities. GeometricAPOHestonPathPricer The path pricer of a discrete geometric average-price Asian option on a Heston path: the discounted payoff at the geometric average of the asset's values at the fixing indices and the past fixings. GeometricAPOPathPricer The path pricer of a discrete geometric average-price Asian option: the discounted payoff at the geometric average of the path's fixings and the past ones. GreeksFunctions The default Greek calculations of QuantLib's greeks.hpp. HestonExpansion A Heston expansion formula for the implied volatility. HestonExpansionEngine The Heston expansion engine: Black's formula at an expansion's implied volatility. HestonHullWhitePathPricer The European path pricer of a hybrid Heston-Hull-White multi-path: the payoff on the underlying's last value over the numeraire at the exercise. IntegralCdsEngine The integral engine for credit default swaps: each coupon period's default leg integrated over steps of a fixed period, from the later of the period's start and the evaluation date. IntegralEngine The pricing engine for European vanilla options by integrating the payoff against the lognormal density of the underlying at expiry, by the segment rule on 5,000 intervals over ten standard deviations each side. IsdaCdsEngine The ISDA engine for credit default swaps: the ISDA CDS Standard Model, the J.P. Morgan CDX model ISDA adopted in 2009, which integrates the protection and the default accrual exactly between the curves' nodes. JamshidianSwaptionEngine The Jamshidian swaption engine: a European swaption decomposed into options on the fixed leg's discount bonds. JuQuadraticApproximationEngine The quadratic approximation engine for American options of N. Ju and R. Zhong ("An Approximate Formula for Pricing American Options", Journal of Derivatives, Winter 1999), on Barone-Adesi and Whaley's critical price. JumpDiffusionEngine The jump-diffusion engine for vanilla options (Merton 1976): the Poisson-weighted sum of Black-Scholes prices conditional on the number of jumps, each on a constant rate and volatility. KirkEngine Kirk's engine for a European spread option on two futures: E. Kirk, "Correlation in the Energy Markets", Managing Energy Price Risk, Risk Publications and Enron, pp. 71-78. LPP2HestonExpansion Lorig, Pagliarani and Pascucci's expansion of order 2 for the Heston model's implied volatility. LPP3HestonExpansion Lorig, Pagliarani and Pascucci's expansion of order 3 for the Heston model's implied volatility. MCAmericanBasketEngine The Longstaff-Schwartz Monte Carlo engine for American and Bermudan basket options on correlated processes. MCAmericanEngine The American Monte Carlo engine: Longstaff and Schwartz's least-squares estimator on Black-Scholes paths, with an optional control variate on the European option. MCBarrierEngine The Monte Carlo pricing engine for barrier options, with the Brownian bridge correction for the barrier's crossings (BarrierPathPricer) or without it (BiasedBarrierPathPricer). MCDigitalEngine The pricing engine for American cash-or-nothing digital options by Monte Carlo simulation, with the Brownian bridge correction for the strike's crossings (DigitalPathPricer). MCDiscreteArithmeticAPEngine The Monte Carlo engine for discrete arithmetic average-price Asian options on a Black-Scholes process, with the geometric average as an optional control variate priced by AnalyticDiscreteGeometricAveragePriceAsianEngine. MCDiscreteArithmeticAPHestonEngine The Monte Carlo engine for discrete arithmetic average-price Asian options on a Heston process, with the geometric average as an optional control variate priced by AnalyticDiscreteGeometricAveragePriceAsianHestonEngine. MCDiscreteArithmeticASEngine The Monte Carlo engine for discrete arithmetic average-strike Asian options on a Black-Scholes process. MCDiscreteAveragingAsianEngineBase<TMc, TPath, TStats> The base of the Monte Carlo engines for discrete-averaging Asian options: a time grid of the fixings to come, paths of the process on it, and a control variate's value from a control engine. MCDiscreteGeometricAPEngine The Monte Carlo engine for discrete geometric average-price Asian options on a Black-Scholes process. MCDiscreteGeometricAPHestonEngine The Monte Carlo engine for discrete geometric average-price Asian options on a Heston process. MCEuropeanBasketEngine The Monte Carlo engine for European basket options on correlated processes. MCEuropeanEngine The European option pricing engine by Monte Carlo simulation. MCEuropeanGJRGARCHEngine The Monte Carlo GJR-GARCH engine for European options. MCEuropeanHestonEngine The Monte Carlo engine for European options under a Heston-like process. MCForwardEuropeanBSEngine The forward-start European option pricing engine by Monte Carlo simulation on a Black-Scholes process. MCForwardEuropeanHestonEngine The forward-start European option pricing engine by Monte Carlo simulation on a Heston process. MCForwardVanillaEngine<TMc, TPath, TStats> The Monte Carlo engine base for forward-start vanilla options. MCHestonHullWhiteEngine The Monte Carlo engine for European options under the hybrid Heston-Hull-White process. MCHullWhiteCapFloorEngine The Monte Carlo Hull-White cap/floor engine: the short rate simulated in the forward measure of the last payment, each path priced by NanoQL.PricingEngines.HullWhiteCapFloorPricer. MCLDAmericanBasketEngine MCAmericanBasketEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDAmericanBasketEngine, QuantLib's MCAmericanBasketEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDAmericanEngine MCAmericanEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDAmericanEngine, QuantLib's MCAmericanEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDBarrierEngine MCBarrierEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDBarrierEngine, QuantLib's MCBarrierEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDDigitalEngine MCDigitalEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDDigitalEngine, QuantLib's MCDigitalEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDDiscreteArithmeticAPEngine MCDiscreteArithmeticAPEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDDiscreteArithmeticAPEngine, QuantLib's MCDiscreteArithmeticAPEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDDiscreteArithmeticAPHestonEngine MCDiscreteArithmeticAPHestonEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDDiscreteArithmeticAPHestonEngine, QuantLib's MCDiscreteArithmeticAPHestonEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDDiscreteArithmeticASEngine MCDiscreteArithmeticASEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDDiscreteArithmeticASEngine, QuantLib's MCDiscreteArithmeticASEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDDiscreteGeometricAPEngine MCDiscreteGeometricAPEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDDiscreteGeometricAPEngine, QuantLib's MCDiscreteGeometricAPEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDDiscreteGeometricAPHestonEngine MCDiscreteGeometricAPHestonEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDDiscreteGeometricAPHestonEngine, QuantLib's MCDiscreteGeometricAPHestonEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDEuropeanBasketEngine MCEuropeanBasketEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDEuropeanBasketEngine, QuantLib's MCEuropeanBasketEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDEuropeanEngine MCEuropeanEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDEuropeanEngine, QuantLib's MCEuropeanEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDEuropeanGJRGARCHEngine MCEuropeanGJRGARCHEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDEuropeanGJRGARCHEngine, QuantLib's MCEuropeanGJRGARCHEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDEuropeanHestonEngine MCEuropeanHestonEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDEuropeanHestonEngine, QuantLib's MCEuropeanHestonEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDForwardEuropeanBSEngine MCForwardEuropeanBSEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDForwardEuropeanBSEngine, QuantLib's MCForwardEuropeanBSEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDForwardEuropeanHestonEngine MCForwardEuropeanHestonEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDForwardEuropeanHestonEngine, QuantLib's MCForwardEuropeanHestonEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDHestonHullWhiteEngine MCHestonHullWhiteEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: MCLDHestonHullWhiteEngine, named as QuantLib-Python names its siblings, QuantLib's MCHestonHullWhiteEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDHullWhiteCapFloorEngine MCHullWhiteCapFloorEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: MCLDHullWhiteCapFloorEngine, named as QuantLib-Python names its siblings, QuantLib's MCHullWhiteCapFloorEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDLookbackEngine MCLookbackEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: MCLDLookbackEngine, named as QuantLib-Python names its siblings, QuantLib's MCLookbackEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDPerformanceEngine MCPerformanceEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDPerformanceEngine, QuantLib's MCPerformanceEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. MCLDVarianceSwapEngine MCVarianceSwapEngine on low-discrepancy draws with QuantLib's default statistics: QuantLib-Python's MCLDVarianceSwapEngine, QuantLib's MCVarianceSwapEngine<LowDiscrepancy>, its calculations closed at LowDiscrepancy and GeneralStatistics. api/NanoQL.Processes.BatesProcess.html.summary: Class BatesProcess Namespace NanoQL.Processes Assembly NanoQL.dll The Bates process: the Heston square-root stochastic-volatility process with log-normal jumps, dS = (r − q − λm)S dt + √v S dW₁ + (e^J − 1)S dN, dv = κ(θ − v) dt + σ√v dW₂, dW₁dW₂ = ρ dt, N a Poisson process of intensity λ and J normal with mean ν and standard deviation δ, m = e^{ν + δ²/2} − 1. public sealed class BatesProcess : HestonProcess Inheritance object StochasticProcess HestonProcess BatesProcess Inherited Members HestonProcess.InitialValues() HestonProcess.InitialValues(Span<double>) HestonProcess.Diffusion(double, Vector) HestonProcess.Apply(Vector, Vector) HestonProcess.Pdf(double, double, double, double) HestonProcess.Time(Date) HestonProcess.Size HestonProcess.S0 HestonProcess.V0 HestonProcess.Rho HestonProcess.Kappa HestonProcess.Theta HestonProcess.Sigma HestonProcess.DividendYield HestonProcess.RiskFreeRate StochasticProcess.Expectation(double, Vector, double) StochasticProcess.StdDeviation(double, Vector, double) StochasticProcess.Covariance(double, Vector, double) object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable, a HestonProcess as QuantLib's derives from it: its drift less λm, two more factors, the first drawing the step's number of jumps through the inverse Poisson distribution and the second their sizes, and QuantLib's default discretization, full truncation, where the Heston process's is the quadratic-exponential martingale scheme. The in-place Evolve(double, ReadOnlySpan<double>, double, ReadOnlySpan<double>, Span<double>) allocates nothing where the Heston step doesn't. Constructors BatesProcess(YieldTermStructure, YieldTermStructure, double, double, double, double, double, double, double, double, double, HestonProcessDiscretization) Initializes a new instance of the BatesProcess class. public BatesProcess(YieldTermStructure riskFreeRate, YieldTermStructure dividendYield, double s0, double v0, double kappa, double theta, double sigma, double rho, double lambda, double nu, double delta, HestonProcessDiscretization d = HestonProcessDiscretization.FullTruncation) Parameters riskFreeRate YieldTermStructure The risk-free curve. dividendYield YieldTermStructure The dividend curve. s0 double The underlying's value. v0 double The variance's value. kappa double The variance's mean-reversion speed κ. theta double The variance's long-run mean θ. sigma double The variance's volatility σ. rho double The correlation ρ of the two Brownian motions. lambda double The jumps' intensity λ. nu double The log jump size's mean ν. delta double The log jump size's standard deviation δ. d HestonProcessDiscretization The discretization the Heston part steps by; full truncation by default. Exceptions ArgumentNullException A curve is null. ArgumentOutOfRangeException d isn't a member of its enum. Properties Delta Gets the log jump size's standard deviation δ. public double Delta { get; } Property Value double Factors Gets the number of independent factors of the process; by default, its Size. public override int Factors { get; } Property Value int Remarks Three for Broadie and Kaya's schemes, which sample the integrated variance with the third; two otherwise. Lambda Gets the jumps' intensity λ. public double Lambda { get; } Property Value double Nu Gets the log jump size's mean ν. public double Nu { get; } Property Value double Methods Drift(double, Vector) The drift part of the equation, μ(t, x_t). public override Vector Drift(double t, Vector x) Parameters t double The time. x Vector The state. Returns Vector A new vector. Exceptions ArgumentException x holds fewer values than the state, where QuantLib reads past its end. Evolve(double, Vector, double, Vector) The state after a time interval Δt; by default E(x0, t0, Δt) + S(x0, t0, Δt) · Δw, where E is the expectation and S the standard deviation, applied to the expectation by Apply(Vector, Vector). public override Vector Evolve(double t0, Vector x0, double dt, Vector dw) Parameters t0 double The start of the interval. x0 Vector The state at its start. dt double The interval's length. dw Vector The Brownian increments, one per factor. Returns Vector A new vector. Exceptions ArgumentException The sizes don't match. NanoQLException The quadratic-exponential martingale correction has no solution ("illegal value"), or the variance's law can't be inverted. ArgumentException x0 holds fewer values than the state, or dw fewer increments than the process's factors, where QuantLib reads past its end. NanoQLException The Heston step refuses. ArgumentException dw holds fewer increments than the process's factors, where QuantLib reads past its end. Evolve(double, ReadOnlySpan<double>, double, ReadOnlySpan<double>, Span<double>) The state after a time interval Δt, written into the caller's span: the in-place form of Evolve(double, Vector, double, Vector), by default its values, copied. public override void Evolve(double t0, ReadOnlySpan<double> x0, double dt, ReadOnlySpan<double> dw, Span<double> result) Parameters t0 double The start of the interval. x0 ReadOnlySpan<double> The state at its start, of the process's Size. dt double The interval's length. dw ReadOnlySpan<double> The Brownian increments, one per factor. result Span<double> The state at the interval's end, of the process's size at least; it mustn't overlap x0 or dw. Remarks The truncation, reflection and quadratic-exponential schemes step without allocating, by QuantLib's arithmetic, so the values are Evolve(double, Vector, double, Vector)'s bit for bit; the exact schemes step through it. Exceptions ArgumentException The sizes don't match. NanoQLException The quadratic-exponential martingale correction has no solution ("illegal value"), or the variance's law can't be inverted. ArgumentException x0 holds fewer values than the state, or dw fewer increments than the process's factors, where QuantLib reads past their end; or result is shorter than the state. NanoQLException The Heston step refuses. ArgumentException dw holds fewer increments than the process's factors, where QuantLib reads past its end.

api/NanoQL.Processes.CoxIngersollRossPro.summary: Class CoxIngersollRossProcess Namespace NanoQL.Processes Assembly NanoQL.dll The Cox-Ingersoll-Ross process, governed by dx(t) = k(θ − x(t))dt + σ√x(t) dW(t), discretized by Leif Andersen's quadratic-exponential scheme ("Efficient Simulation of the Heston Stochastic Volatility Model"). public sealed class CoxIngersollRossProcess : StochasticProcess1D Inheritance object StochasticProcess StochasticProcess1D CoxIngersollRossProcess Inherited Members StochasticProcess1D.Apply(double, double) StochasticProcess1D.InitialValues() StochasticProcess1D.Drift(double, Vector) StochasticProcess1D.Diffusion(double, Vector) StochasticProcess1D.Expectation(double, Vector, double) StochasticProcess1D.StdDeviation(double, Vector, double) StochasticProcess1D.Covariance(double, Vector, double) StochasticProcess1D.Evolve(double, Vector, double, Vector) StochasticProcess1D.Apply(Vector, Vector) StochasticProcess1D.Size StochasticProcess.InitialValues(Span<double>) StochasticProcess.Evolve(double, ReadOnlySpan<double>, double, ReadOnlySpan<double>, Span<double>) StochasticProcess.Time(Date) StochasticProcess.Factors object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Variance(double, double, double) is the conditional variance the scheme's own step reads, x₀σ²e^(−kΔt)(1 − e^(−kΔt))/k + θσ²(1 − e^(−kΔt))²/(2k), at the state given, and Diffusion(double, double) is σ√x, the header's SDE (K2): a divergence, QuantLib's variance reading the process's initial value for the state and θσ²/k for its level term, and its diffusion σ (coxingersollrossprocess.cpp:32-38, .hpp:90-92; Divergences/CirProcessMomentsTests.cs). api/NanoQL.Processes.G2Process.html.summary: Class G2Process Namespace NanoQL.Processes Assembly NanoQL.dll The G2 stochastic process: the two-factor G2++ process with its state shifted so that the two components sum to the short rate, (z₁, z₂) = (x + φ(t), y), x and y the zero-mean Ornstein-Uhlenbeck factors and φ the deterministic offset that fits the initial curve; without a curve, the two zero-mean processes (φ ≡ 0). public sealed class G2Process : StochasticProcess Inheritance object StochasticProcess G2Process Inherited Members StochasticProcess.InitialValues(Span<double>) StochasticProcess.Evolve(double, Vector, double, Vector) StochasticProcess.Evolve(double, ReadOnlySpan<double>, double, ReadOnlySpan<double>, Span<double>) StochasticProcess.Apply(Vector, Vector) StochasticProcess.Time(Date) StochasticProcess.Factors object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A path generated on it satisfies r(tᵢ) = z₁ᵢ + z₂ᵢ, its expectation φ(tᵢ). The step's conditional correlation, QuantLib's ρση(1 − e^(−(a+b)Δt))/(a + b) over ½ση√((1 − e^(−2aΔt))(1 − e^(−2bΔt))/(ab)), is written as ρ·f((a+b)Δt)/√(f(2aΔt)·f(2bΔt)), f(x) = (1 − e^(−x))/x, and held in [−1, 1], ρ itself where a = b; φ's terms as G2's: a divergence, QuantLib's √(1 − ρ²) of a correlation an ulp past ±1 being NaN at ρ = ±1 with a = b (Divergences/G2ProcessCorrelationBoundTests.cs), and its terms cancelling at small reversion. api/NanoQL.Processes.GJRGARCHProcess.htm.summary: Class GJRGARCHProcess Namespace NanoQL.Processes Assembly NanoQL.dll The GJR-GARCH(1,1) process in its continuous-time limit: dS = μS dt + √v S dW₁ and dv = (ω + (β + αq₂ + γq₃ − 1)v) dt + (ασ₁₂ + γσ₁₃)v dW₁ + √(α²(σ₂² − σ₁₂²) + γ²(σ₃² − σ₁₃²) + 2αγ(σ₂₃ − σ₁₂σ₁₃)) v dW₂, with the moments of the news shocks at the market price of risk λ, the daily parameters scaled by the days per year. Its state is the underlying and the annualized variance. public sealed class GJRGARCHProcess : StochasticProcess Inheritance object StochasticProcess GJRGARCHProcess Inherited Members StochasticProcess.Expectation(double, Vector, double) StochasticProcess.StdDeviation(double, Vector, double) StochasticProcess.Covariance(double, Vector, double) StochasticProcess.Factors object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable: the curves, the spot and the parameters are fixed at construction, where QuantLib's process holds handles and a quote; the shocks' moments, which depend on λ, α, γ and the days per year only, are computed once there by QuantLib's arithmetic, where QuantLib's process recomputes them in each call. Pdf(double, double, double, double) The joint density of the log spot x and the variance v at time t: the variance's non-central chi-squared density times the log spot's conditional density given it, from the integrated variance's characteristic function (Broadie and Kaya). public double Pdf(double x, double v, double t, double eps = 0.001) Parameters x double The log spot. v double The variance. t double The time, on the risk-free curve's clock. eps double QuantLib's accuracy for a tail search whose result its own code overwrites (hestonprocess.cpp:307-323): the density depends on it neither there nor here. Returns double The density. Remarks The dividend curve is read at the instant t denotes on the risk-free curve's clock, nothing accrued before its own reference date (the mismatched-dates class); QuantLib's read, the dividend curve's own time t, where the two curves share their times. QuantLib's density doesn't hold its digits (hestonprocess.cpp:300-334). It integrates over the integrated variance up to twice a Cornish-Fisher quantile whose skew and kurtosis are finite differences of the characteristic function at a step of 1e-2, which rest on its last bits, and that cut-off can fall where the integrand is still a fifth of its peak (10% low on ordinary inputs); and its 128-point Gauss-Laguerre rule for the conditional density reaches u ≈ 500, where at short times the characteristic function hasn't decayed (NaN and negative densities at a quarter of a year). Here the log spot's conditional density given the variance is the inversion of its characteristic function: given the integrated variance ξ the log spot is normal, with mean x₀ + a − cξ and variance (1 − ρ²)ξ, c = ½ − ρκ/σ, as QuantLib's integrand has it, so its characteristic function given the variance is e^{iu(x₀ + a)}·Φ(−uc + i·½u²(1 − ρ²)), Φ the integrated variance's, with the Bessel ratio in its exponentially weighted form. The inversion integral runs by 32-point Gauss-Legendre panels no wider than the integrand's oscillation and decay allow, out to where E[e^{−½u²(1 − ρ²)ξ}], which bounds the integrand, falls below 1e-17. A documented divergence (Divergences/HestonPdfTests.cs), checked by the log spot's marginal, the density integrated over the variance, against the log spot's density from Heston's characteristic function, which QuantLib's analytic Heston engine prices by. Where the variance's density is 0 the density is 0. The value's absolute accuracy is about 1e-13, the inversion's rounding floor: far from the density's mass it is noise of that size, of either sign. Exceptions NanoQLException Boost's non-central chi-squared refuses its arguments; |ρ| is 1, where the log spot's conditional density has no variance; or the inversion doesn't converge within 100,000 panels. api/NanoQL.Processes.HestonProcessDiscre.summary: Enum HestonProcessDiscretization Namespace NanoQL.Processes Assembly NanoQL.dll The schemes Evolve(double, Vector, double, Vector) steps by: QuantLib's HestonProcess::Discretization. public enum HestonProcessDiscretization Fields BroadieKayaExactSchemeLaguerre = 7 Broadie and Kaya's exact scheme, its integrated variance by Gauss-Laguerre integration. BroadieKayaExactSchemeLobatto = 6 Broadie and Kaya's exact scheme, its integrated variance by Gauss-Lobatto integration. BroadieKayaExactSchemeTrapezoidal = 8 Broadie and Kaya's exact scheme, its integrated variance by the trapezoid rule on sine integrals. FullTruncation = 1 Euler's step, the variance floored at zero throughout. NonCentralChiSquareVariance = 3 The variance sampled exactly from its non-central chi-squared law. PartialTruncation = 0 Euler's step, the variance floored at zero in the diffusion and the drift's square root. QuadraticExponential = 4 Andersen's quadratic-exponential scheme. QuadraticExponentialMartingale = 5 Andersen's quadratic-exponential scheme with its martingale correction. Reflection = 2 Euler's step on the variance's absolute value.

The Hull-White process the hybrid evolves, its model and its numeraire's end discount are on the Heston process's risk-free curve, from the given process's reversion, volatility and forward-measure time, which HullWhiteProcess returns; the given process's own curve isn't read. QuantLib builds its model on the Heston curve but takes the short rate from the given process's curve (hybridhestonhullwhiteprocess.cpp:37-46, :64, :137, :179), so the numeraire prices a bond on one curve at a rate taken from the other; here all of it runs on the one curve, QuantLib's bits where the two curves are one. api/NanoQL.Processes.html.summary: Namespace NanoQL.Processes Classes BatesProcess The Bates process: the Heston square-root stochastic-volatility process with log-normal jumps, dS = (r − q − λm)S dt + √v S dW₁ + (e^J − 1)S dN, dv = κ(θ − v) dt + σ√v dW₂, dW₁dW₂ = ρ dt, N a Poisson process of intensity λ and J normal with mean ν and standard deviation δ, m = e^{ν + δ²/2} − 1. BlackProcess Black's (1976) process for a forward or futures contract, d ln S(t) = −σ(t, S)²/2 dt + σ dW_t: the generalized process with its risk-free curve as the dividend curve too. BlackScholesMertonProcess Merton's (1973) extension of the Black-Scholes process to a stock or stock index paying a continuous dividend yield, d ln S(t) = (r(t) − q(t) − σ(t, S)²/2) dt + σ dW_t. BlackScholesProcess The Black-Scholes (1973) stochastic process, d ln S(t) = (r(t) − σ(t, S)²/2) dt + σ dW_t: the generalized process with no dividend yield. The interface is expressed in S; the internal calculations work on ln S. CoxIngersollRossProcess The Cox-Ingersoll-Ross process, governed by dx(t) = k(θ − x(t))dt + σ√x(t) dW(t), discretized by Leif Andersen's quadratic-exponential scheme ("Efficient Simulation of the Heston Stochastic Volatility Model"). EndEulerDiscretization Euler end-point discretization for stochastic processes: over a time interval Δt, the drift μ(t0 + Δt, x0) Δt, the diffusion σ(t0 + Δt, x0) √Δt and the covariance σ(t0 + Δt, x0) σ(t0 + Δt, x0)ᵀ Δt. EulerDiscretization Euler discretization for stochastic processes: over a time interval Δt, the drift μ(t0, x0) Δt, the diffusion σ(t0, x0) √Δt and the covariance σ(t0, x0) σ(t0, x0)ᵀ Δt. ForwardMeasureProcess A stochastic process whose dynamics are expressed in the forward measure of a time T. ForwardMeasureProcess1D A one-dimensional stochastic process whose dynamics are expressed in the forward measure of a time T. G2ForwardProcess The forward G2 stochastic process: G2Process's in the forward measure of a time T, its state again shifted so that z₁ + z₂ = r(t), with the T-forward corrections to the drift and the conditional expectation. G2Process The G2 stochastic process: the two-factor G2++ process with its state shifted so that the two components sum to the short rate, (z₁, z₂) = (x + φ(t), y), x and y the zero-mean Ornstein-Uhlenbeck factors and φ the deterministic offset that fits the initial curve; without a curve, the two zero-mean processes (φ ≡ 0). GJRGARCHProcess The GJR-GARCH(1,1) process in its continuous-time limit: dS = μS dt + √v S dW₁ and dv = (ω + (β + αq₂ + γq₃ − 1)v) dt + (ασ₁₂ + γσ₁₃)v dW₁ + √(α²(σ₂² − σ₁₂²) + γ²(σ₃² − σ₁₃²) + 2αγ(σ₂₃ − σ₁₂σ₁₃)) v dW₂, with the moments of the news shocks at the market price of risk λ, the daily parameters scaled by the days per year. Its state is the underlying and the annualized variance. GarmanKohlagenProcess The Garman-Kohlhagen (1983) process for an exchange rate, d ln S(t) = (r(t) − r_f(t) − σ(t, S)²/2) dt + σ dW_t: the generalized process with the foreign risk-free curve as the dividend curve. QuantLib's spelling of the class name is kept. GeneralizedBlackScholesProcess The generalized Black-Scholes stochastic process, d ln S(t) = (r(t) − q(t) − σ(t, S)²/2) dt + σ dW_t, on a risk-free curve, a dividend curve and a Black volatility, with its local volatility σ(t, S) derived from the Black one. The interface is expressed in S; the internal calculations work on ln S. GeometricBrownianMotionProcess The geometric Brownian-motion process, governed by dS(t, S) = μS dt + σS dW_t. GsrProcess The GSR model's state process, with piecewise constant volatilities and reversions, its dynamics expressed in the forward measure of a time T. For a derivation of the formulas, see http://ssrn.com/abstract=2246013. HestonProcess The Heston square-root stochastic-volatility process: dS = μS dt + √v S dW₁, dv = κ(θ − v) dt + σ√v dW₂, with dW₁dW₂ = ρ dt. Its state is the underlying and the variance. HestonSLVProcess The Heston stochastic-local volatility process: the Heston process's spot with its volatility √v scaled by a leverage function L(t, S), and its variance's volatility scaled by a mixing factor. HullWhiteForwardProcess The forward Hull-White stochastic process: HullWhiteProcess's dynamics in the forward measure of a time T, the drift less B(t, T)σ² and the expectation less M_T(t₀, t₀ + Δt, T). HullWhiteProcess The Hull-White stochastic process: the short rate r = x + α(t), x an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process of speed a and volatility σ from the curve's instantaneous forward at 0, and α(t) = f(t) + ½(σ(1 − e^(−at))/a)², f the curve's instantaneous forward. HybridHestonHullWhiteProcess The three-factor hybrid of a Heston equity and a Hull-White short rate in its forward measure: its state is the underlying, its variance and the short rate, the equity correlated with the short rate. JointStochasticProcess A multi-model process for hybrid products: its constituents' states stacked, their factors correlated across models by a derived class's cross-model correlation. Merton76Process The Merton-76 jump-diffusion process: a Black-Scholes-Merton diffusion with lognormal jumps at a Poisson intensity. MfStateProcess The Markov-functional model's state process, dx = σ(t) e^{at} dW(t), with a piecewise constant volatility σ and a constant reversion a. OrnsteinUhlenbeckProcess The Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, governed by dx = a (r − x_t) dt + σ dW_t. SquareRootProcess The square-root process, governed by dx = a(b − x_t) dt + σ√x_t dW_t. StochasticProcessArray An array of correlated one-dimensional stochastic processes. Enums GJRGARCHProcessDiscretization The schemes GJRGARCHProcess steps by: QuantLib's GJRGARCHProcess::Discretization. HestonProcessDiscretization The schemes Evolve(double, Vector, double, Vector) steps by: QuantLib's HestonProcess::Discretization. HybridHestonHullWhiteProcessDiscretization The schemes HybridHestonHullWhiteProcess steps by: QuantLib's HybridHestonHullWhiteProcess::Discretization.

api/NanoQL.Quotes.EurodollarFuturesImpli.summary: Class EurodollarFuturesImpliedStdDevQuote Namespace NanoQL.Quotes Assembly NanoQL.dll The standard deviation implied by a Eurodollar futures option's price: QuantLib's EurodollarFuturesImpliedStdDevQuote. public sealed class EurodollarFuturesImpliedStdDevQuote Inheritance object EurodollarFuturesImpliedStdDevQuote Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The futures price and strike are quoted as 100 less a rate; the solve is on the rate, so a call on the futures is a put on the rate. Where the rate strike, 100 less the strike, is above the rate forward, 100 less the futures price, QuantLib solves a call on the rate at the put's price, and otherwise a put on the rate at the call's price; it reads only that price. QuantLib's isValid isn't ported: an index with no stored fixing is refused at construction, with QuantLib's text. The reference date is the last stored fixing's date on or before the evaluation date, where QuantLib's is the earlier of the last stored date and the evaluation date (lastfixingquote.cpp:40-43): on a store holding fixings after the evaluation date, as a backtest on one full history does, QuantLib's is the evaluation date itself, whose fixing is refused on a non-fixing day or forecast where it is missing. Where the store holds no fixing on or before the evaluation date, the reference date is QuantLib's, the evaluation date. A documented divergence; on a store that ends on or before the evaluation date the two agree. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.AbcdCalibratio.summary: Class AbcdCalibration Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll The abcd instantaneous volatility fitted to Black volatilities by their maturities: the root-mean-square error of the abcd Black volatilities, minimized over a, b, c and d through QuantLib's transformation (c, d and a + d positive), the fixed parameters at their guesses. public sealed class AbcdCalibration Inheritance object AbcdCalibration Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable: Compute() returns the fitted calibration, where QuantLib's compute() changes the object; before it the parameters are the guesses, and the weights 1/n. One of QuantLib's refusals is narrowed: QuantLib's transformation leaves b free, so its optimizer can step to a trial point the abcd function's validation refuses, and the fit throws. Here such a trial point's residuals are 1.0 each, a guard that keeps every fit QuantLib completes bit for bit, since none of them reaches such a point. A fit on which the guard acted is returned where it ends inside the valid region and refused with QuantLib's text, its first invalid trial point's, where it ends against the zero floor: its lowest instantaneous volatility below 1% of the smallest Black volatility given, as for data whose total variance shrinks, which no valid curve fits. One of QuantLib's defects is fixed: its transformation gives a as a positive a + d less d, so with a fixed and d free it fixes a + d, and the fit moves a by what it moves d. Here a fixed keeps its guess, and d stays above max(0, −a), the same region; every other choice of fixed parameters is QuantLib's. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.AndreasenHugeV.title: Class AndreasenHugeVolatilityInterpl | nanoql
api/NanoQL.TermStructures.AndreasenHugeV.summary: Class AndreasenHugeVolatilityInterpl Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll Andreasen and Huge's calibration of a local volatility surface to a sparse grid of European options: at each expiry a piecewise volatility in log strike, fitted so that one implicit step of the forward equation from the previous expiry's prices reprices the expiry's options; prices and local volatilities between expiries by partial steps. Andreasen J., Huge B., 2010. Volatility Interpolation, https://ssrn.com/abstract=1694972. public sealed class AndreasenHugeVolatilityInterpl Inheritance object AndreasenHugeVolatilityInterpl Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Immutable, calibrated at construction (the playbook's LazyObject row), where QuantLib calibrates on first use. Its local-volatility and price slices at a time are memoised by that time, as QuantLib caches them, in thread-safe maps inside the object (a named departure from the stateless rule): each slice is computed from the calibration by QuantLib's arithmetic, so its bits are the same whichever thread computes it first, and every query returns what a fresh object returns. Without them an engine reading the surface at every grid point and step would recompute a slice per read, about 130 times QuantLib's cost. The call-put calibration's error picks a put's error for a strike below the forward and a call's above it, where QuantLib compares the forward with the j-th grid point rather than the j-th strike, and so always takes the puts' (andreasenhugevolatilityinterpl.cpp:418). The dividend curve is read at the instants the risk-free curve's times denote, on its own clock, where QuantLib reads it at those times (the mismatched-dates class); curves that share a clock keep QuantLib's bits. Documented divergences. Its dates are the earliest date and the latest date, the BMA value date of the first Wednesday after the swap's maturity; the maturity, latest relevant and pillar dates fall back on the latest date. The copy is priced by DiscountingBondEngine on the curve the helper is bound to, and only on that curve: the bond's floating coupons keep forecasting on their own index's curve, as QuantLib relinks only its discounting handle. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.BootstrapHelpe.summary: Class BootstrapHelper<TTermStructure> Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll The base of the helpers a term structure is bootstrapped on: an instrument's quote, the dates it determines, and the quote the curve implies. public abstract class BootstrapHelper<TTermStructure> : IBootstrapHelper where TTermStructure : TermStructure Type Parameters TTermStructure The kind of term structure the helper prices against. Inheritance object BootstrapHelper<TTermStructure> Implements IBootstrapHelper Derived YoYOptionletHelper RateHelper RelativeDateBootstrapHelper<TTermStructure> Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A helper is immutable. QuantLib's setTermStructure, which links the curve under construction into the helper, becomes SetTermStructure<T>(T, YieldTermStructure): it returns a copy bound to the term structure, which has rebuilt on itself whatever prices against it (an index cloned on the curve, a swap's coupons copied with that index). The helper it was called on stays unbound, and an unbound helper's ImpliedQuote(EvaluationContext) throws "term structure not set". The bootstraps bind copies of a curve's helpers to the curve under construction, and discard them when the curve is built. A helper whose dates follow the evaluation date (QuantLib's RelativeDateBootstrapHelper) computes them in its constructor from the context's evaluation date, which it records. QuantLib's helper re-runs initializeDates() whenever the global evaluation date moves; here, a curve built for another evaluation date binds a copy of the helper re-dated for it, through InitializeDates(EvaluationContext), so a curve's helpers always have its evaluation date's dates. A helper built with explicit dates (updateDates false) is used as built. The five dates are QuantLib's, with its fallbacks: the maturity date falls back on the latest relevant date, which falls back on the latest date, as the pillar date does; the latest date falls back on the stored pillar date. A null date is QuantLib's Date(), which the bootstraps read as earlier than every date. An extension point: the protected date fields are written by a derived constructor and by InitializeDates(EvaluationContext), on a helper under construction or on a fresh copy only. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.CmsMarket.html.summary: Class CmsMarket Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll A set of CMS quotes: the bid and ask spreads over the Ibor leg of CMS swaps of each length on each swap index, with the spreads, spot and forward CMS leg NPVs the market implies and the model gives. public sealed class CmsMarket Inheritance object CmsMarket Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks For each swap length and index the market's spot CMS leg NPV is implied from the spot swap's Ibor leg (its NPV and BPS on the discounting curve at its reference date, and the mid spread), and a forward CMS leg is the difference of two spot ones; the model prices each forward-starting CMS swap's CMS leg with the index's pricer and sums them into spot legs, whose equilibrium spread over the Ibor leg is the model's spread. QuantLib's market is a lazy object that its calibration reprices in place, giving its pricers a new volatility and mean reversion. This one computes at construction, under the context it is given, and Reprice(SwaptionVolatilityStructure?, double?, EvaluationContext) returns a new market whose pricers are copies with the new volatility and reversion, its legs re-priced through CouponPricerFunctions; QuantLib's pricers, shared with other legs, change with its reprice, which an immutable pricer can't. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.CmsMarketCalib.summary: Class CmsMarketCalibration Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll The calibration of a SABR swaption cube's βs, and of the CMS pricers' mean reversion, to a CMS market: QuantLib's CmsMarketCalibration. public sealed class CmsMarketCalibration Inheritance object CmsMarketCalibration Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Each cost evaluation recalibrates the cube's sections at the candidate βs, one swap tenor after another, reprices the market on it at the candidate reversion, and reads the market's weighted errors on the calibration's type. The βs enter the optimizer as y with β = exp(−y²), clamped to [1e-6, 0.999999], and the reversion as y with reversion = √|y|. The βs reach the cube as its sections' β guesses: they are the cube's βs on a cube that fixes β, and the refit's starting point on one that doesn't, whose results' cube holds the βs fitted. QuantLib's calibration recalibrates its cube and reprices its market in place; here each Compute(EndCriteria, OptimizationMethod, Vector, bool, EvaluationContext) starts from the cube and market it was given, each cost evaluation building a new cube from the last one and a new market, as QuantLib's evaluations change the one cube in turn, and it returns the recalibrated cube and repriced market in its results, the calibration's own left unchanged. Three of QuantLib's defects are fixed: the fixed-reversion path's β guess enters the optimizer transformed, as its other paths' do; the reversion is √|y|, where QuantLib's √y returns NaN for an optimizer step to y below 0; and a fixed reversion is passed to the pricers as given, where QuantLib passes it through the transform's round trip, √(m²) = |m|. Its reference date and day counter are the first curve's, read when it is built, and so is its extrapolation flag, set when both curves extrapolate; its calendar, settlement days, maximum date and maximum time are the first curve's, read when they are asked for. Curves that change make a new curve: QuantLib's curve follows its handles. QuantLib reads the second curve's zero rate at the composite's time, a time on the first curve's clock, which the second curve counts from its own reference date on its own day counter. Here the second curve is read at the instant that time denotes: its zero rate is the one implied over the composite's time by its discount from the composite's reference date to that instant, none accruing before its own reference date, the second curve restated on the first's clock. Where the two curves share their reference date and day counter, as QuantLib's case builds them, it is QuantLib's read and bits. A documented divergence. DeWetering, G. Lucas, R. Brenner and A. Shapiro (2001): "Merrill Lynch Exponential Spline Model." Merrill Lynch Working Paper. κ can be given a fixed value, which takes it out of the optimization. Convergence may be slow. Constrained at zero, the first coefficient is 1 less the others' sum, so d(0) = 1. QuantLib's constructor without the optimization method is the first constructor with l2 named. With κ fixed, QuantLib's discount function sums one term fewer than the coefficients it fits (nonlinearfittingmethods.cpp:84, :91), right when the last parameter is κ: the last coefficient is dead. Here every coefficient is summed when κ is fixed, the discount function of the method with κ free at the same coefficients and κ; with κ free it is QuantLib's. A documented divergence.
