The fit can be slow with many bonds, and its speed depends on the method and its convergence under the optimization. Built from given parameters, the curve doesn't fit: it evaluates the method's discount function on them, up to a given maximum date, for example to use parameters fitted to bonds in one currency as a credit spread curve over a discount curve in another. The curve fits in its constructor, as a LazyObject's work is done at construction, so a fit that fails, or an input it refuses, refuses the curve where QuantLib throws at the first read. While it fits, the curve answers at the fit's trial parameters, and its bond helpers are copies bound to the curve itself, as QuantLib binds them to this; nothing outside the constructor sees the curve change. QuantLib's quotes are doubles here, always valid, so its check of an invalid price quote has nothing to refuse. QuantLib's constructors taking settlement days, whose reference date moves with the evaluation date, are the Create(int, Calendar, IEnumerable<BondHelper>, DayCounter, FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod, EvaluationContext, double, int, IEnumerable<double>?, double, int) factories. A curve is always built afresh, fitted from the given guess, the initial guess the L2 penalty's header doc anchors it to. QuantLib's curve keeps its last solution as its guess (fittedbonddiscountcurve.cpp:294-295), so recalculated after a quote moves it starts from, and is penalized towards, its previous fit. A documented divergence. QuantLib's resetGuess, which refits in place, is ResetGuess(IEnumerable<double>, EvaluationContext), which returns the curve refitted. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.FittedBondDisc.summary: Class FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll The base fitting method of a FittedBondDiscountCurve: the methodology that constructs the curve, a discount function of parameters fitted to the bonds' prices. public abstract class FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod Inheritance object FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod Derived CubicBSplinesFitting ExponentialSplinesFitting NaturalCubicFitting NelsonSiegelFitting SimplePolynomialFitting SpreadFittingMethod SvenssonFitting Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A derived method defines DiscountFunction(ReadOnlySpan<double>, double) and Size, the number of parameters fitted. The generic fit is nonlinear, in contrast to the typically faster linear fitting methods. The bonds' price errors are weighted by the given weights, or by their inverse modified durations, normalized; an L2 penalty, if given, applies a Gaussian prior to each parameter around the initial guess. Before the minimum cut-off time and after the maximum one the discount extrapolates with a flat instantaneous forward rate. The parameters of a method may need tuning for a proper, reasonable or fast convergence, depending on the method. QuantLib's public nested class FittedBondDiscountCurve::FittingMethod. A curve fits a copy of its method, made as QuantLib's clone() makes it, and its FitResults is that copy, holding the fit's solution, iterations, cost, end criterion and the weights it used; the method given stays as it was built. So a derived method needs no clone of its own. An extension point, as in QuantLib. Its volatility is the lognormal one implied from them, 0 where it can't be implied. public sealed class Gaussian1dSmileSection : SmileSection Inheritance object SmileSection Gaussian1dSmileSection Inherited Members SmileSection.ReferenceDate() SmileSection.Variance(double) SmileSection.Volatility(double) SmileSection.Volatility(double, VolatilityType, double) SmileSection.DigitalOptionPrice(double, OptionType, double, double) SmileSection.Density(double, double, double) SmileSection.Vega(double, double) SmileSection.ExerciseDate SmileSection.VolatilityType SmileSection.Shift SmileSection.ExerciseTime SmileSection.DayCounter object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks If curves are attached to the index, the engine's default discounting uses them; if not, the model's curve. The at-the-money level and the annuity are computed at construction under the context given, which the section keeps for its prices. An engine is a function, nanoql's engines being static: by default QuantLib's, the Gaussian1d swaption engine on the swap index's discounting curve or the cap/floor engine on the model curve, 64 points a side and 7 standard deviations. Two of QuantLib's defects are fixed. QuantLib's caplet starts on the fixing date, so it fixes two business days before the date of the forward it is quoted against; here it starts on the fixing's value date. And QuantLib 1.44 refuses every section on an Ibor index ("cannot calculate ATM without a BlackCapFloorEngine or BachelierCapFloorEngine"): the caplet its annuity reads is built without a strike or an engine, which its builder needs for the at-the-money strike; here it is struck at the forward, the annuity reading only its dates. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.GlobalBootstra.summary: Struct GlobalBootstrap Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll The global bootstrapper, with additional restrictions: the curve's nodes are solved together, by an optimizer that minimizes the helpers' quote errors and any additional penalties. public readonly struct GlobalBootstrap : IBootstrap Implements IBootstrap Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.GetType() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks A configuration struct (IBootstrap): its zero value is QuantLib's default construction. QuantLib's three constructors are one, with optional parameters. An optimizer or end criteria not given is QuantLib's default, built when a curve is built: a LevenbergMarquardt method and EndCriteria of 1000 iterations and 10 stationary ones, each tolerance the accuracy, which is the curve's when not given. The curve's nodes are its first date, the pillars of its helpers alive at that date and the additional dates after it, sorted, each once. The additional dates are a collection, where QuantLib's are a functor of the evaluation date, since a curve is built once. The error terms are the alive helpers' quote errors, each times its instrument weight, then the additional penalties: together they must be at least as many as the nodes after the first. The additional helpers are bound to the curve as its helpers are, but add no pillar or error term of their own: the penalties price them. The penalties and the initial-guess function receive the curve's working state (IBootstrapState), whose helpers and additional helpers are bound to the curve, and the context, where QuantLib's reach the helpers through the user's own pointers, which the bootstrap has linked to the curve. In a multicurve the members' curves are set up in the order they were added, before any is optimized, so a guess function that prices a helper on a bootstrapped member added after its own curve, or on a curve that reads one, meets that member's refusal, "curve not set up yet"; the penalties run once every member is set up. QuantLib's guess function takes the times and data, and prices nothing. The additional variables (AdditionalVariables) are optimized beside the nodes, the argument's values for the nodes first and then the variables', from their guesses. The helpers that read them are built by VariableHelpers from their values: once at their guesses when the curve is built, which gives their pillars and latest relevant dates, and again at each evaluation of the cost function, as QuantLib's helpers read their quotes then. They follow the curve's helpers, in the order the function returns them: the alive ones add their pillars and their quote errors, after the curve's helpers' and before the penalties, and the instrument weights cover the curve's helpers and then these, one weight each, as QuantLib's error vector reads its instruments in their order, the variables' helpers among them. A later build whose helpers' pillars differ from the first's is refused, as QuantLib fixes the pillars when the bootstrap starts. The curve keeps the variables' values at the optimum (AdditionalVariables), where QuantLib leaves them in its quotes. The guess is the initial-guess function's when given, which is called once per curve built and sees no data, as QuantLib's sees none on a curve with no previous state; otherwise the traits' guess for the whole curve (GlobalGuess(BootstrapState<TTermStructure>, bool)) when they give one, or each node's guess in turn. The traits' transforms (TransformDirect(double, int, BootstrapState<TTermStructure>) and its inverse), when they have them, map the nodes to the unconstrained values the optimizer works on. The curve's nodes are the optimizer's last evaluation, its optimum. QuantLib builds the target interpolation over every node without updating it, and refuses, with no fallback to linear interpolation, a configuration its construction refuses for that many points (CheckPoints(int)); here it is then built over the first data, so a guess function that prices a helper reads the curve at the traits' initial value, where QuantLib's reads an interpolation it hasn't updated. A curve is always built afresh, so its bootstrap starts from the guess, where QuantLib re-bootstraps a curve whose quotes changed from its previous state: a documented divergence. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.IBootstrap.htm.title: Interface IBootstrap | nanoql
api/NanoQL.TermStructures.IBootstrap.htm.summary: Interface IBootstrap Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll A bootstrap: QuantLib's Bootstrap template parameter (IterativeBootstrap, GlobalBootstrap), as a configuration struct whose Calculate<TTermStructure, TTraits, TInterpolator>(BootstrapState<TTermStructure>, TInterpolator, EvaluationContext) fills a curve's working state. public interface IBootstrap Remarks A bootstrap is a readonly struct holding QuantLib's constructor parameters, whose zero value is QuantLib's default construction. QuantLib's bootstrap holds a pointer to its curve and reads and writes the curve's members as its friend; here the curve hands it a BootstrapState<TTermStructure>, the working state of the curve under construction, which the curve freezes into its nodes when Calculate<TTermStructure, TTraits, TInterpolator>(BootstrapState<TTermStructure>, TInterpolator, EvaluationContext) returns. An extension point: a bootstrap of one's own implements it. Methods Calculate<TTermStructure, TTraits, TInterpolator>(BootstrapState<TTermStructure>, TInterpolator, EvaluationContext) Fills the working state: the dates, times and data of the curve's nodes, its interpolation and maximum date, so that each helper reprices its quote. void Calculate<TTermStructure, TTraits, TInterpolator>(BootstrapState<TTermStructure> state, TInterpolator interpolator, EvaluationContext context) where TTermStructure : TermStructure where TTraits : struct, IBootstrapTraits<TTermStructure> where TInterpolator : struct, IInterpolator Parameters state BootstrapState<TTermStructure> The working state of the curve under construction. interpolator TInterpolator The curve's interpolator. context EvaluationContext The evaluation context the helpers are priced in. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.ImpliedTermStr.summary: Class ImpliedTermStructure Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll The term structure another curve implies at a date in the future, its reference date: the original's discounts divided by its discount at that date. public sealed class ImpliedTermStructure : YieldTermStructure Inheritance object Extrapolator TermStructure YieldTermStructure ImpliedTermStructure Inherited Members YieldTermStructure.Discount(Date, bool) YieldTermStructure.Discount(double, bool) YieldTermStructure.ZeroRate(Date, DayCounter, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.ZeroRate(double, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.ForwardRate(Date, Date, DayCounter, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.ForwardRate(Date, Period, DayCounter, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.ForwardRate(double, double, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.JumpDates() YieldTermStructure.JumpTimes() TermStructure.TimeFromReference(Date) TermStructure.ReferenceDate TermStructure.DayCounter TermStructure.Calendar TermStructure.SettlementDays TermStructure.MaxTime Extrapolator.AllowsExtrapolation object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Extension Methods ExtrapolatorExtensions.DisableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) ExtrapolatorExtensions.EnableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) Remarks QuantLib's curve derives from DerivedYieldTermStructure, a class template over its base, which C# can't express; it implements the template's members itself. Its day counter is the original's, read when it is built, and so is its extrapolation flag; its maximum date is the original's, read when it is asked for. QuantLib's constructor taking settlement days, whose reference date moves with the evaluation date, is Create(YieldTermStructure, int, Calendar, EvaluationContext). The original's time and discount at the reference date are read when the curve is built, where QuantLib reads them at the first discount; a curve whose original can't give them refuses to be built. An original that changes is a new curve: QuantLib's curve follows its handle. A time on the curve is read from the original at the time plus the reference date's time on the original's clock, QuantLib's sum, which assumes year fractions add. A date is read by date where they don't: where the sum and the date's own time on the original's clock differ by more than 1e-12 relative, the curve's discount at a date is the original's ratio P(d)/P(ref) by date, the one QuantLib's formula states, and its zero rates and forward rates by date follow it. On Thirty360 and on Actual/Actual ISMA without a schedule QuantLib's sum misses that ratio, by up to 1.25e-4 and 3.7e-3 relative over four years of dates on a zero curve, and gives Thirty360's month-end dates of one time one discount; on every other date, and on the day counters whose year fractions add, the curve keeps QuantLib's bits. Its day counter, maximum date and strike range are the original's. As QuantLib warns, an implied structure makes financial sense only over an original that depends on time alone, not on the asset. A time on the structure is read from the original between the reference date's time on the original's clock and that time plus the time, QuantLib's sum, which assumes year fractions add. A date is read by date where they don't: where the sum and the date's own time on the original's clock differ by more than 1e-12 relative, the structure's variance at a date is the original's forward variance from the reference date to that date by date, and its volatilities and forward variances by date follow it. On Thirty360 QuantLib's sum misses that variance, by +3.70% at 28 February and +0.75% at 30 June over a constant volatility; on every other date, and on the day counters whose year fractions add, the structure keeps QuantLib's bits. A reference date before the original's accrues no variance before the original's, where QuantLib's read counts the original's variance at a negative time (the mismatched-dates class). A documented divergence. ExtrapolatorExtensions.DisableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) ExtrapolatorExtensions.EnableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) Remarks Each strike spread's volatility spreads are interpolated bilinearly over the swap lengths and the option times, extrapolating linearly. The smile section of an option date and a swap tenor is linear between the at-the-money strike plus each strike spread, at the at-the-money volatility plus the spread interpolated there, from the section's standard deviations on Actual/365 (Fixed); a section by option time rounds the swap length to whole months and adjusts the option date to a fixing date of the swap index the tenor's at-the-money strike uses. A section's at-the-money strike is a swap index's fixing, which QuantLib computes at the query under the global evaluation date, fixings and at-par switch, and the volatility queries take no context. So the cube keeps the context it was built with, and its sections read it: a query under another context still reads the build context. Its results are QuantLib's whenever QuantLib's query runs under the settings it was built under. QuantLib's cube computes its spread interpolations on its first query; here they are built with the cube, so a refusal of the grid (a single option or swap tenor) comes at construction. QuantLib's volSpreads(i) reads past its matrices for an index past the strike spreads; it is refused here. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.IterativeBoots.summary: Struct IterativeBootstrap Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll The universal piecewise-term-structure bootstrapper: each node is solved in turn so that the helper whose pillar it is reprices its quote, and the passes repeat until the nodes stop moving when the interpolation is global or a pillar comes before its helper's latest relevant date. public readonly struct IterativeBootstrap : IBootstrap Implements IBootstrap Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.GetType() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks A configuration struct (IBootstrap): its zero value is QuantLib's default construction, every field stored so that zero reads as QuantLib's default. It reproduces QuantLib's sequence: the helpers sorted by pillar, the expired ones skipped, Brent's solver on the first pass and FiniteDifferenceNewtonSafe once the data are valid, the retries with widened brackets, the fallback without throwing, the convergence loop, and the node keeping the last value the solver evaluated, since QuantLib ignores the solver's return value. On its first pass QuantLib builds the interpolation over the nodes solved so far before each node's values are known, and takes linear interpolation instead where a global interpolation refuses to be built over that many points. The interpolation here is built with its values in one call, so the fallback is decided by the interpolator's own construction checks, CheckPoints(int); every other refusal of the interpolation is met when the solver builds it, as QuantLib meets it when the interpolation is updated. The interpolator chosen on the first pass's last node serves the later passes and the built curve. A curve is always built afresh, so its bootstrap starts from the traits' first guess: QuantLib re-bootstraps a curve whose quotes changed from its previous state, which the two reach within the bootstrap's accuracy (a documented divergence). api/NanoQL.TermStructures.KahaleSmileSec.summary: Class KahaleSmileSection Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll An arbitrage-free smile section by Kahale's C¹ interpolation and extrapolation of a source section's call prices (Kahale, "An arbitrage-free interpolation of volatilities", Risk, May 2004). public sealed class KahaleSmileSection : SmileSection Inheritance object SmileSection KahaleSmileSection Inherited Members SmileSection.Variance(double) SmileSection.Volatility(double) SmileSection.Volatility(double, VolatilityType, double) SmileSection.DigitalOptionPrice(double, OptionType, double, double) SmileSection.Density(double, double, double) SmileSection.Vega(double, double) object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The source's arbitrage-free region (SmileSectionUtils) is its core. Left of it the call prices are a Black call plus a constant, right of it a Black call or, with exponential extrapolation, an exponential; inside it the source's prices are kept, or, with interpolation, replaced by Kahale's segment functions, one per grid interval. So in the leftmost interval and right of the last grid point the source's smile is always replaced. A shifted source is handled by shifting its forward and strikes and fitting as for a lognormal one; a normal source is refused. The fit runs at construction. Five of QuantLib's defects are fixed. The put branch of the volatility implies it from the call at the shifted strike, where QuantLib's adds the unshifted one (kahalesmilesection.cpp:255), so with a shift every put-branch volatility reads 0. The left wing's check reads a digital at the wing's midpoint, (k₁ − 2·shift)/2 unshifted for the wing's shifted end k₁, where QuantLib's reads it at (k₁ − shift)/2 (:109-110), which lies in the core once its left end is negative unshifted, so the check fails and the core moves right; with interpolation it also reads a segment function not yet fitted, undefined behaviour. A segment that fails to fit removes the unfitted slot after its own, where QuantLib's removes the slot at the grid index after the segment's (:163), past the slots' end once the core's left index is 2 or more, undefined behaviour; every slot either removes is unfitted, so the two agree wherever QuantLib's is in range. And AtmLevel() is the given or the source's level, where QuantLib's returns it shifted (kahalesmilesection.hpp:142, .cpp:59), so with a shift its vega and its converted volatilities read the forward plus the shift. And a segment whose fitted function's forward runs far above its strikes, to 10¹⁴ and more, so that QuantLib's Black call and constant cancel and its prices are the cancellation's, even below their intrinsic value (:150-173), is solved again, and evaluated, anchored at its left end's price, the Black call's change taken through complementary normal integrals; a segment whose terms round within 1e-8 of its ends' prices, relative, is QuantLib's, solved and evaluated as QuantLib's, at any scale; one the anchored solve can't fit fails as QuantLib's unsolved one, its right point removed. And with interpolation, a segment whose fit misses its right end's price is refitted (Divergences/KahaleMissedSegmentTests.cs). QuantLib's fit solves for the segment's slope a by a Brent search (kahalesmilesection.cpp:151-155), but a forms the law's tails at the segment's ends, N(d₂(k₀)) = a − c′₀ and N(d₂(k₁)) = a − c′₁, by subtraction, so where the root's lognormal law puts less than about 1e-16 of its mass beyond an end, adjacent doubles of a skip over the root and the search's bracket closes on a non-root (brent.hpp:87-90). The segment then misses its right end's price and the section jumps there, an arbitrage: on a lognormal SABR smile (a forward of 5% for a year, α 0.3, β 1, ν 0.3, ρ −0.3) QuantLib's call a millionth of the forward below a strike of 7.5% is 0.000326 against 0.000646 at it. A fitted segment that misses its right end by more than 1e-8 of the price, QuantLib's own test's tolerance, and its evaluation's rounding is solved again to the same ends and slopes on the law's tail parameter u, its mass below k₀ (1 − Δ)·σ(u) and above k₁ (1 − Δ)·σ(−u), Δ = c′₁ − c′₀ and σ the logistic function, so that every member of the family is reachable, and evaluated without the law's forward, its first moment on the segment through Mills' ratios where the forward would overflow. A refit keeps QuantLib's ends and slopes, so nothing else in the section moves; a segment no refit fits fails as QuantLib's unsolved one, its right point removed. Without interpolation, the default, no segment is fitted and the core keeps the source's prices. Two of QuantLib's limits are kept. Where a segment's solve fails, its right point is removed, as QuantLib's is, which can leave one segment over most of the core (on the smile above, from 1% to 150% of the forward) far from the source; the same refit would fit most such segments, but a rescued segment far out in a wing carries QuantLib's averaged-secant slopes over a wide interval and can stray from the source further than QuantLib's Black wing does. And the left wing's fit can run its forward to 10⁵ to 10⁷ times the section's, its constant near minus that, so its prices step by an ulp of that forward, a few calls falling below their intrinsic value by about 1e-11; anchoring it at its right end would move the core through QuantLib's wing check, which reads the wing's digital. QuantLib's public helper structs (cFunction and the three solvers' functions) are the fit's internals here. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.LocalBootstrap.summary: Struct LocalBootstrap Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll The localised bootstrapper: QuantLib's LocalBootstrap, which solves each section of a curve on a non-local interpolation from the few helpers around it, so that each helper's risk stays local. public readonly struct LocalBootstrap : IBootstrap Implements IBootstrap Inherited Members ValueType.Equals(object) ValueType.GetHashCode() ValueType.ToString() object.GetType() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks A configuration struct (IBootstrap, D12): its zero value is QuantLib's default construction, a localisation of 2, positivity forced and the curve's accuracy. The curve's nodes are its first date and every helper's pillar, sorted; two helpers on one pillar are refused. From the localisation-th helper on, each step builds the interpolation over the nodes so far through LocalInterpolate(ReadOnlySpan<double>, ReadOnlySpan<double>, int, Interpolation?, int), keeping the earlier sections, and solves the step's last nodes by Levenberg-Marquardt (at most 100 iterations, the accuracy as the function's tolerance, positive values where positivity is forced) so that its last localisation helpers reprice their quotes. The interpolator must be an ILocalInterpolator (of QuantLib's, ConvexMonotone); another is refused when the curve is built, where QuantLib's template fails to compile. As QuantLib's, each calculation is a cold start, and a step's guess for its new node is the traits' guess at the step's index, QuantLib's Traits::guess(iInst, ts_, false, 0) (localbootstrap.hpp:229), kept as written. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.MultiCurve.htm.summary: Class MultiCurve Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll Builds a set of curves that form a dependency cycle, solving the bootstrapped ones together with one optimizer. public sealed record MultiCurve : IEquatable<MultiCurve> Inheritance object MultiCurve Implements IEquatable<MultiCurve> Inherited Members object.GetType() object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) Remarks The steps to set up the cycle's members: Create a MultiCurveMember for each member, with the member's reference date and day counter, to represent it: QuantLib's empty internal handle. Build the cycle's indexes and rate helpers on the members. Add each member with its curve's arguments: AddBootstrappedCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator>(MultiCurveMember, Date, IEnumerable<BootstrapHelper<YieldTermStructure>>, DayCounter, IEnumerable<double>?, IEnumerable<Date>?, TInterpolator, GlobalBootstrap) for a piecewise curve on a GlobalBootstrap, in either of the piecewise curve's forms, and AddNonBootstrappedCurve(MultiCurveMember, YieldTermStructure) for any other curve. Build(EvaluationContext): it builds the bootstrapped members, links each member once to its curve, bootstraps the bootstrapped curves jointly, every curve's data being set before any helper is priced, and returns the curves in the order they were added. An immutable builder: each Add… returns a copy. The members are linked by Build(EvaluationContext), not by the Add… calls, since a curve is built in an evaluation context; a member already linked, or already added, is refused, so a second Build(EvaluationContext) of the same builder refuses. A non-bootstrapped curve reads the curves it references when it is queried, so it needs nothing from the joint bootstrap. QuantLib's checks that a curve is a multicurve bootstrap provider with a contributor have no counterpart: a bootstrapped member is built on GlobalBootstrap by Build(EvaluationContext) itself. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.MultiCurveMemb.summary: Class MultiCurveMember Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll A member of a cycle of curves (MultiCurve): QuantLib's internal handle, a curve on which the cycle's indexes and helpers are built before the member exists, and which the multicurve's Build(EvaluationContext) links once to the member it builds. public sealed class MultiCurveMember : YieldTermStructure Inheritance object Extrapolator TermStructure YieldTermStructure MultiCurveMember Inherited Members YieldTermStructure.Discount(Date, bool) YieldTermStructure.Discount(double, bool) YieldTermStructure.ZeroRate(Date, DayCounter, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.ZeroRate(double, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.ForwardRate(Date, Date, DayCounter, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.ForwardRate(Date, Period, DayCounter, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.ForwardRate(double, double, Compounding, Frequency, bool) TermStructure.TimeFromReference(Date) TermStructure.ReferenceDate TermStructure.MaxTime Extrapolator.AllowsExtrapolation object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Extension Methods ExtrapolatorExtensions.DisableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) ExtrapolatorExtensions.EnableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) Remarks A cycle of curves has no build order, so where every other handle becomes the object itself, a member is the one reference written after it is built: once, by Build(EvaluationContext). The link is shared by every copy of the member (EnableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) returns a copy), so an index built on a copy taken before Build prices after it. Before Build, a member answers its reference date and day counter, both given when it is created, and the times they measure (TimeFromReference(Date)), and refuses every query that needs its curve, "multicurve member not built". After Build, a query is checked against the member's own range and extrapolation flag, then forwarded to the curve it is linked to with extrapolation allowed, so the member's flag rules; its calendar, settlement days and jumps are that curve's. Build links it only to a curve with its reference date and day counter, since it measures a date's time from its own reference date with its own day counter and the curve reads that time against its own; so its day counter is the one it was created with, before Build and after. Build writes the members' working state while their handles are linked, so no other thread may read a member during Build; once built, a member is immutable, as its curve is. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.Multiplicative.summary: Class MultiplicativePriceSeasonality Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll Multiplicative seasonality in the price index (CPI, RPI, HICP). public class MultiplicativePriceSeasonality : Seasonality Inheritance object Seasonality MultiplicativePriceSeasonality Derived KerkhofSeasonality Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Stationary multiplicative seasonality in the price implies that zero-coupon inflation swap rates are affected and year-on-year rates aren't; a non-stationary one affects both. The factors are a multiple of those one year needs at the frequency (12 for monthly), reused for as long as needed: 24 factors repeat every two years. A multi-year seasonality is fragile: its corrections at whole years before and after the term structure's base date must be the same, which IsConsistent(InflationTermStructure) enforces for frequencies lower than daily. The factors are normalized to the term structure's base date for zero inflation and to one year earlier for year-on-year inflation, and the seasonality is piecewise constant. Built whole: QuantLib's default constructor, which leaves the frequency uninitialized until set, and set itself, whose only caller is the constructor, aren't ported. The constructor's checks are QuantLib's validate, which isn't virtual here; nor are the three inspectors, two of which it reads (the playbook's constructor-read row), and no QuantLib class overrides them. An extension point: KerkhofSeasonality derives from it. An empty calendar, day counter, end-of-month flag or fixed-leg frequency leaves the builder's default; a pricer given is set on the swap's overnight leg. The overnight coupons build every daily value date, telescopic or not (playbook §2's telescopic row). The latest relevant date is the latest of the maturity, the last payment and the end of the last fixing's deposit, and the latest date stays that date whatever the pillar, where QuantLib's FRA and swap helpers reset theirs to the pillar date. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.OptionletStrip.summary: Class OptionletStripper1 Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll Strips optionlet (caplet and floorlet) volatilities, also called forward-forward volatilities, from the cap and floor term volatilities of a CapFloorTermVolSurface. public sealed class OptionletStripper1 : OptionletStripper Inheritance object StrippedOptionletBase OptionletStripper OptionletStripper1 Inherited Members OptionletStripper.OptionletStrikes(int) OptionletStripper.OptionletVolatilities(int) OptionletStripper.AtmOptionletRates(EvaluationContext) OptionletStripper.TermVolSurface OptionletStripper.IborIndex OptionletStripper.VolatilityType OptionletStripper.Displacement OptionletStripper.OptionletFrequency OptionletStripper.PaymentLag OptionletStripper.OptionletFixingTenors OptionletStripper.OptionletMaturities OptionletStripper.OptionletFixingDates OptionletStripper.OptionletFixingTimes OptionletStripper.OptionletPaymentDates OptionletStripper.OptionletAccrualPeriods OptionletStripper.DayCounter OptionletStripper.Calendar OptionletStripper.SettlementDays OptionletStripper.BusinessDayConvention object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The strip runs in the constructor, in QuantLib's order: the optionlets' dates and at-the-money rates, the switch strike, then per strike the caps' or floors' prices on the term volatilities, the optionlets' prices by difference and their implied volatilities. The strip reads the context it is given, its evaluation date and fixings, and is done once: a new evaluation date or market is a new stripper. Each shifted lognormal implied standard deviation is solved from QuantLib's first guess, 0.14, where QuantLib's recalculation starts from the previous calculation's result; a normal one takes no guess. A failure it was told not to throw leaves 0. Out-of-the-money options are used: floors below the switch strike and caps from it. The strike below which floors are used, or null, QuantLib's Null<Rate>(), for the average of the at-the-money rates. accuracy double The implied volatilities' accuracy. maxIter int The implied volatilities' maximum number of evaluations. discount YieldTermStructure The discount curve, or null, QuantLib's empty handle, for the index's forwarding curve. type VolatilityType The type of the stripped volatilities. displacement double The displacement of shifted lognormal volatilities. dontThrow bool Whether an optionlet whose volatility can't be implied gets 0, instead of the strip throwing. optionletFrequency Period? QuantLib's curve derives from its traits' interpolated curve; this one derives from DefaultProbabilityTermStructure and is that curve through IInterpolatedCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator>, with the traits' formulas, so a piecewise hazard-rate curve isn't a HazardRateStructure here; no QuantLib code casts to one. The members its bootstrap calls on the curve under construction are sealed. QuantLib's settlement-days constructors are Create(int, Calendar, IEnumerable<BootstrapHelper<DefaultProbabilityTermStructure>>, DayCounter, EvaluationContext, IEnumerable<double>?, IEnumerable<Date>?, TInterpolator, TBootstrap). Its constructor on a one-factor affine model of the default intensity is the one taking a OneFactorAffineModel, for the affine hazard-rate traits: the curve calls the traits' model-aware members when it holds a model, which other traits refuse, and the landed formulas otherwise. QuantLib's piecewise affine curve is a one-factor affine survival structure, with its conditional survival; this one can't change its base by its traits, so that structure is built on its nodes. A curve is always built afresh, as the piecewise yield curve is. Unsealed for its named class, which adds constructors only. SpreadTraits<Discount> is Discount with that curve type, its guesses, bounds and iteration counts Discount's. So this curve is the piecewise discount curve on a base: its discount is the base's times the interpolated spread discount, and its maximum date the earlier of its own and the base's (see PiecewiseYieldCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator, TBootstrap>); its reference date, calendar, settlement days, day counter and extrapolation flag are the base's, read when it is built. ExtrapolatorExtensions.DisableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) ExtrapolatorExtensions.EnableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) Remarks The curve bootstraps in its constructor, as a LazyObject's work is done at construction. While its bootstrap runs, the curve answers from a working state (BootstrapState<TTermStructure>), and its helpers are copies bound to the curve itself, as QuantLib binds them to this; when the bootstrap returns, the state is frozen into the curve's nodes and dropped, and the bound copies are discarded. Nothing outside the constructor sees the curve change. The helpers whose dates follow the evaluation date are re-dated for the context's (see BootstrapHelper<TTermStructure>). A curve in a cycle of curves, each bootstrapped with the others, is built by a MultiCurve. QuantLib's curve derives from its traits' interpolated curve; this one is that curve through IInterpolatedCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator>, with the traits' formula and maximum-date rule. The members its bootstrap calls on the curve under construction (DiscountImpl(double), MaxDate, MaxTime, DayCounter) are sealed. Unsealed for its named classes, which add constructors only. A spread curve (PiecewiseSpreadYieldCurve<TInterpolator, TBootstrap>) is bootstrapped on a base curve: its nodes are the spread discount factors, its discount the base's times theirs and its maximum date the earlier of its own and the base's, QuantLib's InterpolatedSpreadDiscountCurve; it allows extrapolation when the base does, when it is built. The base is read with extrapolation on, as the other derived curves read their originals. Every other curve has no base. A curve is always built afresh: QuantLib's curve, recalculated after a quote or the evaluation date changed, starts from its previous state and, when its reference date is fixed, keeps its first evaluation date's pillars. Both are documented divergences. Its maximum date is the earliest of the five structures'. QuantLib reads every structure at the time the dividend curve's day counter measures, with its own comment that this assumes one day count and "should be QL_REQUIREd" (quantotermstructure.hpp:124-131), so curves equal at every date but on different day counters give different quanto rates. Here a structure on another day counter or reference date is read at the instants the curve's times denote, on its own clock: the curves' discounts and the volatilities' variances accrued from the curve's reference date to the time, the correlation term the root of the two variances' product. Where every structure shares the dividend curve's day counter and reference date, the zero rate is QuantLib's. A documented divergence, as the finite-difference engine's mismatched times are. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.SabrFunctions..summary: Class SabrFunctions Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll The SABR functions: Hagan's lognormal and normal expansions of the SABR volatility, Le Floc'h and Kennedy's expansion, the parameters' validation and Le Floc'h and Kennedy's initial guess for a calibration. public static class SabrFunctions Inheritance object SabrFunctions Inherited Members object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The expansions keep QuantLib's order of operations, so their values are QuantLib's bit for bit wherever the C runtime's functions agree with .NET's. A VolatilityType outside its members is refused on entry, where QuantLib takes any value other than Normal as lognormal. Methods SabrFlochKennedyVolatility(double, double, double, double, double, double, double) Le Floc'h and Kennedy's expansion of the lognormal SABR volatility, with no check of its arguments. public static double SabrFlochKennedyVolatility(double strike, double forward, double expiryTime, double alpha, double beta, double nu, double rho) Parameters strike double The strike. forward double The forward. expiryTime double The time to expiry. alpha double SABR's α. beta double SABR's β. nu double SABR's ν. rho double SABR's ρ. Returns double The volatility; a second-order Taylor expansion where the strike is within 0.25% of the forward. SabrGuess(double, double, double, double, double, double, double, double, double, double, VolatilityType) Le Floc'h and Kennedy's initial guess for a SABR calibration (Le Floc'h and Kennedy, "Explicit SABR Calibration through Simple Expansions"): the parameters matching the at-the-money volatility, skew and curvature that three volatilities around the forward give. public static ImmutableArray<double> SabrGuess(double k_m, double vol_m, double k_0, double vol_0, double k_p, double vol_p, double forward, double expiryTime, double beta, double shift, VolatilityType volatilityType) Parameters k_m double The strike before the one closest to the forward. vol_m double Its volatility. k_0 double The strike closest to the forward. vol_0 double Its volatility. k_p double The strike after the one closest to the forward. vol_p double Its volatility. forward double The forward. expiryTime double The time to expiry. beta double SABR's β, which the guess returns as given. shift double The shift. volatilityType VolatilityType Normal, or shifted lognormal. Returns ImmutableArray<double> The guesses α, β, ν and ρ, in that order. Remarks A non-finite argument is refused, where QuantLib computes on it: a NaN smile gives ρ the sign of a NaN, which depends on which NaN an operation keeps, so QuantLib's value there isn't a number a caller can use. α is the smallest positive root of the guess's cubic, or its first estimate where the cubic has none, as QuantLib's. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.SabrInterpolat.summary: Class SabrInterpolatedSmileSection Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll A shifted lognormal smile section whose volatilities are a SABR fit to market volatilities at given strikes. public sealed class SabrInterpolatedSmileSection : SmileSection Inheritance object SmileSection SabrInterpolatedSmileSection Inherited Members SmileSection.ReferenceDate() SmileSection.Variance(double) SmileSection.Volatility(double) SmileSection.Volatility(double, VolatilityType, double) SmileSection.OptionPrice(double, OptionType, double) SmileSection.DigitalOptionPrice(double, OptionType, double, double) SmileSection.Density(double, double, double) SmileSection.Vega(double, double) SmileSection.ExerciseDate SmileSection.VolatilityType SmileSection.Shift SmileSection.ExerciseTime SmileSection.DayCounter object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The fit (SABRInterpolation) runs when the section is built: QuantLib's lazy calculation. QuantLib's quote forms are the value forms here, a quote being its value, and a volatility quote that isn't valid is a null value, its strike left out of the fit. With floating strikes, the strikes are offsets from the forward and the volatilities spreads over the at-the-money volatility. QuantLib's sections float with the evaluation date, having no reference date; here the Create factories take the evaluation context and fix the date. QuantLib reads one strike per volatility, past the strikes' end where there are fewer strikes than volatilities; they are refused here. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.SimpleQuoteVar.summary: Class SimpleQuoteVariables Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll Additional bootstrap variables that are plain values, each with an initial guess and an optional lower bound: QuantLib's SimpleQuoteVariables. public sealed class SimpleQuoteVariables : AdditionalBootstrapVariables Inheritance object AdditionalBootstrapVariables SimpleQuoteVariables Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks A variable with a lower bound lb is optimized as log(v − lb), its value exp(x) + lb; one without is optimized as itself. As QuantLib's detail::get reads them, a variable past the guesses given takes the last guess, or 0 where none is given, and one past the bounds given takes the last bound, or none where none is given. Immutable: QuantLib's variables are quotes the optimizer writes and the helpers read; here Values(ReadOnlySpan<double>) returns the values, which the global bootstrap's VariableHelpers reads, and the curve keeps the optimum's. Since a nanoql curve is always built afresh, Initialize(bool) gives the guesses whatever its argument, where QuantLib's reads the quotes' values, a previous bootstrap's, on a valid curve. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.SmileSectionUt.summary: Class SmileSectionUtils Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll A smile section's grid of strikes and call prices and its arbitrage-free region: the widest range of the grid, around the at-the-money point, on which the call prices decrease and are convex in the strike. public sealed class SmileSectionUtils Inheritance object SmileSectionUtils Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The moneyness is absolute (the strike less the at-the-money level) for a normal section and relative (the shifted strike over the shifted level) for a shifted lognormal one. A shifted lognormal grid starts at a moneyness of 0, the strike at minus the shift, whose call price is the shifted level. Where a strike falls outside the section's strike range, the range's end takes its place, once. Immutable: the grids and the region are computed at construction. The relative moneyness of a range's end is its shifted strike over the shifted level, as at the grid's other points. QuantLib divides the shifted strike by the unshifted level (smilesectionutils.cpp:100-101, :107-108), so with a shift the endpoints' moneyness is off: the grid can come out unsorted, and the at-the-money point is then located in the wrong place. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.SpreadFittingM.summary: Class SpreadFittingMethod Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll The spread fitting method: a spread curve fitted on top of a discounting curve, by an underlying parametric method, so that the fitted discount is the method's times the discounting curve's. public sealed class SpreadFittingMethod : FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod Inheritance object FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod SpreadFittingMethod Inherited Members FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod.Discount(ReadOnlySpan<double>, double) FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod.Solution FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod.NumberOfIterations FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod.MinimumCostValue FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod.ErrorCode FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod.ConstrainAtZero FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod.Weights FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod.L2 FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod.OptimizationMethod FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod.Constraint object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The method takes the underlying method's constraint at zero, weights, optimization method and L2 penalties, and its own cut-off times; the underlying method's own cut-offs apply to its part. When the discounting curve has another reference date than the fitted curve, its discount is rebased to the fitted curve's reference date. A discounting curve that changes is a new curve: QuantLib's method follows its handle. QuantLib reads the discounting curve at the fitted curve's time (nonlinearfittingmethods.cpp:414-416), which the discounting curve counts from its own reference date on its own day counter: dated 30 days earlier, the fitted discount misses the rebased discounting curve by up to 3.1e-3, and by up to 1.05e-2 on Act/360. Here the discounting curve is read at the instant the fitted curve's time denotes; where the two curves share their reference date and day counter it is QuantLib's read and bits. A documented divergence. volatility spreads are a row per option and swap tenor pair, the pair (j, k) of the j-th option tenor and the k-th swap tenor in row j·(swap tenors) + k, with a column per strike spread. A cube's grid, reference date and conventions are its at-the-money structure's: the constructor passes that structure's reference date, calendar, business-day convention, day counter and settlement days to SwaptionVolatilityDiscrete, whose constructor computes the grid from them. Its maximum date and time, maximum swap tenor, volatility type and shift are the at-the-money structure's, read when asked; its strikes are unbounded. The at-the-money strike of an option date and a swap tenor is the fixing of a swap index of that tenor, with the conventions of the long swap index for a tenor past the short index's, else of the short one: it reads the context's evaluation date, its fixings and its at-par switch. A derived structure that answers another structure's conventions, as QuantLib's cube answers its ATM structure's, passes them to the constructor instead. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.UltimateForwar.summary: Class UltimateForwardTermStructure Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll The Dutch regulatory term structure for pension funds: another curve, the original, up to a first smoothing point, and past it a forward rate extrapolated from the last liquid forward rate towards an ultimate forward rate, for discounting long-dated liabilities. public sealed class UltimateForwardTermStructure : ZeroYieldStructure Inheritance object Extrapolator TermStructure YieldTermStructure ZeroYieldStructure UltimateForwardTermStructure Inherited Members YieldTermStructure.Discount(Date, bool) YieldTermStructure.Discount(double, bool) YieldTermStructure.ZeroRate(Date, DayCounter, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.ZeroRate(double, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.ForwardRate(Date, Date, DayCounter, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.ForwardRate(Date, Period, DayCounter, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.ForwardRate(double, double, Compounding, Frequency, bool) YieldTermStructure.JumpDates() YieldTermStructure.JumpTimes() TermStructure.TimeFromReference(Date) TermStructure.ReferenceDate TermStructure.DayCounter TermStructure.MaxTime Extrapolator.AllowsExtrapolation object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Extension Methods ExtrapolatorExtensions.DisableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) ExtrapolatorExtensions.EnableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) Remarks Past the cut-off point T_c, the first smoothing point, the forward rate from T_c to T is UFR + (LLFR − UFR)·B(T − T_c), with B(x) = (1 − e^(−αx))/(αx) and α the growth factor. The documentation is the Dutch Central Bank's: the FTK term structure documentation (Financieel toetsingskader, https://www.dnb.nl/media/4lmprzrk/vaststelling_methode_rentetermijnstructuur_ftk.pdf), the UFR 2013-2019 term structure documentation (https://www.dnb.nl/media/0vmbxaf4/methodologie-dnb.pdf) and the UFR 2023 term structure documentation (p. 46, https://www.tweedekamer.nl/downloads/document?id=2022D50944). The zero rates may be rounded to a number of decimal places in a given compounding: rounding a rate of 1.5555% to 5 places gives 0.01556, 1.556%. QuantLib's curve derives from RelativeDerivedYieldTermStructure<ZeroYieldStructure>, a class template over its own base, which C# can't express; it implements the template's members itself, as ZeroSpreadedTermStructure does. Its reference date and day counter are the original's, read when it is built, and so is its extrapolation flag; its calendar and settlement days are the original's, read when they are asked for. Its maximum date is the latest date. Quotes or an original that change make a new curve: QuantLib's curve follows its quotes and its handle. The rounding is built with the curve, so a precision it refuses refuses the curve. Two documented divergences. QuantLib's B(x) is unguarded: α = 0 gives 0/0 and the curve throws "positive compound factor required", and α = 1e-12 puts the 60-year zero rate 9e-9 below its limit; here it is −expm1(−αx)/(αx), and 1 at αx = 0, its limit, as upstream's own oneMinusExpOverX after the pin. QuantLib reads the original without extrapolation (ultimateforwardtermstructure.hpp:168, :173), so past a base that doesn't extrapolate the curve throws although its maximum date is the latest date, where the zero- and forward-spreaded curves extrapolate; here it reads the original with extrapolation on, as theirs do. ExtrapolatorExtensions.EnableExtrapolation<T>(T, bool) Remarks The cube fits the model's smile to the market volatilities, the at-the-money volatility plus each spread, at each node of its grid (the sparse parameters). An at-the-money-calibrated cube then fills a dense grid, the union of its grid and its at-the-money structure's: off its own nodes, a strike's volatility is the at-the-money volatility plus the spread interpolated between the four surrounding nodes' fitted smiles at the strike of the same strike spread (a normal cube) or moneyness (a lognormal one), and it fits the smile there again (the dense parameters). In a single pass, the dense grid's spreads are the quoted ones interpolated the same way and the dense fit is the only one; with at-the-money calibration each node's α is then solved so that the section returns the at-the-money volatility, and the node's errors are recomputed at that α. Each fit starts from the parameter guesses interpolated at its node, and restarts as its model's fit does. A node whose fit ends on its iteration limit, or whose error reaches the tolerance, is refused with QuantLib's text. A query's smile section is the model's section at the parameters and forward interpolated at its option time and swap length, bilinearly between the nodes or, with backward-flat interpolation, backward flat in option time and linear in swap length, both flat outside the grid. It reads only what the cube stores, not the context. QuantLib's cube calibrates on its first query, and recalibrates when its quotes, its structures or the evaluation date change; this one calibrates when it is built, under the context it is given, so a refusal of the calibration comes at construction, and a new market is a new cube. The parameter guesses are read on the cube's grid, its at-the-money structure's, where QuantLib reads them on the grid of its construction-time reference date, the evaluation date: the two differ where the structure's reference date isn't that date. Immutable and thread-safe once built. QuantLib's recalibration members change a calibrated cube: they set a swap tenor's β guesses and refit that tenor's sections, and updateAfterRecalibration then refits the dense grid. Here each Recalibration(IEnumerable<double>, Period, EvaluationContext) overload returns a new cube, a copy of this one's calibrated state with both steps applied, and leaves this cube unchanged. The β values are the fits' guesses, so they are the sections' βs where the cube fixes β and the refit's starting point where it doesn't. An extension point, as in QuantLib: a model of one's own is a TModel, and QuantLib-Python's named cubes derive from it, as SabrSwaptionVolatilityCube does. The swap's two legs share one annual schedule, generated backwards from the maturity, unadjusted. Without a start date the swap starts on the evaluation date, which the helper's dates follow; with one, they don't. Inheritance object SmileSection ZabrInterpolatedSmileSection<TEvaluation> Derived ZabrFullFdInterpolatedSmileSection ZabrLocalVolatilityInterpolatedSmileSection ZabrShortMaturityLognormalInterpolatedSmileSection ZabrShortMaturityNormalInterpolatedSmileSection Inherited Members SmileSection.ReferenceDate() SmileSection.Variance(double) SmileSection.Volatility(double) SmileSection.Volatility(double, VolatilityType, double) SmileSection.OptionPrice(double, OptionType, double) SmileSection.DigitalOptionPrice(double, OptionType, double, double) SmileSection.Density(double, double, double) SmileSection.Vega(double, double) SmileSection.ExerciseDate SmileSection.VolatilityType SmileSection.Shift SmileSection.DayCounter object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The fit (ZabrInterpolation<TEvaluation>) runs when the section is built, QuantLib's lazy calculation. QuantLib's quote forms are the value forms here, a quote being its value, and a volatility quote that isn't valid is a null value, its strike left out of the fit. With floating strikes, the strikes are offsets from the forward and the volatilities spreads over the at-the-money volatility. QuantLib's sections float with the evaluation date, having no reference date; here the Create factories take the evaluation context and fix the date. QuantLib reads one strike per volatility, past the strikes' end where there are fewer strikes than volatilities; they are refused here. Unsealed for its named classes, QuantLib-Python's (ZabrShortMaturityLognormalInterpolatedSmileSection, ZabrShortMaturityNormalInterpolatedSmileSection, ZabrLocalVolatilityInterpolatedSmileSection and ZabrFullFdInterpolatedSmileSection). Its constructor reads the exercise time, so ExerciseTime is sealed here. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.ZabrModel.html.summary: Class ZabrModel Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Assembly NanoQL.dll The ZABR model (J. Andreasen and B. Huge, "ZABR - Expansions for the masses", 2011): SABR with the volatility's own volatility scaled by a power γ of the volatility. Its short-maturity lognormal and normal volatilities, and its local volatility, and call prices by finite differences: on the Dupire equation in the strike under that local volatility, and on the model's full two-dimensional equation in the forward and the volatility. public sealed class ZabrModel Inheritance object ZabrModel Inherited Members object.GetType() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks Nu is the transformed ν, ν α1−γ, as QuantLib's is. The volatilities rest on the expansion's x(K): for γ close to 1 its closed form, SABR's; otherwise the solution of an ordinary differential equation in y, integrated outward from y = 0 by AdaptiveRungeKutta<T> to each strike's y in turn, in QuantLib's order. The vector members take strictly ascending strikes, positive where β is 1. An empty vector is refused, where QuantLib reads its first element. Immutable and thread-safe. Exceptions ArgumentException A parameter is out of its range, the forward is negative, or the time isn't positive. Inheritance object SmileSection ZabrSmileSection<TEvaluation> Derived ZabrFullFdSmileSection ZabrLocalVolatilitySmileSection ZabrShortMaturityLognormalSmileSection ZabrShortMaturityNormalSmileSection Inherited Members SmileSection.ReferenceDate() SmileSection.Variance(double) SmileSection.Volatility(double) SmileSection.Volatility(double, VolatilityType, double) SmileSection.DigitalOptionPrice(double, OptionType, double, double) SmileSection.Density(double, double, double) SmileSection.Vega(double, double) SmileSection.VarianceImpl(double) SmileSection.ExerciseDate SmileSection.VolatilityType SmileSection.Shift SmileSection.DayCounter object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ToString() object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() Remarks The section builds its ZabrModel from α, β, ν, ρ and γ at its exercise time and forward. With the short-maturity lognormal kernel its volatility is the model's lognormal volatility at the strike, floored at 1e-6, and its option prices are SmileSection's. With the normal kernel its option prices are Bachelier's with the model's normal volatility, and its volatility is the lognormal one implied from them, 0 where that can't be implied, as QuantLib's catches every failure. The finite-difference kernels price calls at a strike grid, the moneyness grid times the forward (by default 0.01 to 20, its non-positive strikes dropped) with fdRefinement points between two of its strikes: by FdPrice(ReadOnlySpan<double>), or by FullFdPrice(double) at each strike. A cubic spline through those prices and the forward at strike 0 prices up to the grid's last strike, an exponential fitted to its end beyond; puts by parity; and the volatility is the lognormal one implied from those prices, as the normal kernel's. The short-maturity kernels don't read the grid. QuantLib's date constructor, whose section floats with the evaluation date, is Create(Date, double, ReadOnlySpan<double>, EvaluationContext, DayCounter?, ReadOnlySpan<double>, int), which takes the evaluation context and fixes the date. QuantLib's short-maturity kernels read the five parameters unchecked; fewer are refused here, for every kernel, with the text of QuantLib's local-volatility kernel. Unsealed for its named classes, QuantLib-Python's (ZabrShortMaturityLognormalSmileSection, ZabrShortMaturityNormalSmileSection, ZabrLocalVolatilitySmileSection and ZabrFullFdSmileSection). Its constructor reads the exercise time, so ExerciseTime is sealed here. Its reference date and day counter are the original's, read when it is built (a term structure has a fixed reference date), and so is its extrapolation flag; its calendar, settlement days and maximum date are the original's, read when they are asked for, and so are its zero rates. So it can be built on a MultiCurveMember before the cycle is built, whose reference date and day counter it reads then, as QuantLib builds it on an empty handle. The spread is added in the given compounding and frequency: the original's zero rate at a time in them, plus the spread, converted to continuous compounding at that time. A spread or an original that changes is a new curve: QuantLib's curve follows its quote and its handle. A compounded rule with no frequency, the default frequency, builds and is refused at every query that reads a zero rate, as QuantLib's is. QuantLib's constructor that takes a day counter, which it ignores, is deprecated and not ported. api/NanoQL.TermStructures.html.title: Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures | nanoql
api/NanoQL.TermStructures.html.summary: Namespace NanoQL.TermStructures Classes AbcdCalibration The abcd instantaneous volatility fitted to Black volatilities by their maturities: the root-mean-square error of the abcd Black volatilities, minimized over a, b, c and d through QuantLib's transformation (c, d and a + d positive), the fixed parameters at their guesses. AbcdFunction The abcd functional form for instantaneous volatility, f(T − t) = (a + b·(T − t))·e−c·(T − t) + d, in Rebonato's notation. AbcdFunctions QuantLib's free function of abcd.hpp. AbcdSquared The instantaneous covariance of two abcd rates as a function of time, f(T − t)·f(S − t): QuantLib's helper for its integration tests. AdditionalBootstrapVariables Variables a global bootstrap optimizes beside the curve's nodes, such as model parameters its helpers read (a futures helper's convexity adjustment): QuantLib's AdditionalBootstrapVariables. AndreasenHugeLocalVolAdapter The local volatility structure of an AndreasenHugeVolatilityInterpl: its local volatility, the strike clamped to its grid. AndreasenHugeVolatilityAdapter The Black volatility structure of an AndreasenHugeVolatilityInterpl: at a time and strike, the implied variance of its out-of-the-money option's price, by Li's rational approximation refined. AndreasenHugeVolatilityInterpl Andreasen and Huge's calibration of a local volatility surface to a sparse grid of European options: at each expiry a piecewise volatility in log strike, fitted so that one implicit step of the forward equation from the previous expiry's prices reprices the expiry's options; prices and local volatilities between expiries by partial steps. Andreasen J., Huge B., 2010. Volatility Interpolation, https://ssrn.com/abstract=1694972. AtmAdjustedSmileSection A smile section with an at-the-money level of its own, the source section's smile optionally recentred on it: the volatility at a strike is the source's at that strike moved by the source's level less the given one. AtmSmileSection A smile section with an at-the-money level of its own: another section's volatilities, its options priced on the given level. BMASwapRateHelper A rate helper for bootstrapping over BMA swap rates: the Libor fraction of the BMA swap, built at construction, that the curve prices at par. BlackConstantVol A constant Black volatility, with no time or strike dependence. BlackVarianceCurve A Black volatility curve modelled as a variance curve: the market's at-the-money Black volatilities at a set of dates, interpolated on their variances, linearly by default. For strike dependence, see BlackVarianceSurface. BlackVarianceSurface A Black volatility surface modelled as a variance surface: a matrix of the market's Black volatilities by strike and date, interpolated on their variances, bilinearly by default. BlackVarianceTermStructure The adapter that lets a Black-volatility structure implement only BlackVarianceImpl(double, double): its volatility is the square root of the variance over the time, at a time of 0.00001 where the time is 0. BlackVolTermStructure The Black-volatility term structure: the base of the structures that give Black volatilities and variances by maturity and strike. Volatilities are on an annual basis. BlackVolTimeExtrapolation The time extrapolation of Black volatility structures beyond their last time, for a strike-dependent surface and for an at-the-money curve, by one of BlackVolTimeExtrapolationType's strategies. BlackVolatilitySurfaceDelta A Black volatility surface quoted by delta: put deltas, call deltas and optionally an at-the-money quote at each expiry, each delta's volatilities a BlackVarianceCurve in time, its smile at a time the deltas converted to strikes on the spot and the domestic and foreign curves under the delta and at-the-money conventions, interpolated in strike. BlackVolatilityTermStructure The adapter that lets a Black-volatility structure implement only BlackVolImpl(double, double): its variance is the volatility squared times the time. BondHelper A rate helper for bootstrapping over bond prices: the bond's clean or dirty price on the curve. BootstrapHelperExtensions QuantLib's setTermStructure, as a copy of the helper's own static type. BootstrapHelperFunctions The free functions of QuantLib's bootstraphelper.hpp. BootstrapHelper<TTermStructure> The base of the helpers a term structure is bootstrapped on: an instrument's quote, the dates it determines, and the quote the curve implies. BootstrapState<TTermStructure> The working state of a curve under construction: QuantLib's friend access to the curve's instruments, dates, times, data, interpolation and maximum date, which its bootstrap reads and writes. CPIBondHelper A rate helper for bootstrapping over the prices of CPI bonds: a BondHelper on the CPIBond its arguments describe. CPIVolatilitySurface The base class of zero-inflation (CPI, RPI, HICP) volatility structures, which observe an index with a lag. CapFloorTermVolCurve The at-the-money cap and floor term-volatility curve: the volatility of a cap or floor of a given length, interpolated in the market volatilities of caps and floors of given lengths, whatever the strike. CapFloorTermVolSurface The cap/floor smile volatility surface: the volatility for a given cap/floor, interpolated in a surface of the market term volatilities of a set of caps and floors of given lengths and strikes. CapFloorTermVolatilityStructure The base class of cap/floor term-volatility structures: the volatility of a cap or floor of a given length and strike. CapletVarianceCurve A caplet volatility curve: the caplet volatilities by date, interpolated in variance by a BlackVarianceCurve (not forced monotone), the same at every strike. CdsHelper The base of the credit-default-swap bootstrap helpers: a standard swap from the evaluation date, repriced on the default-probability curve under construction. CmsMarket A set of CMS quotes: the bid and ask spreads over the Ibor leg of CMS swaps of each length on each swap index, with the spreads, spot and forward CMS leg NPVs the market implies and the model gives. CmsMarketCalibration The calibration of a SABR swaption cube's βs, and of the CMS pricers' mean reversion, to a CMS market: QuantLib's CmsMarketCalibration. CmsMarketCalibrationResults<TResult> A CMS market calibration's results: QuantLib's compute result and the members it leaves on the calibration and its cube and market (sparseSabrParameters_, denseSabrParameters_, browseCmsMarket_, error(), endCriteria()). CompositeZeroYieldStructure A zero-yield term structure composed of two curves: its zero rate is a function of the two curves' zero rates, in the given compounding and frequency. ConstantCPIVolatility A constant CPI volatility, with no strike or time dependence. ConstantCapFloorTermVolatility A constant cap and floor term volatility, for every length and strike. ConstantOptionletVolatility A constant caplet and floorlet volatility, for every option date and strike. ConstantSwaptionVolatility A constant swaption volatility, for every option date, swap tenor and strike. ConstantYoYOptionletVolatility A constant year-on-year optionlet volatility, with no strike or time dependence, over a strike range. CubicBSplinesFitting The cubic B-splines fitting method: a discount function d(t) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} c_i N_{i,3}(t) over a set of cubic B-splines. CubicForwardCurve A yield term structure based on cubic interpolation of instantaneous forward rates. CubicInterpolatedSmileSection QuantLib-Python's CubicInterpolatedSmileSection: an InterpolatedSmileSection<TInterpolator> with cubic interpolation, QuantLib's default Cubic unless another is given. CubicZeroCurve A yield term structure based on cubic interpolation of zero rates. DefaultDensityCurve The default-density curve with linear interpolation: QuantLib-Python's DefaultDensityCurve, QuantLib's InterpolatedDefaultDensityCurve<Linear>. DefaultDensityStructure The default-density term structure: an adapter that lets a derived curve implement the default density, from which the hazard rates follow. DefaultProbabilityHelperExtensions QuantLib's setTermStructure for default-probability helpers, as a copy of the helper's own static type. DefaultProbabilityTermStructure The default-probability term structure: the base of the credit curves that give survival and default probabilities, default densities and hazard rates. DepositRateHelper A rate helper for bootstrapping over deposit rates: the deposit's rate is the index fixing the curve forecasts for its fixing date. DiscountCurve A yield term structure based on log-linear interpolation of discount factors. ExponentialSplinesFitting The exponential-splines fitting method: a discount function d(t) = Σ_{i=1}^{9} c_i e^(−κ i t), the constants c_i and κ determined by the fit. FittedBondDiscountCurve A discount curve fitted to a set of bonds: a discount function d(t), a fitting method's, fitted so that the bonds' cash flows discounted on it reproduce their prices in an optimized sense, the price errors weighted by the inverse of the bonds' durations. FittedBondDiscountCurveFittingMethod The base fitting method of a FittedBondDiscountCurve: the methodology that constructs the curve, a discount function of parameters fitted to the bonds' prices. FixedLocalVolSurface A local volatility surface on fixed values: a matrix of local volatilities, one column per time and one row per strike, each time's strikes its own; interpolated in strike at each time, linearly by default, and linearly in time between them, clamped to the first and last times. FixedRateBondHelper A rate helper for bootstrapping over the prices of fixed-rate bonds: a BondHelper on the FixedRateBond its arguments describe. FlatForward A flat forward rate term structure. FlatHazardRate A flat hazard-rate curve. FlatSmileSection A flat smile section: one volatility at every strike. ForwardCurve A yield term structure based on backward-flat interpolation of instantaneous forward rates. ForwardFlatForwardCurve A yield term structure based on forward-flat interpolation of instantaneous forward rates. ForwardSpreadedTermStructure A term structure with a spread added to the instantaneous forward rate of another curve, the original. FraRateHelper A rate helper for bootstrapping over FRA rates: the index fixing the curve forecasts for the FRA's start, or, without the indexed coupon, the simple forward rate between its start and maturity dates. FuturesRateHelper A rate helper for bootstrapping over Ibor index futures prices: the price is 100 less the forward rate the curve implies between the start and maturity dates, plus the convexity adjustment, in percent. FxSwapRateHelper A rate helper for bootstrapping over FX swap rates: the forward points the curve and the collateral curve imply between the swap's earliest and latest dates, the forward being the spot plus the points. Gaussian1dSmileSection A smile section generated by a Gaussian1d model: on a swap index, the model's swaption prices on the swap rate fixing on the section's date, per unit of annuity; on an Ibor index, its caplet prices per unit of the caplet's accrued discount. Its volatility is the lognormal one implied from them, 0 where it can't be implied. Gaussian1dSwaptionVolatility The swaption volatilities a Gaussian1d model implies: each option date and swap tenor's Gaussian1dSmileSection on the index base cloned to the tenor. GlobalLinearSimpleZeroCurve A piecewise linear simple-zero-rate curve bootstrapped globally: QuantLib-Python's GlobalLinearSimpleZeroCurve, the PiecewiseYieldCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator, TBootstrap> on SimpleZeroYield, Linear and GlobalBootstrap. GlobalPiecewiseConvexMonotoneForward A piecewise convex-monotone forward-rate curve bootstrapped globally: QuantLib-Python's GlobalPiecewiseConvexMonotoneForward, the PiecewiseYieldCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator, TBootstrap> on ForwardRate, ConvexMonotone and GlobalBootstrap. GlobalPiecewiseConvexMonotoneZero A piecewise convex-monotone zero-rate curve bootstrapped globally: QuantLib-Python's GlobalPiecewiseConvexMonotoneZero, the PiecewiseYieldCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator, TBootstrap> on ZeroYield, ConvexMonotone and GlobalBootstrap. GlobalPiecewiseCubicZero A piecewise cubic zero-rate curve bootstrapped globally: QuantLib-Python's GlobalPiecewiseCubicZero, the PiecewiseYieldCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator, TBootstrap> on ZeroYield, Cubic and GlobalBootstrap. GlobalPiecewiseFlatForward A piecewise flat (backward-flat) forward-rate curve bootstrapped globally: QuantLib-Python's GlobalPiecewiseFlatForward, the PiecewiseYieldCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator, TBootstrap> on ForwardRate, BackwardFlat and GlobalBootstrap. GlobalPiecewiseKrugerLogDiscount A piecewise Kruger log-cubic discount curve bootstrapped globally: QuantLib-Python's GlobalPiecewiseKrugerLogDiscount, the PiecewiseYieldCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator, TBootstrap> on Discount, KrugerLog and GlobalBootstrap. GlobalPiecewiseLinearForward A piecewise linear forward-rate curve bootstrapped globally: QuantLib-Python's GlobalPiecewiseLinearForward, the PiecewiseYieldCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator, TBootstrap> on ForwardRate, Linear and GlobalBootstrap. GlobalPiecewiseLogCubicDiscount A piecewise log-cubic discount curve bootstrapped globally: QuantLib-Python's GlobalPiecewiseLogCubicDiscount, the PiecewiseYieldCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator, TBootstrap> on Discount, LogCubic and GlobalBootstrap. GlobalPiecewiseLogLinearDiscount A piecewise log-linear discount curve bootstrapped globally: QuantLib-Python's GlobalPiecewiseLogLinearDiscount, the PiecewiseYieldCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator, TBootstrap> on Discount, LogLinear and GlobalBootstrap. GlobalPiecewiseLogMixedLinearCubicDiscount A piecewise log-mixed linear-cubic discount curve bootstrapped globally: QuantLib-Python's GlobalPiecewiseLogMixedLinearCubicDiscount, the PiecewiseYieldCurve<TTraits, TInterpolator, TBootstrap> on Discount, LogMixedLinearCubic and GlobalBootstrap. GridModelLocalVolSurface A local volatility surface parameterised for calibration: one positive parameter per grid point of dates and strikes, all starting at 1, the surface a FixedLocalVolSurface on them. HazardRateCurve The hazard-rate curve with backward-flat interpolation: QuantLib-Python's HazardRateCurve, QuantLib's InterpolatedHazardRateCurve<BackwardFlat>. InterpolatedSimpleZeroCurve<TInterpolator> A yield term structure based on the interpolation of simply compounded zero rates. InterpolatedSpreadDiscountCurve<TInterpolator> A yield curve over a base curve, its discount the base's times an interpolated spread discount factor. InterpolatedSurvivalProbabilityCurve<TInterpolator> A default-probability term structure interpolating survival probabilities. InterpolatedYoYInflationCurve<TInterpolator> An inflation term structure interpolating year-on-year inflation rates.
